**A caution on the premise.** The report concludes the chemistry is validated
because CO "looks correct". Against `sec54.pdr.fin` at matched A_V, from their
own section 6 table:

    A_V    ref CO     theirs      ours      theirs/ref   ours/ref
    2.03   6.87e-09   2.00e-08   1.06e-09      2.9x        0.16
    2.24   1.57e-08   1.20e-06   1.93e-09       76x        0.12
    2.35   2.36e-08   6.50e-06   4.70e-10      275x        0.020

Their CO overshoots the reference by up to 275x while ours undershoots by ~50x,
and their x(C+) oscillates 4.4e-5 -> 9.1e-11 -> 1.6e-4 -> 4.6e-11 between
adjacent cells with Te spiking to 62-70 K where neighbours sit at 21-25 K. Both
trees diverge from 3D-PDR at A_V 2-3, in opposite directions.

### The one live candidate, and its measurement

Tier 2 of `Runaway-Cascade-FIX.txt`, never implemented in either tree.
`emission_mod.f90:720-727`:

    T4 = MAX(5000.,TeUsed)*1.e-4
    alpha2tS = 27.2*(T4**(-0.678))
    correction = alpha2tS * NeUsed*elemAbun(He)*ionDen(He+)*1.45673*hcRyd*1e11
    sumDiffuseHeI(j2TsP) = sumDiffuseHeI(j2TsP) + correction

`j2TsP` is `locate(nuArray, 1.45673, ...)` = 19.82 eV, above the 13.6 eV edge.
In a 14 K cell the rate comes from a 5000 K extrapolation, with no guard. It is
proportional to x(He+), which runs 2-7.5x the reference deep in our PDR - an
excess never explained - and D-227 left exactly three cells still flipping at
iteration 12 "on the real 19.8 eV He I line".

**Result: it is not the leak.** One cell per 0.5 mag of A_V, 90 samples over
A_V 0.494-3.094:

    A_V    cells   Te(K)    ion/gas   corr/ion
    0.49       6  6981.6      0.621   2.66e-02
    0.81      14    24.0      0.108   3.27e-03
    1.32      14    26.0      0.127   3.97e-03
    1.73      14    23.7      0.137   5.29e-03
    2.28      14    14.9      0.425   7.77e-03
    2.77      14    12.5      0.403   8.69e-03
    3.06      14    11.2      0.376   9.22e-03

The term supplies **0.33% to 0.92% of the ionizing gas emission through the
PDR**. The 2.7% in the first row is not a PDR number: that bucket averages
cells straddling the ionization front at a mean 6982 K, where the clamp is
barely active. The hypothesis is discarded.

**Neither proposed fix was ever the right one.** Deleting the `MAX` moves
alpha2tS the wrong way - recombination rises as temperature falls, so at 14 K
the unclamped fit gives ~2334 against 43.5 clamped, a 54x larger injection.
Zeroing below 1000 K is a hardcoded threshold selecting physics at run time,
the anti-pattern CLAUDE.md puts first. Measuring first avoided implementing
either.

### What the probe did find

**The ionizing share of a cold cell's own gas re-emission rises with depth as
the gas cools**: 11-14% at 24-26 K, 38-43% at 11-15 K. That is the D-232 leak
re-measured on a different run through a different code path - not identical to
its 49-62% figure, which was defined over different cells and possibly before
the dust term was split out, but the same mechanism: as kT shrinks the
recombination continua collapse into narrow spikes sitting on their own
thresholds, so a growing share of the gas spectrum lands above 13.6 eV. With
helium's metastable line excluded at under 1%, the remaining ~40% is the H I,
He I and He II recombination continua. **Splitting `ionTot` by species is the
next diagnostic and it is nearly free - the probe already computes the three
sums and prints only their total.**

### How Cloudy does it (c25.00, read from source)

There is no `alpha2tS` analogue at all. 2^3S is a level in the He-like
iso-sequence model atom and its population comes from solving the full
collisional-radiative matrix by LAPACK inversion (`iso_level.cpp:168`), fed by
`HeCSInterp` collision rates (`iso_solve.cpp:527-538`), photoionization out of
the level, and recombination in. There is no closed-form coefficient to clamp.

Recombination coefficients come from Hummer & Storey 1998 photoionization
cross-sections (`helike_recom.cpp:119`) through the Milne relation, integrated
numerically with `qg32` (`iso_radiative_recomb.cpp:45-103`), either at the
actual `phycon.te` or by interpolating a table built that way on the grid
`TeRRCoef[i] = 0.25*i` in log10 T for i = 0..40 - **1 K to 1e10 K** in
quarter-decade steps (`:826`, `N_ISO_TE_RECOMB = 41` in `iso.h:102`). 14 K sits
well inside it, so no clamp is ever needed. Out of range, Cloudy neither clamps
nor extrapolates: it prints "TempInterp called with te out of bounds" and calls
`cdEXIT(EXIT_FAILURE)` (`:1232-1237`). Its only temperature floor,
`TEMP_LIMIT_LOW = 2.8` K (`phycon.h:133`), bounds the temperature solver, not
any rate coefficient.

The decay is A = **1.272e-4 s^-1**, single-photon M1, with 1%/20% error bars
registered through `iso_put_error` (`helike_einsta.cpp:322-325`). The
two-photon channel is set up separately at 4.09e-9 s^-1
(`cont_createpointers.cpp:811`) and Cloudy's own comment notes the M1 rate is
~1e4 larger - so Cloudy emits a single 19.82 eV photon too. **I had started to
write that Cloudy spreads this over a two-photon continuum; the source says
otherwise, and the claim was withdrawn before it was made.**

**The real gap is not the coefficient.** MOCASSIN's emission is
`alpha * Ne * x(He+) * h_nu` with **no destruction channel for 2^3S at all** -
no collisional de-excitation, no transfer to singlets, no photoionization out
of the metastable level. In Cloudy those are what set the population. So the
single-coefficient formula is the wrong model rather than a right model with a
bad constant. Given the measurement above this is now moot for the leak, but it
is the reason neither proposed patch would have been principled.

### Also shipped: two division-by-zero guards

`emission_mod.f90:888` normalised `recPDF` by `recPDF(nbins)` and `:1013`
normalised `dustPDF` by `dustPDF(nbins)`, both unguarded. A cell with no
emission in that channel gave 0/0 -> NaN in the PDF that every gas (resp.
dust, since D-233) absorption samples. Both now test the total first and fall
back to a zeroed PDF - degenerate, but finite and recognisable, which NaN is
not. Taken from the `_testing` tree, the one thing in it worth porting.

**Measured inert**, against `d233-channels` at identical settings:

    control                     d233-channels    d243-heicorr
    radiated energy [e36 erg/s]      2699.80         2699.26   (-0.02%)
    convergence                        87.8%           87.65%
    H II Te, mean                    12095.0 K       11998.4 K  (-0.8%)
    ionization front           r=1.400e19, A_V 0.561    identical
    deep x(H2)                        0.4749          0.4749
    deep x(HI)                      5.013e-02       5.012e-02
    H budget max|1-sum|              1.108e-04       1.084e-04
    deep T_dust                       12.25 K         12.09 K

They only fire on a cell with literally zero emission in a channel, and this
model has none - they are insurance against a NaN, not a change in behaviour.

### An unrelated finding, recorded because it retires a D-233 detail

D-233 reported "a single cell at A_V = 2.24 sitting at 53 K where its
neighbours are 20-23 K: the one place in the model that makes CO in quantity,
23x the reference". In `d233-channels` that cell reads T = 53.26 K, CO/ref
22.8x, OH/ref 41.2x. **In d243, an independent realisation at identical
settings, the same cell reads T = 17.25 K, CO/ref 2.75e-02, OH/ref 3.73e-02.**
The warm CO-producing cell does not reproduce; it was a realisation artefact,
and D-233's remark about it should not be carried forward. This is the same
lesson as D-242 - a deep single cell is not evidence on this fixture - now
demonstrated on the analog side as well as the biased one.

Both analog runs do show the C+ cliff beyond A_V ~1.9 (d243: x(C+)/ref 0.19 at
1.92, 1.3e-2 at 2.03, 2.2e-4 at 2.35), which is expected and is exactly what
D-237 diagnosed and D-239 fixed with biasing - these runs have it switched off.

**Still open, and untouched.** CO 1-2 decades under the reference with carbon
reproduced at 1.00 under biasing. Nothing in D-243 bears on it.

## D-244 - the cold-gas ionizing emission is helium's recombination continuum (2026-09-12)

`runs/d244-species`: the D-243 configuration with the probe's ionizing sum
split by emitter. Analog, `nPhotons 6000000`, `teProbe 1`, no `pathStretch`,
`maxIterateMC 13 95.` (see the OOM note below). 24:56 per processor, clean
exit, 90 `[D244]` lines over A_V 0.494-3.094, no format overflows.

D-243 left a specific gap: the He I 2^3S metastable line carries under 1% of
the ionizing gas emission, but 38-43% of a cold cell's gas spectrum still sits
above 13.6 eV. The probe already computed the three species sums internally and
printed only their total, so exposing them cost one print statement.

### Result

    A_V    Te(K)     fHI     fHeI    fHeII
    0.49   6977.1  0.9549   0.0451   0.0000
    0.81     24.0  0.3943   0.6057   0.0000
    1.32     25.9  0.1910   0.8090   0.0000
    1.73     22.2  0.0462   0.9538   0.0000
    2.28     17.0  0.1282   0.8718   0.0000
    2.77     12.6  0.1148   0.8852   0.0000
    3.06     11.0  0.1319   0.8681   0.0000

**In the hot gas at the front hydrogen supplies 95% of the ionizing emission,
which is correct and expected. Through the whole cold PDR it inverts: helium
supplies 87-95%.** He II is identically zero - absolute ~1e-9 - as it must be
where there is no He++.

`ionHeI` still contains `correction` (added to `sumDiffuseHeI(j2TsP)` before the
probe), but D-243 measured that at 0.33-0.92% of `ionTot`, so subtracting it
moves fHeI by under a point. **The carrier is the He I recombination continuum
at its own 24.6 eV threshold**, not the metastable line.

### Why this matters

The He I recombination continuum is proportional to `x(He+) * Ne`. Deep in our
PDR x(He+) runs **2.1 to 7.5x the reference** (D-241, `runs/d241-photons`):
2.71 at A_V 1.92, 2.29 at 2.24, rising to 7.50 at 3.09. That excess has been on
the open list since D-231 and was never explained - D-233 showed the pooled PDF
was not its cause, and D-234 showed the only source term for helium in
shielded gas is cosmic rays over a recombination sink with charge exchange
zeroed by the 6000 K gate.

So the chain now reads: excess He+ -> excess 24.6 eV recombination continuum ->
emitted inside a cell ~700 optical depths per cell thick at that energy ->
reabsorbed on the spot -> H0 and He0 photoionization. That is the same
architecture as the D-227 relaxation oscillation, through a different channel,
and it is a *loop*: the reabsorbed continuum is itself part of what sustains
x(He+).

**This is a hypothesis about a mechanism, not a measurement of one.** What is
measured is the 87-95% share and the 2-7.5x He+ excess. Whether the continuum
sustains the excess, or merely tracks it, is not established - the excess could
equally be set by the cosmic-ray source with no feedback at all. Distinguishing
them is the next step and it is cheap: the D-234 probe already prints `up` and
`dn` per ion, so comparing the photoionization term for He0 against the
cosmic-ray term in the same cells says directly whether the continuum is
contributing to helium's own ionization balance or only to hydrogen's.

### Two process notes

**Measured at 13 iterations, not 22.** The first attempt was killed by the
harness's low-memory guard at iteration 6. The relaunch shortened the run,
which reduces the exposure window but not the peak footprint, so it was a
probabilistic mitigation rather than a fix. It is validated after the fact:
`ion/gas` agrees with D-243's 22-iteration values to 1-2% in six of seven
buckets (0.620/0.621, 0.109/0.108, 0.129/0.127, 0.403/0.403, 0.375/0.376), the
exception being A_V 1.73 at 0.164 against 0.137. Deep-cell Te differs by ~2 K
between the two runs, which is the D-242 scatter and not a trend.

**Memory, open.** Measured with PSS, this run holds **1.05 GB/rank, 14.74 GB
across 14 ranks** - against the 393 MB/rank (5.5 GB) that the project's
documented model, 234 MB + 10.47 kB/cell at 15204 active cells, predicts. That
is 2.7x, and it is real: PSS 14.74 GB against summed RSS 15.00 GB means shared
pages account for only 0.26 GB. One `(15205, 600)` real array is 36.5 MB, so
1.05 GB/rank is ~29 such arrays where the documented per-cell term implies four
or five. **Cause unknown, and deliberately not written into CLAUDE.md or the
memory note**: distinguishing "regression in this tree" from "the model always
understated this fixture" requires building an older commit and measuring it,
and the `-np 14` guidance and the 58^3 ceiling both derive from that model. My
first reading of this, that the run was a small contributor to system pressure,
was wrong - it held ~60% of available RAM, so the kill was substantially our
own doing.

**Still open and untouched.** CO 1-2 decades under the reference with carbon at
1.00 under biasing. Nothing in D-243 or D-244 bears on it directly, though the
He+ excess and the molecular deficit have both survived every fix so far.

## D-245 - a leak of my own: an allocate guard that outgrew its deallocate (2026-09-12)

Found by asking why D-244's first attempt was killed for memory at iteration 6
when D-243, an identical configuration, had completed 22 iterations an hour
earlier.

### The defect

    :760   if (lgDebug .or. pdrSplitField /= 0) then
              allocate(JDifTemp(0:grid(iG)%nCells, nbins), ...)
    :923   if (lgDebug) then
              if ( allocated(linePacketsTemp) ) deallocate(linePacketsTemp)
              if ( allocated(JDifTemp) )        deallocate(JDifTemp)
           end if

**D-158/D-225 added `pdrSplitField /= 0` to the allocate guard and left the
deallocate under `lgDebug` alone.** That was my edit: the point was to unpack
the reduced diffuse field into `grid%JDif` for the D-225 closure census, and I
changed one guard of a pair.

Why it leaks rather than merely being untidy: **`iterateMC` is `recursive`**
(declared at `:45`). It does not loop over MC iterations - it advances
`nIterateMC` at `:3220` and calls *itself* at `:3227`. A local allocatable is
auto-deallocated on return, but the return does not happen until the whole
recursive chain unwinds, so anything still allocated at the recursive call
stays live in that frame and in every frame beneath it. With `pdrSplitField 1`
and `lgDebug` off - exactly the `hiipdr-split` fixture - each iteration left one
`(15205, 600)` real4 array behind: **34.8 MiB per rank per iteration**.

`JSteTemp` sits two lines below, outside the `lgDebug` block, and is freed every
iteration. That asymmetry is what made the bug invisible on inspection.

### Measured, before and after

Per-rank PSS, `-np 4`, same fixture, `maxIterateMC 6`:

    iteration   before      after     saving
        1       754.6 MB   685.1 MB    -69
        2       789.5 MB   685.1 MB   -104
        3       828.5 MB   689.3 MB   -139
        4       874.6 MB   700.7 MB   -174
        5         --       703.9 MB
        6         --       720.1 MB

Before: monotonic, +34.9 MB at the first step against 34.8 MiB predicted from
the array dimensions, and it never comes back down. After: flat, and the
residual wobble (689 -> 713 -> 700 -> 717 -> 704 -> 720) moves in **both**
directions, which is transient allocation within an iteration rather than
accumulation. The saving grows by ~35 MB per iteration, which is the signature
of one such array per recursion level now being freed.

Extrapolated to the 22-iteration production setting: ~1420 MB/rank, ~19.9 GB
across 14 ranks, against ~700 MB/rank and ~9.8 GB fixed. That is the difference
between the run fitting on this machine and the harness killing it, and it is
why the 2e7-packet and 22-iteration runs had been getting progressively harder
to complete.

### Scope

**No computed quantity is affected.** The leak consumes memory and touches
nothing else, and both affected runs completed. D-243's negative result on the
19.82 eV helium line and D-244's finding that the He I recombination continuum
supplies 87-95% of the cold PDR's ionizing gas emission both stand.

Audit of every other temporary in `iterateMC` - all pair symmetrically, and all
are freed well before the recursive call at `:3227`:

    opacityTemp      alloc :252 unguarded   dealloc :279 unguarded
    dustPDFTemp      alloc :434 lgDust      dealloc :530 lgDust
    recPDFTemp       alloc :455 unguarded   dealloc :566 unguarded
    totalLinesTemp   alloc :463 unguarded   dealloc :561 unguarded
    linePDFTemp      alloc :477 lgDebug     dealloc :564 lgDebug
    JSteTemp         alloc :753 unguarded   dealloc :927 unguarded
    linePacketsTemp  alloc :766 lgDebug     dealloc :924 lgDebug
    JDifTemp         alloc :761 lgDebug|pdrSplitField   dealloc :925 lgDebug

`JDifTemp` was the only mismatch. The fix moves its deallocate out of the
`lgDebug` block so the guard matches the allocation.

The `_testing` tree had already corrected this independently - D-243's diff
listed `if (allocated(JDifTemp)) deallocate(JDifTemp)` among the lines present
only on their side, and I recorded it there as an unremarkable formatting
difference rather than recognising it as a fix. That was a missed signal.

### Still open, and NOT explained by this

**The baseline is 685 MB/rank against the 393 MB the documented model predicts
(234 MB + 10.47 kB/cell at 15204 active cells) - 1.74x, present at iteration 1
before any accumulation.** One `(15205, 600)` real4 array is 34.8 MiB, so
685 MB/rank is ~20 such arrays where the documented per-cell term implies four
or five. Deliberately **not** written into CLAUDE.md or the memory note:
separating "regression in this tree" from "the model always understated this
fixture" requires building an older commit and measuring it, and the `-np 14`
guidance and the 58^3 ceiling both derive from that model.

### Process notes

The first verification attempt was **invalid and I nearly reported it**. Its
`cp` of the fixed binary failed with "Text file busy" - the previous probe's
sampler had exited after a fixed 40 samples while the `mpirun` it launched kept
running - so the verification executed the *old* binary alongside 4 surviving
old ranks, 8 in total, and was killed for memory. The only trace was a
Portuguese error on line 1 of the task output, which I did not read until the
run was over. Two corrections: the retry verifies the copy with `cmp` and
aborts if it did not land, and the sampler's lifetime is tied to the run's
(`while kill -0 $MPID`) with a cleanup pass so nothing survives it.

Separately, `pkill -f "^\./mocassin$"` killed its own invoking shell, because
the pattern appears in that shell's own command line - exit 144 with no output.
`pkill -x mocassin`, which matches the process name rather than the command
line, is the correct form.

## D-246 - the helium loop is dead, and the excess is a sink MOCASSIN never had (2026-09-12)

Following D-244, which found the He I recombination continuum supplying
87-95% of the ionizing emission of cold PDR gas. The question it raised: does
that continuum ionize the helium that emits it - a loop - or does it merely
track an excess set elsewhere?

Answered from data already on disk. No new run was needed: the D-234 probe
already prints `phot` = `nPhotoSte(elem,ion)` per ion, and the cosmic-ray term
is not a variable but the constant at `update_mod.f90:2653-2656`,
`5.98e-18 * zeta/1.3e-17` for H and `6.50e-18 * zeta/1.3e-17` for He, which at
this fixture's `pdrZeta 5.0e-17` is 2.300e-17 and 2.500e-17 s^-1.

### 1. The loop is dead

Over all 434 sampled PDR cells in `runs/d244-species`:

    *H  1  up 2.301E-17  phot 1.000E-20  dn 4.772E-13  Ne*alpha 4.772E-13
    He  1  up 2.501E-17  phot 1.000E-20  dn 4.651E-13  Ne*alpha 4.651E-13

`phot` is min = max = mean = 1.000e-20, the initialisation floor set at
`update_mod.f90:169`, and `up` is exactly the cosmic-ray constant plus that
floor. **Photoionization runs at 4e-4 of the cosmic-ray rate, for hydrogen as
well as helium.** So the ionizing emission D-244 measured produces a field that
ionizes nothing at all.

**The instrumentation artefact was excluded before concluding.** Every He line
prints `nu_th 0.0000`, which would be consistent with the accumulation never
sampling helium's band. It is not: helium has its own branch at `:199-207`,
`IPNuP = HeIlevNuP(1)`, `highNuP = nbins`, with `phXSec` from
`HeISingXSecP(1)` at `:224-230`. The band is covered from threshold to the top
bin. The zero is a display defect in the probe itself - `:2739` prints
`nuArray(elementP(elem,ion,outShell,1))`, and `elementP` and `outShell` are
populated only on the `elem > 2` path. It never touches `nPhotoSte`. Worth
fixing so the probe does not mislead later.

**Consequence: D-244's 87-95% is a consequence of the He+ excess, not its
driver.** That closes the hypothesis D-244 raised, negatively.

### 2. So what does set x(He+)? Not what I predicted

With `phot` at the floor and `chex` zeroed below 6000 K, MOCASSIN's helium
balance reduces to x(He+) = CR/(Ne*alpha). Both codes ionize helium from an
identical zeta with identical coefficients (D-193), so the excess should be
(x(e)_ref/x(e)_our) * (T_our/T_ref)^0.7. Tested:

    A_V     Te    x(e)our    x(e)ref    T_ref   obs He+/ref   predicted
    0.72  23.45  2.736e-04  2.463e-04  105.72        1.52        0.31
    1.30  26.03  2.605e-04  2.293e-04   81.07        3.15        0.40
    1.78  24.96  2.349e-04  2.262e-04   46.94        3.93        0.62
    2.19  25.49  6.448e-05  2.051e-04   30.79       23.97        2.79

**The prediction fails, and with the wrong sign.** Our x(e) is HIGHER than the
reference's and our gas is colder, so CR/(Ne*alpha) says we should have LESS
He+ than the reference. We have more, everywhere.

### 3. Why: the reference is sink-limited, we are CR-limited

Computing CR/(Ne*alpha) from the reference's *own* x(e) and T, against its own
x(He+):

    A_V      T     x(He+)      x(e)    CR/(Ne*alpha)   obs/pred
    0.50  118.4  4.026e-06  2.707e-04    1.099e-04       0.037
    0.99   98.9  1.903e-06  2.333e-04    1.130e-04       0.017
    1.49   66.8  1.637e-06  2.287e-04    8.863e-05       0.018
    2.01   36.4  1.993e-06  2.181e-04    6.193e-05       0.032

**3D-PDR sits 30-60x below its own CR-limited value at every depth.** Its He+
is set by destruction routes other than recombination. The equation was never
valid on both sides, which is why the comparison inverted.

Those routes, from `dataPDR/rates_reduced.d`:

    156/157  He+ + H   -> He + H+     4.85e-15 T^0.18 (10-1000 K), 3.28e-15 T^0.50
     50/170  He+ + H2  -> He + H+ + H / He + H2+
        178  He+ + C   -> C+ + He     6.30e-15 T^0.75 (10-300 K)
      78-92  He+ + CH, CH2, CH3, CH4, OH, H2O, CO, O2   ~1e-9 to 2e-10

**MOCASSIN's ionBalance has exactly one non-recombination sink**: `chex`,
applied as `chex(elem,ion,1)*Hden*x(H0)`, which IS He+ + H -> He + H+ - the
reference's dominant low-temperature route. The coefficient exists
(`chex(2,2,:)` at `:2520`). It is switched off below 6000 K, the gate D-234
flagged as element-dependent by construction. The molecular channels have no
MOCASSIN counterpart at all.

That also explains the depth structure without needing the electron pool to
carry it: the molecular sinks switch on with depth, so the reference's
destruction strengthens inward exactly where our excess grows.

### What is NOT the cause

**Our alpha is fine.** Recovered from the probe as `Ne*alpha`/`Ne`, it reads
1.8-3.0e-11 cm^3/s over 14-26 K and rises as temperature falls, the right
magnitude and sign for He+ radiative recombination. `radRecFit` is Verner &
Ferland (1996) for He-like ions, and the dielectronic term - the one with the
documented negative-fit pathology (D-116) - is added only for `elem >= 3`, so
it never touches helium.

**The electron pool modulates but does not set it.** Biasing restores x(C+) and
with it the electron pool: at A_V ~2.2, x(e) is 2.20e-4 biased against 6.45e-5
analog, and the He+ excess falls from 24x to 2.4x in that bucket. So a large
part of the *depth-dependent* excess is the D-237 estimator floor acting
through the electron donor. But a roughly flat 2-3x remains where carbon is
perfect, and that part is the missing sink.

### The decision this needs

The 6000 K `chex` gate is **not PDR-specific**. Removing it changes the
ionization balance of every MOCASSIN model, not only coupled ones, so it is a
design decision rather than a fix to be applied quietly - exactly the class
CLAUDE.md says belongs in the design. Three things to establish first:

  - whether 6000 K is a stated validity bound on the Kingdon & Ferland fits
    `chex` uses, or an arbitrary guard;
  - the magnitude of He+ + H at 20 K from the reference's own coefficient
    against our `Ne*alpha` in the same cells, i.e. whether that one reaction
    closes the flat 2-3x or only part of it;
  - whether the chemistry's own x(He+), which solves all ~20 sinks, already
    disagrees with MOCASSIN's `ionDen` in the same cells - that would confirm
    the mechanism end to end from data on disk.

**Unresolved and deliberately left so.** Nothing here bears on the CO/OH
deficit, which remains 1-2 decades under the reference with carbon at 1.00.

### Process

Three extraction errors in this entry's own analysis, all mine, all caught by
the data looking wrong rather than by care: `elemLabel` pads single-letter
symbols with an asterisk (`*H`, `*C`) so `$3=="H"` matched nothing; the D-234
header's fields are `AV=$8, Te=$10, Ne=$12, nH=$14` and I read `$10`/`$12`,
reporting "Ne 20.27, nH 0.0"; and earlier an awk table was corrupted by a
comma-decimal locale. The habit that would have prevented all three is to print
one raw line and number its fields before writing the extractor.

## D-247 - full-repository audit: what builds, what works, and the five blockers (2026-09-12)

Requested as a standing audit rather than prompted by a defect. Nothing was
changed; everything below is measured from the tree at 559215e and from run
output already on disk, except the builds, which were run fresh.

### The build matrix, verified

All four flavours compile from a clean object tree, in this order, with
`make clean` between each:

    make PDR=1 PDRGEOM=3D mocassin      OK
    make PDR=1 mocassin                 OK
    make mocassin                       OK
    make PDR=1 mocassinWarm             OK

The default flavour was rebuilt afterwards, so `.pdrflag` reads `1-3D` and the
`mocassin` binary in the root is the ray-traced build. Working tree clean.

### What is working, stated so it is not re-derived

  - The ownership contract is in the code, not in keywords (D-198). The
    production fixture states no ownership keyword at all.
  - `x(H+)_ion / x(H+)_chem` has median 0.99998, p90 1.0015 over 15039 cells.
    The two descriptions of hydrogen's ionization agree - "one reality per
    quantity" holds for the quantity that has cost the most to get there.
  - The hydrogen budget closes: worst 1.0e-5 over 801 cells (V1), 9.9e-6 over
    401 (V2).
  - The V1/V2 slabs reproduce the reference: x(CO)/ref = 1.00, x(H2) 0.4993
    against 0.4993 and 0.5000 against 0.5000.
  - A 13-iteration 3D run of the H II + PDR fixture completes in 24:56 per
    processor with a clean exit.

### The five blockers, ranked

**1. CO and OH are 1-2 decades under the reference in 3D, and exact in 1D.**

    A_V       1.175  1.488  1.917  2.030  2.238  2.345
    CO/ref    0.004  0.090  0.236  0.250  0.029  0.020
    OH/ref    0.013  0.310  0.559  0.593  0.032  0.016
    C+/ref     1.00   1.01   1.03   1.02   0.98   1.00

against x(CO)/ref = 1.00 in both slabs at A_V 8.49. Carbon is right, so C+
starvation is excluded (D-239 correction). The network, the CO formation route
and the H2 chemistry all reproduce the reference in a slab; the deficit appears
only when the 3D coupling is in the path. It is worst at BOTH ends of the PDR
and best in the middle - a shape, not an offset. **The slab/3D contrast is the
sharpest lead in the project and has not been worked.** It is what I would do
first.

**2. The He+ excess is blocked on a design decision, not on measurement.**

D-246 closed the mechanism end to end. `chex` - He+ + H -> He + H+, the
reference's dominant low-temperature sink - is zeroed below 6000 K at
`update_mod.f90:2590`, which is every PDR cell; the reference's molecular sinks
have no MOCASSIN counterpart at all. D-246's three prerequisites are all
undone. The gate is not PDR-specific, so this belongs in the design.

**3. The 87.5% plateau is entirely the Te test, and the log already said so.**

Converged fraction over iterations 9-13: 73.0, 85.4, 87.1, 87.8, 87.5, against
a 95% target. The final iteration's CVPROBE line reads

    which test failed: x(H0) only 2   x(H2) only 0   both 0   Te (any) 1895

and 1895/15204 = 12.5%, exactly the missing fraction. D-228 listed "which of
the three tests those cells fail" as unmeasured; `d244-species` ran with
`teProbe 1`, printed the answer, and it was not read. This is the entry's own
process finding: **an instrument was added, fired, and its output went
unexamined for a day.** Supporting numbers from the same block: the Te solve's
bracket is wider than `thLimit/3` in 12435 cells (81.8%), and TEPROBE itself
reports 99.89% of Te calls converging - so the root finder is not failing, the
inter-iteration test is.

**4. 47% of cells report "Ion balance not reached" at the FINAL iteration.**

Across the run: 1, 51, 50, 49, ..., 47%. The Te-balance counter falls to 0% by
iteration 13; this one does not move. It is incremented at
`update_mod.f90:985` and normalised over `totCells` at `iteration_mod.f90:2844`,
so it is neither PDR-specific nor confined to the zone. It has never been
diagnosed - no probe says which elements, which stages, or where. Every
ionization result in this log, D-246 included, sits on top of it.

**5. Memory is 1.74x the documented model and the cause is unknown.**

685 MB/rank at iteration 1 against the 393 MB that 234 MB + 10.47 kB/cell
predicts at 15204 cells - about 20 `(15205,600)` real4 arrays where the
per-cell term implies four or five. D-245 fixed a genuine leak on top of this
baseline; the baseline itself is untouched, and it has already killed a
production run at iteration 6. It gates the longer and denser runs that
blockers 1-4 need. Separating "regression in this tree" from "the model always
understated this fixture" costs one build of an older commit and one
measurement.

### Below the line

  - **Ownership-switch debt.** 43 `pdr*` keywords. Seven are retired and
    ignored with a log line but still parsed; roughly nine remain live
    ownership switches - `pdrOwnDust`, `pdrDustFeedback`, `pdrUseNePDR`,
    `pdrPEfromPDR`, `pdrCoolZoneGate`, `pdrDustModel`, `pdrFUVmode`,
    `pdrSplitField`, `pdrCoupleIter` - plus `pdrZoneLim = 0.3`, still a runtime
    threshold deciding ownership (latched, D-031). CLAUDE.md names this class
    as the project's largest defect source. The production fixture sets none of
    them, so this is latent complexity rather than active divergence.
  - **The temperature disagrees with the reference in opposite directions**:
    0.59x in hiipdr (colder), 2.3x and 6.0x in V1/V2 (hotter). Same code. That
    is not one missing heating or cooling term.
  - **Repo hygiene.** 70 `mocassin.dNNN` binaries are tracked in git, 78 MB in
    the working tree; `.gitignore` covers `mocassin` but not the dated copies.

### One thing not to chase

`pdrOmega = 0.42d0` at `pdr_mod.f90:207` reads as a CLAUDE.md rule-1 violation
and is **dead**: `omega` is assigned (`input_parameters.F90:65`) and printed
(`writeparams.F90:55`) and never enters a rate expression anywhere in
`source/pdr/`. `pdrAVfac`, which looks like the same kind of constant, is the
opposite case - it is calibrated from MOCASSIN's own dust at `pdr_mod.f90:986`,
`magPerTau*kV/Hden`, and is self-consistent by construction.

Also cosmetic and already noted at D-246: the D-234 probe prints `nu_th 0.0000`
for every helium line because it reads `nuArray(elementP(elem,ion,outShell,1))`
and `elementP`/`outShell` are populated only for `elem > 2`. Display only - it
never touches `nPhotoSte` - but it misled one analysis already.

## D-248 - the 87.5% plateau is the Te test, and most of what it is testing is Monte Carlo noise (2026-09-12)

D-247 found that the plateau is entirely the temperature test - final-iteration
CVPROBE reads `x(H0) only 2, x(H2) only 0, both 0, Te (any) 1895`, and
1895/15204 = 12.5% is exactly the missing fraction. What it could not say is
whether those 1895 cells are *moving* or merely *noisy*. Nothing recorded the
distribution of the Te test statistic, only its verdict.

This entry answers that from data already on disk, then adds the instrument
that measures it directly.

### 1. The floor is stationary, not converging

`cvFailTe` per iteration, three runs of the same fixture:

    d244-species (13 it)  8379 14897 14982 14766 15079 15031 14960 10393 4082 2205 1959 1846 1895
    d236-depth   (13 it)  8584 14902 14983 14723 15077 15027 14960 10355 4220 2317 2020 1896 1836
    d243-heicorr (22 it)  8512 14898 14984 14681 15075 15032 14962 10338 4099 2253 2008 2017 1938
                          1873 1872 1954 1889 1916 1895 1880 1897 1877

**d243-heicorr is the decisive one: twelve consecutive iterations oscillating
in the band 1872-2017 with no downward trend.** A converging sequence does not
look like that. The Te failure count is a floor the model sits on, not a
residual it is working off.

### 2. What a repeat run says the test statistic does under NO physics change

If the physics is converged and only the realisation differs, the test
statistic |dTe/Te| still has a distribution. Two runs of an identical
configuration measure it.

**Choosing the pair took two attempts, and the first was wrong.** I first used
`d236-depth` / `d237-taus`: same input file, both 13 iterations, and
`git diff --stat 6119748 8442c73 -- source/` empty, which I read as "same
code". It is not - `cmp` puts **392,183 bytes** between the two binaries, a
third of the file. Those runs were made from working trees carrying
uncommitted probe changes, and a diff between the two *result* commits cannot
see that. The 18.72% figure that pair gave is withdrawn.

The verified pair is `d239-roulette` / `d242-repeat`: byte-identical input
files AND byte-identical binaries (`cmp` clean), which is what D-242 describes
as re-running the D-239 configuration unchanged.

Measured over the 15204 active cells, comparing final `grid%Te` cell by cell:

    median |dTe/Te|   0.0272
    p90               0.1162
    p99               0.2564
    max               1.3174
    exceeding 0.10    2009 cells = 13.21%

Against an observed failure floor of 1727 (11.36%) in d239 and 1822 (11.98%)
in d242. **The rate at which pure realisation noise breaches the tolerance is
of the same size as - in fact slightly larger than - the rate at which cells
actually fail it.**

By zone, the separation is total: the 165 ionized cells have median scatter
0.0055 and **not one** exceeds 0.10; every one of the 2009 breaches is in the
PDR.

### 3. The failing cells are the noisy cells

Cross-tabulating each run's own per-cell `lgConverged` (it is written to
`grid0.out`, so this needed no new run) against the pair's noise map:

                        d239      d242
    P(noisy | fail)     39.5%     36.4%
    P(noisy | pass)      9.8%     10.1%
    median scatter, failing cells   0.0805    0.0754
    median scatter, passing cells   0.0233    0.0231

A failing cell carries **3.5x** the realisation noise of a passing one, and is
**4x** more likely to be over tolerance on noise alone. The typical failing
cell's noise, 0.08, is 80% of the entire 0.10 budget - so for those cells
almost nothing is left over for physical drift.

By depth, the failure profile and the noise profile track each other:

    A_V band     cells   fail%   noisy%   median scatter
    0.0-0.5        168     1.2%    0.0%       0.0054
    0.5-1.0        684     4.4%    4.1%       0.0033
    1.0-1.5       1496     0.1%    0.2%       0.0069
    1.5-2.0       2628     4.7%    3.5%       0.0232
    2.0-2.5       4203    18.9%   21.5%       0.0527
    2.5-3.0       5724    13.5%   17.0%       0.0331
    3.0+           301     1.3%    2.0%       0.0052

### 4. The noise is not inherited from the field - it is filtered by depth

The obvious story, "the deep field is under-sampled so the deep temperature is
noisy", is wrong. Over the verified pair, the FUV field's own scatter **rises
monotonically** with depth while the temperature's **peaks and falls back**:

    A_V band      n     med chi   med heat   med Te   gain = Te/heat
    0.0-0.5      168     0.0073     0.0095   0.0054       0.57
    0.5-1.0      684     0.0333     0.0143   0.0033       0.23
    1.0-1.5     1496     0.0904     0.0468   0.0069       0.15
    1.5-2.0     2628     0.1969     0.1398   0.0232       0.17
    2.0-2.5     4203     0.3373     0.2845   0.0527       0.19
    2.5-3.0     5724     0.4907     0.4027   0.0331       0.08
    3.0+         301     0.5514     0.3961   0.0052       0.01

Whole-grid medians: chiFUV 0.2911, pdrHeat 0.2289, Te 0.0272. **The field is an
order of magnitude noisier than the temperature it drives**, and the log-log
correlation between them is only 0.197 (heating to Te, 0.265).

The gain, d(lnTe)/d(ln heat), **collapses with depth** - 0.57 at the face,
0.01 in the deepest gas, which absorbs a 40% swing in its heating and moves
0.5% in temperature. So the failure band at A_V 2.0-2.5 is not where the field
is worst; the field is worst at A_V 3+, where almost nothing fails. It is where
the heating noise has grown large while the thermal response has not yet
collapsed. The two curves cross there.

### 5. The temperature floor: real, confirmed, and too small to matter here

I claimed, then withdrew, then restored a finding about `teFloor`, and then had
to cut its size by a factor of five. Recorded in full because the reasoning
errors are the reusable part.

**Claim.** Cells sitting at the 10 K floor have a quantity that cannot move, so
they pass the Te test for free - D-176..D-181 and D-191 again.

**Retraction.** Tested against the true clamp (`Te <= teFloor*1.00001`) on the
stored `grid%Te`, **zero** cells matched; the minimum is 10.0005 (biased) and
10.0080 (analog). Nothing appeared to be clamped.

**Restoration.** The clamp counter disagrees: `teNloclamp` is nonzero in every
run. The stored value is not the tested value - `iterDamp = 0.25` blends the
clamped 10.0 with the previous iteration's temperature *after* the test, which
lifts it just above the floor. **Testing the stored array measured the wrong
quantity.** That is the reusable lesson: where a value is damped after the
test, the array on disk is not what the criterion saw.

**Correction of scale - and it is configuration-dependent.** I first quoted
d239, which carries `pathStretch 0.5`. The plateau being diagnosed is the
*analog* configuration, and it clamps roughly ten times fewer cells:

    final-iteration teNloclamp
      analog   d244  72     d236  60     d243 142
      biased   d239 729     d242 781

    cells within 0.1 K of the floor, and their convergence
      d244 (analog)   202 cells = 1.33% of grid,  0% unconverged
      d239 (biased)  1061 cells = 6.98% of grid,  0% unconverged

**So the mechanism is confirmed and the magnitude is small.** Every near-floor
band in both runs is 0% unconverged - a cell held at the floor does pass for
free, exactly as predicted, and D-165 said so already: *"a cell parked on the
floor is not a solved cell, and 1864 of them were being counted as one."* But
in the configuration that shows the 87.5% plateau it accounts for 1.3% of the
grid, not 12.5%. **It is a real defect in what the convergence number means; it
is not the explanation of the plateau.** Why biasing clamps ten times more
cells at the floor is unexplained and not chased here.

### 6. Why the disk measurement cannot finish the argument

Two biases run in opposite directions and neither is small.

  - `grid1.out` holds the **damped** Te, so the between-run scatter is measured
    on a smoothed quantity. The test compares a **raw** new solution against a
    damped reference. That makes 13.21% an *under*estimate of the true null.
  - The two runs differ by their whole accumulated history, not by one
    realisation. That makes 13.21% an *over*estimate.

The statistic the test actually computes was never recorded. So the instrument.

### 7. The instrument

Diagnostic only, under `teProbe`, mirroring the existing x(H0) probe so the two
are read the same way:

  - `cvTeHist(12)` - |dTe/Te| binned as `cvHist` bins |dx/x|
  - `cvFailTeByAV(7)` - Te failures by A_V band
  - `cvTeNear` - failures within 2x tolerance
  - `cvTeFloorN` / `cvTeFloorPass` - cells at `teFloor`, and how many of them
    pass for free

**Bin semantics, mapped empirically rather than assumed.** `iBin = 9 +
int(log10 x)` with Fortran `int()` truncating toward zero, so the bins are NOT
what the label suggests below 1: bin 8 collects (0.01, **0.10**] and bin 9
collects (0.10, 9.99]. The tolerance sits exactly on the bin 8/9 boundary and
failures are bins 9-12. Confirmed against a trusted count at iteration 1 of
`d248-tehist`: bins 9-12 sum to 8397 and `cvFailTe` is 8397. My first parser
summed from bin 10 and would have under-reported the failing fraction by a
whole decade; it was caught by doing this calibration rather than trusting the
label - the D-246 habit, applied before reading any result.

### 8. Result: the tolerance cuts through the body of the distribution

`runs/d248-tehist`, the `d244-species` configuration byte-for-byte plus the
instrument. 24:39 per processor against d244's 24:56, clean exit, 13
iterations.

**The instrument is validated two independent ways.** Histogram bins 9-12 equal
`cvFailTe` in **all thirteen iterations**, which fixes the bin mapping against
a count already trusted. And `cvFailTeByAV` at the final iteration reads
`[0, 0, 35, 219, 1751, 0]` against `[0, 2, 29, 206, 1660, 0]` predicted
beforehand from d244's on-disk `lgConverged` and `AVeff` - same shape, same
concentration, differing by realisation.

**It is inert**, as a diagnostic must be: `cvFailTe` runs 8397/14899/14985...
against d244's 8379/14897/14982, differences of 18, 2 and 3 cells.

**The distribution of |dTe/Te| at the final iteration:**

    |dTe/Te|             cells    share
    <= 1e-8 (exactly 0)   2515    16.5%
    1e-8 .. 1e-3             0     0.0%
    1e-3 .. 1e-2          3385    22.3%
    1e-2 .. 0.10          7299    48.0%
    > 0.10  (FAILS)       2005    13.19%

    of the 2005 failures, within 2x tolerance:  1168  (58%)

**The two numbers that matter.** The failure rate is **13.19%**. The null rate -
the fraction of cells that breach 0.10 on realisation noise alone, from the
verified repeat pair - is **13.21%**. They agree to two hundredths of a point.

And **48% of the grid sits in the single decade immediately below the
tolerance**. The criterion is not separating a converged population from an
unconverged one; it is slicing the middle of a distribution whose width is set
by Monte Carlo noise. 58% of the failures are within a factor of two of
passing.

**The agreement of 13.19% with 13.21% is closer than the measurement deserves**
and should not be read as a precise identity: section 6's two biases are still
in the null, in opposite directions and neither quantified. What is established
is that the two rates are the same size, which is enough for the conclusion.

### 9. A second population that passes for free, larger than the floor

**2515 cells - 16.5% of the grid - report a temperature change of exactly
zero**, and the population **grows monotonically**: 146, 330, 744, 1153, 2278,
2515 over iterations 8-13. Bins 2-6 are empty, so these are exact zeros, not
small numbers.

It is not structural (zone 0 is 165 cells, near-floor 221, hot 195) and not the
x(H0) probe's behaviour (its bin 1 holds 463 and its distribution is smooth).
It is not the D-215 cooling table snapping cells to nodes: the frozen cells
carry 2395 *distinct* temperatures out of 2398. It is not the PDR pinning Te -
that path, `update_mod.f90:639`, is `if (.false.)` under D-193.

**It is the temperature solver's no-bracket fallback.** The frozen count tracks
`teNnobrack` in lockstep through the converged phase, at a near-constant offset
of ~130 cells:

    iter      10     11     12     13
    frozen   744   1153   2278   2515
    nobrack  872   1281   2404   2667

and the mechanism is explicit at `update_mod.f90:737-744`: with no bracket,
`lgTOk = nIterateT > 1` and then **`TeUsed = TeBest`**, exiting on the second
pass without ever reaching the secant update. Where the entry temperature was
the best point seen, `TeUsed` is returned bit-identical to `TeIterStart`. The
comment states the intent: *"if the sign never flips within 20% of T on either
side, the residual is flat and small there and the best point seen is the
answer."*

So these cells' temperatures are **a fallback, not a root** - and the
convergence test, comparing the returned value against the entry value, sees
zero and passes them. **D-176..D-181 and D-191 again, at 16.5% of the grid and
growing.** They sit where the thermal gain collapsed: 63.3% of the 10-10.1 K
band is frozen, 39.9% of 10.1-11 K, against 2-4% at 12-20 K.

**Not fully closed.** That `TeBest` equals `TeEntry` for these cells is
inferred from the code path plus the lockstep correlation, not measured
per cell. `teProbe > 1` prints `Tin` and `Tout` per cell and would settle it
in one run; it was not worth 25 minutes today.

### 10. What this does and does not license

**Established.** The 87.5% plateau is the Te test (D-247); the Te test statistic
is noise-dominated at the tolerance it is applied at; the failure rate equals
the realisation-noise rate to the precision available; and two separate
populations pass the test with a quantity that cannot move - 74 at `teFloor`,
64 of them passing for free, and 2515 in the no-bracket fallback.

**Therefore the converged percentage is not, at present, a statement about the
physics of the PDR.** Roughly an eighth of the grid fails on noise and roughly
a sixth passes without moving.

**What must NOT be done: raise `convLimit` until the number looks better.**
That is fitting a coefficient to close a gap, which CLAUDE.md forbids, and the
D-247 audit exists partly because convergence percentages have been argued
about rather than measured.

The options, none of them taken here because the criterion is a design
decision:

  - **Report the floor rather than chase it.** State the noise rate beside the
    converged fraction, so a run that reaches it is known to be done.
  - **Make the test noise-aware.** The per-cell MC noise is estimable; a
    criterion that compares the change against that cell's own noise is the
    honest version of what a fixed 10% is trying to approximate.
  - **Fix the free passes independently of the tolerance.** A cell returned by
    the no-bracket fallback should not be counted as converged - it should be
    reported, as D-165 argued for the floor clamp. This is the change with the
    clearest justification and it does not touch the criterion.
  - **Reduce the variance.** Biasing lowers the Te scatter, and the biased runs
    do converge slightly higher (88.0-88.6% against 87.5-87.9%) - but they also
    clamp ten times more cells at the floor, so that comparison is confounded
    and is not evidence for biasing.

**Unchanged by any of this:** the CO/OH deficit (D-247 blocker 1) and the He+
sink (blocker 2). Nothing here bears on either.

## D-249 - the CO deficit is a chain, and its head is a 7x FUV normalisation error in 3D (2026-09-12)

D-247 ranked the CO/OH deficit as blocker 1 on the strength of one contrast:
CO is 0.004-0.250 of the reference in 3D and 1.00 in the V1/V2 slabs, with
carbon correct. Only seven species had ever been compared, so the deficit's
extent was unknown.

### 1. Method: all 33 species, every PDR cell, matched A_V

`tools/` compares seven species on an extracted on-axis profile, and
`d196_axis.py` hardcodes 31^3, so it cannot read the 801-cell slabs at all.
Instead every PDR-zone cell is compared at **its own A_V** - the one depth
coordinate both codes compute for themselves - against the reference
log-interpolated onto it. That needs no axis indexing, works unchanged for the
3D model and both slabs, and uses 8542 cells instead of 29.

Cells outside the reference's own A_V range are excluded, not clamped (D-239).
Verified first: the references really do reach A_V 2.4534 (sec54) and 8.4912
(v1/v2), monotonically, so the slab result quoted at A_V 8.49 is the
reference's last point and is legitimate - a concern I raised and disposed of
before building on it.

### 2. The deficit is a chain, and CO/OH are its symptoms

Sorted by severity, the 3D model separates cleanly into species that are right
and species that descend from one place:

    correct      He 1.000   O 1.000   C+ 1.001   e- 1.043   H2 0.960
    collapsed    H2+ ~5e-5  H3+ 0.009  HCO+ 0.001  CH3+ 0.001  H3O+ 0.002
                 CH4 0.000  H2O 0.013  CO 0.050  OH 0.110

**Everything deficient is downstream of H3+, and H3+ is downstream of H2+.**
The elemental reservoirs - carbon and oxygen - are exactly right, which is why
D-239's finding that carbon is correct never helped: carbon was never the
constraint. A collapsed H3+ starves OH, H2O, HCO+ and CO simultaneously,
through H3+ + O -> OH+ and H3+ + CO -> HCO+, and that is the observed pattern.

**It is geometry-specific, as blocker 1 requires.** H2+/H3+ read 0.142/0.482 in
V1 and 102.8/2.835 in V2 - not collapsed, and in V2 overabundant. The network
is not at fault.

**Cosmic-ray attenuation is excluded.** `CRattenuation.F90` is entirely inside
`#ifdef CRATTENUATION`, which is absent from `PDRFLAGS` (Makefile:87-89), so
`zetalocal = zeta` uniformly and the suspicious `pdr(p)%AV(6)` indexing is dead
code - consistent with the coupling never populating `pdr%AV` at all.

### 3. Where the chain breaks: the H/H2 transition is ~1 mag too deep

Absolute values, not ratios:

    A_V        x(H2) ours    ref     x(H) ours   ref    H3+ ours    ref     T ours  ref
    0.5-1.0     2.919e-06  1.713e-01   1.000   0.657   2.1e-21   9.6e-10     24    104
    1.0-1.5     1.758e-01  4.359e-01   0.648   0.128   1.7e-11   5.1e-9      26     82
    1.5-2.0     4.753e-01  4.854e-01   0.049   0.029   2.0e-10   5.3e-9      23     48
    2.0-2.45    4.742e-01  4.930e-01   0.052   0.014   1.2e-11   5.4e-9      17     29

At A_V 0.5-1.0 the reference is 34% molecular and **our gas is entirely
atomic**, x(H2) = 3e-6, a ~60,000x deficit. No H2 means no H2+ means no H3+,
and the chain below it is empty. The slabs show no such displacement: V1 is
0.343 against 0.443 at A_V 0-0.5 and matches by 0.5.

### 4. The cause: the 3D FUV field is ~7x too strong, and the slope is FINE

    chi ours / chi ref, 3D, by A_V band
      0.0-0.5   9.05      1.0-1.5   3.94      2.0-2.45   5.00
      0.5-1.0   5.25      1.5-2.0   4.10

    slabs, same measure:  1.05 at A_V<0.5, rising to 14.3 by A_V 2-4

Densities match exactly (100, 1e3, 1e5 cm^-3), so this is not a setup mismatch.

**The distinction that matters is between normalisation and slope**, and a
fitted `k = -d ln(chi)/d A_V` separates them:

    model        range        k ours    k ref    ratio     chi at shallowest PDR cell
    3D sec5.4    0.3-2.45      2.951    3.020    0.977     7.33x too HIGH
    V1 slab      0.0-4.00      1.999    3.020    0.662     0.36x (too low)
    V2 slab      0.0-4.00      1.989    3.020    0.659     0.39x (too low)

**In 3D the attenuation slope is correct to 2.3% and the normalisation is ~7x
too high.** The slope is the dust-owned quantity, so this is NOT the "MOCASSIN
owns the dust, report the divergence" case that CLAUDE.md protects - the dust
is behaving. It is a normalisation error, which is a defect with an address.

I had read the band medians as "our field decays too slowly" and wrote that
down; the fit reversed it. The too-shallow slope is the **slabs'** problem
(0.66), not the 3D model's, and the slab medians had misled me because the
bands are unequally populated. Recorded because the wrong reading survived two
paragraphs before the fit killed it.

**This also explains why the slabs "work".** Their field is too *weak* by 2.7x,
so H2 forms early, the transition lands at or before the reference's, and the
chemistry below it is never starved. The slabs are not a control that passed -
they are a different error whose sign happens to be benign.

### 5. What is NOT explained

**The deep H3+ deficit survives.** By A_V 1.5-2.45 our H2 matches the reference
(0.475 vs 0.485, 0.474 vs 0.493) and H3+ is **still 25-450x low**. x(e-) is at
ratio ~1.0 and the temperature is 1.6x off - neither is remotely enough for
25x, let alone 450x. So the FUV normalisation explains the catastrophic band at
A_V 0.5-1.5 and does **not** explain the deep residual. Whether one cause
produces both is open.

**Our gas is colder everywhere** - 24 K against 104 K at A_V 0.5-1.0 - which is
D-227's standing item and interacts with this one: H2 formation on grains
depends on temperature, so the transition displacement and the temperature
deficit are not independent.

**Magnesium is absent by INPUT, not by defect.** Mg and Mg+ are identically
zero in all three of our runs against a reference x(Mg+) = 2.7e-6. The fixture's
`abunV1.in` sets Mg = 0, while the standalone reference carries Mg+ from
`species_reduced.d`. The coupling maps it correctly (`pdr_mod.f90:339-340`,
`linkIon` 9/10 -> Mg I/II) and D-208 already warns that removing Mg+ silently
changes the electron budget. **So the two codes are being compared with
different metal content, and the reference has a deep electron donor we do
not.** That is a property of the comparison, and every deep x(e-) ratio in this
log inherits it.

### 6. Next

The 7x normalisation is the thing to chase, and it is bounded: the slope is
right, so the error is in the field's amplitude at the PDR boundary rather than
in its transport through the dust. D-047's finding that "launch overhang is
reflected back in, so `meanField` IS the incident flux" is marked *Revised* and
is the natural place to start, as is the relation between `chiFUV` and
`chiFUV0` under `planeIonization` versus a point source.

Not attempted here, deliberately: nothing was changed. This entry is a
measurement.

## D-250 - the input audit that D-074 should have been: composition was never in scope, and Mg is deleted by a guard that reports it kept (2026-09-12)

Asked for directly: audit the model inputs against the reference inputs and make
them consistent, because the Mg discrepancy surfaced in D-249 as a side
observation and should have been caught long before.

It should have been. This entry records why it was not, what is actually
consistent, and the one defect the audit found.

### 1. Why D-074 missed it

D-074 (2026-09-01) is titled "the full parameter audit" and its table has
eleven rows: G0, zeta, turbulent velocity, grain radius, A_V conversion,
T_min/T_max, HEALPix level, Fcrit, UV factor, dust-to-gas, chemistry
iterations. **Every one of those is a line in 3D-PDR's `params.dat`** - and
`params.dat` contains no elemental abundances at all. The composition lives in
`species_reduced.d` (and the `.species` list), which the audit never opened.

So the audit was not incomplete by accident; it was **scoped to one file** and
reported as covering "every input parameter". That is the process lesson: an
audit's scope is the set of files it opens, and it must be stated as such.

### 2. What IS consistent - verified, not assumed

Every `params.dat` quantity re-checked against the current fixtures:

    quantity            reference            ours                    verdict
    zeta (v1/v2)        5.000E-17            pdrZeta 5.0e-17         ok
    turbulent velocity  1 km/s               pdrVturb 1.0            ok
    grain radius        1.0e-5 cm            pdrGrainRad 1.0e-5      ok
    UV factor           3.02                 pdrUVfac 3.02           ok
    T_min / T_max       1 / 2e4              1.0 / 2.0e4             ok
    HEALPix level       0                    pdrHealpix 0            ok
    Fcrit               0.005                pdrFcrit 0.005          ok (D-074)
    end time            1e7 yr               pdrEndTime 1.0e7        ok
    ODE rel/abs tol     1e-8 / 1e-30         1.0d-8 / 1.0d-30        ok
    coolants            4, fixed order       same 4, same order      ok
    network             REDUCED              reduced                 ok
    metallicity         1                    pdrMetal 1.0            ok

**The A_V conversion was measured from the reference files themselves** rather
than read from `params.dat`, by integrating their own n_H over their own depth
column:

    reference        A_V/N_H measured     our calibrated pdrAVfac
    sec54.pdr.fin    5.34153e-22          5.34152688e-22    (6 significant figures)
    v1.pdr.fin       5.33997e-22          5.33995522e-22
    v2.pdr.fin       5.33997e-22          5.33995472e-22

So "matched A_V" genuinely means matched hydrogen column, and D-249's
comparison basis is sound. Note the `6.289e-22` in `3D/params.dat` belongs to
the *diffuse* 3D benchmark, not to sec54 - sec54 is a 1D run and used the 1D
value, which its own output confirms.

**Composition, the part never checked before**, derived by summing each
reference's surface row over all carriers of each element:

    reference     C          O          Mg         He      n_H     chi
    sec54      2.20e-04   3.30e-04   2.70e-06   1.0e-01   100    61.24
    v1         1.40e-04   3.00e-04   2.70e-06   1.0e-01   1e3    10
    v2         1.40e-04   3.00e-04   2.70e-06   1.0e-01   1e5    1000

    our hiipdr 2.2e-04    3.3e-04    0          1.0e-01   100
    our v1/v2  1.4e-04    3.0e-04    0          1.0e-01   1e3/1e5

**C, O and He match in all three fixtures. Mg does not, in any of them.**

### 3. The defect: the element is deleted by the guard meant to preserve it

`seedAbunFromMocassin` (`pdr_mod.f90`) opens with `abun = 0.d0` and then, per
linked species,

    if (.not.lgElementOn(iEl)) cycle

`cycle` skips the *assignment*, so the slot keeps the pre-zeroed value. Since
`seedPDR` then does `grid%pdrAbun(iCell,:) = seed`, **Mg+ is set to zero in
every cell of every run.** The comment immediately above the routine states the
opposite intent, in these words:

    A zero MOCASSIN abundance means the element is switched off there, and
    the network's value is left alone rather than deleting the element -
    removing e.g. Mg+ would silently change the electron budget.

And `reportAbun` prints, every run:

    !   Mg network 2.7000000000000000E-006  MOCASSIN: element off - network value kept

**The message is false.** Measured over the output of both runs: Mg and Mg+ are
identically zero in all 15039 PDR cells of `d248-tehist` and all 20018 of
`d233-v1slab` - max = min = 0, zero non-zero cells. The thing the comment warns
against is exactly what the code does, and the log asserts it did not.

Mg is the only affected element. Of the ten `linkIon` calls, only H, He, C, O
and Mg are carried by the REDUCED network, and only Mg is switched off in the
fixtures. (N, Ne and S are zero in the slab fixtures but have no network
species, so nothing is deleted.)

### 4. What it costs, measured against the reference's own electron budget

    reference   A_V    x(e-)      Mg+ share of x(e-)    C+ share
    sec54      0.616  2.56e-04          1.1%             85.9%
    sec54      2.333  1.90e-04          1.4%             94.5%
    v1         2.133  2.31e-05         11.4%             84.1%
    v1         7.864  2.03e-06         89.8%              7.6%
    v2         4.962  1.80e-06         98.8%              0.9%
    v2         7.864  4.38e-07         99.3%              0.5%

**In the slabs' deep gas the electron budget IS Mg+** - up to 99.3% of it -
because C+ has recombined and Mg+ has not. We delete that donor entirely. In
sec54 it is 1.1-1.4%, because C+ stays high across the compared range.

So the severity is geometry-dependent, and it is worst in exactly the two
fixtures this project has been treating as the controls that pass.

### 5. What this does and does not overturn

**It does not rescue D-249's 3D result.** sec54's deep electron budget is
C+-dominated and Mg+ is ~1%, so the missing donor cannot explain the 25-450x
deep H3+ deficit there. The FUV normalisation finding stands.

**It does contaminate every deep slab comparison in this log**, including the
"the slabs reproduce the reference" claim that D-247 ranked blocker 1 on. Our
V1 x(e-) measured 1.79x the reference *while missing the donor that supplies
90% of the reference's deep electrons*, which means something else is
over-supplying electrons there by a larger factor than previously thought.
That is a new discrepancy, not a resolved one.

### 6. Two further inconsistencies found, not yet acted on

**`nbins` 600 in hiipdr against D-013's own requirement of >= 1000.** The slab
fixtures use 1000; the 3D fixture, which is the one every recent entry runs,
uses 600. Either D-013 is wrong or the fixture is.

**Our own FUV attenuation slope is not single-valued across geometries.** From
D-249: k = -dln(chi)/dA_V is 2.951/mag in the 3D model and 1.99/mag in both
slabs, from identical `dust_species.dat`, identical `MdMg`, and calibrated
`pdrAVfac` agreeing to 0.03%. Same dust, two answers. That is a one-reality
violation independent of any reference and is the sharper of the two.

### 7. Unverifiable from disk: sec54's cosmic-ray rate

There is no `params.dat` for sec54 - the repository has v1's and the 3D
diffuse one only, and commit f8d8911 committed `sec54.pdr.fin` without
recording the parameters it was generated with. Our fixture assumes
`pdrZeta 5.0e-17`.

An attempt to infer it from the reference's own deep x(H+) balance gave
1.22e-16 for sec54 - suspiciously close to the 1e-16 of the 3D params - but
**the estimator fails its own control**, returning 7.5e-19 and 1.9e-17 for
v1/v2 where zeta is known to be 5e-17. So it is not evidence, and the value is
recorded as unknown rather than guessed. Closing this needs the reference
regenerated under the D-016 policy, with its parameters committed alongside.

### 8. The decision this needs

Not taken here; nothing was changed.

  - **Turn Mg on in MOCASSIN** - set 2.7e-6 in the three `abunV1.in` files.
    MOCASSIN has `mgi.dat`/`mgii.dat`, so it can carry the element, and this is
    the "one reality per quantity" answer: composition is MOCASSIN's, the
    chemistry reads it. It changes every fixture's ionization and cooling, so
    every comparison in the log would need re-running.
  - **Make the guard do what it claims** - keep the network's value for a
    switched-off element. Cheaper, but it creates a second reality: an element
    the chemistry carries and MOCASSIN does not know about, which is the class
    CLAUDE.md rules against.

Either way `reportAbun`'s message is a defect on its own and must stop claiming
the network value was kept when it was not.

## D-251 - MOCASSIN owns the abundances, and the coupling now refuses to run when it does not (2026-09-12)

The rule, as stated: **if it is set in MOCASSIN's input it has to reflect in the
3D-PDR coupling.** One reality per quantity, and composition is MOCASSIN's.
D-250 found the coupling breaking that rule silently, so this entry enforces it.

### 1. The defect, restated

`seedAbunFromMocassin` builds each cell's seed from zero and `cycle`s past any
element with `lgElementOn` false, so the slot keeps the zero and `pdrAbun` is
overwritten with it. The element is **deleted**, not preserved. Meanwhile
`reportAbun` printed, on every run that had Mg off:

    MOCASSIN: element off - network value kept

which is false, and was false for every hiipdr and slab run in this log.

### 2. Is Mg actually required? Measured, not assumed

Asked directly: can the chemistry run with Mg = 0? **Yes, and that is the
problem.** Magnesium is a CLOSED sub-system in the REDUCED network - of its
eleven reactions, ten make Mg+ from Mg (H3+, CH5+, H+, C+, CH+, CH3+, H2O+,
O2+ charge transfer, plus photoionization and CR) and one makes Mg from Mg+
(radiative recombination). **Nothing produces either from a non-Mg species**, so
x(Mg) + x(Mg+) is exactly conserved at whatever it is seeded with. A zero seed
stays zero for the whole run: no crash, no warning, no failed conservation
check.

What is silently lost is eight charge-transfer sinks that neutralise molecular
ions **without consuming an electron**, and the dominant electron donor of
shielded gas - up to 99.3% of x(e-) in the deep V2 slab (D-250).

So Mg is not required for the solver to run, and *is* required for the model to
mean anything. That is precisely the case for a hard stop rather than a
warning.

### 3. The check

Added in `seedPDR`, which is the only place both tables exist: `initPDRnetwork`
builds the link table but runs **before** `setComposition`, so `lgElementOn`
is not yet populated there - the routine's own comment says so.

For every linked network species with a non-zero initial abundance whose
MOCASSIN element is switched off, the run prints the element, the species and
the abundance that would be discarded, and stops. Hydrogen is exempt
(`elemAbun` is 1 by definition).

**Tested both ways.**

  - Negative (Mg = 0): stops at `seedPDR`, never reaches the MC loop -
    `refusing to run - a network element is absent from MOCASSIN's composition`.
  - Positive (Mg = 2.7e-6): clean exit, and after the chemistry has actually
    run, `x(Mg) + x(Mg+)` has median **2.6971e-06** against the 2.7e-06 seeded,
    max 2.7000e-06. Conservation holds to 0.1%, as the closed sub-system says
    it must.

A process note on the negative test: its log is **binary** - the MPI abort
writes null bytes - so plain `grep` finds nothing in it and reports the check
as having not fired. `strings` shows it did. I read that wrongly once before
checking.

### 4. The fixtures

All nine PDR fixtures now carry `Mg = 2.7e-06`, which is what **both**
references were actually run with (measured from their own output: sec54
2.700e-06, v1 2.700e-06, v2 2.700e-06), not a value chosen here.

Worth recording so it is not mistaken for an error later: the strict Lexington
**HII40 abundance list contains no magnesium** - He, C, N, O, Ne, S only. The
reference carries it because 3D-PDR's `species_reduced.d` defaults Mg+ to
2.7e-6. So setting it is matching what the comparison target ran, and is a
deliberate, documented departure from HII40's list rather than a silent one.

### 5. Two consequences

**`grid2.out` gained an element block, 7 -> 8.** It carries one block per
element switched on, so turning Mg on changes the record structure of every
output file that indexes by element. `tools/d196_axis.py` hardcoded
`NELEM = 7` and would have silently read the wrong ion densities from every new
run; it now derives the count from the files. Any other consumer keyed to 7 has
the same defect.

**Mg III has no data file, and that is normal.** `data/fileNames.dat` lists
`data/mgiii.dat`, which is absent - but so are **143 of its 259 entries**
(`feiii`, `nei`, `nai`, and most of the heavy elements). MOCASSIN ships a
subset and raises no error. Mg III is solved by the ionization balance
regardless - median 9.6e-5, max 0.909 in the test - and only forbidden-line
emission for those stages is unavailable. Pre-existing and general, not
introduced by switching Mg on.

### 6. What this invalidates, and what it does not

**Every comparison in this log was run with magnesium deleted.** D-250
quantified the cost, and it is largest in the two slab fixtures that have been
treated as the controls that pass. Those runs have to be repeated before their
numbers are quoted again.

**It does not rescue D-249, and cannot.** Two independent reasons. sec54's deep
electron budget is C+-dominated, with Mg+ at 1.1-1.4%. And `H3+ + Mg -> Mg+ +
H2 + H` at 1.0e-9 is an H3+ **sink**: restoring magnesium removes H3+, so the
3D H3+ deficit can only deepen, not close. The FUV normalisation finding stands
and is if anything sharpened.

### 7. Not done here

The re-runs. Nothing in this entry re-measures anything - it fixes the input
reality and the guard that let it drift, and the fixtures now differ from every
run on disk.

## D-252 - the corrected composition re-run: D-249 survives, and restoring Mg inverts deep carbon (2026-09-12)

D-251 set Mg = 2.7e-06 in all nine fixtures, so every comparison on disk was
made with a different composition than the code now runs. This is the re-run,
and what it found.

### 1. What was re-run, and what was deliberately not

`runs/d252-hiipdr` is `d248-tehist`'s configuration byte-for-byte with the
corrected `abunV1.in` - `input.in` diffed identical, Mg the only change.
Complete: 13 iterations, 30:16 per processor, clean exit, 85.09% converged,
`reportAbun` confirming `MOCASSIN 2.70000010E-06`.

**The two slabs were started and then deliberately cancelled** (marked
`INCOMPLETE` on disk so they cannot be mistaken for results). The reason is
section 3: MOCASSIN's Mg ionization balance is ~120x too neutral-rich in
shielded gas, and the slabs are the fixtures where Mg+ carries 54% (V1) and
99% (V2) of the reference's deep electrons. Running the two most Mg-sensitive
models with Mg's ionization wrong spends six hours producing numbers the next
fix invalidates. They are re-run after that fix, not before.

### 2. D-249 survives the corrected composition

    species    before Mg    after Mg    reference ratio
    H3+          0.0090      0.0080     still ~125x under
    HCO+         0.0010      0.0010
    CH3+         0.0010      0.0010
    H3O+         0.0020      0.0020
    H2O          0.0130      0.0150
    CO           0.0500      0.0620     still ~16x under
    OH           0.1100      0.1000     still ~10x under
    C+           1.0010      1.0000
    Mg+          0 (absent)  0.9680     now carried correctly

**The chain is unmoved and the molecules are not rescued.** H3+ deepened
slightly, which is the direction predicted: `H3+ + Mg -> Mg+ + H2 + H` at
1.0e-9 is an H3+ SINK, so restoring magnesium removes H3+ rather than
supplying it. The FUV normalisation finding stands as blocker 1.

**A prediction of mine that was half wrong, recorded.** I predicted the 3D model
would "barely move" because Mg+ is only 1.3% of sec54's electron budget. The
whole-grid medians did barely move - x(e-) 1.043 -> 1.046, H2 0.960 -> 0.961,
C+ 1.001 -> 1.000 - but the deepest band moved a great deal, and generalising
from the medians to "the model barely changed" was wrong.

### 3. Restoring Mg INVERTS deep carbon, and MOCASSIN's Mg ionization is why

At matched depth, the same fixed A_V band (1.84-2.4534):

    run              n      x(C+)      x(C)     x(Mg+)     x(e-)    C/C+
    before Mg=0    4647   1.543e-04  6.568e-05  0         1.961e-04  0.43
    after Mg set   5083   4.143e-05  1.785e-04  2.513e-06 8.929e-05  4.31
    reference        12   1.987e-04  2.129e-05  2.693e-06 2.095e-04  0.11

**C/C+ went from 4x the reference to 39x, the wrong way, and deep x(e-)
halved** (ratio 0.95 -> 0.44; C+'s share of the electron budget 78.7% -> 46.4%,
He+'s 9.8% -> 23.9%).

The mechanism is reaction 185, `C+ + Mg -> Mg+ + C` at 1.1e-9, which consumes
**neutral** Mg - and ours is far too abundant:

    neutral Mg fraction, deep PDR cells
      MOCASSIN's ionDen(Mg) stage 1     20.2%
      the chemistry settles at           6.9%
      reference                          0.17%

x(Mg) is 17.9x the reference while x(Mg+) is 0.968 of it. So the element's
total is right and its **ionization state is not**: MOCASSIN leaves ~120x too
much magnesium neutral in shielded gas, the chemistry inherits that through the
seed, and C+ is destroyed at roughly that factor too.

**A hypothesis, not a measurement:** Mg I ionizes at 7.65 eV, well below the
Lyman limit, so this is about sub-13.6 eV photoionization deep in the PDR -
plausibly the same misnormalised FUV field D-249 measured at ~7x too strong.
If so these are one defect seen twice, not two. Untested.

### 4. The electron budget, and a tie to D-246

Measured on the pre-Mg runs, deepest quarter, donor shares ours vs reference:

    V1 slab    He+ 98.75% / 0.29%     C+ 0% / 34.5%    Mg+ 0% / 54.3%
    V2 slab    He+ 99.99% / 0.02%     C+ 0% / 0.71%    Mg+ 0% / 99.1%
    sec54 3D   He+  9.84% / 1.05%     C+ 78.7% / 94.8% Mg+ 0% / 1.31%

**Our shielded-gas electrons were almost entirely spurious He+.** That resolves
D-250's puzzle - "x(e-) is 1.79x the reference while the dominant donor is
deleted" - and ties it to D-246's missing He+ sink, measured independently. It
also means restoring Mg adds the real donor but cannot remove the spurious one.

### 5. Process: four runs lost to the harness memory guard

Four launches were killed with "system running low on memory" at footprints of
9.4, 9.9, 10.2 and **6.5 GB**, the last with system available flat at 46 GB,
swap 6 GB free and /tmp at 257 MB - no memory pressure of any kind. A threshold
theory (~9.4 GB) was proposed and then disproved by the 6.5 GB kill. VSZ
inflation is only 1.3x (8.90 GB against 6.73 GB resident), so that hypothesis
is weak too. **No diagnosis was reached.**

What did work is a **workaround, labelled as such**: run under `setsid` so the
job is its own session leader and not a child of a harness background task,
launched from a foreground call that returns immediately. Every kill hit a
background task; none hit a detached session. `runs/leakcheck.sh` and the
cancelled `runs/slabdriver.sh` are the pattern.

Two contributing errors of mine. The swap was exhausted by **9.3 GB of tmpfs**
- a stale session's scratchpad holding 39 old MOCASSIN run directories under
`/tmp`, which is tmpfs on this machine, so those outputs were sitting in RAM.
Deleting them took swap free from 0.87 GB to 7.04 GB. Before finding that I
suggested killing Chrome (17.6 GB, unnecessary) and then `sudo swapoff`. The
check that would have found it first is per-process `VmSwap` against
`Shmem` in `/proc/meminfo`: processes held only 1.20 GB of the 7 GB used, so no
process was the culprit and files were. **Scratch runs belong in `runs/`, which
is real storage, never `/tmp`.**
