### 3. The MOCASSIN model (`benchmarks/pdr/pn150k/input`)

    TStellar 150000, contShape blackbody, LStar 3.8282   (10^36.583 / 1e36)
    symmetricXYZ, nx = ny = nz = 41, Rin 1.0e16, Rout = edges = 1.8718e18
    Hdensity 1000, TeStart 15000, nbins 600, nuMax 30, nuMin 1.001e-5
    nebComposition abunGASS_pn150k.in   GASS10 (Cloudy solar_GASS10.abn),
                                         Si Mg Al x0.01, Ca and Fe 0
    dustFile: 'dustData/grph2-dl.nk' 0.6667 and 'dustData/grph1-dl.nk' 0.3333,
              0.005-0.25 um; dust_sizes.dat 35 log-spaced sizes, dn/da = a^-3.5
    MdMg constant 2.4827e-3
    pdr 1, reduced network, pdrZeta 4.293e-16, pdrCoolants 4, pdrStartIter 4
    maxIterateMC 11 90., nPhotons 6e6, convLimit 0.10

Choices, and why:
  - **Graphite orientations.** grph2-dl has n = 2.74, k = 1.56 at 0.55 um, the
    metallic E perp c constants, so it takes the 2/3 weight; grph1-dl (2.34,
    0.26) is E par c.
  - **Size weights.** MOCASSIN multiplies the size-file weight by da
    (ph_mod:978-993), so the file holds dn/da.
  - **Size law.** Cloudy's ISM law is data/ism.szd: power law 0.005-0.25 um,
    slope -3.5.
  - **Dust amount.** A short run (11^3, 1 iteration, pdrStartIter 1, 2e5
    packets, 26 s) at MdMg 2.45e-3 gave calibratePDRdust A_V/N_H = 3.5999e-22,
    FUV albedo 0.410, g 0.554, R_FUV 2.63. Scaled to Cloudy's 3.648e-22:
    MdMg 2.4827e-3, which is also within 1.3% of Cloudy's D/G by mass.
  - **R_out.** Cloudy's no-Ca/Fe stop radius. MOCASSIN has no temperature
    stop.
  - **Grid.** 41^3: cells 0.0152 pc; H II region 8.6 cells, He2+ zone 5.5.
    Memory, measured before the run: 1.2 GB/rank, 16.6 GB total, 28 GB free.
  - **Code.** Current, no path biasing; the binary was built at 00215dc plus
    the uncommitted script edits.

### 4. Run and cost (runs/d283-pn150k)

    iteration     1    2     3     4 (PDR)  5     6     7     8     9
    minutes       3    22.5  25.1  28.8     22.2  17.5  13.9  13.2  12.9
    converged %   0    0.01  0.17  0.42     0.53  0.67  1.36  52.7  91.2

Stopped at iteration 9 ("convergence reached", minConvergence 90):
  - total run time per processor 2:39:18;
  - no ion-balance or Te-balance failures in any iteration;
  - radiated continuum 2.65, then 1.24 falling to 1.15, of the 3.83 input

During iteration 2, 8 ranks had finished updateCell and were waiting in an
allreduce. The other 6 were sampled with gdb, in `getGrainRecombination`
(twice, once inside libm's `xflowf`), `setDustGasCollHeatCool` (three) and
`getGrainEmission`.

The grain charge and grain-gas terms dominate: two graphite components x 35
sizes against hiipdr's one silicate x 35, in a 150 kK field. For scale:
hiipdr 31^3 takes 42 min for 11 iterations, and Cloudy 8 min on one core.

Fine-structure lines of the neutral gas:
  - MOCASSIN's lineFlux.out gives [C II] 158 um 0.118 and [O I] 63 um 0.0056
    (Cloudy 0.308, 0.188). lineFlux excites them with electrons only.
  - The chemistry's coolant rates (pdrCoolSp.out, erg s^-1 cm^-3) integrated
    over the grid (x8 for the octant) give:
    - C+ 2.21e34 erg/s = 0.81 Hbeta, against Cloudy's [C II] 0.31;
    - O 3.98e34 = 1.47 Hbeta, against [O I] 63 + 145 um 0.20;
    - C 2.39e33 = 0.088;
    - CO 1.7e29.

### 6. What it means

  - **The photoionized nebula is reproduced.** Hbeta, the [O III] lines, the
    front radii and T_e in the H II gas agree to 1-6%. This is a hotter, harder
    and more line-dominated case than hiipdr, with different grains, and it
    gives no sign of a coupling problem there.
  - **Neon and the low ions run high.** [Ne III] is 35-48% high and [Ne II] 36%;
    [O II] 3726 is 28% high and [O I] 6300 40%. The inner gas carries 2-100x
    more C+, O+ and Mg+ at A_V < 0.1. [O IV] and [Ne V] are 11-14% low. None of
    this is investigated. Candidates, not tested:
    - charge exchange and dielectronic recombination at 15000-25000 K;
    - nuMax 30 Ryd truncating the 150 kK tail;
    - resolution near the star.
  - **O-02 reproduces with graphite.** The PDR gas is ~2x colder than Cloudy's.
    The chemistry's fine-structure cooling is several times Cloudy's line
    intensities: 7.3x for O, 2.6x for C+. That is the first direct
    heating/cooling pointer for O-02. Cooling that strong in 40-190 K gas
    points at the 3D-PDR coolant treatment or at the heating it balances. Not
    yet separated.
  - **O-03 again.** H2 in the ionized gas is ~1e5x Cloudy's, and H2 and CO form
    shallower.
  - **The Ca/Fe removal does not separate the codes.** Cloudy with and without
    them differs by <10% outside the front.

### 7. Not yet known

  - Whether nForLevels can be made per-ion, so GASS-type compositions run with
    Ca and Fe (register item to add).
  - The neon and low-ion excess in the H II gas.
  - Which side of the PDR energy balance is wrong: coolant level populations
    against Cloudy's, or grain photoelectric heating with graphite.
  - Scatter: one run of each.

### 8. Tools

`tools/d260_roellig.py`:
  - elements and abundances come from the run's own nebComposition file
    (`read_composition`) instead of the hardcoded abunV1 lists, which fixes
    part of O-30;
  - new options `--xlim`, `--rticks`, `--grains` (Cloudy's size law for the
    T_dust weights), `--model-cloudy-rin` (a Cloudy model on the model side),
    `--ref-label` and `--prefix`;
  - chemistry and ion y ranges grow with n_H, the temperature range with
    T_max;
  - inside-label positions scale with the front's A_V.

The hiipdr figures regenerated with the new script are pixel-identical to
D-282's.

https://claude.ai/code/artifact/67b186b5-96f7-4e21-875b-ba515c61fe26

## D-284 - the [C II] and [O I] cooling: the pointer was a mis-comparison, and a coolant data defect sits in warm gas (2026-09-15)

Hektor: "[C II] 158 um and [O I] 63 um cooling seems like an important thing to
investigate." D-283 had reported the chemistry's O and C+ cooling at 7.3x and
2.6x Cloudy's lines and called it the first heating/cooling pointer for O-02.

### 1. Where the D-283 numbers came from

The integral was pdrCoolSp over every active cell (x8 for the octant),
compared with Cloudy's 63 + 145 um and 158 um intensities. Two mismatches:

  - **Region.** Binned by radius, 69% of the O cooling and 76% of the C+
    cooling are in ionized cells (pdrZone 0). There the coolant is 12-65x
    Cloudy's far-IR O I emissivity and ~100x its 158 um emissivity. In the
    PDR proper MOCASSIN's far-IR cooling is *below* Cloudy's (0.01-0.5x
    beyond 0.19 pc), as its colder gas implies.
  - **Lines.** dataPDR/16o.dat, 12c+.dat and 12c.dat are 5-level atoms.
    16o.dat includes 1D2 and 1S0 ([O I] 6300, 6363, 5577, 2972), 12c+.dat
    the 4P term (C II] 2326), and 12c.dat 1D2 and 1S0 ([C I] 9850, 8727,
    4621). A coolant total is not a far-IR line.

Also checked on the way: D-266 already excites the C+ coolant at MOCASSIN's C+
share. pdrGrid.out's C+ (0.269 cm^-3, all carbon) is the chemistry's carrier,
and dividing by it gives a wrong per-ion rate.

### 2. The PDR: the cooling functions agree

Cooling per emitter per H nucleus against T, over PDR cells, MOCASSIN at the
coolant-table temperature nearest its Tg (table points are 1.94x apart, so bins
overlap only near them) and Cloudy zones in the same T bin:

| T [K] | O m/c | C+ m/c | f(H2) m / c |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45-70 | 0.98 | 1.26 | 0.42 / 0.73 |
| 70-110 | 1.28 | 1.00 | 0.10 / 0.06 |
| 170-260 | 0.86 | 0.84 | 0 / 0 |
| 260-400 | 1.20 | 0.96 | 0 / 0 |
| 700-1200 | 0.86 | 0.96 | 0 / 0 |

So at a given temperature the chemistry cools like Cloudy. The PDR is ~2x too
cold because it is heated less, not because it cools more.

Heating, as far as the outputs allow:
  - Cloudy (.heat): grain photoelectric is 34% of heating at 632 K, 81-96%
    from 127 K inward. Total ~2.3-5.4e-25 erg s^-1 per H at 0.29-0.48 pc.
  - MOCASSIN: per-cell budget terms (mocBud) exist only in memory. The D-217
    group means at the last iteration, for the 34688 "stayed cold" cells, are
    photoionization 1.05e-25, PE 4.2e-26 and PDR extra 1.2e-26 per H.

A group mean over the whole deep PDR is a pointer, not a measurement: PE looks
5-10x below Cloudy's, and MOCASSIN's photoionization heating is 2/3 of its
total where Cloudy's is a few %. A per-depth split needs mocBud written out.

### 3. The ionized gas: a data defect

Cloudy was rerun (runs/d284-fs-cloudy, the Ca/Fe-off model, overview identical
to D-283's) with emissivities for every transition of the three 5-level atoms.
In the ionized zone Cloudy's O I cooling is 89% optical and its C II cooling 99%
C II] 2326.

MOCASSIN's pdrCoolSp is written at the table point nearest T, which for 23-62
kK excitation energies moves values by factors 0.4-3. Rescaled to each cell's
Te with the dominant line's Boltzmann factor (an estimate), per emitter where
the temperatures agree within 1% (0.08-0.125 pc):

  - C+: 1.10-1.17x Cloudy;
  - O: 1.99-2.18x Cloudy.

Cause. In 16o.dat's O + e block the three 1D2 -> 3P2,1,0 rates are identical
(5.06e-9 cm^3 s^-1 at 1e4 K each), and so are the three 1S0 -> 3P_J rates.
5.06e-9 is Upsilon = 0.29, about the whole 3P-1D collision strength. Cloudy's
o_1.coll (Barklem 2007, partitioned by statistical weight, as its header
says) gives 0.15, 0.09 and 0.03 for J = 2, 1, 0 near 1e4 K. 3P1 and 3P0 are
sub-thermally populated at these densities, so excitation starts almost only
from 3P2, and the excess is ~2x rather than the 3x a sum would suggest.

tools/d284_o5lev.py (a standalone optically thin solve reading 16o.dat):
  - reproduces pdrCoolSp to 1-4% in 21 sampled cells from 27 K to 12 kK;
  - with Barklem's 1D/1S electron rates swapped in, gives 2.07-2.16x less O I
    cooling in the H II gas, 1.08-1.94x at the front, and exactly 1.00x below
    ~1000 K.

The same identical-per-J pattern is in 12c.dat (C + e, 1D and 1S) and in
16o.dat's O + H block. The O + H 1D rates are ~1e-13 cm^3 s^-1 and do not
matter. 12c+.dat's electron rates are J-resolved and look right. The files are
unchanged since the Phase 1 vendoring (49244b1).

### 4. Does it reach the temperature?

Yes, in principle: D-182 removed the zone gate, so these coolants replace
MOCASSIN's own oi.dat / ci.dat cooling in every cell. Its size, against
Cloudy's total cooling in each shell:

| shell [pc] | T_m | T_c | O I share (Cloudy) | MOCASSIN O I / Cloudy total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.10-0.12 | 11894 | 11934 | 0.003 | 0.006 |
| 0.12-0.13 | 10854 | 10702 | 0.025 | 0.046 |
| 0.13-0.135 | 9755 | 9054 | 0.10 | 0.37 |
| 0.135-0.14 | 8575 | 6716 | 0.29 | 1.76 |
| 0.14-0.145 | 6874 | 5029 | 0.42 | 1.83 |
| 0.15-0.16 | 2866 | 918 | 0.68 | 1.85 |

Negligible in the H II gas; at the front O I is a large term in both codes, and
there MOCASSIN is both hotter and cooling harder, so its heating there is
higher too. Correcting the rates would remove cooling from the front. The
expectation is warmer front gas, which widens the existing temperature gap
there. Not measured.

### 5. What it means

  - **O-02 is a heating problem.** The fine-structure cooling is right at a
    given T; D-283's pointer is withdrawn.
  - **A 2x O I (and likely C I) optical cooling excess in warm gas**, from the
    vendored data, which matters at the ionization front.
  - The standalone 3D-PDR reference uses the same files, but its gas never
    reaches the temperatures where 1D is excited, so the reference
    comparisons are unaffected.
  - lineFlux.out still reports MOCASSIN's electron-only [C II] 158 um / [O I]
    63 um while the thermal balance uses the coolants - two realities of one
    line (register item).

### 6. Not yet known / not done

  - The fix is not applied. The candidates differ: partition the file's own
    totals by 2J+1 (keeps its cited source), or adopt Barklem 2007 (what
    Cloudy uses). Not decided.
  - The per-depth heating split (needs mocBud written, then a warm-start
    iteration or a rerun).
  - 12c.dat's size of effect was not solved separately (C I coolant total 3.9x
    Cloudy's all-line C I, 0.09 Hbeta).
  - The coolant table's log-log interpolation under-reads an exponential by
    ~20-37% midway between points for 23-62 kK lines; not measured in the run.
  - One run of each code.

## D-285 - the coolant rates split by J, and the per-cell budget published (2026-09-18)

Hektor: "ok, proceed as suggested" - D-284's two recommendations, the data fix
by statistical weight and the per-depth heating split.

### 1. The fix, and why it is not tuning

D-284 measured each 1D -> 3P_J and 1S -> 3P_J electron rate in 16o.dat and
12c.dat carrying the whole-term value. The question left open was which total
to use. It turned out not to be a choice: the files' own cited sources are
J-resolved, and resolve exactly by statistical weight.

  - CHIANTI's o_1.splups - Zatsarinny & Tayal (2003) plus Bell et al. (1998),
    the two papers 16o.dat's header names - gives Upsilon(3P_J, 1D) in the
    ratio 5:3:1 and totals 0.0326, 0.150, 0.295, 0.544 at 1, 5, 10, 20 kK.
    16o.dat's per-J value is 0.032, 0.146, 0.293, 0.541: the term total, on
    every line of the grid.
  - The same for 1S: file 0.0323 at 1e4 K, source total 0.0322.
  - 12c.dat: per-J 1D Upsilon 0.125, 0.602, 1.141 at 1, 5, 10 kK against
    Cloudy's c_1.coll (Mendoza 1983) totals 0.125, 0.605, 1.149.

So multiplying each u -> 3P_J rate by g_J/9 restores the cited data rather than
importing Cloudy's. Check: the split O + e values are 2.811, 1.687 and
0.562e-9 cm^3 s^-1 at 1e4 K; CHIANTI's J-resolved entries are 2.83, 1.70 and
0.566e-9, under 1%.

Applied by `tools/d285_split_3p.py`, which splits only rows still identical
across J - so it is idempotent, and re-applicable after an upstream merge.
Blocks touched: O + e (1D, 1S), O + H (1D, rates ~1e-13 and irrelevant, done
for consistency), C + e (1D, 1S). 12c+.dat was already J-resolved.
Recorded in source/pdr/UPSTREAM.md as a vendored-data modification.

### 2. What it changes, before any re-run

tools/d284_o5lev.py on the corrected file, same cells as D-284:

| r [pc] | T_e | per O atom, was | now | Cloudy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.082 | 12130 | 3.83e-18 | 1.84e-18 | 1.85e-18 |
| 0.103 | 11839 | 3.45e-18 | 1.67e-18 | 1.66e-18 |
| 0.126 | 10658 | 1.93e-18 | 0.97e-18 | 0.93e-18 |
| 0.180 | 189 | 2.97e-21 | 2.97e-21 | - |

Below ~1000 K nothing moves at all: electrons cannot reach 1D there, which is
why the PDR cooling functions already agreed (D-284) and why the standalone
3D-PDR reference comparisons are unaffected.

### 3. The budget, per cell

D-284 had to answer the heating question with a group mean over 34688 cells,
because MOCASSIN's own budget lives in `mocBud` and never left memory. Now:

  - `grid%mocHeatEl(cell, nElements)`: photoionization heating per H nucleus
    split by element, accumulated in the same loop that builds heatSte and
    stored at the same call that fills mocBud slot 2, so budL(1) is its sum.
  - both gathered after the updateCell reduction. Ownership is fixed -
    `mod(iCell-(taskid+1),numtasks)`, the test updateCell itself uses - so each
    rank contributes its own cells and zero elsewhere, and the sum counts each
    cell once however many iterations have run. The collective is
    unconditional on every rank.
  - written by writeGrid as `output/thermBudget.out`, one record per cell in
    the same order as the other per-cell files: the ten mocBud terms (heating
    phot/PE/PDR, cooling coll/rec/ff/gas-dust/PDR, H-C, and the Te the balance
    was evaluated at) then nElements photoionization columns.

Slot 2 is the last thermBalance call of the cell, i.e. the balance point, at
the solver's last trial temperature - term 10 records it so any gap is visible.

All four flavours build.

### 4. The re-run: the 150 kK model (runs/d285-pn150k)

9 iterations, converged 91.9% (D-283: 91.2%), 3 h 24 min, no ion or Te balance
failure in any iteration. Iterations 2-4 shared the machine with the analysis
of the previous run, so 205 min against D-283's 159 is not a like-for-like
cost. Against the same Cloudy reference:

| | D-283 | D-285 | Cloudy |
|---|---|---|---|
| O coolant, all lines | 1.469 Hbeta | **0.834** | 0.608 |
| C coolant, all lines | 0.088 | **0.036** | 0.024 |
| C+ coolant, all lines | 0.814 | 0.818 | 0.939 |
| Hbeta | 2.712e34 | 2.710e34 | 2.78e34 |
| H+ / He2+ front | 0.1293 / 0.0829 pc | 0.1294 / 0.0830 | 0.128 / 0.088 |
| H/H2 crossing | A_V 0.269 | A_V 0.269 | 0.368 |
| PDR T_gas, A_V > 0.3 | 24-29 K | 24-29 K | 42-67 K |

  - **The O I excess is gone**: 2.4x Cloudy's all-line O I total before, 1.37x
    now. C I follows (3.9x -> 1.5x); C+ was never affected.
  - **The deep PDR did not move at all** - same crossing, same temperatures,
    same molecules - as predicted, because electrons cannot reach 1D there.
  - **The front got slightly hotter**, also as predicted, but *towards* Cloudy,
    not away: 4760 against 4540 K at A_V 0.15, where Cloudy is 7450. The D-284
    expectation that this would widen the gap was wrong; the front is colder
    than Cloudy's, not hotter, at that depth.
  - Line intensities move 1-3%, which is Monte Carlo scatter; [S III] 18.7 um
    -11% and [O II] 3729 +10% are larger and not attributed to the fix.

### 5. O-02 measured: the PDR is heated too little

The first per-depth budget (output/thermBudget.out, tools/d285_heatprofile.py),
per H nucleus, against Cloudy's `save heating`:

| shell [pc] | T_m / T_c | MOCASSIN | Cloudy | MOCASSIN split | Cloudy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25-0.32 | 30 / 69 | 7.9e-26 | 6.4e-25 | PE 0.72, PDR 0.23 | GrnP 0.96 |
| 0.32-0.42 | 28 / 61 | 6.0e-26 | 3.7e-25 | PE 0.78, PDR 0.17 | GrnP 0.97 |
| 0.42-0.55 | 26 / 50 | 4.5e-26 | 2.1e-25 | PE 0.77, PDR 0.17 | GrnP 0.96 |
| 0.55-0.62 | 24 / 43 | 3.8e-26 | 1.6e-25 | PE 0.73, PDR 0.20 | GrnP 0.95 |

Both codes are heated almost entirely by grain photoelectric heating there, and
MOCASSIN's total is 5-8x below Cloudy's - 5-11x on the photoelectric term
itself. With D-284's result that the cooling functions agree to 0.84-1.28 per
emitter at a given temperature, **O-02 is a heating deficit**, and it is the
same term D-261 measured against 3D-PDR (80x there, on silicate).

Two more things the split shows:
  - just outside the front (0.14-0.17 pc) MOCASSIN heats **3x more** than
    Cloudy, almost all of it H and He photoionization, and sits at 6960 K
    against 3886;
  - deep in, MOCASSIN's residual photoionization heating is 91% carbon, where
    Cloudy's C I term is 1-3%.

Not yet known: why the photoelectric rate is low. Candidates not separated -
the grain size range (nothing below 0.005 um here, and BT94-type heating is
carried by the smallest grains), the charging balance, or the FUV field the
term is evaluated on.

### 6. hiipdr re-run (runs/d285-hiipdr): unmoved, as predicted

11 iterations, 39 min, converged 80.3% (D-282's run: 81.0%). The prediction was
that nothing would move, because this fixture's PDR is at 21-26 K, far below
the temperature at which electrons reach 1D, and its H II gas is 8000 K rather
than 12000. Measured:

| | D-282 run | D-285 |
|---|---|---|
| front (radial shells) | 3.832 pc | 3.835 |
| H/H2 crossing | A_V 1.198 | 1.199 |
| C+ = C | A_V 2.269 | 2.276 |
| PDR T_gas, A_V 0.7-2.0 | 21-26 K | 21-26 K |
| T_gas at A_V 0.30 / 0.45 | 8560 / 8210 K | 8690 / 8360 |
| T_gas at r = 1, 2, 3, 3.3 pc | 7950, 8030, 8730, 9450 K | 8000, 8120, 8840, 9560 |
| deep C+/Cloudy, e-/Cloudy, CO/Cloudy | 0.21-0.36, 0.27-0.39, 54-125 | same to 2 digits |

The ionized gas warms by ~1%, which is the [O I] 6300 cooling the fix removed;
everything neutral is unchanged. Convergence differs by 0.7 points, within what
two Monte Carlo runs of this fixture give.

### 7. Both pages republished

'150 kK PN Against Cloudy' and 'hiipdr Against Cloudy' are rebuilt from the
re-runs: figures regenerated, every number recomputed by tools/d285_kpis.py and
tools/d285_kpis_hiipdr.py (each validated first by reproducing the published
numbers from the run the page was built on), the withdrawn 7.3x/2.6x claim
replaced by the coolant-total-against-all-lines comparison, and the O-02
heating measurement written into both.

### 8. Not yet known

  - Whether the photoelectric deficit is the size distribution, the grain
    charge, or the field (section 5).
  - The per-cell budget has not been read for hiipdr, only for the 150 kK
    model.
  - 12c.dat's effect was never sized separately from 16o.dat's.
  - Expectation, from D-284: the front loses cooling and should get hotter,
    which would widen the temperature gap against Cloudy there. If it does,
    that is a result about the front's heating, not about these rates.
  - 12c.dat's effect was never sized separately.
  - hiipdr has not been re-run on the corrected data. Its PDR is cold enough
    that nothing should move; that is a prediction, not a measurement.

## D-286 - Case A recombination cooling, ported and audited (2026-09-19)

Hektor: a bug found while working in `mocassin_HM_2026` - the thermal balance
used Case B recombination cooling fits where Case A is correct - with the
instruction to audit that commit and port it to both branches here.

Source commit: `dd3006c` on that repository's `dev`, "Implement Case A
recombination cooling in thermal balance".

### 1. Is the premise true in this repository?

Yes. The argument for Case A is that the code does not assume on-the-spot
re-absorption: it emits the ground-state recombination continuum into the
diffuse field and transports it, and where those photons are re-absorbed the
photoionization heating integral counts them. Cooling must then count the
kinetic energy the same recombinations removed, which is what Case A
(beta_A = beta_B + beta_1) does. Checked here:

  - `emission_mod` builds `gammaHI` from the H threshold bin `HIPnuP` upward
    (and the He continua from their own thresholds since D-227), so the
    ground-state continuum is emitted, not dropped;
  - there is no on-the-spot option anywhere in `source/` - nothing switches
    that transport off, so the Case A choice is unconditional rather than
    mode-dependent.

### 2. Are the coefficients right?

Checked against values not taken from the commit. The fits give a cooling
coefficient `betaRec` used as `coolRec = n_i n_e betaRec k Te / sqrt(Te)`, so
`betaRec k sqrt(Te) / alpha` is the mean energy removed per recombination:

| | at 1e4 K | Osterbrock |
|---|---|---|
| legacy fit / alpha_B | 0.672 kT | 0.68 kT (Case B) |
| new fit / alpha_A | 0.779 kT | 0.78 kT (Case A) |

with alpha_B = 2.59e-13, alpha_A = 4.17e-13. The implied ground-state term is
0.95 kT per recombination, which is the expected value for direct-to-n=1.
beta_A/beta_B over the fitted range:

    log10Te   3.0    3.4    3.7    4.0    4.3    4.6    5.0
    ratio     1.46   1.59   1.71   1.87   2.06   2.31   2.81

So the H+ and He++ fits are sound, and the change makes recombination cooling
1.5-2.8x larger. Recombination is a minority coolant in H II gas, so the
expected effect on Te is a small cooling, not a restructuring.

### 3. A defect in the He+ branch, ported as-is

The He+ (He+ + e -> He0) coefficient is piecewise: Hummer & Storey (1998)
Table 6 up to log10Te = 4.4, the hydrogenic Hummer (1994) fit above it,
because HS98 stops there. **The two branches do not meet.** At the join:

    HS98 branch   3.0639e-11
    H94 branch    2.4624e-11      ratio 1.244

a 24% step at Te = 25119 K, in a term `iterateT` brackets a root of. The two
fits also diverge steadily below the join (1.008 at log10Te 3.0, 1.031 at 3.5,
1.102 at 4.0), so the step is the accumulated difference between a He-specific
and a hydrogenic fit, not a typo.

It is ported unchanged, so that this repository and `mocassin_HM_2026` compute
the same numbers and any comparison between them is exact. It is recorded here
rather than silently smoothed. Its practical weight is small - above 25000 K
helium is mostly He++ and this term is a few per cent of `coolRec`, which is
itself a minority of the budget - but this project has twice been bitten by
discontinuities in the function the temperature solver brackets (D-166, D-168),
and the same fix should be made in both repositories. Extrapolating the HS98
quartic past the join instead is well behaved to log10Te 5.0 (2.68e-11, still
falling smoothly), which is one of the two candidate fixes; the other is a
blend across a narrow interval.

### 4. The port

  - `source/update_mod.f90`: the three `betaRec` assignments (H+, He++, He+),
    each behind `lgCaseARecCool`, legacy retained in the `else`.
  - `source/common_mod.f90`: `lgCaseARecCool = .true.`.
  - `source/readdata_mod.f90`: reads `MOCASSIN_RECCOOL`, accepting `legacy`,
    `caseB` or `caseb` for the old behaviour, and prints which is in use on
    rank 0. Same variable and spellings as the source commit. This repository
    normally configures through input keywords; the environment variable is
    kept so a run here and a run there are put in the same mode the same way.
  - Not ported: the source commit's rebuilt executables (this repository does
    not track them on this branch) and its `taskid` guards on the Badnell
    print, which is not in this branch.

All four flavours build from clean.

### 5. Measured: hiipdr, Case B against Case A

runs/d286-hiipdr-caseA against runs/d285-hiipdr - the same fixture, the same
build, this change and nothing else. 11 iterations, 39 min, converged 80.9%
(80.3%). The Te-balance transient at iterations 2-4 is 18/17/14% against the
baseline's 16/18/15%, so the stronger cooling does not destabilise the solve.

Ionized gas, matched in radius (MOCASSIN Case B -> Case A, Cloudy):

    r = 1.0 pc   8000 -> 7620 K   (Cloudy 9230)
    r = 2.0 pc   8120 -> 7750     (8060)
    r = 3.0 pc   8840 -> 8510     (8180)
    r = 3.3 pc   9560 -> 9250     (8760)

About 4% cooler everywhere, which is the expected size: recombination cooling
roughly doubles but is a minority coolant in H II gas. Against Cloudy the
change cuts both ways - it improves the outer H II gas, where MOCASSIN ran
hot (3.0 pc: 8% high -> 4% high; 3.3 pc: 9% -> 6%), and worsens the inner,
where it already matched or ran cool (2.0 pc: 1% high -> 4% low). Cloudy
transports its own diffuse field, so its values are already the Case A-like
ones and the comparison is fair.

The neutral gas does not move at all:

    A_V 0.70   23.8 -> 23.9 K       A_V 2.00   21.6 -> 21.7
    A_V 1.00   25.7 -> 25.7         A_V 2.90   11.1 -> 11.1

nor does the structure: front 3.835 -> 3.825 pc, H/H2 crossing A_V 1.199 ->
1.196, C+ = C 2.276 -> 2.275. So this changes the ionized gas and leaves O-02
and the deep-carbon questions where they were.

**'hiipdr Against Cloudy' re-plotted from the Case A run** (figures, both
tables and the ionized-gas numbers), with the change written into the page.
**'150 kK PN Against Cloudy' is still Case B** - it needs a 3.5 h re-run,
not done.

## D-287 - The photoelectric rate: a missing Lya field and a size-independent yield (2026-09-19)

Hektor: "now lets work on the photoelectric rate investigation."

D-285 left O-02 as a grain photoelectric heating deficit of 5-11x against
Cloudy, with three candidates named and none separated: the grain size range,
the charging balance, or the FUV field the term is evaluated on. This entry
separates them. Nothing in the code was changed.

The comparison is `runs/d285-pn150k` against `runs/d283-150k-cloudy-noCaFe`,
both graphite, both MRN 0.005-0.25 um in 35/10 sizes, A_V/N_H matched at
3.648e-22 (MdMg 2.4827e-3), n_H = 1e3 uniform - so A_V and radius are the same
axis in both and matching on either gives the same answer. `tools/d287_pe.py`.

### 1. The size distribution is not a candidate at all

Cloudy's input is `grains ISM graphite 1 linear`, which is the same MRN
0.005-0.25 um, and it has no PAHs (they need an explicit `grains PAH`). So
"nothing below 0.005 um here", the first candidate in D-285, cannot be the
difference *against Cloudy*: Cloudy has nothing below 0.005 um either. It
remains a difference against 3D-PDR, whose WD01 formula assumes PAHs and a
gas-to-dust of 100 (this model's is 403).

### 2. The field is 3.2x low, and by a constant

Cloudy's `save PDR` writes G0 per zone (`hmi.UV_Cont_rel2_Habing_TH85_depth`:
the 6-13.6 eV flux, incident plus diffuse continuum plus outward lines, over
1.6e-3). MOCASSIN's `pdrFUV.out` writes chi over 0.472-1.0 Ryd in Draine units,
and with lgDebug off Jste carries the diffuse field too (D-158), so both sides
are the full local field. Draine/Habing = 8.94e-14/5.29e-14 = 1.69.

| r [pc] | G0 MOCASSIN | G0 Cloudy | ratio | PE_m/PE_c | T_m/T_c |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.13 | 134 | 342 | 0.39 | 0.29 | 10035 / 9797 |
| 0.16 | 75.4 | 221 | 0.34 | 0.11 | 1016 / 381 |
| 0.20 | 44.1 | 134 | 0.33 | 0.06 | 89 / 117 |
| 0.30 | 16.7 | 53.7 | 0.31 | 0.13 | 30 / 63 |
| 0.50 | 4.41 | 14.9 | 0.30 | 0.16 | 25 / 50 |
| 0.60 | 2.58 | 9.05 | 0.29 | 0.16 | 24 / 44 |

At A_V 0.05, inside the ionized gas, the ratio is 0.98. So the offset is
established across the front and then held: the two codes attenuate at the
same rate, and MOCASSIN starts the PDR with 3.2x less field. That is a
normalisation difference, not a transfer-slope difference.

Where it comes from: at 0.6 pc Cloudy's G0 is **4.6x** the unattenuated
stellar FUV flux at that radius, MOCASSIN's only 1.3x. A field larger than the
unattenuated direct field can only be diffuse, so Cloudy's PDR is lit mostly by
radiation made in the H II region, and MOCASSIN's is not.

### 3. Why: MOCASSIN throws away every line photon at creation

`newPhotonPacket`, `case("diffuse")`, on drawing a line rather than a continuum
photon (photon_mod.f90:921):

    ! line photons escape so don't care which one it is unless debugging
    if (lgDebug) then
       call getNu2( grid(gP)%linePDF(...), nuP )
    else
       nuP = 0
    end if

`initPhotonPacket` then sets `nu = 0.` and `lgLine = .true.`, and
`energyPacketRun` calls `pathSegment` only for `.not. lgLine`; the else branch
bins the packet into `linePackets` under lgDebug and otherwise does nothing.
The packet is never traced. So no line photon is ever in Jste - not Lya, not
the heavy-element resonance lines.

This is a deliberate assumption of MOCASSIN's, and a sound one for a dust-poor
ionized nebula where the line escapes. It is not sound at a PDR front, where
Lya is a first-order heating agent.

Its size here, from Cloudy's own `.lines` (intrinsic intensities per unit inner
area, x 4 pi Rin^2):

    L(Lya) intrinsic   4.03e35 erg/s     = 3.0 x L_FUV(stellar)
    L_FUV(stellar)     1.33e35 erg/s     (pdrFUV.out header, 0.472-1.0 Ryd)
    L(Lya) emergent    0.70e35 erg/s     - 83% is absorbed, nearly all by dust

Three times the stellar FUV luminosity, mostly deposited - which is the
observed factor, arriving from the right direction and with the right size.

`resLinesTransfer` does not repair this. It defaults to 101 (never; the run
log carries MOCASSIN's own warning 14 times) and no fixture here sets it, but
turning it on would not put Lya in the field either: `initResLinePackets`
computes the resonance-line energy *absorbed by grains*, `(1 - fEscape)`, and
emits it as extra `chTypeD = "diffuse"` packets, whose frequency is then drawn
from the local re-emission PDF. The energy comes back as infrared. It warms the
dust - which is what the keyword is documented to do - and leaves the
photoelectric integrand untouched.

### 4. The rate is 3-7x low as well, at matched grain charge

Dividing the field out is not enough, because the photoelectric efficiency
depends on the charging parameter psi = G0 sqrt(T) / n_e, and MOCASSIN's lower
field gives it a lower psi. Binning each code's own cells by psi and comparing
the heating per H nucleus per unit G0:

| psi | MOCASSIN | Cloudy | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100-300 | 5.18e-27 | 1.74e-26 | 0.30 |
| 300-1000 | 2.57e-27 | 1.14e-26 | 0.23 |
| 1000-3000 | 1.38e-27 | 8.93e-27 | 0.15 |

(The T medians differ between the bins - 27-60 K against 45-128 K - but the
BT94 numerator moves 3% over that range, so this is not a temperature effect.)

So at the same field *and* the same charge, MOCASSIN heats 3-7x less. The
charging is excluded as the cause and excluded in the informative direction:
MOCASSIN's psi is 4-5x lower than Cloudy's at matched radius, which should make
its grains *more* efficient, not less. The threshold is excluded too - grainVn
is 0.323 Ryd = 4.39 eV for both graphite files, the standard work function.

What is left is the yield. `setPhotoelHeatCool` uses Baldwin et al. (1991):

    Yn = min( Y0*(1 - nu_0/nu), Y1 )        Y0 = 0.5, Y1 = 0.2

which depends on frequency and on the material's work function and **not on
the grain radius**. WD01's, which Cloudy uses, rises towards unity as the grain
radius falls below the electron escape length - and an MRN distribution has
most of its *surface area* in the smallest grains, so a grey yield capped at
0.2 loses exactly where the absorption happens. A flat 0.2 is generous for a
0.25 um grain and several times too small for a 0.005 um one.

### 5. Why the two factors do not multiply to 5-11x

3.2 x (3 to 7) is 10-22, and the measured total gap is 5-11x. They do not
multiply because they are coupled: supplying the missing Lya would raise psi
by the same 3.2x and charge the grains further, and MOCASSIN's efficiency falls
with psi more steeply (about psi^-0.53 over its range) than Cloudy's
(psi^-0.29). Fixing only the field would move the heating far less than 3.2x.
The two have to be considered together, and the yield is the one that does not
cancel against itself.

### 6. What this does not establish

  - The 3-7x is attributed to the yield by elimination - charge, threshold,
    size distribution and field are each excluded by measurement - not by a
    direct calculation of WD01's yield on this grain population. That
    calculation has not been done.
  - Nothing has been measured on hiipdr. Its central star is far cooler, so
    the Lya-to-stellar-FUV ratio there will be quite different and the split
    between the two factors should not be assumed to carry over.
  - MOCASSIN's FUV band starts at 0.4724 Ryd against Cloudy's 0.441, about 6%
    of the band for a 150 kK blackbody, and the photoelectric integral itself
    runs from the work function 0.323 Ryd rather than from either. These are
    small against a factor 3 and have not been corrected for.
  - No claim is made here about which yield is right. WD01 is the modern
    treatment and Cloudy's, but this project's rule is that a difference
    against a reference is measured and reported, not closed.

## D-288 - The yield premise checked, and refuted (2026-09-19)

Hektor: "proceed as recommended" - the recommendation at the end of D-287
being to replace the Baldwin et al. (1991) photoelectric yield with WD01's,
on the grounds that it is the factor that does not partly cancel itself.

The premise was checked before it was implemented, and it does not hold.

### 1. WD01's yield is lower than MOCASSIN's here, not higher

`tools/d288_yield.py` evaluates both on this grain population. WD01's neutral
carbonaceous yield is min(y0 y1, 1) with their eqs 12-16; the photon
attenuation length la = lambda/(4 pi k) comes from `dustData/grph1-dl.nk` and
`grph2-dl.nk` on the 1/3 : 2/3 axis weighting `dust_species.dat` sets, so no
constant here stands in for something the model already knows. Z = 0
throughout, because MOCASSIN applies the Coulomb suppression separately as
`Yhat` - the like-for-like comparison is with the neutral yield.

| photon | 6 eV | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 13 | 13.6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOCASSIN (any a) | 0.134 | 0.186 | 0.200 | 0.200 | 0.200 | 0.200 | 0.200 | 0.200 | 0.200 |
| WD01, a = 0.005 um | 0.0003 | 0.0062 | 0.0505 | 0.178 | 0.288 | 0.264 | 0.275 | 0.341 | 0.400 |
| WD01, a = 0.05 um | 0.0001 | 0.0016 | 0.0107 | 0.036 | 0.064 | 0.079 | 0.109 | 0.148 | 0.173 |
| WD01, a = 0.25 um | 0.0001 | 0.0008 | 0.0046 | 0.015 | 0.033 | 0.058 | 0.092 | 0.129 | 0.150 |

Averaged over the MRN distribution and weighted by absorbed photons, for a
150 kK blackbody attenuated to the depth given:

    A_V 0.0    <Y> MOCASSIN 0.179   WD01 0.142    0.79x
    A_V 0.5                 0.167        0.107    0.64x
    A_V 1.0                 0.153        0.073    0.48x

(insensitive to the Qabs weighting: capping Qabs at 1 or at 2 moves the ratio
by 0.01.) So **adopting WD01's yield at fixed grain charge would lower
MOCASSIN's photoelectric heating**, by about a factor two in the deep PDR -
away from Cloudy, not towards it. D-287's attribution of the residual 3-7x to
the yield is withdrawn.

It was reached by elimination - field, charge, threshold and size distribution
each excluded by measurement - and elimination is only as good as the
completeness of the list. The list was not complete, and the eliminated
candidate was eliminated on the wrong variable (see below).

### 2. What the yield table does show

The defect is in the spectral shape, not the normalisation. Baldwin's
`min(0.5(1 - nu_0/nu), 0.2)` saturates at 0.2 only 3.6 eV above a 4.4 eV
threshold and is flat from 8 eV up. WD01's rises as the fifth power of the
photoelectron energy and does not reach 0.2 until ~9.5 eV even for the
smallest grain. Near threshold MOCASSIN is **100-400x too high**, and that is
precisely the part of the band that survives into the deep PDR, where the
>11 eV photons have been absorbed.

### 3. The hypothesis that replaces it: the grains are over-charged

Too much photoemission near threshold drives the equilibrium potential up, and
`Yhat = Yn (1 - V_g/(nu - nu_0))` together with the energy term then suppresses
what is left. Three things point that way, none of them yet a measurement of
the potential:

  - Reproducing MOCASSIN's measured heating per absorbed photon with Y = 0.2
    and a 10 eV photon requires V_g ~ 4.6 V. Cloudy prints <Pot> = 0.5-1.4 V
    for its ten graphite bins in this model.
  - MOCASSIN's efficiency falls as psi^-0.53 against Cloudy's psi^-0.29
    (D-287, section 4). A steeper fall with the charging parameter is what an
    over-charged grain gives.
  - D-287 excluded the charge on psi = G0 sqrt(T)/n_e, which is the *driver*
    of the charge, not the charge. Two codes at the same psi need not sit at
    the same potential if their yields differ - and now we know they do.

### 4. The potential is now written out

It never has been: `grainPot` is a local of `updateCell`, and nothing in
`output_mod` or `grid_mod` touched it, which is why every entry from D-261 on
has argued about the grain charge from proxies. Added, on the D-285 pattern
(allocate in `setMotherGrid` and `resetGrid`, fill in `setPhotoelHeatCool`,
gather by cell ownership in `iteration_mod`, write on unit 54): `mocGrain`,
six slots appended to `thermBudget.out`, accumulated over exactly the
photoelectric integral so that

    heating per H  =  slot 4 * slot 2 * slot 3 * hcRyd

holds identically rather than approximately.

    1  <V_g> [Ryd], weighted by absorbed photons above threshold
    2  <Y>, electrons per absorbed photon, after the Coulomb barrier
    3  <E> [Ryd], net energy per escaping electron
    4  absorbed photons per H per s, above threshold
    5  absorbed energy per H per s [erg], above threshold
    6  geometric grain area per H [cm^2]

Slot 5 also removes the last estimated quantity in D-287's efficiency
comparison, where the FUV cross-section per H had to be guessed from A_V/N_H.

All four flavours build. `runs/d288-pn150k` is the 150 kK model re-run to
measure it.

### 5. Measured: the grains are over-charged by 3-6x

`runs/d288-pn150k`, 9 iterations, 91.4% converged, 2 h 51 min, clean exit;
the fixture's published numbers are unmoved (Hbeta 2.743e34, H+ front 0.1294
pc, PDR 24-29 K), as a diagnostic-only change should leave them. Cloudy
re-run as `runs/d288-cloudy-grain` with `save grain potential`, which writes
the floating potential in eV per zone per grain bin; MOCASSIN's is the
absorbed-photon-weighted mean over species and sizes, Cloudy's is weighted by
absorbing area over its ten bins. `tools/d288_charge.py`.

| r [pc] | T_m / T_c | V_g MOCASSIN | V_g Cloudy (small/large) | <Y>_m | <E>_m [eV] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.13 | 10024 / 9797 | +1.05 | **-1.15** (-1.26/-1.34) | 0.098 | 2.09 |
| 0.16 | 988 / 381 | 3.77 | 0.72 (0.60/0.40) | 0.060 | 1.71 |
| 0.20 | 92 / 117 | **4.77** | 1.00 (0.82/0.60) | 0.048 | 1.51 |
| 0.25 | 34 / 73 | 4.60 | 1.43 (1.19/0.92) | 0.048 | 1.54 |
| 0.30 | 30 / 63 | 4.07 | 1.35 (1.11/0.86) | 0.054 | 1.61 |
| 0.40 | 27 / 57 | 3.13 | 0.78 (0.65/0.46) | 0.065 | 1.66 |
| 0.50 | 26 / 50 | 2.49 | 0.53 (0.46/0.28) | 0.071 | 1.63 |
| 0.60 | 24 / 44 | 1.96 | 0.41 (0.39/0.19) | 0.082 | 1.60 |

The prediction was 4.6 V from the heating per absorbed photon; the measured
peak is 4.77 V. MOCASSIN's grains are held **2.8-5.6x** more positive than
Cloudy's at every depth in the PDR, and in the ionized gas the two do not even
agree in sign - Cloudy's grains are negative there, where electron collisional
charging wins, and MOCASSIN's are positive.

The consequence is in the two columns after it. `<Y>` is the yield *after* the
Coulomb barrier: 0.048-0.098, against a neutral-grain yield of 0.15-0.20 for
this Baldwin form. The barrier is removing two thirds to three quarters of the
photoelectrons, and cutting what survives to 1.5-2.1 eV each.

### 6. The 5-11x, fully decomposed

With `Eabs` now measured rather than estimated from A_V/N_H (slot 5), and
Cloudy's absorbed energy inferred by scaling on G0 - legitimate because the
grain area per H is matched by measurement, not assumption:

| r [pc] | field x | efficiency x | product | measured PE ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.20 | 3.03 | 5.17 | 15.7 | 0.06 |
| 0.30 | 3.17 | 2.50 | 7.9 | 0.13 |
| 0.40 | 3.22 | 1.99 | 6.4 | 0.16 |
| 0.50 | 3.33 | 1.82 | 6.1 | 0.16 |
| 0.60 | 3.47 | 1.80 | 6.2 | 0.16 |

So O-02's photoelectric deficit is, at last, two measured numbers and not an
attribution: a field low by 3.0-3.5x because line photons are discarded
(D-287), and a conversion efficiency low by 1.8-5.2x because the grains are
over-charged. Both have a single identified cause, and they are not
independent - the yield that over-charges the grain is the same yield whose
near-threshold excess D-288 section 2 measured.

Two validations of the new diagnostic, both passed:

  - the identity `heating/H = N_abs <Y> <E> hcRyd` holds to 7e-6 over every
    active cell;
  - the grain cross-section per H comes out 5.453e-22 cm^2, against 5.60e-22
    computed analytically for MRN a^-3.5 over 0.005-0.25 um at rho = 2.2 and
    MdMg = 2.4827e-3 - 3%, which is the size discretisation. The dust
    inventory is therefore excluded as a candidate by measurement.

### 7. What is decided and what is not

  - **The WD01 yield is the right change, for the opposite reason to
    D-287's.** Being 100-400x *lower* near threshold, it removes the
    photoemission that is holding the grain at 4.8 V; the potential should
    fall towards Cloudy's, the Coulomb barrier open, and the net heating rise
    even though the neutral yield falls by 0.47-0.79x. That is a prediction,
    and the reason to make the change is that it is the better physics, not
    that it closes a gap.
  - **Not implemented yet.** It has to go into `getGrainEmission` and
    `setPhotoelHeatCool` together - one yield, one reality - or the charge
    balance and the heating will run on different physics.
  - Whether the heating rises *enough* is not predictable from here: the
    Coulomb term and the yield move in opposite directions, and only the run
    will say. It will not close the field half in any case.
  - The field half of D-287 is untouched and still stands: MOCASSIN discards
    every line packet at creation, and Lya here is 3.0x the stellar FUV band
    luminosity.
  - Nothing has been measured on hiipdr.
  - MOCASSIN's positive grain charge in the ionized gas, where Cloudy's is
    negative, is not explained here and is not part of O-02. It is worth its
    own look: it bears on the gas-grain collisional term as well.

## D-289 - The WD01 yield, implemented and measured (2026-09-19)

Hektor: "proceed" - implement the yield change D-288 ended on, in the charge
balance and the heating together.

### 1. What went in

One yield, one table. `ph_mod` builds `grainYield(nSpecies, nSizes, nbins)`
once at setup, and both `getGrainEmission` - the charge balance - and
`setPhotoelHeatCool` - the heating - read it. Each previously carried its own
copy of the Baldwin expression, which is precisely the duplication that lets
two realities drift apart. The neutral yield does not depend on the grain
potential (the Coulomb part is `Yhat` at the point of use), so tabulating it
is exact, not an approximation, and it takes the yield out of the innermost
loop of a Newton solve that D-283 already found dominates the runtime.

Weingartner & Draine (2001) eqs 12-16, with everything the model can supply
taken from the model:

  - the small-grain escape factor needs the photon attenuation length
    `la = lambda/(4 pi k)`, read from the same optical constants the
    absorption cross sections are built from, so the yield tracks this grain
    population instead of being grey;
  - the bulk fit is carbonaceous or silicate by `MsurfAtom` in the grain's own
    data file - 12.004 for graphite and amorphous carbon, 20-36 for the
    silicates and oxides - reported at setup rather than assumed silently;
  - `W` is the grain's own `grainVn`, not WD01's tabulated 4.4 / 8 eV;
  - `Theta` is measured from MOCASSIN's threshold, the same one bounding the
    integral. WD01's size-dependent shift for a neutral grain (+0.16 eV at
    50 A) is deliberately not applied: a threshold inside the yield differing
    from the threshold bounding the integral would be two realities again.

`MOCASSIN_YIELD=baldwin` restores the legacy yield, the same spelling as
`MOCASSIN_RECCOOL` (D-286). It is read in `makeDustXsec` rather than
`readData`, because `mocassin.f90` calls `initXSecArray` *before* `readData`
and `mocassinWarm` does not call `readInput` at all - the point of use is the
one place every executable passes through. `Y0`/`Y1` moved to `constants_mod`,
removing a duplicated pair of constants.

Validated before the run: the table reproduces `tools/d288_yield.py`'s
independent calculation to 4-6%, the residual being that the code treats each
graphite axis separately rather than averaging k first, which is the correct
order; the legacy branch returns a flat 0.200.

Two bugs in the first cut, both caught by that check rather than by the run:
`grainYield` was allocated beside `MsurfAtom`, where `nSizes` is still zero -
heap corruption, and a table of 1.0 throughout - and the two helper procedures
were placed inside `makeDustXsec`, which has no `contains`.

### 2. Measured: the over-charging halves, the heating does not move

`runs/d289-pn150k-wd01`, 9 iterations, 91.9% converged, 2 h 54 min, clean
exit. Against `runs/d288-pn150k`, the same model on the Baldwin yield:

| r [pc] | V_g Baldwin | V_g WD01 | V_g Cloudy | PE Baldwin | PE WD01 | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.13 | 1.05 | 0.22 | -1.15 | 3.19e-24 | 4.68e-24 | +47% |
| 0.20 | 4.77 | 4.34 | 1.00 | 9.68e-26 | 1.05e-25 | +8% |
| 0.30 | 4.07 | 3.44 | 1.35 | 5.55e-26 | 6.12e-26 | +10% |
| 0.40 | 3.13 | 2.29 | 0.78 | 4.39e-26 | 4.95e-26 | +13% |
| 0.50 | 2.49 | 1.46 | 0.53 | 3.40e-26 | 3.62e-26 | +6% |
| 0.60 | 1.96 | 0.89 | 0.41 | 2.60e-26 | 2.42e-26 | -7% |

Over the PDR as a whole (A_V > 0.3): `<Y>` 0.0705 -> 0.0371, `<E>` 1.63 ->
2.58 eV, `V_g` 2.594 -> 1.607 V, photoelectric heating 3.61e-26 -> 3.91e-26,
gas temperature 23.9-29.3 -> 23.6-30.3 K. Hbeta 2.743 -> 2.737e34 and the
front 0.1294 -> 0.1295 pc, both Monte Carlo scatter.

**The prediction was right in direction and wrong in size.** The grain
potential did fall - by 38% through the PDR, and by 55% at 0.6 pc, where the
over-charging against Cloudy goes from 4.8x to 2.2x. But the heating rose 8%,
and the gas temperature did not move at all.

### 3. Why: the term is self-regulating

Three factors move together and very nearly cancel:

  - `<Y>` **falls** by 47%, which is the lower WD01 yield doing what D-288
    measured it would;
  - `<E>` **rises** by 58%, because a grain at 1.6 V instead of 2.6 V takes
    less energy from each escaping electron;
  - `N_abs` **rises**, because the integral starts at `max(Vn + Vg, Vn)` and
    that threshold drops with the potential.

Lowering the yield lowers the charge, and lowering the charge gives back most
of what the yield took. That is a real property of the photoelectric balance,
not a numerical accident, and it is why a factor-2 change in the yield buys
8% in the heating. It also means the converse: the 3-7x D-287 was looking for
was never available in the yield alone, whichever direction it pointed.

### 4. Where O-02 stands now

The efficiency factor moves from 1.8-5.2x to 1.7-4.8x; the field factor is
untouched at 3.0-3.5x. The deep PDR is still 24-30 K against Cloudy's 42-67.
**Nothing here is to be tuned to close that** - the yield is now the better
physics and it stays whatever the temperature does.

What remains, in order of what the evidence supports:

  - **The electron-collection side of the charge balance has never been
    looked at.** MOCASSIN's grains are still held 2.2-4.3x more positive than
    Cloudy's with the photoemission now on WD01, so the imbalance is at least
    as likely to be in `getGrainRecombination` as in what is left of the
    emission. In the ionized gas the two codes still disagree in sign.
  - MOCASSIN solves for a single mean potential; Cloudy solves a charge
    distribution over discrete Z. Whether that alone can account for a factor
    2-4 in the mean is not known and has not been estimated here.
  - The field half (D-287) is unaddressed and is the larger of the two.

### 5. '150 kK PN Against Cloudy' rebuilt

The page was three code changes behind - it still showed the pre-Case-A run -
and is rebuilt from `runs/d289-pn150k-wd01`, which carries the corrected
coolant data (D-285), Case A (D-286) and the WD01 yield together. All three
Roellig figures regenerated, and every number in the headline, selected-depths,
line-intensity and cost tables recomputed.

A new section, *The photoelectric term, measured*, carries a new figure
(`tools/d289_pefig.py`): the FUV field, the grain potential and the heating
per H against depth, with the Baldwin and WD01 runs and Cloudy on one axis.
Panel (c) is the self-regulation - the two MOCASSIN curves lie almost on top
of each other although their yields differ by a factor two. The section states
the two factors and that the yield change bought 8%.

Two other corrections to the page: the dust inventory is now excluded as a
suspect by measurement rather than assumption, and the cost table shows this
run's undisturbed 2 h 54 min rather than the previous run's contended timings.

### 6. Not yet known

  - Nothing has been measured on hiipdr, whose star is far cooler; neither
    the yield change nor the Lya deficit should be assumed to carry over.
  - **The hiipdr page is now the one that is behind**: it is on Case A but
    predates the WD01 yield, and its PDR is at 21-26 K where this model's is
    at 24-30, so the yield change there is a prediction, not a measurement.
  - The +47% photoelectric heating in the ionized gas changes no temperature
    there, photoionization dominating, but it has not been checked against the
    dust temperature, which D-283 already had 8-25% warm.

## D-290 - The grain charge balance is out by 4 pi^2 (2026-09-19)

Found while gathering facts for the Lya work, by re-reading the two places
D-289 had just made share a yield. They do not share a convention for the
radiation field.

### 1. What Jste is

`Jste` is the angle-integrated energy flux, erg cm^-2 s^-1, summed per bin -
not the mean intensity J. Two independent confirmations, neither of them a
reading of the code:

  - `pdrFUV.out` reports `chi = sum(Jste)/(c u_Draine)` against
    `chi_thin = L_FUV/(4 pi r^2 c u_Draine)`, and their ratio is 1.14-1.27 at
    r = 0.02-0.08 pc, where the field is the unattenuated direct one. If Jste
    were J the ratio would be 1/4pi.
  - D-288's `mocGrain` slot 5, the absorbed energy per H built from Jste and
    sigma_abs, matches G0 x 1.6e-3 x (area/H) with <Q_abs> = 0.68 - which is
    the right value for graphite MRN in the FUV.

`setPhotoelHeatCool` therefore uses it correctly: photons per second per
grain = (Jste/h nu) x sigma_abs.

### 2. What getGrainEmission does with it

    photFlux =  grid%Jste(cellP,ifreq)/(hcRyd*nuArray(ifreq))
    photFlux = photFlux*fourPi
    Qa = XSecArray(dustAbsXsecP(global_isp,ai)+ifreq-1)/(1.e-8*grainRadius(ai)**2)
    getGrainEmission = getGrainEmission+Yhat*photFlux*Qa

`XSecArray` holds sigma_abs = Q_abs pi a^2 (ph_mod:1401), so dividing by a^2
gives **pi Q_abs**, not Q_abs. Together with the second `fourPi` the emission
term carries a spurious **4 pi x pi = 4 pi^2 = 39.478**.

`getGrainRecombination` returns `n <v> eta`. The rate at which electrons reach
a sphere is n<v>/4 x 4 pi a^2 = n<v> pi a^2, so n<v> is exactly the collection
rate per unit geometric cross section - correct, and in the convention the
emission term should have been written in.

### 3. Measured on the converged model

At the potential `runs/d289-pn150k-wd01` actually converged to, with both
sides recomputed in correct units from `mocGrain` (absorbed photons per unit
grain area = slot 4 / slot 6, electrons = x slot 2) and from n_e, T_e:

| r [pc] | T [K] | n_e | V_g [V] | emission | collection | collection/emission |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.20 | 87.4 | 0.822 | 4.340 | 7.10e7 | 2.76e9 | **38.8** |
| 0.25 | 33.9 | 0.311 | 4.135 | 4.51e7 | 1.59e9 | **35.3** |
| 0.30 | 30.6 | 0.302 | 3.444 | 3.65e7 | 1.36e9 | **37.1** |
| 0.40 | 28.0 | 0.294 | 2.288 | 2.42e7 | 9.18e8 | **37.9** |
| 0.50 | 25.8 | 0.291 | 1.465 | 1.56e7 | 6.06e8 | **38.7** |
| 0.60 | 23.8 | 0.288 | 0.894 | 9.81e6 | 3.82e8 | **38.9** |

Flat at 35-39 across a factor 7 in field strength and 3 in temperature,
against 4 pi^2 = 39.478. The residual few percent is the ion collection term,
which is left out of the check and is suppressed but not zero at V_g > 0.

The code is therefore converging to the potential at which the TRUE
photoemission is about 39x below the TRUE electron collection. A grain that
should sit near neutral is driven positive until the Coulomb factor
`Yhat = Yn (1 - V_g/(nu - nu_0))` has thrown away 97% of the photoelectrons.

### 4. What this explains

  - **D-288's over-charging.** 0.9-4.8 V against Cloudy's 0.4-1.5.
  - **Why D-289's yield change did almost nothing.** Halving the yield moves
    the balance point by a factor two inside a balance that is wrong by forty;
    the potential falls a little and the heating recovers 8%.
  - It is the efficiency half of O-02 (1.7-4.8x), and it is a units defect
    rather than a modelling choice, so it is not a question of which reference
    to prefer.

### 5. Not yet done

  - **Not fixed.** The fix is to drop the second `fourPi` and divide the cross
    section by `Pi*1.e-8*grainRadius**2`, so that `getGrainEmission` returns
    Y Q_abs N per unit geometric cross section, matching
    `getGrainRecombination`. That is a one-place change, but it moves every
    grain potential in every model, so it wants its own run and its own entry.
  - The effect on the heating is NOT predictable from the 39x alone: the
    Coulomb barrier will open, and the equilibrium will move to wherever
    emission and collection now cross. Measure it.
  - D-289's `<E>` and `<Y>` and the dust temperature are all downstream of the
    potential and will move too.
  - The field half (D-287, discarded Lya) is untouched by this.

### 6. Fixed, and measured

`getGrainEmission` now returns `Y Q_abs N` per unit geometric cross section:
the second `fourPi` dropped, and the cross section divided by
`Pi*1.e-8*grainRadius**2` so it is Q_abs rather than pi Q_abs.
`MOCASSIN_GRAINQ=legacy` restores the defect, so every result recorded before
this entry stays reproducible. All four flavours build.
`runs/d290-pn150k-grainq`: 11 iterations, 89.6%, 2 h 42 min, clean exit, 0%
ion or Te balance failures in any iteration.

Over the PDR (A_V > 0.3), against the two runs before it:

| | D-288 Baldwin | D-289 WD01 | **D-290 WD01, fixed** | Cloudy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V_g [V] | 2.594 | 1.607 | **0.059** | 0.41-1.43 |
| <Y> | 0.0705 | 0.0371 | 0.0318 | |
| <E> [eV] | 1.63 | 2.58 | **3.31** | |
| PE heating | 3.61e-26 | 3.91e-26 | **6.84e-26** | |
| T_gas [K] | 23.9-29.3 | 23.6-30.3 | **24.6-47.3** | 42-67 |

and depth by depth:

| r [pc] | V_g D-289 | V_g D-290 | V_g Cloudy | T D-289 | T D-290 | T Cloudy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.13 | +0.22 | **-2.00** | **-1.15** | 10025 | 9953 | 9797 |
| 0.20 | 4.34 | 0.38 | 1.00 | 87 | **123** | 117 |
| 0.30 | 3.44 | 0.26 | 1.35 | 31 | **52** | 63 |
| 0.40 | 2.29 | 0.11 | 0.78 | 28 | 38 | 57 |
| 0.60 | 0.89 | 0.03 | 0.41 | 24 | 25 | 44 |

Three things worth stating separately:

  - **The sign now agrees in the ionized gas.** MOCASSIN's grains were +1.05 V
    at 0.13 pc where Cloudy's are -1.15; they are now -2.00. Electron
    collisional charging wins there in both codes, as it should. That is a
    qualitative check the defect was hiding, and not something the fix was
    tuned to produce.
  - **The conversion efficiency deficit is gone.** Heating per absorbed erg is
    0.78, 0.57, 0.74, 1.01, 1.40 of Cloudy's at r = 0.2-0.6 pc, against
    1.7-4.8x low in D-289. MOCASSIN's is now almost flat at 1.41-1.49% where
    Cloudy's varies 0.84-1.97%, because MOCASSIN's grains are near neutral
    everywhere and have no charging suppression left to vary with depth.
  - **What remains of O-02 is the field**, 3.06-3.54x, and nothing else. The
    residual under-charging is consistent with it: a field 3x low gives a
    charging parameter 3x low, so the potential should sit below Cloudy's
    until the Lya is restored.

### 7. What this cost

Not everything improved, and the fix stays regardless:

  - Convergence 91.9% at iteration 9 (D-289) -> 89.6% at iteration 11, using
    every iteration allowed and never reaching the 90% target. The
    temperatures now have much further to move, so this is expected rather
    than alarming, but the model is harder to converge than it was.
  - Hbeta 2.737 -> 2.669e34 against Cloudy's 2.78, i.e. 0.98 -> 0.96.
  - H2 at A_V 0.20 rises from 18 to 58 cm^-3 against Cloudy's 0.015, and the
    H/H2 crossing moves from A_V 0.269 to 0.261 against Cloudy's 0.368 -
    slightly the wrong way, in a hotter PDR where it should have gone the
    other. Not understood; not investigated.
  - He2+ front 0.0828 -> 0.0855 pc against Cloudy's 0.0880, which is better.
  - Dust temperature essentially unmoved.

## D-291 - What the two references do with Lya, and what MOCASSIN does (2026-09-19)

Hektor, after D-290 landed: "lets work on the discarded Lya", then "how does
3DPDR handles this?". This entry is what the measurements say before any code
is written. Nothing has been implemented.

### 1. Cloudy's PDR field is two thirds lines - measured, not inferred

D-287 argued from the Lya *luminosity* (3.0x the stellar FUV band) that the
missing field must be Lya. That was an inference. `save ionizing continuum
every zone` decomposes the local field per bin into incident / OTS / outward
line / outward continuum, and `runs/d290-cloudy-field` measures it directly.
Over the whole PDR, 6-13.6 eV:

| source | share |
|---|---|
| outward lines | 66.4% |
| outward continuum | 24.7% |
| attenuated stellar | 8.8% |
| on-the-spot | 0.1% |

The non-line fraction is **33.5%**, and D-287 measured MOCASSIN's field at
29-39% of Cloudy's. Those agree, which is a far stronger confirmation than the
luminosity argument: what MOCASSIN is missing is exactly the line channel.

Per line, at A_V 0.54:

| line | share of the whole field |
|---|---|
| H I 1216 (Lya) | 46.1% |
| C III] 1909 | 8.4% |
| He II 1640 | 6.3% |
| C IV 1548/51 | 1.9% |
| C II 1335 | 0.4% |

### 2. But Cloudy's Lya should not be there

`rt_continuum.cpp` attenuates the outward line flux by
`AttenuationDilutionFactor = opac.ExpZone[i]*DilutionHere`, and
`opac.ExpZone[i] = sexp(opac.opacity_abs[i]*radius.drad/2.*...)` - the
**continuum** opacity. Once a line photon is in the outward beam Cloudy
propagates it as if it were a continuum photon at that wavelength, with no
re-absorption in the line.

The data show it: H I holds 46.3%, 46.1% and 46.0% of the field at A_V 0.22,
0.54 and 0.70. A share that is flat to three digits over half a magnitude of
extinction is the signature of a component attenuated by exactly the same
opacity as the continuum it is being compared with.

Physically, at A_V 0.54 the H I column is 1.2e21 cm^-2 and the Lya line-centre
cross-section ~6e-14 cm^2, so tau(Lya) ~ 1e8. Lya entering neutral gas is
resonantly scattered and destroyed by dust within a very thin layer at the
ionization front. It cannot be 46% of the field at A_V 0.54.

**So reproducing Cloudy's deep-PDR field would be tuning to a reference's
approximation**, which the project rule forbids. The defensible statement is
that Lya deposits its energy AT the front, not through the PDR.

### 3. D-287's account of the MOCASSIN side needs correcting

D-287 said MOCASSIN "discards every diffuse line packet at creation, so Lya
never enters Jste". The first clause is true and the conclusion is true, but
they are not connected: **Lya was never in MOCASSIN's line channel to begin
with.** `linePDF` is built over `iup = 3,15 / ilow = 2,min(8,iup-1)` for H I
and `iup = 3,30 / ilow = 2,min(16,iup-1)` for He II, and `totalLines =
normRec + normFor` sums exactly the same set. The Lyman series is excluded by
construction, in both the PDF and its normalisation - consistently, so there
is no energy-accounting error either.

What MOCASSIN discards is therefore the **optically thin** lines: the Balmer
and higher H series, the He I and He II recombination lines, and every
forbidden and intercombination line. In Cloudy's decomposition that family is
C III] 1909 + He II 1640 + C IV + C II ~ **17% of the PDR field**, and those
do legitimately stream and are dust-attenuated.

### 4. 3D-PDR does not address this at all

  - **The FUV field is a boundary condition.** `UVfield.F90`:
    `rad_surface = Gext(1)/nrays`, then
    `UVfield = sum_j rad_surface(j)*EXP(-AV(j)*UV_fac)`. External, isotropic,
    dust-attenuated along each HEALPix ray. There is no internal source, and
    3D-PDR does not model an ionized region, so Lya has nowhere to come from.
  - **Internally generated photons exist only as chemistry rates.** The
    cosmic-ray-induced secondary photon field (Prasad-Tarafdar) is present as
    15 `CRPHOT` reactions in the reduced network, at
    `ALPHA*ZETALOCAL*(T/300)^BETA*GAMMA/(1-OMEGA)`. It photodissociates
    molecules and never enters `UV_FIELD`, so it never reaches the
    photoelectric heating, which runs on `HABING_FIELD = 1.68*UV_FIELD`.
  - **X-ray induced Lya is declared and disabled:** `130 RATE(I)=0.0D0` for
    `XRLYA`, and the same for `XRPHOT`.

### 5. Where that leaves it

Neither reference can settle this. Cloudy transports Lya into the PDR without
line re-absorption; 3D-PDR has no Lya at all. MOCASSIN-PDR is in a position
neither is in - it models the ionized region and the PDR in one calculation,
with 3D transfer and an existing resonance-line escape-probability routine
(`setResLineEscapeProb`, 64 directions per cell, dust destruction against the
line opacity) - so it can put Lya where it is actually destroyed rather than
copy either shortcut.

Options, none taken yet:

  1. **Transport the optically thin lines.** Correct regardless of the Lya
     question, worth ~17% of the field (field factor 3.0 -> ~2.0). Needs a
     line-index -> frequency-bin map in `linePDF` order, which does not exist;
     `getNu2(linePDF)` returns a line index and `linePackets` is indexed the
     same way.
  2. **Deposit Lya at the front** through `fEscapeResPhotons`. Physically the
     right thing and the one place MOCASSIN can beat both references. It will
     heat a thin layer near the front and will NOT warm the deep PDR.
  3. Neither, and record the deep-PDR field difference as a divergence from
     Cloudy caused by Cloudy's line transport.

### 6. Not known

  - How much of the front's heating Lya actually supplies here has not been
    estimated; only that its luminosity is 3.0x the stellar FUV band.
  - Whether Cloudy's escape probabilities let Lya into the outward beam at all
    behind the front, or whether the 46% is emitted closer in and then
    streams, has not been separated.
  - Nothing has been measured on hiipdr.

## D-292 - The thin lines transported, and the PDR destroyed (2026-09-19)

Hektor: "proceed with 1, then 3, then we re evaluate option 2" - D-291's
option 1 being to transport the optically thin diffuse lines, which MOCASSIN
creates as packets and throws away, and which D-291 measured at ~17% of
Cloudy's PDR FUV field.

### 1. The change

`setLineNuP` builds `lineNuP(1:nLines)`, the frequency bin of every line in
`linePDF`'s exact order:

  - H I and He II recombination lines from the Rydberg formula, the latter at
    Z = 2 - no data needed, and exact;
  - He I from column 4 of `HeIrecLines.dat`, which is the wavelength in A and
    was simply never read;
  - forbidden and intercombination lines from `equilibrium`'s optional `wav`
    argument, which already existed and was never used. The wavelengths are
    atomic data, so one call per ion at a nominal 1e4 K tabulates them.

All **419 of 419** lines map. `newPhotonPacket` then emits the packet at that
frequency with `lgLine = .false.`, so `pathSegment` transports it, instead of
setting `nuP = 0` and letting `energyPacketRun` drop it.

### 2. Three pre-existing defects, and D-158's segfault explained

None of this could run until three older defects were fixed. D-158 recorded
that MOCASSIN's debug mode "segfaults on an array sized before nLines is
known" and could not say why. It is all three of these together:

  - **`linePackets` and `linePDF` were allocated with `nLines = 0`.**
    `initCartesianGrid` sizes them with `nLines`, and `nLines` is computed by
    `makeElements`, which `mocassin.f90` called *after* the grid. Both arrays
    were `(0:nCells, 1:0)`. `makeElements` now runs before the grid - the same
    ordering the D-022 comment three lines above already established for the
    PDR network.
  - **`nLines` counted 20 He I lines.** `HeIrecLines.dat` holds 34 per
    density, `linePDF` writes 34, `normRec` sums 34 and `outputGas` applies
    the extinction curve to 34. The counter's `9 + 11` was the only place that
    said otherwise, so the PDF overran its own array by 14 elements per cell.
    nLines is now 419, not 405.
  - **`linePDF`'s MPI reduction was gated on `lgDebug`.** Each rank fills only
    the cells it owns, so a packet emitted anywhere else sampled an all-zero
    PDF and `getNu2` ran off the end.

These are kept regardless of what happens to the line transport: they are
correct independently, and they make the debug path usable for the first time.

### 3. What it did: the PDR does not form

`runs/d292-pn150k-lines`, killed at iteration 3, against `runs/d290-pn150k-
grainq` at the same point:

| | D-290 | D-292 |
|---|---|---|
| mean Te | 301.8 K | **7576 K** |
| hot cells | 5.13% | **100.00%** |
| f_mol | 0.9105 | **0.0000** |
| CO per H | 3.66e-28 | 2.04e-36 |

Optically thin forbidden and recombination lines cannot heat a PDR to 7600 K.
`f_mol = 0` says the H2 is being photodissociated outright, so the sub-Lyman
field became enormous. This is a defect in the change, not a result, and the
switch now defaults off.

### 4. Two hypotheses tested, both insufficient

  - **Stray ionizing photons.** Short-wavelength transitions among the upper
    levels of highly charged ions could in principle land above 1 Ryd and
    ionize hydrogen. Instrumented and measured: **0 of 419 lines** map at or
    above 1 Ryd. Refuted.
  - **A mis-normalised `totalLines`.** It is the probability that a diffuse
    packet is a line, formed as `totalLines/(normHI + normHeI + normHeII +
    totalLines)`, and the line sums (`normRec + normFor`, the forbidden part
    already scaled by 1.9865e9) do not obviously share units with the
    continuum sums (`diffuse_scale*widFlx*emissionHI` summed over bins).
    Because every line packet was discarded before, this number never had to
    be right. Probed: **P(line) = 0.298**, four cells, identical. That is a
    plausible share and would raise the delivered diffuse field by 1/(1-0.3)
    = 1.43x, not the ~25x the temperatures imply. Not the explanation.

Also measured, from the model's own `lineFlux.out`, to size the physical
budget independently of the packet machinery: MOCASSIN's 315 He II
recombination lines carry 4.59 Hbeta in total, of which **3.52 Hbeta falls in
912-1930 A = 0.70 x the stellar FUV band luminosity**, and 0.79 Hbeta in the
912-1108 A Lyman-Werner band. He II 1640 alone is 2.09 Hbeta. So the line
emission is real and substantial - it should roughly double the PDR's FUV
field - but it is not 25x, and it is not fictitious.

### 5. What is left to test

Untested hypothesis, and the one that now fits best: **a diffuse packet is the
re-emission of an absorbed packet, not a draw on a luminosity budget.**
Killing line packets was therefore a sink of ~30% *per absorption event* on
the entire radiation field, not a one-off loss of the line channel. Removing
it lets a packet survive repeated absorb-and-re-emit cycles, and the energy
density can rise far more than the 1.43x the single-event arithmetic suggests.
If so the fix is not to restore the sink but to stop line photons being
re-absorbed by gas at all: below 1 Ryd hydrogen is transparent and dust should
be the only absorber, so a 1640 A photon should stream until a grain takes it.

Not yet done: measure the FUV field directly with transport on and off - the
number that would settle this - which needs `pdrFUV.out` from a completed run
or a mid-run probe.

### 6. Unchanged by any of this

Lya is still untreated, and D-291's account of it stands: Cloudy's deep-PDR
Lya is an artifact of attenuating outward line flux by continuum opacity
alone, and 3D-PDR has none. Option 2 remains parked.

### 7. '150 kK PN Against Cloudy' rebuilt on D-290 (option 3)

The page is rebuilt from `runs/d290-pn150k-grainq`, all four figures
regenerated and every number recomputed. The photoelectric section is
rewritten around what the week actually established:

  - the charge balance was out by 4 pi^2, and fixing it closed the conversion
    efficiency half - 0.57-1.40 of Cloudy's where it had been 1.7-4.8x low -
    and warmed the PDR from 24-30 to 25-47 K against Cloudy's 42-67;
  - the field half, 3.0-3.5x, is all that remains;
  - **and Cloudy's field is not the target.** The page now states that 66% of
    Cloudy's PDR FUV field is outward lines, that Lya is 46 of those points,
    and that Cloudy attenuates outward line flux by continuum opacity alone -
    with the flat 46.3/46.1/46.0% at A_V 0.22/0.54/0.70 given as the evidence,
    and tau(Lya) ~ 1e8 as the reason it cannot be real.

The two checks the fix was not tuned to produce are on the page as well: the
grain charge now agrees with Cloudy in SIGN in the ionized gas, and
MOCASSIN's grains end up slightly less charged than Cloudy's, which is what a
field still 3x low should give.

The photoelectric figure now contrasts the fixed run against the unfixed one
and Cloudy, so panel (b) shows the 4.4 V peak collapsing to near zero while
panel (a) is unmoved - the field is untouched by anything done to the grains.

## D-293 - Sizing the Lya deposition before implementing it (2026-09-19)

Option 2 of D-291 - deposit Lya where it is actually destroyed, using the
escape-probability machinery already in the tree - is the only route left to
O-02's remaining factor. Before spending a run on it, three numbers decide
whether it is worth building: how much energy, over what depth, and whether
this grid can resolve the answer. `tools/d293_lya.py`, everything from
`runs/d290-pn150k-grainq`'s own structure.

### 1. How much

L(Lya) from the model's own recombinations, Case B with 0.68 Lya photons per
recombination:

    L(Lya)          8.26e35 erg/s   = 31 x Hbeta
    Case B expects  23 x Hbeta      -> this estimate is good to about 30%
    Cloudy, same model, intrinsic   4.03e35 erg/s = 14.5 x Hbeta

Cloudy's is *below* the Case B ratio, which is consistent with some of its Lya
already being destroyed before the intrinsic tally. Either way Lya is several
times the stellar FUV band:

    Lya flux at the front       0.375 erg cm^-2 s^-1 = 235 Habing
    stellar FUV at the front    0.061                =  38 Habing
    ratio                                               6.2

### 2. Over what depth

Lya entering neutral gas random-walks and is destroyed by dust. The standard
criterion for essentially complete absorption in a dusty medium is
`(a tau_0)^(1/3) tau_a >~ 1`, with `a` the Voigt parameter and tau_0, tau_a
the line-centre and dust-absorption optical depths from the front. Just past
the front this model has T = 193 K and n(H0) = 922, giving sigma_0 = 4.3e-13
cm^2 and a = 3.4e-3; the dust absorption cross-section is 5.0e-22 cm^2 per H.

| A_V past the front | tau_0 | tau_a | (a tau_0)^1/3 tau_a |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.005 | 5.8e6 | 0.0069 | 0.19 |
| 0.010 | 1.2e7 | 0.0138 | 0.47 |
| 0.015 | 1.8e7 | 0.0207 | 0.81 |
| **0.020** | 2.3e7 | 0.0276 | **1.18** |
| 0.100 | 1.2e8 | 0.138 | 10.1 |

**Lya is destroyed within A_V 0.020 of the front** - 27 times shallower than
the A_V 0.54 at which Cloudy still reports it as 46% of the FUV field. The
criterion scales as N^(4/3), so being wrong by a factor 10 moves the depth
only 10^(3/4) = 5.6x, to A_V 0.11 - still nowhere near 0.54. **D-291's
conclusion is robust to an order of magnitude.**

### 3. And whether the grid can see it

    heating in that layer   6.9e-21 erg s^-1 per H  (nearly all into grains)
    into the gas at 1.5%    9.9e-23 erg s^-1 per H
    the model has there     6.3e-25                 -> a factor 157

    41^3 cell               0.0152 pc = A_V 0.0171
    deposition layer        A_V 0.020 = 1.17 cells

So the physics is real and very large - 157x the local photoelectric heating -
and it lands in **one cell**. Implementing option 2 on this grid would put
that energy into the first PDR cell and let the cell size, not the physics,
set the temperature there. Worse for the purpose: the deep PDR, A_V 0.3-0.7,
where O-02's remaining factor actually lives, receives **nothing**.

### 4. What this means for O-02

  - **Option 2 will not close the remaining factor.** It heats a layer the
    deep PDR does not see, and it would need a grid refined near the front -
    a much larger change than the transfer itself - before its answer meant
    anything.
  - It is still worth doing eventually, for the front and for the dust
    temperature there, but as a physics improvement rather than as a route to
    O-02.
  - **The remaining 3.0-3.5x in the FUV field is therefore not Lya.** With Lya
    excluded by depth and the thin lines worth ~17% (D-291) and currently
    broken (D-292), what is left of O-02 no longer has an identified cause,
    and the honest position is that a large part of Cloudy's deep-PDR field is
    its own line-transport artifact rather than something MOCASSIN is missing.

### 5. MOCASSIN's own formula says the same, more strongly

Section 2 used a textbook scaling. MOCASSIN has its own answer, in
`setResLineEscapeProb` - Kwan & Krolik (1981) direction escape probabilities
over 125 directions, then Harrington, Cohen & Hess (1984) eq A5 for dust
destruction:

    fEsc = 1 / (1 + 2 k_d dx / (k_l Pbar))

with `k_d` the dust absorption opacity at the line and `k_l = sigma_0 n(H0)`.
The routine is gated behind `resLinesTransfer` and is never called in any run,
so the formula was evaluated offline on this run's radial structure, with the
125 directions reduced to two streams - inward to the star and outward to the
edge. That is the split that matters here: inward the gas is ionized and
nearly transparent to Lya, outward it is not.

| r [pc] | n(H0) | T [K] | tau_in | tau_out | fEsc | destroyed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.05 | 1.3 | 15052 | 3.4e3 | 2.4e8 | 0.276 | **72%** |
| 0.10 | 11.9 | 11991 | 4.2e4 | 2.4e8 | 0.245 | **76%** |
| 0.12 | 248 | 10843 | 4.4e5 | 2.4e8 | 0.551 | 45% |
| 0.16 | 989 | 2104 | 7.6e6 | 2.3e8 | 0.484 | 52% |
| 0.30 | 255 | 50 | 1.6e8 | 8.1e7 | 0.179 | 82% |
| 0.50 | 56 | 29 | 2.2e8 | 1.8e7 | 0.172 | 83% |

**Three quarters of the Lya produced in the ionized gas is destroyed by dust
in the ionized gas.** It does not merely fail to reach A_V 0.54 - it largely
fails to reach the front at all. Whatever Cloudy is streaming through its PDR,
MOCASSIN's own physics says it should not be there, and this is now two
independent routes to that conclusion.

A side prediction worth recording: the ~6e35 erg/s that implies is dust
heating in the ionized gas that the model does not currently have, since the
packets are never emitted. D-283 already found MOCASSIN's dust 8-25% *warmer*
than Cloudy's. Implementing Lya deposition should therefore make the dust
temperature agreement **worse**, not better - which is a real test of it, and
a reason not to expect it to improve the comparison overall.

### 6. Not known

  - The escape probability above is for LOCALLY PRODUCED Lya, and the two
    streams stand in for 125 directions. It is not a transfer calculation of
    Lya propagating from the ionized gas into the PDR, which is the quantity
    option 2 would actually need.
  - L(Lya) is good to ~30%, and the Case B branching and alpha_B fit here are
    approximations.
  - Nothing has been measured on hiipdr, whose front conditions differ.

## D-294 - D-292 blamed the wrong change (2026-09-20)

D-292 concluded that transporting the optically thin diffuse lines destroys
the PDR. It does not. The change that does is moving `makeElements` before the
grid, which D-292 made in the same commit as one of three "pre-existing defect
fixes" and never tested on its own.

This is a process failure before it is a physics one: several things were
changed at once and the result was attributed to the headline one. The control
cost 30 minutes and should have been run first.

### 1. The control

`runs/d294-probe-off` - the D-292 code with `MOCASSIN_LINES` off - against
`runs/d292-pn150k-lines` with it on, and `runs/d290-pn150k-grainq` from before
D-292, all at the first PDR pass:

| run | transport | code | mean Te | hot | f_mol |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d290 | off | pre-D-292 | 301.8 K | 5.13% | 0.9105 |
| d292 | **on** | D-292 | 7576 K | 100% | 0.0000 |
| d294-probe-off | **off** | D-292 | 7578 K | 100% | 0.0000 |

Transport off and on give the same destroyed PDR to three digits.

### 2. The bisect

`runs/d294-probe-bisect` is the same binary with `makeElements` put back where
it was, and nothing else changed. It restores the PDR:

| | mean Te | hot | f_mol |
|---|---|---|---|
| d290 (pre-D-292) | 301.8 K | 5.13% | 0.9105 |
| **bisect** | **304.6 K** | **5.21%** | **0.9100** |
| d294-probe-off | 7578 K | 100% | 0.0000 |

and it tracks the old convergence from the first iterations, where the D-292
code had already left it:

    iteration          1        2           3
    d290 (pre-D-292)   0.00     0.00        0.170%
    bisect             0.00     0.00        0.161%
    d294-probe-off     0.00     0.187%      4.561%

These first iterations are deterministic in this fixture - every earlier run
