But `grains_mie.cpp:565` says precisely what Cloudy does with them:

    for( gd.cAxis=0; gd.cAxis < gd.nAxes; gd.cAxis++ ) {
        mie_cs_size_distr(wavlen,&sd,&gd,mie_cs,&cs_abs,&cs_sct,&cosb,&Error);
        acs_abs[p][i] += cs_abs*gd.wt[gd.cAxis];
        acs_sct[p][i] += cs_sct*gd.wt[gd.cAxis];
        a1g[p][i]     += cs_sct*(1.-cosb)*gd.wt[gd.cAxis];
    }

Mie per axis, **cross sections** summed with the axis weights, one opacity per
bin, one temperature. The in-code average is therefore not just the defensible
reading of Draine's 1/3-2/3 rule - it is what the reference computes, which is
a much stronger footing than a citation.

Two things worth keeping from that check. Cloudy's `a1g` is weighted by
`cs_sct`, which is independently the D-280 correction MOCASSIN already made to
its own `<g>`. And the two codes' graphite is **not the same data**: Cloudy's
is Martin & Rouleau (1991), rho = 2.26, work function 0.3235 Ryd, sublimation
1750 K; MOCASSIN's is Draine & Lee, rho = 2.2, 0.323 Ryd, 2200 K. Different
sources, and D-305 measured the resulting opacities agreeing to 0.4% on
N_H/A_V, so this has never mattered - but it should be on the record rather
than assumed away.

### And the Q-file route is blocked

D-309 floated `dustData/Car_90.cat`, Draine's tabulated graphite Q, as the
obvious single-species candidate. It cannot be used as things stand:
`setGrainYield` is called at `ph_mod.f90:1253`, **inside the `'nk'` branch
only**. A `'Q'` species would get `grainYield = 0` and lose its photoelectric
heating entirely - which, in a PDR model whose gas temperature is set by grain
photoelectric heating, would have been a spectacular way to break everything
quietly. The WD01 yield needs Im(m) and a Q file does not carry it, so the
branch cannot simply be extended either.

Recorded because the file is sitting there looking usable.

### The implementation

In `makeDustXsec`, immediately after the species loop closes. At that point
`Cabs`/`Csca` still hold **Q** - `pi a^2` is applied further down - so
averaging them is averaging the cross sections, exactly as Cloudy does.

The average is written back into every entry of the component rather than
collapsing the arrays to one. That is deliberate: `nSpecies`, `dustComPoint`,
`grainAbun`, `grainLabel`, `rho`, `TdustSublime`, `grainVn`, `MsurfAtom`,
`grainYield` and `grainCarb` are all sized and indexed on the original species
count, and collapsing would mean re-indexing every one of them. With identical
optics in each slot, each solves the same temperature and the abundance
weighted mean over species becomes the correct single temperature, with no
re-indexing at all. `gCos` is weighted by `Csca`, per D-280.

**Whether the entries are axes of one material is asked of the data, not of a
keyword** - identical density, work function, surface-atom mass, sublimation
temperature and size range. This is a definition, not a gate: silicate plus
graphite differ in all five and correctly remain two species at two
temperatures, which is right, because they are genuinely two materials.

### Verified

On the D-308 fixture, seconds rather than hours:

    before:  nS=1  44.79 K     nS=2  22.45 K     mean 37.35 K
    after:   nS=1  26.8480 K   nS=2  26.8480 K

and D-309's independent solve for a grain with the averaged cross section in
that same cell predicted **26.76 K** - 0.3%.

All four flavours build. `runs/d310-orient` is running the production model to
re-measure against Cloudy. D-309 predicts reported/Cloudy moving from
1.26-1.30 to about 0.93-0.95.

## D-311 - declared, not inferred (2026-09-22)

D-310 made the principal axes of graphite share one temperature, which is
right. It decided *which* entries were axes by inference, which is not.

The objection that prompted this: distinct species must not be given one
temperature. Correct, and the inference could have done exactly that.

### Why the inference was unsafe

D-310 treated a component's entries as axes of one material when they shared
density, work function, surface-atom mass, sublimation temperature and size
range. Checking `dustData/`:

    grph1-dl.nk        grph1-dl    2200. 2.2  0.323 12.004
    grph2-dl.nk        gr2_dl_hgk  2200. 2.2  0.323 12.004   <- genuinely axes
    amC-zb1.nk         CamC-zb1    2200. 1.85 0.323 12.004
    amC-zb2.nk         CamC-zb1    2200. 1.85 0.323 12.004   <- NOT axes
    amC-zb3.nk         CamC-zb1    2200. 1.85 0.323 12.004   <- NOT axes
    crSil.nk           ScrSil      1400. 3.6  0.588 20.077
    astroSilD2003.nk   Ssil_dl     1400. 3.6  0.588 20.077   <- NOT axes

The three Zubko amorphous carbons are three different laboratory samples with
different optical constants and byte-identical header constants. So are the
two silicates. A model listing `amC-zb1` and `amC-zb2` together would have had
them averaged into one grain at one temperature, silently, with nothing in the
output to say so.

That is the same class of mistake as the one being fixed - deciding two things
are one material without being told - and it would have been harder to find,
because unlike the graphite case there would have been no reference
disagreement pointing at it.

### The replacement

The species-count line may now carry the word `axes`:

    2 axes
    'dustData/grph2-dl.nk' 0.6667 0.005 0.25
    'dustData/grph1-dl.nk' 0.3333 0.005 0.25

Without it, nothing is averaged and every entry keeps its own temperature -
the pre-D-310 behaviour, correct for real mixtures. A bare integer still
parses, so no existing species file changes meaning.

This is how Cloudy states it too. `graphite.rfi` carries

    2        # number of principal axes
    1 2      # relative weights of axes

declared, not deduced from the material constants that sit in the same file.

### Declared is not the same as true

A declaration can be wrong, so it is checked. If `axes` is declared and any
entry differs from the first in density, work function, surface-atom mass,
sublimation temperature or size range, the run stops:

    ! makeDustXsec: component 1 declares `axes`, but entry 2 differs from
    ! entry 1 in density, work function, surface-atom mass, sublimation
    ! temperature or size range.
    ! makeDustXsec: those are not axes of one material. Remove `axes` if they
    ! are distinct species.

The same test that was wrong as an inference is right as a validation: it
cannot prove entries are axes, but it can refuse ones that certainly are not.

### What declares it

Only `benchmarks/pdr/pn150k` and the 150 kK model. `benchmarks/test_Problem`
(astronomical silicate 0.98 plus PAH 0.02, over different size ranges) and
every single-species fixture are untouched, and keep a temperature per
species. That is not a concession - it is required. Silicate and graphite in
the same nebula really do sit at different temperatures, and so do two
different amorphous carbons.

### The averaging itself is unchanged

Still in `makeDustXsec` immediately after the species loop, where `Cabs` and
`Csca` still hold Q because `pi a^2` is applied further down - so averaging
them is averaging cross sections, which is what `grains_mie.cpp` does per
axis. `gCos` is weighted by `Csca` per D-280. The average is written back into
every entry rather than collapsing the arrays, so each entry solves the same
temperature and the abundance-weighted mean MOCASSIN already takes becomes
that single temperature, with no re-indexing of `nSpecies`, `dustComPoint`,
`grainAbun`, `grainLabel`, `rho`, `TdustSublime`, `grainVn`, `MsurfAtom`,
`grainYield` or `grainCarb`.

### Two self-inflicted build breaks, recorded because both were avoidable

Editing `ph_mod.f90` while a `make` was running clobbered that build - the
compiler read a half-written file. And a Python-to-Fortran string replacement
emitted `their own.""` for a closing quote, giving "Unterminated character
constant beginning at (1)". Neither reached a run, because the four-flavour
rule catches exactly this, but both cost a build cycle. Do not edit sources
under a running build, and check generated Fortran string literals.

## D-312 - the tag moves to the species line, and a manual (2026-09-22)

D-310 put the axis declaration on the species *count* line (`2 axes`). The
objection: that is confusing, and the files listed in `dust_species.dat`
should be correct per species. Both fair, and the counter-proposal - a flag on
a species saying it should be averaged with others carrying the same flag - is
better than what it replaces.

It reads on the line it governs. It allows several independent axis sets, and
untagged species, to coexist in one component. And it needs no state outside
the record.

    <optical-data file> <abundance> [<amin/um> <amax/um>] [axes:<name>]

    'dustData/grph2-dl.nk' 0.6667 0.005 0.25 axes:graphite
    'dustData/grph1-dl.nk' 0.3333 0.005 0.25 axes:graphite

Backward compatible: every existing species file parses unchanged and keeps a
temperature per species.

### The part of the instruction that could not be followed

The instruction was also that the user should supply properly averaged n,k
files, with MOCASSIN doing nothing. That cannot be done correctly, and saying
so is more useful than implementing it.

Draine's 1/3-2/3 rule averages **cross sections**. Mie is non-linear in
(n, k), so there is no single (n, k) whose Q equals
`(2/3)Q(eps_perp) + (1/3)Q(eps_par)` across size and wavelength. Measured on
this project's own graphite files, naive averaged-n,k divided by the correct
cross-section average:

    a [um]   0.1 um   0.55 um   10 um   100 um
    0.005     0.96     1.21     2.14     0.09
    0.0354    1.00     1.16     2.11     0.09
    0.25      1.02     1.01     1.44     0.12

Fine in the ultraviolet, where the grain absorbs. **8 to 11 times too little
at 100 um, where it radiates** - which would push the dust temperature far
above the truth, a larger error than the 1.3x the change exists to remove.
Averaging the dielectric function instead is no better: 0.07 to 1.77 over the
same points.

So the average must happen after Mie, inside the code. What the data can
declare - and all it needs to declare - is *which files are axes of one
grain*. That is exactly what the tag does.

### The Q-file route, documented as a trap

`setGrainYield` is called only from the `nk` branch of `makeDustXsec`, because
the WD01 yield needs Im(m) and a `Q` file does not carry it. A `Q` species
therefore gets `grainYield = 0` and loses its photoelectric heating silently.
In a PDR model, where the gas temperature is set by that term, this would be a
spectacular and quiet failure. It is now written down in `doc/dust.md` rather
than left as a discovery.

### Verified both ways, in seconds

On the 5^3 fixture, same cell, same size:

    tagged     axes:graphite     26.6857 K and 26.6857 K
    untagged   (no tag)          44.4391 K and 22.2739 K

D-309's independent solve for a grain with the averaged cross section in that
cell gave 26.76 K, so the tagged path is right to 0.3%. The untagged path
reproduces the old behaviour exactly, with no averaging message - **that is
the regression that matters**, because distinct species must keep distinct
temperatures, and a mechanism that can merge them must be provably inert when
not asked for.

Validation kept from D-311: a group needs at least two members, and members
must share density, work function, surface-atom mass and sublimation
temperature or the run stops. The size-range test was dropped, because
`amin`/`amax` are per-species fields that a user might legitimately set
differently while still describing one material's axes; the material constants
are the real test.

### doc/dust.md

The first usage manual in this project. Covers the three input files and the
MdMg-to-Ndust conversion; the `axes:` tag with the measurement above, so the
next person meets the reason and not just the rule; the `nk` and `Q` formats
including the clamping of out-of-range optical constants and the yield
warning; what MOCASSIN actually computes for opacity, A_V, grain temperature,
photoelectric heating and stochastic heating; the diagnostics
(`MOCASSIN_DUSTPROBE`, `dustGrid.out`, the two audit tools); and the known
limitations from D-305 - graphite-only R_V = 4.57, undepleted carbon counted
twice, H2 absent from gas-grain coupling, and the size-parameter cap at 100.

## D-313 - the average moves out of the code (2026-09-22)

D-312's per-species `axes:` tag was rejected in turn: a keyword that couples
species together is confusing, and the files listed in `dust_species.dat`
should each simply be correct on their own. The in-code averaging is reverted.

Instead the orientation average is done once, outside MOCASSIN, and the model
is given one species.

    ~/miniforge3/envs/astro/bin/python tools/mkqfile.py \
        --out dustData/grph-avg.cat --label grph-avg \
        --sizes input/dust_sizes.dat \
        dustData/grph2-dl.nk:0.6667 dustData/grph1-dl.nk:0.3333

    1
    'dustData/grph-avg.cat' 1.0000 0.005 0.25

`mkqfile.py` runs Mie per axis and sums the cross sections with the axis
weights - Draine's rule, and what `grains_mie.cpp` does - then writes a
Draine-style Q table on the model's own radii.

### The Q path had never been run

Two bugs, both fatal, found in the first minute of trying to use it.

**Double allocation.** The `Q` branch allocates `CTsca` and `CTabs`, which are
already allocated before the component loop. The second `allocate` returns a
non-zero status, which the guard immediately below turns into a `stop`. The
`nk` branch has the identical two lines commented out. Any Q-file model died
at startup with "error allocation memory for array".

**No photoelectric yield.** `setGrainYield` is called only from the `nk`
branch (`ph_mod.f90:1253`), because the WD01 yield needs Im(m) and a standard
Q file does not carry it. A `Q` species therefore ran with `grainYield = 0` -
no photoelectric heating at all, silently. In a PDR model, whose gas
temperature is set by that term, this would have been both fatal and
invisible.

Fixed by an optional sixth column carrying Im(m), which `mkqfile.py` writes.
**If the column is absent and photoelectric heating is on, MOCASSIN now
stops** and says so, rather than running without a yield.

A third, smaller trap: the header reader assumed exactly two comment lines.
My own generated file had four, and the failure surfaced as "Bad integer for
item 1 in list input" pointing at the *data block*. It now skips lines until
NRAD parses.

### Verified three ways

**The file against direct Mie.** Reading the generated table back and
comparing to Mie of the 2/3-1/3 mixture at the same radius:

    E [Ryd]    25    10     5    2.7   1.5   1.0   0.5   0.1  0.01  0.001
    Qabs      1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.001 1.000 1.000 1.000
    Qsca      1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 1.000 0.999 1.001 1.000 1.001 1.000

and the 150 kK blackbody-weighted absorbed energy, `integral Q_abs B dnu`,
ratio **1.0000**.

**MOCASSIN's own arrays against the nk path**, same size, same frequency bin,
which removes any question of where the probe samples:

    ai = 18, 0.44 Ryd
      nk path   0.6667 x 7.86287e-11 + 0.3333 x 3.47691e-11 = 6.4012e-11
      Q path                                                   6.3933e-11   (0.12%)
    ai = 18, 2.0 Ryd
      nk path   0.6667 x 2.82018e-11 + 0.3333 x 3.53606e-11 = 3.0588e-11
      Q path                                                   3.0588e-11   (exact)

**The internal balance**, with `dustAbsIntegral` bracketing `emInt(iT)` as it
must.

### Two generator pitfalls, found by measurement

Both are now defaults and both are documented, because both cost real time.

  - **The table must span the model grid.** `nuMin = 1.001e-5 Ryd` is 9104 um.
    A first version stopped at 1000 um, and everything longward was clamped -
    exactly where a 26 K grain radiates. Worth 0.7 K on its own.
  - **Radii need enough digits.** MOCASSIN locates the model radius in the
    table and interpolates, so a 3-significant-figure radius puts every size
    slightly off its own grid point. The generator now writes 8.

### doc/dust.md

Rewritten for this route: `mkqfile.py`, the two pitfalls above, the `Q`
format including the Im(m) column and the history of the two bugs, and the
measurement showing why a pre-averaged *n,k* file cannot work at all - it
gives 0.09 to 0.12 of the correct Q at 100 um, which would be a larger error
than the one being fixed.

## D-314 - regression, and what the implementation is validated to do (2026-09-22)

Two things asked for: a regression check, since significant parts of the code
changed; and then, in preference to re-running the heavy fixtures, a first
validated version of the PDR implementation with its limitations known.

### The change surface is narrow, which shapes the test

The diff touches five source files, but functionally it is:

  * `lgLineTransfer` defaults `.true.` instead of `.false.` (D-307);
  * the `MOCASSIN_LINES` read moved from `makeDustXsec` to `readInput` and
    inverted, so it can only switch transport *off*;
  * the `Q` branch of `makeDustXsec` fixed - double allocation, missing
    photoelectric yield, rigid header parse (D-313);
  * probes in `dust_mod` and `update_mod`, inert unless
    `MOCASSIN_DUSTPROBE=on`.

So the decisive question is not "did many things change" but "with the default
put back, is anything different?" If nothing is, every historical result stays
valid for the lines-off configuration and only the new default needs
re-measuring.

### Two findings about the harness, before any result

**MOCASSIN is not bitwise reproducible.** Two runs of the same binary, same
input, same rank count give different output. So a regression cannot be read
against zero; it has to be read against the run-to-run scatter, which means
running the reference twice. `tools/regress_cmp.py` does that, and reports
aggregate medians alongside per-cell statistics because the per-cell scatter
is dominated by cells where the quantity is near zero.

**A short fixture does not exercise the PDR.** The first attempt used 2
iterations. With `pdrStartIter 4` the chemistry never engaged, A_V was
identically zero, and the check would have validated nothing while appearing
to pass. Raised to 6.

### The result

5^3 fixture, nk-path dust, 6 iterations, `-np 2`. Baseline is b83e0e0, the
commit this cycle started from.

    quantity     noise floor    new vs base    verdict
    T_gas          36.71%         18.49%       within
    n_e             4.03%          2.35%       within
    T_dust          0.08%          0.11%       marginal
    A_V             0.00%          0.00%       exact
    J(FUV)          0.73%          0.03%       within
    J(.01-.44)      0.83%          0.35%       within
    J(<.01Ryd)      1.49%          0.68%       within
    totalLines      8.15%          1.00%       within

**The inertness test passes.** A_V matching to zero in both comparisons is the
strongest single line: it comes straight from `absOpac + scaOpac`, so the dust
cross-section and opacity chain is provably untouched by D-307 and D-313.

T_dust at 0.11% against a 0.08% floor is nominally outside, but a floor from a
single pair is not a bound, and 0.03 percentage points on a quantity every
other measure agrees on is not a signal.

### The 18% that was not a signal

Median T_gas came out 18.5% higher on the new binary, which against the
*2-iteration* floor of 0.03% looked alarming and was reported as a flag. The
control retired it: the **same binary** run twice at 6 iterations swings
median T_gas by **36.7%**.

That is worth keeping as a limitation of the harness rather than a footnote.
A 5^3 grid is 125 cells, the median runs over a bimodal ionized/neutral
population, and once the PDR engages the statistic is hopeless. **This fixture
cannot regress the gas temperature** - the very quantity the coupling exists
to produce. Three fixes, in increasing cost: take the median over PDR cells
only, raise the photon count, use the configured grids.

### Two register items closed

From the converged production run (`runs/d302-trim-on`):

  * **O-11**, ion balance not reached in 16-18% of cells (D-267): now **0%**.
  * **O-17**, convergence plateau below the 90% target: now **90.4%**.

### doc/pdr-status.md

The consolidation asked for. It states what is validated, with every number
traceable to a DEVLOG entry: conservation and internal consistency (the
thermal residual at 7e-4..7e-3, the grain diagnostic closing at 1.00, the
emission table at 1.000, the radiative-equilibrium solve reproduced
independently to 0.9988); agreement with Cloudy on quantities both codes own
(N_H/A_V to 0.4%, dust mass per H to 0.7%, Mie against Draine to 0.1-1%,
x(C+) to 1.001-1.006, photoelectric efficiency 0.66-1.10); and the [C II]
thermostat verified inside MOCASSIN alone at 0.986-1.014.

Then eighteen limitations, L-1..L-18, graded by their effect on a published
number rather than by how untidy they are. The two that matter most:

  * **L-1** - every result predating D-307 was computed on a model that
    *deleted* about 60% of the PDR's bolometric flux, including the current
    `150 kK PN Against Cloudy` artifact;
  * **L-2** - the dust temperature was an arithmetic mean of two crystal
    axes' temperatures rather than a temperature, worth 26-30% against
    Cloudy, fixed in D-313 with the re-measurement in flight.

And a section that exists because absence of a reported problem is not
evidence: **what has not been checked** - the slabs, `ifront`, `hiipdr`, the
warm start beyond compiling, the 1D PDR flavour beyond compiling, any model
reaching A_V > 0.7, and Cloudy's own charging exponent, which D-304's
correction currently borrows from MOCASSIN.

### What this cycle does not yet support

A claim that the implementation is validated *in general*. It is validated on
one model, at one density, over A_V 0 to 0.68, against one code, with the
run-to-run scatter now measured for the first time but no published comparison
yet carrying an error bar. That is a defensible first version, and the
limitations register is the honest part of it.

## D-315 - the dust fix, measured (2026-09-22)

`runs/d313-qavg`: 11 iterations, 89.58% converged, 2h00m, one species read
from `dustData/grph-avg.cat` - the orientation average built outside the code
by `tools/mkqfile.py`.

### Convergence is undisturbed

    iter      pre-fix (d302-trim-on)    dust fixed (d313-qavg)
     3              0.2%                      0.175%
     4              1.2%                      1.204%
     7              1.2%                      1.385%
     8             68.7%                     65.08%
     9             88.6%                     88.61%
    11             90.4%                     89.58%

Iteration 9 landing on 88.61% against 88.6% is the evidence that a change
confined to the grain temperature left the ionization and thermal solve alone.
The characteristic shape is intact: flat through iterations 1-7 while the
front is still moving, then the jump once the structure locks in.

### The result

Dust temperature against Cloudy, number-weighted over the size distribution
on both sides:

    A_V     before (D-306)    after (D-315)
    0.20        1.289             0.906
    0.30        1.304             0.902
    0.50        1.272             0.873
    0.65        1.256             0.869

**L-2 is closed.** The 26-30% excess is gone.

D-309 predicted 0.951/0.952/0.931/0.929, by recovering each cell's absorbed
energy from the old run's own balance and re-solving it for the averaged cross
section. The measured values sit about 5% below that, and the reason is that
the prediction held the field fixed while the run does not: cooler grains
re-emit less infrared, which lowers the diffuse field, which cools them
slightly further. A small positive feedback, in the expected direction.

### The residual has the opposite sign, and an explanation

Re-measuring the bolometric field on this run gives 1.35, 1.30, 1.28, 1.23,
1.16 of Cloudy's at A_V 0.15 to 0.65 - **unchanged from the pre-fix run**. So
MOCASSIN holds *more* total radiative energy at every depth, and its grains
are nonetheless cooler.

The band shares say why. At A_V 0.30:

                     >1 Ryd    FUV    0.01-0.44    <0.01 Ryd
    MOCASSIN          0.000   0.107     0.504        0.389
    Cloudy            0.000   0.255     0.362        0.383

Cloudy carries **2.4 times MOCASSIN's share in the FUV**, where C_abs is
orders of magnitude larger than in the infrared, while MOCASSIN carries more
in the broad 0.01-0.44 Ryd band. A smaller field concentrated where grains
actually absorb heats them more than a larger field that is not.

So O-02's dust half is closed as a defect and reopened, far smaller, as a
question about **where each code puts its reprocessed energy in frequency**.
That is the same diffuse-transport difference D-307 measured from the other
side - MOCASSIN's angle-integrated 4 pi J exceeding the undimmed stellar flux,
which a 1D outward-only treatment will not reproduce. Registered as L-19.

### Tooling

`tools/d305_tdust.py` assumed the two-file graphite layout and indexed
`dust_species.dat` positionally; it now reads whatever species count the file
declares. `doc/pdr-status.md` L-2 updated from predicted to measured.

## D-316 - the warm start, exercised at last (2026-09-22)

L-14 recorded that `mocassinWarm` had never been run - it compiled, and that
was the whole of its coverage. Running it found it broken three ways, and one
of the three was caused by D-307 in this same cycle.

### First, the fixtures could not run at all

Every PDR benchmark input carried

    pdrDataDir "/home/hmonteiro/software/mocassin-pdr/dataPDR"

a directory left behind by a rename. Nine fixtures - `hiipdr` and its five
variants, `v1slab`, `v2slab`, `ifront` - plus `pn150k`, none of which could
start. Repointed at the repository's own `dataPDR`.

This is worth sitting with. The slab checks and O-09 have been deferred for
several cycles as "expensive"; they were not expensive, they were impossible,
and nothing surfaced that because nobody ran them.

### The warm start, defect by defect

**(1) `linePDF` unallocated - and D-307 caused it.** `mocassinWarm` never
called `setLineNuP` or `allocLineArrays`. That was dormant for as long as line
transport was off by default, because `linePDF` was then needed only under
`lgDebug`. Making transport the default turned the omission into an immediate
stop:

    ! setDiffusePDF: linePDF unallocated with line transport on -
    !   allocLineArrays did not run (D-294). nLines = 16892

Fixed by mirroring `mocassin.f90`: `setLineNuP()` to settle `nLinesPDF`, then
`allocLineArrays` per grid.

**This is a regression D-314's suite could not have caught**, because that
suite runs `mocassin`. A four-flavour *build* rule does not exercise a
flavour, and this is the second time in two cycles that the difference has
mattered.

**(2) `resetGrid` was called twice.** The driver had

    do iGrid = 1, nGrids
       call resetGrid(grid3D(iGrid))
    end do
    call resetGrid(grid3D)

`resetGrid`'s dummy is `grid(maxGrids)` - an array. The loop form passes a
scalar, which by sequence association aliases the same storage, so the grid
was reset and every checkpoint file re-read twice. Reduced to the single call
on the array that it always meant.

**(3) Still broken: a segfault in `updateCell`.** With both fixes in, the
warm start now reads the checkpoint, rebuilds the cross sections, runs the
Monte Carlo transfer to completion, writes the SED - "Total energy radiated
out of the nebula 3.785 of 3.828" - and then dies at the first cell of
`updateCell`, immediately after the D-116 recombination audit.

The obvious candidate is `seedPDR`, which `mocassin.f90` calls after
`fillGrid` and the warm driver does not call at all. **It is the wrong fix.**
`seedPDR` assigns

    grid(iG)%pdrAbun(iCell,:) = seed

overwriting the chemistry with its initial values - which would destroy
exactly the state a warm start exists to resume. So what the warm path is
missing is whatever allocation or linkage `seedPDR` does *incidentally*, not
the seeding, and separating the two has not been done.

### Status

L-14 moves from "not exercised" to "broken, two of three defects fixed, the
third localised to `updateCell` with the obvious fix ruled out". The flavour
still does not run. That is a worse-sounding status than before and a better
one to have: the previous entry recorded an unknown, this one records a
bounded problem.

All four flavours still compile, which is precisely the point - compiling was
never evidence.

## D-317 - the warm start runs (2026-09-22)

D-316 left `mocassinWarm` with two defects fixed and a segfault in
`updateCell`. This finishes it. Five defects in total, all found by running
the flavour once, and the root cause turned out to be a workaround for
another one.

### Naming the segfault

The optimised build gave bare addresses. A `CO=bounds` build - which the
Makefile already provides, from D-124 - named it in one run:

    At line 2888 of file source/update_mod.f90
    Fortran runtime error: Index '2' of dimension 1 of array 'grid%aveff'
    above upper bound of 0

    #3 ionbalance      at update_mod.f90:2888
    #4 iteratet        at update_mod.f90:889
    #5 updatecell      at update_mod.f90:301
    #6 iteratemc       at iteration_mod.f90:1260
    #8 mocassinwarm    at mocassinWarm.f90:117

`AVeff` with an upper bound of zero is the zeroed descriptor of an
**unallocated** allocatable, not a mis-sized one.

### Why it was unallocated

`readInput()` is commented out at `mocassinWarm.f90:48`. `lgPDR` defaults
`.false.` in `common_mod.f90:772`. Nothing else assigns it. So for the whole
warm start `lgPDR` was false, `resetGrid`'s `if (lgPDR)` guard skipped **every**
PDR allocation - `AVeff`, `pdrZone`, `chiFUV`, all of them - and `updateCell`
still entered its PDR code, because that is gated by the *compile-time*
`#ifdef PDR`, not the runtime flag.

That `resetGrid` expects `readInput` to have run is not a guess. At
`grid_mod.f90:3590`:

    if (lgPDR) then
       if (.not.lgPDRrestart) then
          print*, "! resetGrid: this run has pdr enabled but output/grid3.out"
          print*, "!   carries no PDR state - the checkpoint predates PDR support."

`lgPDR` comes from the input and `lgPDRrestart` from the checkpoint; the
second corroborates the first and was never meant to supply it.

### Why it had been commented out

Restoring `call readInput()` made that obvious: the run died at
`grid_mod.f90:3402`, `allocate(TStellar(nStars))`, because `readInput` had
already allocated it. `resetGrid` re-allocates module-level state that
`readInput` owns.

So the two halves of `grid_mod.f90` disagree about the warm start's contract -
one assumes `readInput` ran, the other assumes it did not - and commenting out
the call resolved the contradiction in the direction that ran, at the cost of
silently disabling the PDR resume. **A workaround for an allocation clash
disabled a whole subsystem, and nothing caught it because the flavour was
never run.**

### The real fix

Guard the overlap rather than skip the input. Nine star arrays:

    TStellar, LStar, nPhotons, starPosition, contShape,
    contShapeIn, spID, tStep, deltaE

and six further module arrays found by listing every non-`grid%` allocation in
`resetGrid` and checking which `readInput` also allocates:

    abundanceFile, dustSpeciesFile, nSpeciesPart,
    viewPointPhi, viewPointTheta, lgDataAvailable

all now `if (.not. allocated(...)) allocate(...)`. The values are still read
from the checkpoint, so the resumed run uses the checkpoint's state; only the
re-allocation is suppressed. `ionDenUsed`, `dl` and `p` are genuinely local to
`resetGrid` and were left alone.

### It works

Exit 0, no runtime errors, iteration 5 at **100% converged**, energy closing
at 3.784 of 3.828e36 erg/s. And it resumed rather than restarted:

    quantity            checkpoint   after warm
    median A_V            0.44643      0.44643     identical
    cells with A_V > 0         53           53
    PDR cells                  50           50
    f_mol                  0.3975       0.1475
    median n(CO)          9.34e-06     4.48e-06

A_V identical to five figures over the same cells is the checkpoint's dust
state restored exactly. The chemistry moves because the warm run iterates on
to full convergence from a 6-iteration snapshot - and the values are
intermediate, not the network's initial seeds, which is what re-seeding would
have produced.

### What is NOT verified

**Warm against cold.** Resuming and converging has not been compared with
running cold to convergence on the same model. That is the test that would
license using the warm start for production, and it has not been done. L-14
moves from "broken" to "runs; equivalence unverified", which is progress and
not a clean bill.

### The pattern, for the third time

A module flag consumed before anything sets it, silently taking its default:

  * D-299: `lgElementOn` read by `makeElements` before `setComposition` set
    it, killing all CEL cooling.
  * D-316/D-317: `lgPDR` read by `resetGrid` before anything set it,
    skipping every PDR allocation.

Both were found only because something downstream broke loudly. A systematic
sweep of module logicals for read-before-set is worth more than a fourth
one-off, and is now on the register.

## D-319 - the published PN figures were drawn on hiipdr's axis (2026-09-22)

The user, looking at the artifact: *"the plots of the 150K PN artifact have Av
axis going to 3 but the model ends before that around Av ~ 0.8 so fix the plot
range"*.

Correct, and the cause is a constant that could not track the model.

### What was there

`tools/d260_roellig.py` carried two module constants:

    XLIM   = (0.04, 3.2)
    RTICKS = None   ->  [1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15] pc

Both are hiipdr's. D-283 generalised the script for pn150k and added
`--xlim`/`--rticks`, but deliberately left hiipdr's values as the defaults so
that hiipdr's own figures would come out pixel-identical. pn150k was then
plotted without either flag, and inherited them.

The measured extents:

                     model A_V        model r        Cloudy A_V
    pn150k        0.0084 - 0.6706   0.015 - 0.61 pc   0.00015 - 0.679
    hiipdr        0.0518 - 2.999    1.12  - 19.4 pc   0.00015 - 2.95

So the pn150k panels ran to A_V 3.2 on a model that stops at 0.67. Roughly a
third of the panel width was blank, and the curves were compressed into the
left two thirds.

### Two further consequences, neither visible as an error

**The inside labels below A_V 0.04 were simply not drawn.** `draw()` places
them at `xa * A_front / 0.4659`, scaling hiipdr's hand-picked positions by the
front ratio. pn150k's front is at 0.1287, a factor 0.276, so `He^2+` (0.065 ->
0.018), `e-` (0.07 -> 0.019), `He+` and `C^2+` (0.1 -> 0.028) all landed left
of x0 = 0.04. Matplotlib clips them without complaint.

**The top radius axis was worse than empty.** Every default tick (1 to 15 pc)
lies outside pn150k's 0.015-0.61 pc span, and the placement is

    top.xaxis.set_major_locator(FixedLocator(np.interp(rt, rc[ok], avr[ok])))

`np.interp` clamps outside its range, so all six ticks resolved to the same
A_V and piled up at the right-hand edge - an axis labelled 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15
with every label on top of the last. The caption said *"the upper axis is
MOCASSIN's radius"*, and it was not.

### The fix

By the project rule - no hardcoded value standing in for something the model
already knows - the range is not a setting, it is a property of the run. Both
are now derived when not given:

    def auto_xlim(run, ref):
        lo = float(np.nanmin(run['AV'])) / 1.05
        hi = max(float(np.nanmax(run['AV'])),
                 float(np.nanmax(ref['AV']))) * 1.05
        return lo, hi

The lower edge follows the **model**, not the reference. Cloudy's first zone
is far thinner than a MOCASSIN cell - 0.00015 against 0.0084 here, a factor 57
- and letting it set the lower edge would give two and a half decades of
single-code curve before the comparison begins. The upper edge takes whichever
code reaches deeper, so neither is truncated.

`auto_rticks` picks the round distances from a fixed ladder that fall inside
the model's own radial extent, so the top axis is never extrapolated. Fewer
than three rungs falls back to five geometric points rather than drawing a
bare axis.

`--xlim` and `--rticks` still override, and the tool now prints what it
resolved and whether it was given or derived:

      A_V axis 0.007984-0.713 (from the run); r ticks [0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2,
      0.5] pc (from the run)

### What it does to each fixture

    fixture     A_V axis: was        now              r ticks: was       now
    pn150k      0.04 - 3.2           0.0080 - 0.713   1-15 (all clamped) 0.02-0.5
    hiipdr      0.04 - 3.2           0.0493 - 3.149   1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15 2, 3, 5, 10, 15

hiipdr moves by under 2% at either end - the hand-picked constants were good
ones for the fixture they were picked on - but it now loses the 1 pc tick,
which sat below the model's 1.12 pc inner radius and was therefore
extrapolated. D-283's "pixel-identical" property is given up deliberately:
it was protecting a number that should never have been a number.

### The page

'150 kK PN Against Cloudy' rebuilt (v9). The figures were generated with **no
flags at all**, so the page now reproduces from the run:

    tools/d260_roellig.py runs/d313-qavg runs/d302-cloudy-trim-rad/150k \
        <outdir> --cloudy

One number in the prose was also wrong: the lede said the medians were taken
over "464 in the ionized gas, 34 920 in the PDR". The run's own zone column
gives 450 and 34 934 - the same total, so the same run, but a stale split.
Corrected.

### What this was not

Not a physics change. No run was repeated, no quantity recomputed; the curves
are the same data on an axis that fits them. It is worth recording only
because the defect was invisible from inside the code - the figures were
produced without error, and the missing labels and collapsed radius axis would
have been read as properties of the model rather than of the plot.

## D-320 - hiipdr on the current code, and three more fixture constants (2026-09-22)

L-1 recorded that any artifact built on a lines-off run rests on a model that
does not conserve energy (D-306). The pn150k page was rebuilt at D-315; the
hiipdr page predated the line-transport result entirely. `runs/d316-hiipdr`
was launched to close the rest of it and finished at 16:33.

### The run

31^3, 22 iterations, 1 h 40 min, **73.75% converged**, 0% ion-balance
failures, 0% Te-balance failures. The convergence plateaus early and stays
there - 73.7, 74.3, 74.7, 73.8 over iterations 19-22 - so it is a plateau and
not a trend that was cut short. It is well below pn150k's 89.6% on the same
code, and the reason is the geometry: hiipdr is a 31^3 grid over 19 pc, and
the H II region spans about five cells. That was already noted at D-264 and is
not new.

### The result reverses the published sign

Against `runs/d277-cloudy`, the same reference the v7 page used:

    quantity                     D-282 (published)    D-316 (now)
    H+ front, x = 1/2            3.82-3.85 / 3.77     3.795 / 3.765 pc
    H/H2, 2n(H2) = n(H)          A_V 1.20 / 1.09      1.168 / 1.090
    C+ = C                       A_V 2.27 / 2.95      2.242 / 2.950
    H II gas T                   -                    9027 / 9274 K

and the PDR temperature, which is the headline:

    A_V     MOCASSIN    Cloudy     was published as
    0.70       72.4       48.0
    1.00       61.9       49.3     "PDR T_gas 22-26 vs 29-49 K"
    1.50       39.2       43.9
    2.00       23.2       28.7
    3.00       11.2       12.7

**MOCASSIN is no longer 2x too cold.** It is 1.3-1.5x too warm from the front
to A_V ~1.4, crosses over there, and is modestly cold below that. The added
energy is D-292's line transport, on by default since D-307 - the same change
that moved pn150k, and in the same direction.

This is worth stating plainly: the published claim "the PDR is about twice too
cold", which has been the standing description of this coupling since D-264,
was measured on a configuration that deletes ~60% of the bolometric flux in
the PDR. It was a real number about a model that was losing energy.

### Dust

Number-weighted over the size distribution on both sides, at five depths
across hiipdr's own PDR:

    A_V     MOCASSIN   Cloudy   ratio
    0.73      31.54     33.70   0.936
    1.03      25.80     27.49   0.939
    1.45      19.89     21.97   0.906
    2.05      15.50     16.96   0.914
    2.91      12.96     13.54   0.957

0.906-0.957, against pn150k's 0.869-0.906 (D-315). Same sign, same shape,
smaller residual - consistent with L-19, where the remaining difference is
*where in frequency* each code puts its reprocessed energy rather than how
much of it there is.

### Deep carbon: unchanged

Past A_V 2.3, C+ 0.21-0.38 of Cloudy's, n_e 0.28-0.45x, CO 50-100x high. The
same numbers D-282 reported. The line-transport energy did not touch it, which
is what one would expect of a region whose carbon balance is set by the
cosmic-ray rate and the chemistry rather than by the FUV field.

### Three more fixture constants, found by running the tools twice

D-319 fixed the plot range because it was hiipdr's constant applied to
pn150k. Pointing the same tools at hiipdr found three more of exactly the same
kind, in the opposite direction - pn150k's constants applied to hiipdr:

**1. The Cloudy grain size span.** `GRAINS = (0.005, 0.25, -3.5)` is pn150k's
law. hiipdr's Cloudy model uses 0.01-0.30. The constant sets the weights that
turn Cloudy's ten per-bin temperatures into one number, so hiipdr's reference
dust was being weighted over the wrong span. D-306 worked out how to measure
this from Cloudy's own output and then wrote the answer down as a constant;
the method needs no constant. `cloudy_grain_ratio` reads the `<D/G>` line from
the "Average Grain Properties" block, checks the bin-to-bin ratio really is
constant (it is, to 2e-4 relative), and inverts

    R = (amax/amin)^((slope+4)/nb)

It recovers **29.987** for hiipdr and **50.002** for pn150k, against the true
30 and 50. Only the ratio reaches the weights - they are normalised - so no
absolute size is needed. Effect on hiipdr's reference temperature: 0.11%. On
pn150k's: none, which is the regression check.

**2. `d305_tdust.py` could not read hiipdr at all.** `dust_sizes.dat` carries
a trailing ` slope (p): -3.5` line in hiipdr's fixture and not in pn150k's,
and the reader was `np.loadtxt(..., skiprows=2)`. It now reads the count the
header declares. This is the D-313 NRAD defect again: a reader that assumes a
file ends where this fixture's file happens to end.

**3. Its sample depths were pn150k's.** `for av in (0.20, 0.30, 0.50, 0.65)` -
sensible for a PDR ending at A_V 0.67, and on hiipdr it sampled the first
fifth and stopped. Now five depths spread over the model's own PDR, with
explicit depths still accepted on the command line.

### Regression

pn150k re-measured with all three changes in place gives 0.906 / 0.902 /
0.873 / 0.869 at A_V 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.50 / 0.65 - D-315's published values to
the last digit - and its figures move by at most 1.2e-5 points, which is
several orders below a pixel. The pn150k page was not republished for it.

### The pattern

Four constants now, in two tools, all found the same way: run the tool on a
second fixture. Each was correct for the fixture it was written on, and each
became silently wrong on the other. None produced an error; two produced
figures that looked entirely reasonable. The general form is that **a tool
that has only ever been run on one model cannot distinguish a property of that
model from a property of the physics**, and neither can its author.

## D-321 - L-1 closed, and a published headline withdrawn (2026-09-22)

D-320 measured hiipdr on the current code. This entry is what was done with
the measurement.

### The page

'hiipdr Against Cloudy' rebuilt as v10 from `runs/d316-hiipdr`. What changed:

  - **The headline.** Four KPI tiles, the "Selected depths" table, the
    ionized-gas table and two of the "what agrees" bullets all carried the
    lines-off numbers. All recomputed.
  - **A withdrawal, written as one.** The page had said "the PDR is about
    twice too cold" since D-264, and that reading is now wrong. The new
    section does not quietly replace the number; it states that the old one
    was measured on a model losing ~60% of its bolometric flux in the PDR,
    gives 0.384 against 1.215, and says what replaces it - a disagreement
    about the *shape* of the temperature profile rather than its level.
  - **The ionized gas**, which nobody was looking at, moved by the same
    mechanism and in the same direction: 4-8% below Cloudy before, 7-12%
    above now.
  - **The issue register** on that page is a D-267 snapshot from 2026-09-14
    and had drifted badly - its O-02 row still asserted the claim the page
    now withdraws. Rather than silently editing thirty rows, the register is
    labelled as a snapshot, the four rows this work actually moved (O-02,
    O-08, O-23, O-30) are restated, and it points at `doc/pdr-status.md` as
    the maintained register.

### The control worth naming

The ionization structure did not move. Front 3.795 against 3.765 pc, H/H2
crossing 1.168 against 1.090, C+ = C 2.242 against 2.950, deep C+ 0.21-0.38x,
n_e 0.28-0.45x, CO 50-100x - every one of these is within its own run-to-run
scatter of what D-282 published on the lines-off run.

That is the useful part of a result that changes a headline. The added energy
is real and it moved what it should move: the gas and dust temperatures, which
are energy balances. It did not move the front, which is set by the Lyman
continuum and the geometry, and it did not move the deep carbon, which is set
by the cosmic-ray rate and the chemistry. An energy change that had moved
everything would have been a reason to distrust it.

### L-1 closed

Both artifacts that rested on lines-off runs are rebuilt:
`150 kK PN Against Cloudy` on `runs/d313-qavg` (D-315, v9) and
`hiipdr Against Cloudy` on `runs/d316-hiipdr` (v10). Stated narrowly in
`doc/pdr-status.md`: nothing *standing* now rests on a lines-off run, but
conclusions in DEVLOG entries before D-307 still do, and they are marked
where they are quoted rather than rewritten.

### L-21 added

The four constants of D-319 and D-320 are registered as one limitation rather
than four fixed bugs, because the fixing is the smaller half. The risk that
remains is the general one:

> a tool that has only ever been run on one fixture cannot distinguish a
> property of that model from a property of the physics, and neither can its
> author.

Two of the four produced no error and no visibly wrong figure. The test that
found all four was simply running each tool on a second fixture, and
`tools/d196_axis.py` still hardcodes 31^3 and has not had it.

## D-322 - the hiipdr budget: it is not the field (2026-09-22)

D-321 left the successor to O-02 named but not measured: MOCASSIN deposits too
much energy inside A_V 1 and too little beyond 1.5. This decomposes it.

### The reference had to be re-run

`runs/d277-cloudy` saved `.ovr`, `.pdr`, `.gtemp` and `.dens` and nothing else;
the budget needs `.heat`, `.cool`, `.ele_C`, `.gheat` and `.gpot`.
`runs/d322-cloudy-hb` is the same input with five `save` lines added - 700
zones, 3 iterations, 305 s. **Check first:** `.ovr`, `.pdr`, `.dens` and
`.gtemp` come back byte-identical to `runs/d277-cloudy`, so the reference
behind the published figures is unchanged and the new files can be read
against them.

### Cooling is exonerated at every depth, including across the crossover

The [C II] thermostat test predicts T_m from the heating ratio alone:

    A_V     T_c    T_pred   T_m    T_m/T_pred
    0.73   48.3     69.3   71.7      1.035
    0.97   49.1     65.5   62.3      0.952
    1.27   49.2     52.0   48.9      0.940
    1.68   38.1     30.7   30.5      0.994
    2.21   24.1     21.4   19.3      0.904

Within 10% at every gated depth, on **both sides** of the crossover. D-304
established this on pn150k, whose PDR ends at A_V 0.67 and which is therefore
entirely on the warm side; hiipdr reaches 2.9 and crosses. The temperature
disagreement is the heating disagreement, and nothing else.

### And the heating is grain photoelectric, on both sides

    A_V   PE_m       GrnP_c     m/c
    0.73  9.11e-26   5.32e-26   1.71
    0.97  6.79e-26   4.55e-26   1.49
    1.27  3.04e-26   2.95e-26   1.03
    1.68  6.99e-27   1.37e-26   0.51
    2.21  7.11e-28   2.90e-27   0.245

**The ratio crosses 1 at A_V ~ 1.3, which is where T_m/T_c crosses 1.** The
whole of the profile-shape disagreement is in this one term.

### Splitting it: the field is the smaller half

    A_V   G0 m/c   (PE/G0) m/c   product
    0.73   0.81       2.17        1.76
    0.97   0.82       1.81        1.48
    1.27   0.69       1.52        1.05
    1.68   0.59       0.85        0.50
    2.21   0.47       0.52        0.24

Over A_V 0.73 to 2.21, in logs: field -0.54, efficiency -1.43. **The
conversion efficiency carries 72% of the swing and the field 28%.**

This retires the hypothesis D-321 left standing. The FUV attenuation slopes
nearly agree over the warm half - `d ln G0/dA_V` = -3.24 against Cloudy's
-3.13 over A_V 0.7-1.7 - and part only deep, -2.59 against -2.02 over 1.2-2.9.
**O-33's C I-edge excess (-3.83 against -2.65) does not carry over to the
Habing band.** Those are different bands and they behave differently; assuming
otherwise would have been the error.

### What the efficiency loss is not

**Not the grain charge.** MOCASSIN's grain potential is *below* Cloudy's at
every depth - 2.18 V against 2.71 at A_V 0.73, 0.56 against 1.34 at 1.27,
0.017 against 0.122 at 2.21, a ratio falling 0.80 to 0.14. A lower potential
is a lower barrier, which *raises* the yield. If charge were the driver the
efficiency ratio would grow with depth. It falls.

**Not the yield.** MOCASSIN's own `<Y>` rises 0.041 -> 0.081 with depth as the
grain discharges, and saturates. The D-288 identity PE = Nabs x <Y> x <E>
closes to 0.98-1.02 at every depth, so the diagnostic is reading the same term
the solver used.

### What it is

    Nabs/H  falls  1.43e-12 -> 5.92e-15   = 242x     (A_V 0.73 -> 2.21)
    G0      falls      52.5 -> 0.589      =  89x
                                            ratio 2.71

**MOCASSIN's count of absorbed photons above threshold falls 2.7 times faster
with depth than its own Habing-band field.** The band integral and the
photoelectric integral disagree about what is left deep in the cloud, which is
a statement about the *shape* of the spectrum inside the FUV band, not its
magnitude.

That is the same quantity as **L-19**, measured there from the other side:
at A_V 0.30 in the 150 kK model MOCASSIN carries 0.107 of its energy in the
FUV against Cloudy's 0.255, while holding *more* total energy (D-315). One
root, two symptoms - the dust runs cool because too little of the field is
where C_abs is large, and the gas crosses over because too little of it is
where the work function is.

### The deepest point is not physics

At A_V 2.91 MOCASSIN's PE is exactly `0.00e+00`: `<Y>` and `<E>` are both
zero although `Nabs/H` is 1.6e-16. No packet above the work function reached
those cells. That is the Monte Carlo floor of O-01/O-34, and the A_V 2.91 row
should not be read as a physical result in either direction.

### Tooling: a fifth instance of L-21

`d304_budget.py` sampled `(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.65)` -
pn150k's depths again. On hiipdr that covers the first fifth of the PDR and,
worse, **stops short of the crossover the run was made to reach**. Now derived
from the model: two points ahead of the front, six across its own PDR.
Explicit depths still override, and pn150k reproduces D-304's table on its
original eight.

Five constants, four tools. The pattern has not changed and neither has the
test that finds it.

### What this opens

The question is now specific enough to attack: **why does MOCASSIN's FUV band
soften with depth faster than Cloudy's?** Candidates, none measured:

  - the dust albedo and asymmetry across the FUV band - a scattering-dominated
    band attenuates differently from an absorbing one, and D-280 already found
    `g` averaged over area rather than `C_sca` once;
  - 3D diffuse transport against 1D outward-only, which is L-19's own
    hypothesis and would put *more* soft light deep, not less;
  - the frequency resolution of the band in `nbins=600` against Cloudy's
    continuum mesh.

The next measurement is the specific intensity per frequency bin at matched
A_V, both codes, which is a file-reading exercise on runs already on disk.

## D-323 - the optics are not the cause, and a near-miss (2026-09-22)

D-322 ended with a specific question: why does MOCASSIN's FUV band soften with
depth faster than Cloudy's? It listed three candidates and put the optics
first, because it is the cheapest to test and needs no run - if MOCASSIN's
grain cross section rises more steeply across 0.44-1 Ryd than Cloudy's, the
band reddens faster for that reason alone and no transport difference is
needed.

### The test

`tools/d323_fuvshape.py`. MOCASSIN's side is computed from the run's own
`dust_species.dat` and `dust_sizes.dat` with the Mie code of D-305, summed
over the size distribution with the weights `ph_mod.f90` uses. Cloudy's side
is read from the compiled `.opc`, whose `abs_cs_nn` and `sct_cs_nn` blocks are
already cross section per hydrogen per bin; summing its ten bins gives the
whole distribution. Both are therefore per H, which is the only form in which
they are comparable - the codes carry different material densities and
different size grids to reach the same A_V/N_H.

### The answer is no

Normalised at the band's red edge:

    E[Ryd]   C_abs/C_abs(0.44)      albedo
             MOCASSIN   Cloudy    MOC   Cloudy
     0.44      1.000     1.000   0.808  0.810
     0.50      1.988     1.988   0.674  0.676
     0.60      3.969     3.975   0.476  0.478
     0.70      4.809     4.793   0.419  0.421
     0.80      5.282     5.240   0.407  0.410
     0.90      5.692     5.607   0.400  0.404
     1.00      5.775     5.661   0.392  0.397

    d ln C_abs / d ln E   MOCASSIN +1.852   Cloudy +1.828   diff +0.024
    d ln C_ext / d ln E   MOCASSIN +0.730   Cloudy +0.708   diff +0.022

**Shape to 2%, albedo to 1%.** The optics cannot produce a factor 2.7, and are
eliminated.

There is a second result here that was not the point of the exercise. This is
the **first independent check of MOCASSIN's Mie path against another code's
compiled silicate** - D-305 checked it against Draine's tabulated Q, which is
the same source the .nk file comes from. Cloudy compiles `sdraine03.rfi`
through its own Mie and its own size quadrature, and the two agree across the
band to 2%. That is worth more than the negative result it was collected for.

### The near-miss

The first run of this tool weighted the size distribution by `n(a)` and gave

    d ln C_ext / d ln E   MOCASSIN +1.923   Cloudy +0.708   diff +1.214

Over the band's factor 2.27 in energy that is 2.27^1.214 = **2.66**, against
the **2.71** D-322 measured for the photoelectric/energy divergence. A clean
mechanism, the right sign, and a number matching the observation to 2%.

It was wrong. `ph_mod.f90` makeDustXsec builds

    da(ai)          = central difference of the radius grid
    grainWeight(ai) = n(a_i) da_i / sum_j n(a_j) da_j

and the grid is logarithmic, so `da` goes as `a`. Weighting by `n(a)` alone
over-weights the small grains by a factor ~a, and small grains are precisely
what carries the blue end of the band. The error steepened MOCASSIN's slope
and left Cloudy's alone, because Cloudy's came from a file that already had
its own quadrature applied.

Recorded because of how it would have read. The agreement with D-322's
independently measured 2.71 was a coincidence of two errors of similar size,
and it is exactly the kind of coincidence that ends an investigation early. It
was caught by reading the weighting out of `ph_mod.f90` rather than by
disbelieving the number - the number was, if anything, too good.

### Where L-19 now stands

Eliminated: the grain optics (this entry), the grain charge and the yield
(D-322), the cooling (D-322, D-304), the size-distribution weighting (D-306),
stochastic heating (D-306), the crystal-axis average (D-315).

Standing: **3D diffuse transport against 1D outward-only.** It is L-19's own
hypothesis and the only candidate left that can put energy somewhere the
other code cannot. D-306 already measured its signature from the other side -
MOCASSIN's angle-integrated 4 pi J at A_V 0.30 is 1.215x the *undimmed*
stellar flux, which a 1D outward-only treatment cannot produce.

### Next

`runs/d322-cloudy-hb` is re-running with `save last ionizing continuum
... every`, which gives Cloudy's local spectrum per zone. MOCASSIN's side has
no equivalent: `pdrRad.out` holds four band sums per cell and nothing finer,
so a per-bin comparison needs a diagnostic that writes `Jste` over the 37 FUV
bins (384-420) per cell - about 4.5 MB at this grid - and a re-run. That is
the first thing in this cycle that cannot be answered from files already on
disk.

## D-324 - D-322's mechanism corrected: it is the grain charge after all (2026-09-22)

D-323 eliminated the optics and left transport as the only candidate. Getting
Cloudy's per-zone spectrum to test that instead falsified the D-322 claim the
whole line of reasoning rested on.

### What D-322 compared

`update_mod.f90`, the D-288 diagnostic:

    th = max(grainVn(global_ns)+grainPot(global_ns,na), grainVn(global_ns))
    call locate(nuArray,th,thP)
    do ifreq = thP, nbins
       ...
       grnAbs = grnAbs + grnWgt

`grnAbs` integrates from **the work function plus the local grain potential**.
That threshold *moves with depth*: as the grain discharges, the integral
widens. D-322 divided this by `G0`, a fixed 0.44-1 Ryd energy integral, found
the ratio fell 2.71x, and read the whole of it as a difference in the
spectrum's shape. It is mostly the threshold.

### Measured on Cloudy's own spectrum

`runs/d322-cloudy-hb` re-run with `save last ionizing continuum ... every`
(262 MB, its local spectrum in every zone). Computing the same N/G0 ratio from
it three ways, each normalised to its own A_V 0.73:

    threshold used                       fall over A_V 0.73 -> 2.21
    fixed at the work function, 0.5883      4.93x
    moving, Cloudy's own grain potential    1.65x
    moving, MOCASSIN's potential history    2.15x
    -------------------------------------------------
    MOCASSIN, its own moving threshold      2.71x

Two things follow. The threshold motion is worth a factor **3.0** on its own
(4.93 -> 1.65), so it dominates. And the honest like-for-like comparison -
each code on its own moving threshold - is 2.71 against 1.65, while driving
Cloudy with MOCASSIN's threshold history gives 2.15. **The threshold-matched
spectral residual is 1.26x, not 2.7x.**

A 1.26 cannot carry an efficiency swing of 4.2.

### What does carry it

    (PE/G0), relative to its own value at A_V 0.73, by A_V 2.21
      Cloudy    2.75x   (it RISES with depth)
      MOCASSIN  0.66x   (it FALLS)
      ratio     0.24    = the 2.17 -> 0.52 of D-322

Since PE = Nabs x <Y> x <E>, and N/G0 falls 1.65x in Cloudy and 2.71x in
MOCASSIN, the yield-and-energy factor must rise

      Cloudy    ~4.54x   (inferred; its <Y> and <E> are not written separately)
      MOCASSIN   1.94x   (measured: <Y> 0.0405 -> 0.0811, <E> 0.0712 -> 0.0693)

a factor 2.34 between them, and the largest single term in the whole budget.

**That is the grain charge**, which D-322 explicitly ruled out. The argument
there was that MOCASSIN's potential is *below* Cloudy's at every depth, so a
lower barrier should raise its yield and the sign is wrong. That compares the
**level** of the potential when what enters the yield's depth dependence is
the **change** in Coulomb suppression as the grain discharges. The suppression
is `1 - Vg/(hnu - Vn)`, so a grain that starts more charged has more to
recover: Cloudy starts at 2.711 V against MOCASSIN's 2.178 and both end near
zero, and Cloudy gains the larger factor. The sign is right; D-322 read it
backwards.

### What survives D-322 unchanged

  - Cooling exonerated at every depth by the [C II] thermostat test, on both
    sides of the crossover. Independent of all of the above.
  - Heating is grain photoelectric on both sides.
  - PE_m/PE_c crosses 1 at A_V ~ 1.3, which is where T_m/T_c crosses.
  - The split into field (28%) and efficiency (72%), which is arithmetic on
    measured G0 and PE and does not depend on the mechanism.

What is withdrawn is the *mechanism* - "a spectral-shape difference inside the
FUV band" - and with it D-322's claim that this was "the same quantity as
L-19, one root, two symptoms". The dust result (L-19) stands on its own
measurement; the gas result no longer points at it.

### Why this was not caught earlier

D-322 quoted `Nabs/H` from a diagnostic whose docstring says, in the source,
"the photons and the energy absorbed ABOVE THRESHOLD (not the whole FUV
band)". The words were read; the fact that the threshold *moves* was not, and
nothing in the printed table shows it moving. The check that would have caught
it immediately - recomputing the same integral on the reference with the same
threshold convention - is the one D-323 was built to do for the optics and
that this entry finally did for the spectrum.

Two corrections in two entries now, both from the same habit: taking a derived
diagnostic at face value instead of reading what it integrates. D-323's
near-miss was the mirror image - a weighting read out of the source in time.

### Where this leaves the question

The gas-temperature crossover is now: **both codes' grains discharge with
depth and their photoelectric yields recover, and Cloudy's recovers about 2.3x
more because its grains start more charged.** Why the two codes' grain charge
balances differ by that much, at fields that agree to a factor 0.8-0.5, is the
question - and D-290 already found and fixed a 4 pi^2 units defect in exactly
that balance, so it is a place where this code has been wrong before.

`tools/d304_budget.py` already prints `Vg_m` against Cloudy's per-bin range.
The next step is to read the charge balance term by term, not the temperature.

## D-325 - psi, and the hardcoded sticking coefficient (2026-09-22)

The user suggested looking at 3D-PDR's source for clues. It has two, and the
second one reframes the whole question.

### What 3D-PDR has

`source/pdr/heatingfunctions.F90` carries the Weingartner & Draine (2001)
photoelectric heating formula, whose only variables are

    psi = G0 sqrt(T) / x(e)

That is not a fitting variable. It is the ratio of the photoemission rate to
the electron collection rate, so it is what sets the equilibrium grain charge,
and every treatment of this physics is a function of it.

Evaluating WD01's formula directly was a dead end and is recorded as such:
hiipdr's PDR runs at psi ~ 1e6, two decades outside the diffuse-ISM range the
coefficients were fitted in, and both codes sit 30-120x above it. The formula
also assumes PAHs and a 100:1 gas-to-dust ratio that this model does not have.
**The variable is the useful part, not the fit.**

### The reframing

Comparing PE/G0 *at matched psi* separates the photoelectric physics from the
field, temperature and ionisation that feed it:

    A_V      psi_m     PE/G0_m  |    psi_c     PE/G0_c  | ratio at matched psi
    0.73   1.438e+06  1.741e-27 | 1.453e+06  8.274e-28  |  2.087
    0.97   5.866e+05  3.052e-27 | 6.356e+05  1.682e-27  |  1.730
    1.27   2.122e+05  3.895e-27 | 3.088e+05  2.586e-27  |  1.361
    1.68   5.333e+04  3.014e-27 | 9.822e+04  3.523e-27  |  1.043
    2.21   1.271e+04  1.165e-27 | 2.654e+04  2.303e-27  |  0.506

**At matched psi MOCASSIN is always at or above Cloudy - it never crosses.**
The crossover in the raw numbers is not in the photoelectric physics.

What it is: both efficiencies are **peaked** in psi - the grain must discharge
enough to lift the Coulomb barrier, but not so deep that the field has gone -
and the two codes peak at different psi (MOCASSIN near 2e5, Cloudy near 1e5).
MOCASSIN's psi falls **113x** across this range against Cloudy's **55x**,
because its G0 falls 89x against 50x and its temperature falls faster as well,
and both enter psi. So it passes its own peak earlier in A_V and is descending
the far side while Cloudy is still near the top.

**This puts the field back as the driver**, through psi rather than linearly.
D-322's "28% field, 72% efficiency" divided G0 out once and called the
remainder efficiency - but G0 also sets psi, which sets the efficiency. The
split is arithmetic and correct; reading it as *causal* was not.

### The offset, and its name

`update_mod.f90`, `getGrainRecombination`:

    S  =1. ! electron sticking probability
    ...
    S = 1.            ! again, for every ion

Cloudy, `grains.cpp`:

    static const double STICK_ELEC = 0.5;
    static const double STICK_ION  = 1.0;
    gv.bin[nd].StickElecPos = STICK_ELEC*(1.-exp(-AvRadius/elec_esc_length(...)))

The ion values agree. The **electron** sticking does not: MOCASSIN sticks every
electron it collects, Cloudy sticks half. Sticking multiplies the collection
rate, so at the same nominal psi MOCASSIN's grains charge less - which is the
direction and roughly the size of the offset.

Testing it: divide psi by each code's own S and re-interpolate.

    efficiency ratio at matched psi     0.73   0.97   1.27   1.68
    S equal (nominal psi)              2.087  1.730  1.361  1.043   spread 4.13
    each code's own S (1.0 vs 0.5)     1.151  1.164  1.129  1.307   spread 2.58

**Flat to 15% where it drifted by a factor two.** The two codes' photoelectric
physics agrees once the sticking convention is matched.

### Why this is a defect and not a choice

D-289 replaced Baldwin et al. (1991)'s photoelectric yield with Weingartner &
Draine (2001)'s, in the grain charge balance and the gas heating together. It
did not touch the sticking coefficient, which is still Baldwin's 1.0. **Two
halves of one prescription now come from different papers** - WD01's yield
against a collection rate WD01 does not use - which is the project rule about
one reality per quantity, in a place where the two halves multiply.

`tools/d325_psi.py` holds the test.

### A thing not to miscite later

3D-PDR's `calc_reac_rates.F90` also has `STICKING=0.3D0`, twice. That is
**freeze-out** - accretion of neutrals and of singly charged ions onto grain
surfaces - not the charge balance, and it is not evidence about electron
sticking. Recorded because the constant is easy to find and easy to quote for
the wrong quantity.

### Caveats

  - psi is a similarity variable. Dividing it by S is the leading-order way
    sticking enters the collection rate, not a derivation.
  - Cloudy's curve is interpolated log-linearly through five points.
  - The A_V 2.21 column is 0.506 in every row because MOCASSIN's field there
    is approaching its Monte Carlo floor (PE is exactly zero by 2.91). It is
    not evidence for or against any of this.

### Next

Set the electron sticking to WD01's own value, which is what D-289's yield
assumes, and re-run hiipdr. That is a one-line change to
`getGrainRecombination` with a measurable prediction: the PDR temperature
behind the front should fall toward Cloudy's, and the crossover should move
deeper or disappear. It is the first change in this cycle with a prediction
attached before the run.

## D-326 - the sticking fix, and its prediction stated first (2026-09-22)

The change of D-325, written before the run so the prediction cannot be
retrofitted to the result.

### The change

`source/update_mod.f90`, `getGrainRecombination`:

    -  S  =1. ! electron sticking probability
    +  S  = 0.5 * (1. - exp(-grainRadius(ai)/1.e-3))   ! a, l_e both in um

Weingartner & Draine (2001)'s electron sticking, with l_e = 10 A the
zero-energy escape length, which is what Cloudy's `grains.cpp` uses
(`STICK_ELEC*(1.-exp(-AvRadius/elec_esc_length(0.,nd)))`). The function gains
`ai` so it can see the grain size, matching `getGrainEmission(Vg, isp, ai)`
which already took it. Ion sticking is left at 1.0, which is also Cloudy's
value - only the electron term differed.

The exponential is 0.5 to four figures over the 0.01-0.30 um distribution this
fixture uses. It is written out rather than folded to a constant so that a
PAH-sized bin, if one is ever added, gets the right value instead of a
silently wrong one.

### The prediction

Halving the electron collection rate raises the equilibrium grain potential,
which is the same as doubling the effective charging parameter. MOCASSIN's own
measured efficiency-against-psi curve (D-325, `runs/d316-hiipdr`) is

    psi        1.438e6   5.866e5   2.122e5   5.333e4   1.271e4
    PE/G0      1.74e-27  3.05e-27  3.90e-27  3.01e-27  1.16e-27
    A_V           0.73      0.97      1.27      1.68      2.21

It **peaks near psi = 2e5**. Doubling psi moves every depth to the right along
that curve, so the effect changes sign across the peak:

  - **Behind the front** (A_V 0.73-1.27, psi above the peak) the efficiency
    falls. PE should drop by roughly 20-40%, and the gas should cool toward
    Cloudy from its present 72 and 62 K against 48 and 49.
  - **Deep** (A_V 2.21, psi below the peak) doubling psi moves back *toward*
    the peak and the efficiency **rises**, perhaps by a factor ~2. The gas
    should warm toward Cloudy from 19.3 K against 24.1.

So the prediction is not "everything cools". It is that **the profile rotates
about A_V ~ 1.3**: too-warm becomes cooler, too-cold becomes warmer, and the
crossover flattens or disappears. That is a sharper test than a level shift,
because a simple normalisation error could not produce it.

Second-order, and expected to blunt this: cooler gas behind the front lowers
sqrt(T), which lowers psi again and partly undoes the move. The effect should
therefore come out smaller than the curve above suggests.

### What would falsify it

  - The whole profile moving one way, which would mean the sticking is acting
    as a normalisation and the psi picture is wrong.
  - The ionization front, the H/H2 crossing or the deep carbon moving. None of
    them should: this touches the grain charge balance only, and D-320 showed
    those are set by the Lyman continuum, the geometry and the cosmic-ray rate.
  - Dust temperature moving. Grain charge does not enter the grain's radiative
    equilibrium.

### Status

Four flavours build. `runs/d326-stick` launching at 31^3, 22 iterations, the
same fixture and settings as `runs/d316-hiipdr`, so the two are comparable
run-to-run. Result in the next entry.

## D-327 - is Case A still right without Lyman alpha transfer? (2026-09-22)

The user, while the D-326 run was going: *"I was thinking about the Case A fix
on the thermal balance that we made. If we are not doing the transfer of
LyAlpha, is that still correct?"*

**Yes - and the reason is that the two "Lyman" quantities are different
photons.** But checking it properly turned up a real energy sink next door.

### The two photons

`update_mod.f90` takes Case A from Hummer (1994) as `beta_A = beta_B +
beta_1`. `beta` is the **electron kinetic energy** carried off per
recombination, and `beta_1` is the n=1 term. Recombination to n=1 emits a
**Lyman continuum** photon, >= 13.6 eV.

Lyman alpha is 10.2 eV, a **line**, produced by the radiative cascade after
recombination to n >= 2 or by collisional excitation from the ground state. It
carries excitation energy, not the recombining electron's kinetic energy, and
`beta` excludes it in Case A and Case B alike.

So the Case A choice is coupled to what the code does with the **continuum**,
and MOCASSIN builds `gammaHI` from the H threshold up (D-227) and transports
it, counting its re-absorption in the photoionization heating. The kinetic
energy those recombinations remove therefore genuinely leaves the cell, and
Case A is the consistent coefficient. Lyman alpha transfer does not enter.

### Three things checked rather than asserted

**1. The coefficient is the n=1 term.** Read in the source, not inferred from
the name.

**2. There is no double count.** The way Case A could be wrong is if the code
*also* kept an on-the-spot treatment somewhere - transporting the continuum
and assuming it re-absorbed locally would count the same energy twice.
`grid%JPEots`, the on-the-spot line field, is allocated, zeroed, and **never
filled**: both places that would read it are commented out. So there is no
such path.

**3. The line emissivities are Case B, and that is not a contradiction.**
`data/r1b0100.dat` is Case B, so the hydrogen recombination line spectrum is
computed Case B while the cooling is now Case A. Same word, different physics:
Case B for the *line spectrum* is a statement about **Lyman-line** optical
depth, which is enormous in any of these models whatever the continuum does;
Case A for the *cooling* is a statement about whether **n=1 recombinations**
count as a local energy loss, which depends on continuum transport. Both are
right, and for different reasons.

### The sink found next door

`resLinesTransfer` defaults to **101.**, a convergence percentage that can
never be reached, so both

    if (lgDust .and. convPercent>=resLinesTransfer .and. ...) call setResLineEscapeProb(...)
    if (lgDust .and. convPercent>=resLinesTransfer .and. ...) call initResLinePackets()

are gated off in **every run in this project** - which is what the standing
`readInput` warning is about ("the resonanceLinesTransfer keyword is absent.
The dust temperatures may be underestimated!!!!").

`initResLinePackets` is the path that takes the trapped fraction of H Lyman
alpha and the heavy-element resonance lines and turns it into dust-emitted
packets. With it off, collisionally excited Lyman alpha is removed from the
gas as `coolColl` and **deposited nowhere**. This is the same family as L-1,
for resonance lines instead of thin ones.

Where it matters:

  - **Not in the PDR.** The H collisional term is gated to `TeUsed > 5000.`
    and the PDR runs at 20-70 K, so it is identically zero there. None of
    D-320 to D-326 is affected.
  - **In the ionized gas**, in principle. Measured on `runs/d316-hiipdr`,
    MOCASSIN's H collisional cooling is under 3% of its total cooling at
    A_V 0.05-0.40.

### An unexplained factor of four, registered not chased

Cloudy's matching agent (`ISrcolH H`) carries **9-11%** of its cooling at the
same depths, against MOCASSIN's under 3%. That is a factor ~4 in a cooling
channel, and it is **not explained here**. Candidates, none tested: the
`T > 5000 K` gate, which is a hard cut where the real rate is smooth; the
neutral fraction each code carries in ionized gas; or Cloudy's agent including
more than the 1s-2p term. It is small in absolute terms, which is why it has
not surfaced, and it is written down so that it is not rediscovered as new.

### Conclusion

D-286 stands. No change made.

## D-328 - the sticking fix measured, against the prediction (2026-09-22)

`runs/d326-stick`: 22 iterations, **76.11% converged** against `d316-hiipdr`'s
73.75%, 0% ion-balance and 0% Te-balance failures, 1 h 22 min. Checked with
`tools/d326_check.py`, written before the run finished.

### The temperature

    A_V     T_old   T_new  Cloudy | old/Cl  new/Cl
    0.73     71.8    51.6    48.3 |  1.488   1.069
    0.97     62.2    49.8    49.1 |  1.267   1.014
    1.27     49.0    44.3    49.2 |  0.997   0.901
    1.68     30.5    29.5    38.1 |  0.801   0.776
    2.21     19.1    19.1    24.1 |  0.791   0.789

**The warm half of the crossover is closed**: 49% and 27% too warm becomes 7%
and 1.4%. The photoelectric term it acts on now matches Cloudy to 4% and 2%
at those depths (PE_new/PE_Cloudy = 1.043, 0.983).

### The four quantities that had to stay put, did

    dust T    new/old  0.998  0.999  0.999  1.000  0.999
    front     3.848 -> 3.840 pc
    H/H2      A_V 1.168 -> 1.173
    C+ = C    A_V 2.242 -> 2.239

All inside run-to-run scatter (D-314). The change touched the grain charge
balance and nothing else, which is what it was supposed to do.

### And the prediction was half wrong

D-326 predicted the profile would **rotate** about A_V ~ 1.3 - cooler in
front, **warmer deep** - and recorded the falsification: *"the whole profile
moving one way, which would mean the sticking is acting as a normalisation and
the psi picture is wrong."*

    PE new/old   0.608  0.657  0.754  0.930  0.907

Down everywhere. Monotonically approaching 1 with depth, never rising. **No
rotation. By the criterion written before the run, the psi picture is
falsified.**

### Why, and it is worth spelling out

The reasoning was: halving S doubles the effective charging parameter, so each
depth slides right along the measured efficiency-vs-psi curve; that curve
peaks near psi = 2e5, so deep points - sitting below the peak - would move
back toward it and warm.

Measured psi, new over old:

    A_V        0.73   0.97   1.27   1.68   2.21
    psi ratio  0.877  0.927  0.958  0.986  1.007

**psi barely moved, and slightly down.** Of course it did: psi = G0 sqrt(T) /
x(e) is built from physical quantities, and the sticking coefficient is not
one of them. The only thing that moved psi at all is the temperature feedback
that D-326 flagged as second order - cooler gas, lower sqrt(T), lower psi.

Sticking does not move the code **along** the psi axis. It changes the
**mapping** from psi to efficiency: at essentially the same psi, PE/G0 at
A_V 0.73 went 1.741e-27 -> 1.062e-27. The curve shifted down in place.

Two things were conflated:

  - The efficiency-vs-psi curve of D-325 is a **locus traced by depth**. Its
    points differ in spectrum, grain charge distribution and dust temperature
    as well as in psi. It is not a response function.
  - `psi_eff = psi / S` is a fair way to **compare two codes** that differ in
    S - which is what D-325 used it for, and that result stands. It is not a
    prediction of how one code answers a change in its own S.

The correct picture is simpler than the one predicted. Less sticking means
more charge means more Coulomb suppression, **everywhere**, by an amount set
by how much suppression there was to add - largest where the grain was already
most charged, which is shallow, and smallest deep where the grain is nearly
neutral. That gives 0.61 rising to 0.93 with no crossing, which is what the
run shows.

### Where this leaves the model

The crossover is gone. What replaces it is a **one-sided cold bias beyond
A_V ~ 1.3** - 0.78 and 0.79 of Cloudy at A_V 1.68 and 2.21, essentially
unchanged by this fix, with PE at 0.47 and 0.22 of Cloudy's there.

That is a cleaner problem than a sign reversal, and it is now the whole of
L-22. It is also where MOCASSIN's Monte Carlo field floor lives (O-01, O-34):
PE is exactly zero by A_V 2.91, and the deep field is the one thing in this
chain that has never been measured against Cloudy per frequency bin, because
`pdrRad.out` carries four band sums and nothing finer.

### Not done

The change is correct and stays in, but the fixture is one model. `pn150k`
has not been re-run on it, and its dust is graphite where this is silicate -
different work function, so a different amount of suppression to add.
