## D-330 - the [S III] audit, and a dataset that was already in use (2026-09-23)

The user asked whether `mocassin_HM_2026`'s [S III] atomic data commit is
worth implementing here. Auditing it found something larger.

### The commit itself

`4894d6d` replaces, in `data/siii.dat`:

    upsilons   Mendoza (1983)              -> Hudson et al. (2012, ApJ 750, 65)
    A values   Mendoza & Zeippen (1982)    -> Podobedova (2009) / Froese Fischer (2006)
    energies   -                           -> NIST ASD
    T grid     5000-20000 K, 4 points      -> 1000 K - 1e10 K, 17 points

routed through Cloudy c25.00's Stout database. The numbers:

    transition   upsilon(10^4 K)  new/old      A       new/old
      1-2          2.59 -> 2.26     0.87
      1-4          0.93 -> 0.73     0.78    5.82e-6 -> 5.64e-6   0.97
      2-4          2.80 -> 2.17     0.78    2.21e-2 -> 1.95e-2   0.88
      2-5          0.40 -> 0.33     0.83    7.96e-1 -> 6.88e-1   0.86
      4-5          1.88 -> 1.40     0.74    2.22    -> 2.19      0.99

Energies move by under 0.5% - NIST refinements, not a change.

**The port is exact.** Checked directly against
`cloudy-c25.00/data/stout/s/s_3/s_3.coll` and `.tp`: all ten collision
strengths at all seventeen temperatures and all nine A values agree to machine
precision. The temperature grid is Stout's own.

**No code change is needed.** `hydro_mod.f90` reads `NCOMS`, skips that many
comment lines, then reads `NLEVS, NTEMPS` and allocates everything
dynamically, so 4 comment lines and 17 temperatures parse. And
`linear_interpolation` **clamps** at the table edges rather than
extrapolating, so the old 4-point table was not producing nonsense below
5000 K - it was returning the 5000 K value. The wider grid is an improvement,
not a bug fix.

### The larger finding

`data/siii.dat` in this repository is **not the file the runs read.**

The Makefile sets `PREFIX = $(HOME)/.local`, and every run log in this project
says so:

    Data directories: /home/hmonteiro/.local/share/mocassin/data

That directory holds 172 files, all dated **2026-09-18 14:24**, and every one
of them is **byte-identical to the sibling repository's `data/`**. Someone ran
`make install` from `mocassin_HM_2026` on the 18th. Against it, **113 of this
repo's 143 `.dat` files differ**: 98 are CHIANTI 10 -> 10.1, 14 are Stout
ports (including `s_3`), one has no provenance line.

So the answer to "is it worth implementing here" is that **it has been in
effect here for five days**, along with a hundred other files, and the
repository has been describing a dataset its own results were not computed
with.

### Which results this touches

    d283-pn150k          2026-09-14    OLD data
    d290-pn150k-grainq   2026-09-19    new
    d292-pn150k-lines    2026-09-19    new
    d302-trim-on/off     2026-09-21    new
    d313-qavg            2026-09-22    new
    d316-hiipdr          2026-09-22    new
    d326-stick           2026-09-22    new

Only `d283-pn150k` predates the change.

**Not confounded.** D-315's dust result compares `d302-trim-on` with
`d313-qavg`, and D-328's sticking result compares `d316-hiipdr` with
`d326-stick`. Both pairs sit on the same side of the 18th, so both stand.

**Confounded.** Anything that sets D-283's numbers against a later run. That
includes D-283's own line-flux table - [Ne III] +35-48%, [O II] 3726 +28%,
[O I] 6300 +40% and the rest - which was measured on CHIANTI 10 with Mendoza
[S III] and has never been re-measured. Those figures are not on the current
artifact, which was rebuilt on `d313-qavg`, but they are in the DEVLOG and
should not be quoted against present-day runs.

### What was done

`data/` synced to what the runs read, so the repository describes its own
results again. This is the project rule about one reality per quantity, in the
place where it is easiest to violate silently: a data directory that is
installed rather than read in place.

**What was not done:** the other 112 files were not individually audited. The
`s_3` port was verified against Cloudy because it is what the user asked
about; the CHIANTI 10 -> 10.1 bump and the thirteen other Stout ports are
taken on the provenance headers they carry. That is a weaker standard than
this project usually applies, and it is recorded as such.

### Expected direction, before the run

Lower [S III] upsilons mean **less** cooling and a **hotter** ionized gas -
[S III] carries 9-13% of Cloudy's ionized-gas cooling in these models, so a
~20% cut removes ~2% of the total. The awkward part is that our ionized gas is
already 6-8% hotter than Cloudy beyond 1 pc, so this makes the comparison look
worse, not better.

That is not a reason to reject it. Cloudy is a reference, not a benchmark, and
we were running hot **while carrying more [S III] cooling than Cloudy did** -
the old data was partly masking whatever really causes the excess. Both codes
now use Hudson (2012), so the remaining difference is attributable elsewhere.

## D-331 - molecular line observables: what exists, what is missing (2026-09-23)

The user, while `d330-pn150k` was running: the code looks production-level on
hiipdr, and the next step for doing science is observables - integrated line
intensities and emissivities of selected molecular lines. How hard, does
3D-PDR already have the machinery, does Cloudy, which is better?

### The emissivities already exist

`source/pdr/escape_probability.F90`, line 194:

    line(ilevel,jlevel) = A_COEFFS(ilevel,jlevel)*HP*frequencies(ilevel,jlevel) * &
                        & s_pop(ilevel)*beta_ij*(S_ij-BB_ij)/S_ij

That is the per-transition emissivity in erg cm^-3 s^-1. It is formed for
every radiative transition of every coolant in every cell on every iteration.
`pdr_mod.f90` passes `lline(1:nlev,1:nlev)`, uses the summed `coolK` for the
thermal balance, and **discards the array** - `lline` is a local.

Counting what is already being computed and thrown away:

    CO    40 radiative transitions   (J = 1-0 up to ~40-39)
    C+     9                         (includes [C II] 158 um)
    C      7                         (includes [C I] 370, 609 um)
    O      7                         (includes [O I] 63, 145 um)
    ---
          63 transitions per cell

`beta_ij` is already inside `line`, so this is the emission that **escapes**
the cell, not what is locally emitted.

### So the two asked-for observables are different sizes of job

**Per-cell emissivities:** allocate a persistent array, fill it where `lline`
is already filled, write it. No new physics, no new data, no new solver.
`pdrMaxLev` is already `max` over the coolants, so there is no cap to raise.
Storage at 41^3 is ~69k cells x 63 x 8 B = **33 MB**, comparable to
`pdrGrid.out`.

**Integrated line luminosities:** once the above exists, a volume sum
`sum_cells line(i,j) * V_cell`, which can go straight into `lineFlux.out`
beside the CELs. Essentially free.

**What is NOT in scope:** position-velocity cubes or line profiles. There is
no velocity field in the model. Maps at a viewing angle are a smaller step -
`viewPointTheta/Phi` and `nAngleBins` already exist for SEDs.

### The species that are already available

`dataPDR/` vendors **15 LAMDA files**, not the 4 in use. Matching them against
the REDUCED network's 33 species:

    usable today   C+, C, CO, O (active), and OH, HCO+, CH+ (inactive)
    no carrier     C2H, CN, CN-hfs, HCN, HNC, N2H+, SiO

So three more species could be switched on without touching the chemistry -
though each adds levels to the solve, so cost and convergence would need
watching. The rest need a larger network, which is a chemistry decision, not
an observables one.

### 3D-PDR or Cloudy

**3D-PDR, and it is not close.**

  - The machinery is in-tree, running, and already trusted enough to drive the
    thermal balance this project has spent 300 entries validating.
  - LAMDA is the community-standard format. Adding a species is dropping in a
    file, which is exactly why 15 of them are already sitting there.
  - The escape probability already carries the optical depth, and under
    `RAYTHEIA` it is averaged over HEALPix rays - which is the one thing a 1D
    code structurally cannot do, and the reason this coupling exists at all.
  - Cloudy's equivalent would mean porting a foreign level solver **and** its
    chemistry, to duplicate what is already here.

Cloudy's right role is **validation**, not implementation: it has
`save lines emissivity`, the matched models already exist
(`runs/d322-cloudy-hb`, `runs/d302-cloudy-trim-rad`), so every new line can be
checked against it the day it appears. That is the same division of labour
that has worked for the temperature and the dust.

### Three caveats that belong on any published line

**CO lines would be wrong today.** Deep CO is 50-100x Cloudy's - a standing
disagreement since D-264 and unmoved by everything in this cycle. The whole
ladder inherits it. [C II] and [O I] are on much firmer ground: they are the
thermostat, and D-322's [C II] test predicts the temperature from the heating
ratio alone to within 10% at every depth.

**`pdrNbadPop` must be reported.** The level solve can return a singular
matrix as NaN rather than failing, which is why that counter exists. A line
intensity computed from populations that silently fell back to the previous
iterate is not a measurement.

**H2 is the real gap.** There is no `h2.dat`, so 1-0 S(1) at 2.12 um and the
0-0 S(n) ladder are unavailable - among the most-observed PDR diagnostics.
And it is not another file drop: H2 level populations are FUV-pumped, not
collisionally set, so it needs excitation physics the coolant path does not
have.

### On "production level"

Agreed for the ionized gas and for the [C II]/[O I] thermostat. Not yet for
the deep molecular region, which is where CO lines would come from: CO
50-100x, C+ 0.21-0.38x past A_V 2.3, and the Monte Carlo field floor where the
photoelectric heating reaches exactly zero by A_V 2.9. Those bound what
molecular observables would currently mean, and they should be quoted
alongside the first ones produced.

No code written. This entry is the design record.

## D-332 - pn150k with the sticking fix, and what the data sync did not tell us (2026-09-23)

`runs/d330-pn150k`, input byte-identical to `runs/d313-qavg`.

### Convergence improved

    d313-qavg    11 iterations   89.58%   2 h 00 min
    d330-pn150k   9 iterations   90.15%   1 h 18 min

It stopped at iteration 9 by reaching the 90% target rather than exhausting
the iteration limit - the first time this fixture has done so. 0% ion-balance
and 0% Te-balance failures.

### The sticking fix is much weaker here than on hiipdr

    A_V         0.21   0.28   0.37   0.49   0.65
    T new/old  0.952  0.911  0.963  0.981  0.999
    PE new/old 0.832  0.854  0.903  0.947  0.958

against hiipdr's PE 0.608 / 0.657 / 0.754 / 0.930 / 0.907. D-328 flagged this
in advance: *"pn150k has not been re-run on this; its graphite has a different
work function and so a different amount of suppression to add."* It does, and
the difference is a factor of two in the size of the effect.

Unmoved, as a change confined to the grain charge balance must be: dust
temperature 0.996-0.999 of the old run, and the size-weighted ratios against
Cloudy come back 0.905 / 0.899 / 0.872 / 0.869 against D-315's published
0.906 / 0.902 / 0.873 / 0.869. H+ front 0.129 pc and H/H2 crossing A_V 0.248,
both unchanged.

### pn150k is a different regime from hiipdr, and stays cold

    A_V         0.21   0.28   0.37   0.49   0.65
    T / Cloudy 0.726  0.757  0.736  0.623  0.669
    PE/ Cloudy 0.308  0.404  0.419  0.313  0.260

No crossover here, and never was one: this PDR is **uniformly cold**, at
0.62-0.76 of Cloudy, with the photoelectric heating at a quarter to two fifths
of Cloudy's. The sticking correction makes it marginally colder. That is the
honest cost of using the right coefficient, and it is the same situation as
the [S III] data below - the model was closer to the reference for a reason
that was not physics.

So hiipdr and pn150k disagree with Cloudy in different ways, and the L-22
picture built on hiipdr alone does not transfer. Worth stating plainly: one
fixture is not a validation.

### What this run does NOT measure

The user asked for this re-run partly to see what the [S III] atomic data
does. **It cannot say.** `d313-qavg` ran on 2026-09-22, four days after the
installed data directory was replaced (D-330), so both sides of this
comparison already carry Hudson et al. (2012). No run in this project differs
from another only by that file.

What can be done without a run is a direct 5-level solve at the model's own
conditions. At pn150k's ionized gas (T = 11907 K, n_e = 1065 cm^-3), cooling
per S(2+) ion:

    Mendoza 1983   6.647e-17 erg/s
    Hudson 2012    5.467e-17
    ratio          0.823        ->  [S III] cooling -17.7%

and 0.78 to 0.85 across 6000-15000 K. That is a bound on the channel, not a
measurement of the model: what it does to the temperature depends on [S III]'s
share of the total cooling and on the thermostat's response, neither of which
this calculation contains.

**Isolating it would cost one run** - swap `data/siii.dat` back to Mendoza,
change nothing else, 1 h 18 min. Not done, and recorded as not done.

### Tooling

`tools/d326_check.py`, written *yesterday*, had hiipdr's five sample depths
hardcoded. Pointed at pn150k it sampled A_V 0.73-2.21 on a PDR that ends at
0.67. That is L-21 again, in a tool written after L-21 was registered. Depths
now derived from the model's own PDR, explicit depths still accepted. The
"ROTATION" verdict, which was hiipdr's prediction, is now reported as the
shape of the change rather than a pass/fail against one fixture's expectation.

Five tools, six constants. The register entry stands and so does its lesson.

## D-333 - What stands between this code and science production (2026-09-23)

The user's question: with the code at what looks like production level, what
are the major outstanding issues? The register in `doc/pdr-status.md` holds 22
limitations; this entry ranks them against one criterion - *does it stop us
publishing a number* - and records the three measurements taken to do the
ranking, two of which found something the register did not have.

### The ranking

**Tier 1 - blocks any published number, regardless of physics.**

*1. There is no reproducibility, and no error bar on anything.*
`source/photon_mod.f90:83-100` seeds the generator from the wall clock:

    call date_and_time(values=dt)
    msec = dt(8)
    call random_seed(get = seed)
    seed = seed + msec + taskid
    call random_seed(put = seed)

There is no input keyword to override it - the only `seed` keywords in
`set_input_mod.f90` are `pdrTseed`, the deterministic start for the thermal
march (D-051), and the chemistry seeding of D-208. So a run cannot be
regenerated, and D-314 measured what that costs: **37% swing in median T_gas
on a 5^3 fixture, same binary, same input.** Aggregate KPIs on the production
grid are much tighter, but no published comparison in this project carries an
error bar (L-13/O-25). Every "agrees to 5%" and every "9-13% cool" in the
artifacts is a single draw against a single draw.

This is the cheapest item in the whole list - one keyword read into a module
variable, defaulting to the present clock behaviour so nothing changes unless
asked - and it gates the *meaning* of every other number, including all of
D-322 through D-332.

*2. Two fixtures, and they disagree with each other.* hiipdr crosses Cloudy at
A_V ~1.3 and moved 28% under the sticking fix; pn150k never crosses, sits
uniformly at 0.62-0.76 of Cloudy, and moved 5% (D-328, D-332). The same change,
the same code, opposite readings. The slabs and `ifront` have not been run this
cycle and could not have been before D-316 (L-11). L-21 is the same disease in
the tooling: six fixture-specific constants across five tools, every one found
only by pointing a tool at a second model.

**Tier 2 - blocks the science the code is being taken to production *for*.**

*3. The carbon chemistry is ready for exactly one of the three molecular
observables.* New measurement, `runs/d326-stick` against the vendored 3D-PDR
reference `benchmarks/pdr/baseline3dpdr/sec54.pdr.fin` (Bisbas et al. 2015
§5.4), both at n_H = 100, columns mapped through `v1.species` (C+ 11, C 25,
CO 28, over 8 leading columns):

    A_V  | x(C+) moc/ref | x(C) moc/ref | x(CO) moc/ref
    0.60 |     1.00      |    0.16      |    0.00
    0.90 |     1.00      |    0.20      |    0.05
    1.25 |     1.00      |    0.20      |    0.39
    1.60 |     1.01      |    0.23      |    0.62
    1.90 |     1.03      |    0.36      |    2.27
    2.10 |     1.01      |    0.93      |    3.38
    2.33 |     0.38      |    3.76      |    3.24

C+ is right to 1-3% over a factor 400 in field, which is a real result and the
first time this fixture's chemistry has been checked against the code it came
from rather than against Cloudy. Neutral C is 5x low through the shallow PDR.
CO is two orders low at A_V 0.6, crosses unity near 1.7 and ends 3x high.
Carbon conserves to the total at every depth (C+ + C + CO = 2.20e-4 within a
per cent), so this is a transition **placed too shallow and too sharp**, not a
mass-loss bug.

That ranks D-331's implementation order on evidence rather than on expectation:
**[C II] 158 um** rests on a carrier good to 1-3% and can be built now;
**[C I] 609/370 um** rests on one 5x low; **CO** rests on one wrong by two
orders of magnitude and changing sign with depth.

*4. L-3 is live, and the register mis-states it.* `doc/pdr-status.md` says of
L-3 (O-01, the deep C+ drop past A_V ~2.1) that "the reference model reaches
only A_V 0.68, so it does not exercise the affected region". That was true of
pn150k and is not true now: `runs/d326-stick` spans A_V 0.466-2.999 and the
3D-PDR reference reaches 2.453, so there is half an A_V of overlap on the far
side of the transition. In it, MOCASSIN's C+/C ratio is 0.45 at A_V 2.33 where
the reference's is 4.45 - a factor **9.9** - and MOCASSIN's C+ keeps falling,
to 4.1e-5 by A_V 2.6. The defect is measurable today on a run already on disk.

*5. No observables pipeline exists, and the output path is unverified.* D-331
is a design record with no code. The emissivities are computed in every cell
already (`source/pdr/escape_probability.F90:194`) and written to no file.
Separately, L-20: `mocassinPlot` and `mocassinOutput` carry the D-317 fix but
have never been run against a grid, so the post-processing that would turn a
converged grid into a spectrum is verified only to the extent D-317's fix was
before it was exercised - which is to say, not at all.

**Tier 3 - open physics that will show up in results.**

*6. The photoelectric deficit on pn150k is not closed.* PE/Cloudy 0.26-0.42,
T/Cloudy 0.62-0.76, uniformly, with the sticking fix making it marginally
colder (D-332). D-322 through D-328 explained hiipdr's *crossover*; they did
not explain pn150k's *uniform* deficit, and a factor 2.5-4 in the dominant PDR
heating term on the reference model is a first-order open problem.

*7. L-19*, the frequency placement of reprocessed energy: field 1.16-1.35x high
while grains run 9-13% cool. *8. L-4/O-14*, the 3D self-shielding tracer - the
one limitation that bites specifically on the reason to use MOCASSIN at all.
*9. L-9*, gas-grain coupling skipping H2: negligible at n_H = 1e3, decisive at
high density, so dense knots are out of scope until it is fixed.

**Tier 4 - absolute realism.** L-5 (carbon counted twice, gas not depleted for
what is in grains), L-6 (R_V 4.57, not a Milky Way curve), L-7 (no PAHs - and
PAHs dominate photoelectric heating in real PDRs, which is the very term
running low), L-8 (stochastic heating off), L-10 (bulk graphite optics on the
smallest bin, 10-32x off in the far-IR, which is where a dust SED would be
compared). Every one is common-mode with the Cloudy reference, so no
code-to-code comparison is affected - and every one is wrong in absolute terms,
which is what science on a real object needs.

**Tier 5 - provenance.** D-330's lesson is recorded but not closed: runs read
`~/.local/share/mocassin/data` while the repo holds `data/`, nothing pins or
checksums the installed copy, 112 of the 143 synced files were never audited,
and a silent undeclared change has already happened once. The asymmetry is the
tell - `pdrDataDir` in every fixture points *into* the repo, so the PDR coolant
data is versioned with the code and the ionized-gas data is not.

### A hypothesis, recorded before it is tested

L-3 and hiipdr's deep cold may be one defect. [C I] 609 um has E/k = 23.6 K
against [C II] 158 um's 91.2 K. At the 15-25 K MOCASSIN reaches beyond A_V 2,
[C II] is nearly frozen out and [C I] is not, so **converting C+ to C too early
switches on a coolant the gas can actually drive** - which cools the deep gas
rather than warming it, the direction observed. All four coolants are active in
this fixture (`pdrCoolants 4 "12co.dat" "12c+.dat" "12c.dat" "16o.dat"`), so
`pdrCoolSp.out` already holds the split and the test costs no run.

Falsified if the [C I] share past A_V 2 is small, or if forcing the reference's
C+/C ratio at those depths leaves the temperature where it is.

### One flagged question, not a finding

Against the same 3D-PDR reference at matched density, MOCASSIN's PDR runs
**0.46-0.65x** in T_gas at matched A_V while carrying **6-10x** the FUV field;
matched on *field* instead (G0 ~ 1.3-1.4) it is 24.4 K against the reference's
85.1 K. Two reasons this is not yet a defect claim: the A_V zero points differ
(the reference is a bare slab, hiipdr has an H II region in front of its PDR,
whose own A_V starts at 0.466), and the G0 unit convention - Habing against
Draine, a factor 1.71 - has not been checked across the two codes. What it does
establish is that **the vendored reference has never been used as a temperature
reference for this fixture**; every published comparison is against Cloudy.
Making that comparison properly is an outstanding item in its own right.

### What this entry does not do

No code changed. The register in `doc/pdr-status.md` is updated for the L-3
mis-statement; the rest of the ranking lives here rather than being duplicated
into it.

## D-334 - Seed control, and the defect the seed test found (2026-09-23)

Tier 1 item 1 of D-333: make a run repeatable, so that a disagreement with a
reference can be told from Monte Carlo noise. The keyword took an afternoon.
Verifying it took the rest, and the verification is what mattered.

### The keyword

`randomSeed`, read in `set_input_mod.f90`, held in `common_mod.f90`, used in
`photon_mod.f90`'s `energyPacketDriver`. Omitted or negative it keeps the
historical path **exactly**: perturb the running generator state with the
millisecond field of `date_and_time` plus the rank. A run that does not ask for
a seed behaves as every run before this entry did.

Given a seed, the state is *replaced* rather than perturbed, so it cannot
depend on anything the run did earlier:

    smix = ieor(int(randomSeed,8), ishft(int(taskid,8), 20))
    smix = ieor(smix, ishft(int(nSeedCalls,8), 40))
    smix = ieor(smix, 88172645463325252_8)
    do i = 1, seedSize
       smix = ieor(smix, ishft(smix,  13))
       smix = ieor(smix, ishft(smix,  -7))
       smix = ieor(smix, ishft(smix,  17))
       seed(i) = int(ishft(smix, -33), kind=4)
    end do

Three details that are not decoration. **`nSeedCalls`** exists because
`energyPacketDriver` is called once per star per iteration *and*, when
`Ldiffuse > 0`, once per emitting cell - without it every call would replay the
same photons. The **xorshift mixer** is there because consecutive integers make
poor seeds for the generator behind `random_number`; adjacent calls would start
in neighbouring parts of the state space. It is written with `IEOR`/`ISHFT`
rather than a multiplicative LCG so that **nothing relies on signed integer
overflow**, which is undefined behaviour and which `-O2` is entitled to exploit.

The contract is: **repeatable at fixed input and fixed rank count.** Both
drivers now print which regime the run is in, so a log says whether the run it
describes can be reproduced.

### The test, and what it refused to do

Four runs of the 5^3 fixture, `runs/d334-seed`: A and B at seed 12345, C at
seed 999, D with no keyword at all. Two questions, and they are not the same
one - if only the first is asked, a seed that is silently ignored passes it for
free, which is the D-176..D-181 failure mode of a test that cannot move.

  - same seed, must be identical
  - different seed, must differ

C and D both differ from A in iteration 1, so the seed is genuinely used. But
**A and B were not identical.** Iterations 1, 2 and 3 were byte-identical and
iteration 4 was not - and iteration 4 is this fixture's `pdrStartIter`.

So the Monte Carlo was already reproducible, and something in the PDR coupling
was not.

### `ionDenPrev` is read and never written

`grep -rin iondenprev source/` returns, in full: the declaration
(`iteration_mod.f90:33`), the allocation (:1955), the `.not.allocated` guard
(:1954), a comment, and **two reads** (:2220, :2229). There is no assignment
anywhere in the tree.

The second read is not a diagnostic:

    grid(iG)%ionDen = real((1.d0-pdrCoupleDamp)*dble(grid(iG)%ionDen) &
         &          + pdrCoupleDamp*dble(ionDenPrev))

With the defaults `pdrCoupleDamp = 0.25` and `pdrCoupleIter = 5`, that mixes
**a quarter of uninitialised memory into the ionization fractions on four of
every five coupling passes, on every MC iteration from `pdrStartIter` onward,
in every PDR run this project has ever done.** Whether the allocation lands on
fresh zero-filled pages or on recycled heap is what makes two identical runs
diverge - and it is why the divergence appears exactly when the PDR turns on.

The comment directly above it, from D-216, reads: *"ionDen is written by
updateCell, which now runs once per MC iteration ... so ionDen does not change
across chemistry passes and this measures zero."* The reasoning about `ionDen`
was right. It simply did not occur to its author - or to me, reading it - that
the *other* operand had never been written. The line it defends printed
**1.95e30** in run A and **2.26e6** in run B, for a quantity bounded by 1, and
had been printing values like that for as long as the diagnostic has existed.

A number was on the screen, in every log, wrong by thirty orders of magnitude,
under a comment explaining why it should read zero. It was read past.

### The fix

Take the snapshot the damping always assumed it had - at the **top** of each
pass, since `ionDenPrev` must hold `ionDen` as it stood before that pass:

    do iCouple = 1, max(pdrCoupleIter, 1)
    #ifdef PDR
          if (lgPDR .and. allocated(ionDenPrev)) ionDenPrev = grid(iG)%ionDen

plus `ionDenPrev = grid(iG)%ionDen` at the allocation site, because the
allocation sits further down the same loop body and so has not happened on the
first pass.

The D-119 residual now reads **exactly 0.00000000** on every pass. That is
worth more than a silenced warning: it *confirms* D-216's claim - that `ionDen`
does not change across chemistry passes - which until now was an assertion in a
comment. The damping is provably an identity, and if that ever stops being true
the line will say so.

### What it was worth

Measured at fixed seed, so there is **no Monte Carlo noise in the comparison at
all** - the first change in this project measurable without a scatter estimate,
which is precisely what the keyword was for:

    5^3 fixture, seed 12345, A (unfixed) against E (fixed)

    PDR-zone median T_gas     4050 K   ->    44 K     (x 0.011)
    x(H2)                     0.0205   ->  0.1985     (x 9.7)
    x(H+)                   4.26e-4    -> 2.42e-5     (x 0.057)
    H II zone median T_gas   10533 K   -> 10431 K     (x 0.990)
    T_dust                   39.41 K   -> 38.29 K     (x 0.972)
    x(C+)                   2.688e-4   -> 2.678e-4    (x 0.997)

The ionized gas and the dust barely move. The PDR moves by a factor of 92, and
in the direction that makes it a PDR: the unfixed run held the molecular zone
at 4050 K with the hydrogen 18x too ionized and the H2 suppressed tenfold. A
4050 K PDR was never physical, and it sat in this fixture unremarked.

After the fix, A/B-style repeats are **byte-identical across all eight output
files** (`tools/d334_seedcheck.py`).

### What this costs, and what is not yet known

**Every published PDR number in this project was computed with this defect.**
Both artifacts - `150 kK PN Against Cloudy` (v10) and `hiipdr Against Cloudy`
(v11) - rest on runs that carried it, as does every conclusion from D-304
through D-333 that depends on a PDR temperature or abundance.

What is **not** known is how large the effect is on the production fixtures.
The 5^3 model runs 6 MC iterations of which only 3 are PDR iterations, and
D-314 measured it as the noisiest fixture in the project; hiipdr and pn150k run
9-11 iterations and reported PDR temperatures of 11-72 K, which are not the
4050 K seen here. It is entirely possible the effect is far smaller there, and
entirely possible it is not. **It gets re-run rather than argued about**, at
fixed seed, which now means the answer will be exact.

### Tools

`tools/d334_seedcheck.py` - the two-sided seed test, byte identity first.
`tools/d334_scatter.sh` - build an ensemble differing only in the seed.
`tools/d334_spread.py` - the error bar: mean, sd and full range over an
ensemble, on the quantities the artifacts quote, at depths derived from the run
rather than hardcoded (L-21).

## D-335 - The first error bar, and a correction to D-334 (2026-09-23)

Four repeats of hiipdr on the D-334 code, differing only in `randomSeed`:
`runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001` .. `s1004`, seeds 1001-1004, 1h22-1h48 each, from
`runs/d326-stick/input` verbatim. Convergence 74.86 / 76.26 / 75.58 / 75.94%
against the published run's 76.11% - inside the spread, so the fix does not
change how the model converges either.

### The error bar

Sample depths derived from the run (L-21): A_V 0.81, 1.11, 1.53, 2.10, 2.89.

    quantity                mean        sd        rel      range
    T_gas   A_V 0.81       51.52   +- 0.082     0.16%    51.43 - 51.63
    T_gas   A_V 1.11       47.31   +- 0.096     0.20%    47.19 - 47.41
    T_gas   A_V 1.53       35.59   +- 0.137     0.39%    35.46 - 35.71
    T_gas   A_V 2.10       21.33   +- 0.074     0.35%    21.24 - 21.40
    T_gas   A_V 2.89       11.30   +- 0.007     0.06%    11.29 - 11.31
    T_dust  A_V 0.81       30.02   +- 0.027     0.09%    30.00 - 30.06
    T_dust  A_V 2.89       13.08   +- 0.006     0.04%    13.07 - 13.09
    PE      A_V 0.81    5.327e-26  +- 2.4e-28   0.45%
    PE      A_V 2.10    1.138e-27  +- 2.1e-29   1.81%
    front (pc)             3.837   +- 0.003     0.08%    3.835 - 3.842
    H/H2 A_V               1.170   +- 0.002     0.20%    1.168 - 1.173

**D-314's 37% is retired.** That number - median T_gas swing between two runs
of the same binary - has been this project's noise floor since it was measured,
is quoted in L-13, and sits on both artifact pages as the reason no comparison
carries an error bar. It was measured on the 5^3 fixture: six MC iterations, of
which three are PDR iterations, 75% converged, and - as D-334 established
afterwards - carrying a quarter of uninitialised memory in `ionDen`. It is a
property of that fixture, not of the Monte Carlo on a production grid.

The consequence is large, and for once in this project's favour. hiipdr's
temperature ratios against Cloudy are 1.058 / 0.949 / 0.838 / 0.815 / 0.788
with sigma of 0.2-0.4%, so the departures from unity are **15 to 300 sigma**.
Every disagreement published here - the dust running 9-13% cool, the
temperature crossover, pn150k's uniform 30% deficit - is a measurement and not
a draw. That could not be said before today.

The honest caveat on the error bar itself: four draws, so the sd carries about
40% relative uncertainty of its own. The full range is printed beside it for
that reason. It is enough to separate 0.3% from 37%; it is not enough to quote
three significant figures.

### The correction

D-334 said, of the uninitialised `ionDenPrev`: *"every published PDR number in
this project was computed with this defect"* and *"both artifacts must be
rebuilt on re-runs"*. The first is true. **The second is wrong for hiipdr.**

    A_V   | published (v11)  ensemble mean     new/old   sigmas
    0.81  |     51.49          51.52 +- 0.082  1.0005      0.3
    1.11  |     47.28          47.31 +- 0.096  1.0006      0.3
    1.53  |     35.56          35.59 +- 0.137  1.0008      0.2
    2.10  |     21.31          21.33 +- 0.074  1.0008      0.2
    2.89  |     11.31          11.30 +- 0.007  0.9994      1.0

PE heating likewise, within 1.2 sigma at every depth. **The fix changes nothing
measurable on this model**, and the artifact does not need rebuilding on its
account.

The factor of 92 seen on the 5^3 fixture did not transfer, and the reason is
visible in the code rather than a matter of luck: `updateCell` recomputes
`ionDen` from scratch at the top of every MC iteration, so the garbage injected
by the damping is overwritten each iteration and can only perturb the chemistry
*within* one. A model given 22 iterations converges out of that perturbation.
A model given 6, of which 3 are PDR iterations, does not.

The defect was real - it was undefined behaviour, it made the code
irreproducible, and it is what the seed test was for. The fix is right and
stays. But **its effect on converged production models is null**, and D-334
claimed otherwise from a single fixture within hours of D-333's Tier 1 item 2,
which says in as many words that a conclusion from one fixture is a property of
that model rather than of the code. Written down, then done anyway.

pn150k's ensemble is still running and will say whether the same holds there.
It has 9-10 iterations against hiipdr's 22, so it sits between the two cases
and the answer is not obvious.

### One observation, not chased

PE heating at A_V 2.89 is **exactly** 0.000e+00 in all four ensemble runs and
in the published one, while total heating there is 8.4e-28 carried by the other
two channels. Across the last three sample depths it runs 1.113e-27 ->
1.010e-28 -> 0. A steep decline is expected as the band burns out against a
rising grain potential; an *exact* zero looks like a threshold being crossed
rather than a quantity going small. Recorded here so it is not lost - it may be
`grnAbs` correctly finding no photons above a threshold that has moved past the
band, in which case it is physics, or it may be a cutoff. Not yet looked at.

## D-336 - pn150k's ensemble, and the close of Tier 1 item 1 (2026-09-23)

Four repeats of pn150k differing only in `randomSeed`:
`runs/d334-pn150k/s1001` .. `s1004`, from `runs/d330-pn150k/input` verbatim,
1h28-1h43 each. All four took **10** iterations to 90.13-90.81% where the
published run took **9** to 90.15% - inside the spread of where this fixture
crosses its own 90% target, not a change in how it converges.

### The error bar

Sample depths derived from the run (L-21): A_V 0.21, 0.28, 0.37, 0.49, 0.65.

    quantity                mean        sd         rel
    T_gas   A_V 0.21       108.4   +- 2.35       2.17%
    T_gas   A_V 0.28       56.92   +- 0.120      0.21%
    T_gas   A_V 0.37       45.09   +- 0.030      0.07%
    T_gas   A_V 0.49       33.75   +- 0.027      0.08%

    front (pc)             0.129   +- 4.2e-5     0.03%
    H/H2 A_V              0.2513   +- 1.8e-4     0.07%

One depth carries a visible bar: A_V 0.21, the PDR's outer edge nearest the
ionization front, at 2.17%. It has the fewest cells in its window and sits
where the temperature gradient is steepest. hiipdr's outermost sample behaves
the same way (D-335). Everywhere else the production-grid noise is a few parts
in a thousand.

Together with D-335 this retires **D-314's 37%** on both published fixtures
rather than one. That figure is a property of the 5^3 fixture - six MC
iterations, three of them PDR iterations, 75% converged, and carrying the
D-334 defect - and it should never have been carried forward as the noise
floor of this code. L-13 is updated accordingly.

### The published comparison, with bars

    A_V   | T_moc/T_Cloudy       D-332 published | PE/PE_Cloudy       D-332
    0.21  |  0.698 +- 0.015           0.726      | 0.310 +- 0.001     0.308
    0.28  |  0.750 +- 0.002           0.757      | 0.403 +- 0.001     0.404
    0.37  |  0.737 +- 0.000           0.736      | 0.422 +- 0.001     0.419
    0.49  |  0.625 +- 0.000           0.623      | 0.317 +- 0.001     0.313
    0.65  |  0.668 +- 0.000           0.669      | 0.263 +- 0.001     0.260

Every published value is reproduced inside the ensemble spread. pn150k's
uniform cold and its factor 2.5-4 photoelectric deficit stand at **20 to 250
sigma**. They are measurements.

### D-334's alarm, fully withdrawn

    A_V   | published  ensemble        new/old   sigmas
    0.21  |   111.27   108.39 +- 2.349  0.9741     1.2
    0.28  |    57.19    56.92 +- 0.120  0.9953     2.2
    0.37  |    45.03    45.09 +- 0.030  1.0013     2.0
    0.49  |    33.72    33.75 +- 0.027  1.0011     1.4
    0.65  |    25.72    25.66 +- 0.017  0.9974     4.1

D-334 said both artifacts must be rebuilt because of the uninitialised
`ionDenPrev`. D-335 withdrew that for hiipdr; it is now withdrawn for pn150k
too. The largest departure, 2.6% at A_V 0.21, sits at the noisiest depth and
is within 1.2 sigma of it.

The one systematic the fix leaves is photoelectric heating **+0.6 to +1.0% at
every depth**, the same sign at all five - too consistent to be noise, and too
small to matter. That distinction is worth stating plainly because several
entries in the table above are formally 2-4 sigma while being three parts in a
thousand: **an error bar makes small real effects visible, it does not make
them important.** Reading significance as size is the mirror image of the
mistake D-314 led this project into, and it would be easy to make now that the
bars are this tight.

### Status

**Tier 1 item 1 of D-333 is done.** Seed control implemented and verified in
both directions (D-334), the uninitialised-array defect it uncovered fixed, and
the run-to-run noise floor measured on both published fixtures (D-335, D-336).
Every comparison this project has published is now known to be outside its own
noise, which is a claim it could not make yesterday.

**Tier 1 item 2 is not started**: v1slab, v2slab and ifront have still not been
run this cycle (L-11), and the two fixtures in hand still disagree with each
other about what the code does - hiipdr crossing Cloudy and moving 28% under
the sticking fix, pn150k uniformly cold and moving 5%.

What the ensembles also give, without extra cost, is a reproducible baseline:
`runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001` and `runs/d334-pn150k/s1001` can be regenerated
exactly at `-np 14`, so any future change can be measured against them the way
D-334's fix was measured - with no Monte Carlo noise in the comparison at all.

## D-337 - Both artifacts rebuilt on the ensembles (2026-09-24)

At the user's direction, after D-336 closed Tier 1 item 1.

  - **hiipdr Against Cloudy** &rarr; v12, https://claude.ai/artifact/PBCP2hf3SzMMn5t6PYLDtx
  - **150 kK PN Against Cloudy** &rarr; v11, https://claude.ai/artifact/DofNhQwr6apCKo2BR8y1JV

### A claim of mine that was wrong

When offering to do this I told the user that both pages "state that no
comparison carries an error bar, citing the 37%". **Neither page cites D-314 or
the 37% anywhere.** That text lived in `doc/pdr-status.md`'s L-13, which the
D-336 commit had already corrected. I had conflated the register with the pages
that draw on it.

What the pages actually carried was weaker, more specific, and in two places
flatly wrong rather than merely stale:

  - hiipdr's caveat rail: *"One MOCASSIN run and one Cloudy run. Monte Carlo
    scatter in deep CO and OH was measured at up to a decade (D-242)."*
  - hiipdr's register, O-25: *"Cloudy comparison is one run of each code ...
    Next: Repeat MOCASSIN once to bound the scatter on the published profiles."*
  - hiipdr's register, O-18: *"Deep CO/OH differ up to 25x between identical
    runs ... Next: Quantify scatter per profile with repeats before reading
    deep ratios."*
  - the PN page: nothing about run-to-run scatter at all, anywhere.

Reading the pages before editing them turned one vague edit into four precise
ones, and is the only reason O-18 got tested rather than restated.

### What each page gained

A section, placed above the previous "since version" section so the newest
reading is first:

  - the four-run ensemble table for that fixture;
  - the published ratios restated with bars, and what they are in sigma
    (hiipdr 15-300, pn150k 20-250);
  - D-314's 37% retired, with the reason it was never the production noise
    floor;
  - the D-334 `ionDenPrev` defect stated plainly - read and never written, a
    quarter of uninitialised memory into `ionDen` on four of every five
    coupling passes, in every PDR run this project has made - together with its
    **measured null effect** on that fixture and the mechanism (`updateCell`
    rebuilds `ionDen` each MC iteration, so 22 or 9 iterations converge out of
    what 6 do not);
  - and on the PN page, the residual the fix does leave: PE heating 0.6-1.0%
    higher at every depth, same sign at all five, real and negligible.

### O-18 refuted, not closed

The retest cost no run - the D-335 ensemble already held it. Across four seeds,
at A_V 1.5, 2.1, 2.5 and 2.9:

    species   spread across seeds    max/min
    CO           0.24 - 0.68%        1.006 - 1.016
    OH           0.16 - 1.10%        1.003 - 1.025
    C            0.01 - 7.14%        1.000 - 1.182
    C+           0.00 - 0.64%        1.000 - 1.015
    H2           0.00 - 0.04%        1.000 - 1.001

against the recorded **25x**. The only species with real scatter is neutral
carbon at A_V 2.10, at 7.1% - the steep part of the C+ -> C transition, where a
finite bin samples a large gradient, and where L-3 lives. Everything else is at
or below the temperature's own noise. The 25x belonged to an older code state:
before line transport, before the dust fix, and with path biasing on. It is
marked REFUTED on the page with the measurement beside it, rather than deleted.

### O-25 half closed, deliberately

MOCASSIN now has four runs of each fixture; **Cloudy still has one.** So every
bar published on either page is MOCASSIN's alone, and both pages say so in the
same paragraph as the bars. Bounding the Cloudy side is left open under O-25
rather than quietly dropped.

Both pages also carry the caution from D-336: with bars this tight, three parts
in a thousand reads as several sigma, and significance is not size.

## D-338 - The slabs demoted, and what that leaves (2026-09-24)

The user's call, after D-337: `v1slab`, `v2slab` and `ifront` are 1D slab
fixtures and sit outside the 3D scope this version of MOCASSIN is being taken
to production for, so they drop to low priority. L-11 is updated; they stay in
the tree as regression fixtures rather than as validation targets.

Agreed. They were carried in the register as an outstanding validation item
largely because they had been outstanding for a long time, which is not the
same as their being on the path.

### What it does not dispose of

D-333's Tier 1 item 2 asked for a third and fourth fixture for a specific
reason: the two in hand disagree about what the code does. hiipdr crosses
Cloudy near A_V 1.3 and moved 28% under the sticking fix; pn150k never crosses,
sits uniformly at 0.63-0.75 of Cloudy, and moved 5%. Two fixtures that
contradict each other cannot say which behaviour is the code's and which is the
model's. That need stands. What the user's call changes is that the answer has
to be a **3D** fixture.

### Which existing fixtures qualify: none, and the reason matters

    fixture    geometry       density
    hiipdr     symmetricXYZ   Hdensity 100   (uniform)
    pn150k     symmetricXYZ   Hdensity 1000  (uniform)
    ifront     -              densityFile 'input/front.den'
    v1slab     -              densityFile 'input/v1.den'
    v2slab     -              densityFile 'input/v1.den'

The only fixtures in the tree with a structured density are exactly the three
just demoted, and those are 1D. So:

**Every PDR result this project has published comes from a spherically
symmetric, uniform-density model run in a 3D Monte Carlo code.**

That reframes L-4/O-14. The 3D self-shielding tracer is not untested because a
test was run and came out badly; it is untested because **no fixture in the set
can test it.** With one column per direction and every direction identical, the
HEALPix ray average has nothing to average - it returns the 1D answer by
construction, and would do so even if the tracer were wrong. A passing result
on either production fixture carries no information about it.

The consequence is worth stating in one sentence: **the one capability that
distinguishes MOCASSIN from a 1D photoionization code is the one the validation
set cannot reach.**

### What Tier 1 item 2 becomes

A fixture to be *built*, not a run to be launched. It needs structure that
makes direction matter - an asymmetric shell, a clump, a density gradient
across the grid - so that the column to the star genuinely differs by ray. The
two existing 3D fixtures already span a useful range in the other parameters
(40 kK against 150 kK, n_H 100 against 1000, silicate against graphite, A_V 3
against 0.68), so the third should vary geometry rather than adding another
point in that space.

Two things to decide when it is built, recorded now so they are decided rather
than defaulted: what the reference is (Cloudy is 1D and cannot supply one for
an asymmetric model, so the comparison would have to be internal - for instance
the same mass in a smooth shell against a clumped one), and whether it is sized
to run in the ~1.5 h that makes a four-seed ensemble affordable, which D-334
now makes the natural unit of evidence.

Not started. Recorded as the next thing, with its shape settled.

## D-339 - What the 3D self-shielding tracer actually does (2026-09-24)

The user asked me to explain D-338's claim that L-4/O-14 is untested because no
fixture can test it. Reading the code and O-14's own register row, instead of
reasoning from the geometry, showed the claim was wrong in three ways. D-338's
account is withdrawn.

### O-14 is a diagnosis, not a gap

Its row, verbatim:

> **3D self-shielding tracer not fit to be the only geometry.** No reflection
> at mirror walls, slab rays truncated at 59% of depth, isotropic chi/12
> weighting of a one-sided field, HEALPix rings about z (D-259).
> **Next:** Fix the tracer, decide the angular model, then make PDRGEOM=3D the
> single flavour.

Four named, measured defects. "Untested" was the opposite of the truth, and
D-338's proposed next step - build a structured 3D fixture - contradicts
O-14's own ordering, which puts fixing the tracer first. A defect already
measured does not need a new fixture to reveal it.

### What is on the path, and what is not

`calc_columndens` / `raytheia` (`source/pdr/columndensity.F90`, under
`RAYTHEIA_MO`) is the vendored 3D-PDR tracer, and it is **dead in this build**:
its only caller is 3D-PDR's own `chemicaliterations.F90`. MOCASSIN drives
`pdrStep` per cell and never enters it. I found that file first and wrote
D-338 partly from it.

What MOCASSIN actually runs is its own tracer, `computeRayColumns`
(`pdr_mod.f90:1467`, D-190): twelve HEALPix nside=1 directions per cell, walked
outward through the real grid once per MC iteration, accumulating N(H2), N(C),
N(CO) and A_V along each.

So D-338's "the ray average has nothing to average" was wrong. The twelve
columns differ from one another even in a spherically symmetric model, because
the distance to the boundary depends on direction - and D-190 shows that
mattered a great deal. Before it, all twelve rays were given the single
source-ward column, which over-shielded the illuminated face and pinned x(H2)
near 0.04 where 3D-PDR gives 1.6e-6.

### Which of the three per-ray arrays is actually directional

`CALCULATE_REACTION_RATES` takes three arrays of length 12:

    radSurf(0:11) = chi/12            ! pdr_mod.f90:2545  - ISOTROPIC
    AVray(0:11)   = av                ! pdr_mod.f90:2546  - one scalar, x12
    colH2/colCO/colC(0:11)            ! pdr_mod.f90:2694  - RAY-TRACED

Only the shielding columns carry direction. The first two are uniform by
design (D-001/D-026): giving every ray chi/12 and the same effective A_V makes
3D-PDR's internal `sum_k alpha*rad_surface(k)*exp(-gamma*AV(k))` collapse
exactly to `alpha*chi*exp(-gamma*A_V,eff)`, so MOCASSIN's Monte Carlo field and
its own grain extinction own the attenuation rather than 3D-PDR re-deriving it.
A per-ray A_V *is* computed - `colRayAV` at :1537 - and never reaches the rate
routine.

That is the "isotropic chi/12 weighting of a one-sided field" in O-14. In a
centrally-illuminated nebula the FUV arrives from one direction; the model
gives a twelfth of it to each of twelve directions and then shields each with
its own column. Defensible as an effective treatment in a symmetric model, and
without justification in an asymmetric one.

### The defect that is live right now

The ray walk terminates at the grid boundary:

    if (px < xAxis(1) .or. px > xAxis(nx) .or. ...) exit    ! :1515-1521

with no reflection. Both production fixtures are `symmetricXYZ` - octants with
mirror walls at x=0, y=0, z=0. Of the twelve HEALPix RING directions, the four
at mu = -2/3 all point downward through the z=0 mirror, and rays 6 and 7 point
through the x=0 and y=0 mirrors. **Roughly half the rays terminate early on
every run this project has published.**

A truncated column *under*-shields. That raises the photodissociation rate on
those rays, which suppresses H2 and CO. D-259 measured the truncation at 59%
of depth.

So this is not a future concern and not a fixture problem. It is a defect in
current results, on the two models both artifacts are drawn from, and an
asymmetric fixture would not touch it. Whether it is worth much is unmeasured:
the H/H2 crossing agrees with Cloudy to 7% on hiipdr and is 32% off on pn150k,
and nobody has asked how much of that is this.

### What replaces D-338's next step

O-14's ordering stands: fix the tracer, decide the angular model, then make
`PDRGEOM=3D` the single flavour. The cheapest first measurement is to add
mirror reflection to `computeRayColumns` and re-run one fixture at a fixed
seed, which after D-334 is an exact comparison - no Monte Carlo noise in the
difference at all.

The structured-3D fixture of D-338 is still wanted eventually, for L-4's other
half - the angular model - but it is second, not first.

---

## D-340 - Mirror reflection in computeRayColumns (2026-09-24)

O-14's first named defect, taken in O-14's own order. Written up after D-341,
because the commit that landed the code carried no DEVLOG entry - see the
process note at the end.

### The defect

`computeRayColumns` walked each of twelve HEALPix rays outward and stopped at
the grid boundary:

    if (px < xAxis(1) .or. px > xAxis(nx) .or. ...) exit

`symmetricXYZ` builds axes as `xAxis(i) = (i-1)/(nx-1)*Rnx`, so the grid is an
octant with x = y = z = 0 as **planes of symmetry**, not edges. Of the twelve
RING directions, the four at mu = -2/3 point down through the z = 0 plane and
rays 6 and 7 through x = 0 and y = 0. About half the rays were being cut off at
a wall that is not a wall. D-259 measured the truncation at 59% of depth.

A truncated column **under**-shields, so the photodissociation rate comes out
too high and H2 and CO too low.

### The change

A ray crossing a plane of symmetry continues into gas identical to the gas it
just left, so folding the sample point about the plane samples exactly that:

    if (lgSymmetricXYZ) then
       if (px < xlo) px = 2.d0*xlo - px
       if (py < ylo) py = 2.d0*ylo - py
       if (pz < zlo) pz = 2.d0*zlo - pz
    end if

One fold per axis is exact rather than approximate: each coordinate is
monotonic along a straight ray, so it crosses each plane at most once and the
fold holds for every later step. The **upper** faces stay terminal - they are
the edge of the model. The walk was lengthened to `2*dmax`, because in the
unfolded picture a reflected ray runs through the mirrored octants as well and
would otherwise run out of steps before leaving.

### The prediction, committed before the run

`tools/d340_mirror.py`: columns can only grow, so the gas is better shielded,
H2 and CO form **shallower**, and the H/H2 crossing moves to **smaller** A_V.
Falsified by the crossing moving deeper, by H2 or CO falling, or by the
ionization front or the dust temperature moving. Size deliberately not
predicted - D-259's 59% truncation converts into abundance through a steeply
non-linear self-shielding curve.

The comparison run used `randomSeed 1001` to match `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001`, so
the difference would carry no Monte Carlo noise at all.

### Outcome

The change is correct and was **entirely inert**: D-341 found that the arrays it
writes are never allocated, so this prediction is **untested** - neither
confirmed nor refuted.

### Process note

This entry exists only because D-341 needed to reference it. The commit that
landed the fix (`53d9400`) contained the code and the prediction tool and no
DEVLOG entry. The standing rule is that every decision gets an entry as it
lands; skipping it left the prediction living in a docstring, and for one commit
the history did not record what had changed or why. Recorded rather than
quietly backfilled.

---

## D-341 - The mirror fix was inert, and why (2026-09-25)

`runs/d340-mirror` finished and came back **byte-identical to
`runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001` in all seven output files** - `grid1`, `grid2`,
`grid3`, `temperature`, `thermBudget`, `pdrGrid`, `lineFlux`.

At a fixed seed that is not a small effect, it is a decisive null: the code I
had edited never ran. (Runtime differed - 1 h 22 against 1 h 48 - which is
machine load, not physics. The first s1001 run was the opening run of an
eight-run batch.)

### The cause, proved rather than inferred

The Makefile compiles `source/grid_mod.f90` with the generic rule:

    %.o: %.f90 .pdrflag Makefile
        $(FC) $(FFLAGS) $< -c -o $@

`$(PDRFLAGS)` - which is where `RAYTHEIA` is defined - is attached to exactly
three targets: `source/pdr_mod.o`, `source/pdrSmokeTest.o` and
`source/pdr/%.o`. `grid_mod.f90` is not one of them.

Preprocessing settles it:

    occurrences of colRayH2 in the preprocessed grid_mod.f90
      with the flags the build actually uses   0
      with -DRAYTHEIA added                    4

So both of grid_mod's allocation blocks - one in the grid build, one in
`resetGrid` for the warm start - were compiled away in **every build this
project has ever made**. Therefore:

  - `colRayH2/C/CO/AV` were never allocated;
  - `computeRayColumns` ran every iteration and hit
    `if (.not.allocated(grid(iG)%colRayH2)) cycle` for every grid, doing
    nothing;
  - `pdrStep`'s `if (allocated(grid%colRayH2))` override never fired, so
    `colH2 = sH2` stood - the single source-ward slab scalar, copied to all
    twelve rays.

**Nothing failed loudly.** An unallocated allocatable reports `.false.`; there
is no error, no warning, no crash. The feature reported itself absent and the
absence looked like a correct guard.

### What it corrects

**D-339 is corrected.** It said "only the shielding columns are directional".
They are not. All three per-ray arrays reaching `CALCULATE_REACTION_RATES` -
`radSurf = chi/12`, `AVray = av`, and the columns - are twelve copies of one
number. **There is no directional shielding anywhere in this build.** The
slab-equivalent treatment described in `pdrStep`'s D-001/D-026 comment is the
whole of it, and the comment at the column assignment describing what "the
traced values give each ray" is describing something that has never happened.

**D-190 gets a caveat, not a retraction.** Its index row claims mean Te -23%,
per-iteration change 26.8% -> 6.9%, and the two-cell front oscillation gone.
That change bundled three things: un-blanking 11 of 12 rays, dividing the
escape probability, and the per-ray columns. The first two live in `pdr_mod`
and `source/pdr/`, which do receive the flag, so they were live. The measured
-23% is real; it simply **cannot be attributed to the per-ray columns**, which
never ran. D-190's headline named them first.

### The fix

The arrays are now allocated in `computeRayColumns` itself - the file where the
flag that guards the feature actually arrives - and grid_mod's two dead blocks
are replaced by signposts saying why a `RAYTHEIA`-guarded block cannot work
there. Allocation and use now sit in one file under one flag, which is the only
arrangement the Makefile's scoping cannot silently break.

### How widespread is the trap

A sweep of every file built by the generic rule for macros defined only in
`PDRFLAGS` (`RAYTHEIA`, `RAYTHEIA_MO`, `THERMALBALANCE`, `REDUCED`,
`H2FORM_CT02`, `CHEMSTEADY`, `CHEMRETRY`, `FORCECONVERGENCE`, `NGACCEL`,
`NGCYCLE`, `NGRELAX`, `ILLINOIS`, `REBRACKET`, `SOBOLEV`, `ONEDIMENSIONAL`,
`GRAINRECOMB`, `BALG`) returns exactly two files:

  - `common_mod.f90` - which hit this trap and worked around it, declaring the
    fields unconditionally with a note at the declaration saying that
    PDRGEOMFLAG does not reach its compilation;
  - `grid_mod.f90` - where nobody noticed.

So the trap was known, documented in one file, and live in the one next to it.

### Attribution, deliberately split

Turning the arrays on and adding mirror reflection in one step would confound
two changes that have never been measured. Two runs at `randomSeed 1001`:

  - `runs/d341-percol` - per-ray columns live, fold disabled. Tests D-190's
    never-tested third component.
  - `runs/d341-mirror` - per-ray columns live plus the fold. Isolates O-14's
    first defect against the former.

The fold was disabled for the first by a throwaway experiment binary built from
a temporarily edited source, not by a keyword: the shipped source carries no
switch, and the binary rebuilt from the restored source is byte-identical to the
one used for the second run. Both runs are in flight.

---

## D-342 - The two halves of O-14 are a matched pair (2026-09-25)

With D-341's allocation in place, the per-ray columns ran for the first time.
Two runs at `randomSeed 1001`, each an exact comparison with no Monte Carlo
noise in the difference:

  - `runs/d341-percol` - per-ray columns live, mirror fold off
  - `runs/d341-mirror` - per-ray columns live, mirror fold on

### Turning the per-ray columns on destroys the PDR

`runs/d341-percol` against `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001`:

    A_V    x(H2) new/old   x(CO) new/old   x(C) new/old   T_gas new/old
    0.83       0.002           0.077          1.051           0.919
    1.13       0.000           0.035          1.142           0.875
    1.55       0.001           0.078          1.255           0.861
    2.11       0.012           0.230          1.347           1.146
    2.89       0.208           0.661          1.057           1.674

    H/H2 crossing   A_V 1.168  ->  never
    ionization front  3.8416   ->  3.8820 pc   (+1.05%, should not move)
    dust temperature  0.996 - 1.000            (correctly unmoved)

The molecular zone is gone. Hydrogen never reaches 2n(H2) = n(H) anywhere, so
there is no H/H2 transition to speak of, and the deep gas runs 18.9 K where it
ran 11.3 K because the coolants that set that temperature are no longer there.

**And the run looked better while being worse.** Convergence went from 74.86% to
92.07% and the wall time from 1 h 48 to 18 minutes. That is the D-176..D-181
lesson in new clothes: a PDR with no molecules has no stiff chemistry left to
solve, so both the convergence fraction and the speed improved *because the
physics had gone away*. If this had been judged on the KPIs it would have
looked like the best run of the cycle.

### Why - arithmetic, not opinion

`radSurf(k) = chi/12` on all twelve rays. With the slab-equivalent column on
all twelve as well, the rate sums to

    sum_k (chi/12) * exp(-gamma*A_V) * shield(N_source)
      = chi * exp(-gamma*A_V) * shield(N_source)

which is exactly the right one-dimensional answer. Twelve identical rays each
carrying a twelfth of the field **are** the one physical ray. The pairing that
looked like a lazy approximation is in fact self-consistent.

Now give each ray its own traced column and leave the field isotropic. The six
or seven rays pointing *out* of the cloud have almost no column in front of
them, so `shield ~ 1`, and each delivers its full `chi/12` unattenuated at every
depth. That invents FUV arriving from outside the nebula, where there is no
source. Deep in the cloud `shield(N) ~ 1e-5`, so the dissociation rate rises by
roughly four orders of magnitude and H2 cannot form. The measured collapse of
500-1000x is the size this predicts.

So the "slab-equivalent columns" and the "isotropic chi/12 field" are not two
independent defects in O-14's list. **They are a matched pair, and either one
alone is worse than both together.**

It is therefore fortunate that D-190's columns were dead. Had grid_mod's
allocation compiled, hiipdr would have had no molecular zone since 2026-09-08
and every PDR comparison published since would have been drawn on a model with
no H2.

### O-14's ordering, corrected again

D-339 said the tracer should be fixed before the angular model, following
O-14's own "Next". That is now measured to be backwards: **`rad_surface` has to
know which direction the star is in before a per-ray column means anything.**
The angular model comes first, or the two change together.

For a central point source the physical decomposition is not difficult to
state: the direct stellar field arrives along one direction, `-r_hat`, with the
source-ward column in front of it, and the diffuse field is the part that is
genuinely closer to isotropic. MOCASSIN holds those two separately already.
Writing that down is the next design question, and it is a design question, not
a patch.

### The mirror fold, finally live, is worth almost nothing

`runs/d341-mirror` against `runs/d341-percol`: every abundance 0.986 - 1.010,
dust temperature 1.0000 - 1.0004, ionization front identical to four digits,
temperatures within 0.25%. Runtime 18 -> 23 minutes, the cost of walking the
reflected rays.

So O-14's first named defect is far smaller than its third, and **D-340's
prediction is neither confirmed nor refuted: it is untestable in a model with
no molecular zone.** There is no H/H2 crossing left for it to move. It stays
open, to be read once the angular model makes a molecular zone exist again.

### What was reverted, and what was kept

Reverted: `pdrStep`'s per-ray override, and the call to `computeRayColumns` -
which was costing twelve ray walks per cell per iteration, about a quarter of
runtime, for output nothing consumed. Both replaced by comments carrying the
measurement above, so the next reader finds the result rather than the
temptation.

Kept: D-341's lazy allocation, so grid_mod's landmine stays disarmed; and
`computeRayColumns` itself, correct and with its mirror reflection, for the
angular-model work.

### Not separately excluded

A scale error inside the tracer - wrong `ds` units, a missing conversion -
would look much like this, and has not been ruled out independently.
Comparing `colRayAV` against the cell's own A_V would settle it in one run,
since the two are computed from the same path with the same step. The
incoherence above accounts for the observed size on its own, so this is listed
as the check to run before the angular-model work, not as a competing
explanation.

### Verification

With the revert, hiipdr at seed 1001 must reproduce `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001`
**byte-identically** - the revert restores the exact validated state or it does
not. `runs/d342-revert` is in flight.

## D-343 - The revert verifies, and the design premise is corrected (2026-09-25)

### The revert verifies

`runs/d342-revert` against `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001`, same seed, same input:
**15 of 17 output files byte-identical**, and the per-iteration convergence
trace matches on all 22 iterations to nine digits. The D-342 revert restored the
exact validated state, not merely something close to it. Before the seed keyword
existed three days ago this question could only have been answered "within the
scatter", and the scatter figure available was 37% and wrong.

Two files differ. `summary.out` is wall-clock timestamps. `SED.out` has **all
2400 spectral entries identical** and one changed line:

    Final SEDratio:    1.12103877E-44     (d342-revert)
    Final SEDratio:   -2.51470980E+36     (s1001)

for a quantity defined as a ratio of two luminosities. `SEDratio` is assigned
inside `do imu = 1, nAngleBins` and printed after the loop. Every PDR fixture
configures no viewpoints, so `nAngleBins = 0`, the loop body never ran, and the
print read an uninitialised local.

It is harmless: the same loop that assigns it is the loop that would divide the
SED by it, so the spectral columns never touched it. But it is the **third
uninitialised read found this session** - after `ionDenPrev` (D-334) and the
dead allocation blocks of D-341 - and it made the byte-identity test
permanently dirty, which is the one test the seed keyword exists to enable.
Initialised to 1 with the measurement recorded at the site.

### The design premise was wrong, and the user caught it first

I had read `chiFUV` as the direct stellar field alone, because
`mocassinToPDR` builds it as

    uFUV = sum over FUV bins of Jste(cell,ifreq)
    if (lgDebug) uFUV = uFUV + Jdif(cell,ifreq)

and `lgDebug` is off. The user pointed out that **`Jste` already carries the
diffuse packets summed into it**; `Jdif` is a *mirrored subset* kept as a
diagnostic (D-158), not a separate term waiting to be added.

That changes what the work is. The diffuse component is **not missing from the
magnitude**: `chiFUV` is the total local field, and the D-026 inversion folds
scattering into `A_V,eff` - an effective extinction smaller than the true dust
column precisely because scattered light arrives. What is wrong is only its
**direction**: the diffuse part is given the source-ward molecular column for
its line shielding, when physically it arrives from many directions with
different H2 in front of each.

This also makes the split far safer than D-342's failure implies. There, **all**
of the field was spread isotropically over twelve rays, six of which had no
column, so half the field arrived unshielded at every depth and H2 died. Here
only the genuinely diffuse **fraction** is treated that way, so the size of any
such effect is bounded by that fraction rather than being the whole field.

### The design, recorded before implementation

Thirteen rays rather than twelve:

    ray 12   direct   radSurf = chiFUV0            (analytic unattenuated stellar)
                      AVray   = A_V,eff            (source-ward)
                      cols    = sH2/sCO/sC         (source-ward)

    rays 0-11 diffuse radSurf = chi_dif/12
                      AVray   = 0                  (the MC already attenuated it;
                                                    attenuating again double-counts dust)
                      cols    = colRay{H2,CO,C}(k) (traced per direction)

Two properties this has to keep. It must **reduce to today's calculation** as
the diffuse fraction goes to zero - it does, because ray 12 *is* today's
calculation. And it must **conserve the measured field**: that requires the
direct ray's effective `A_V` to be inverted against `Jste - Jdif` rather than
against `Jste`, or the total will be counted as more than the Monte Carlo
measured.

`A_V = 0` on the diffuse rays is the part most likely to be questioned later, so
the reason is recorded here: 3D-PDR's `rad_surface(k)` is a *boundary* value and
`AV(k)` transports it inward, whereas MOCASSIN hands over a *local* intensity
that has already been through the full dust transfer. The line shielding still
has to be applied, because MOCASSIN's dust RT knows nothing about H2 lines -
hence columns but no extinction.

### The blocking unknown, and why nothing is implemented yet

`Jdif` is reset and MPI-reduced **only** when `pdrSplitField /= 0` or debug is
on, both off by default. Left alone it is stale across iterations and carries
roughly one rank's share - D-225 already hit this, reporting a "diffuse
fraction" of ~0.07 whatever the truth was.

So the size of the entire effect is currently unknown, and building the
machinery before measuring it would repeat D-342's mistake in a new place. Two
cheap steps instead:

  - a `chi_dif` column added to `pdrFUV.out`, documented in the file's own
    header as meaningless unless one of those switches is set;
  - `runs/d343-diffuse`: hiipdr at seed 1001 with `pdrSplitField 1`.

That one run answers two questions. It gives the diffuse fraction against depth,
which sizes the design. And byte-comparing its physics outputs against s1001
tests whether `pdrSplitField` is genuinely physics-neutral, which the code
claims ("Diagnostic only: nothing reads Jdif for physics unless lgDebug") and
which has never been checked.

No field-splitting code written yet, deliberately.

---

## D-344 - The diffuse fraction, and what it does to the design (2026-09-25)

`runs/d343-diffuse`: hiipdr, seed 1001, `pdrSplitField 1`, 22 iterations,
74.8553009%, 1 h 22 min.

### pdrSplitField is physics-neutral, now checked

All 22 iterations match `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001` to nine digits, and 14 of 17
output files are byte-identical. The three that differ: `summary.out`
(timestamps), `pdrFUV.out` (the `chi_dif` column added for this), and `SED.out`
in the single `SEDratio` line D-343 initialised. The switch resets and
MPI-reduces `Jdif` on every iteration while the chemistry is live and moves
nothing. The code asserted this ("Diagnostic only: nothing reads Jdif for
physics") and nobody had tested it.

### The measurement

Diffuse fraction of the FUV field, `chi_dif/chi_MC`, over 15204 cells:

    A_V range     cells    chi_MC      chi_dif     diffuse fraction
    0.00 - 0.20      43   9.614e+02   3.030e+02        0.346
    0.20 - 0.47     104   2.396e+02   1.371e+02        0.572
    0.47 - 0.80     440   4.622e+01   3.365e+01        0.747
    0.80 - 1.20     938   1.003e+01   8.600e+00        0.866
    1.20 - 1.60    1514   2.899e+00   2.689e+00        0.929
    1.60 - 2.10    3129   8.440e-01   8.125e-01        0.966
    2.10 - 2.60    4851   2.440e-01   2.404e-01        0.991
    2.60 - 3.05    4185   9.151e-02   9.061e-02        1.000

Monotonic, and physically what it should be: the direct beam is extinguished
exponentially while the scattered field is replenished from every side, so
**deep PDR gas sees essentially no direct starlight.** In the PDR proper
(A_V > 0.47) the field is 75% to 100% diffuse.

So the angular question is not a few-per-cent effect to be closed as
negligible. It is most of the field.

### And the measurement kills D-343's design

D-343 specified the diffuse rays as carrying `chi_dif/12` with the column
traced **outward** from the cell to the grid boundary. That column measures only
the *last leg* of a scattered photon's path.

A photon scattered near the outer edge and travelling inward crossed the inward
column from the star **before** it scattered, and none of that H2 appears in the
outward trace. Using the outward column therefore under-counts the H2 the
photon actually passed through - which is exactly the error D-342 measured, with
H2 falling 500-1000x and the molecular zone disappearing.

Turning the diffuse fraction from 100% (D-342, all rays) to 75-100% (this
design) does not rescue it. The mistake is in the column, not the weighting.

The corollary is worth stating plainly: **the slab-equivalent treatment is a
better approximation than it looks.** The dominant H2 column along almost any
FUV photon's path is the inward leg from the star, which is the leg the
slab-equivalent column measures and shares with the direct beam. Proper
treatment needs the line-absorption history accumulated along each packet's
path - a Monte Carlo problem MOCASSIN is actually equipped for, since it
transports the packets - not a twelve-ray post-hoc geometry.

### A sharper question displaces it

The band in use is bins 384-420, 0.4537 - 0.9997 Ryd, i.e. 2010 - 912 A. But
the reactions that matter live in a narrower window:

    H2 Lyman-Werner        1110 - 912 A     0.821 - 0.999 Ryd
    CO dissociation        1076 - 912 A     0.847 - 0.999 Ryd
    C I ionization         1101 A           0.828 Ryd
    ------------------------------------------------------------
    Lyman alpha            1216 A           0.7496 Ryd   <- inside the band,
                                                            BELOW the window

If the diffuse FUV is Lyman-alpha dominated - which an H II region makes likely,
and which D-303/D-304's existing Lya correction against Cloudy already hints at
- then the single band-integrated `chi` handed to every photoreaction is
**inflated for precisely the reactions it is used for**, by a component that
cannot drive them. The model would over-dissociate H2.

That is consistent with something already on the hiipdr page: the H/H2 crossing
sits at A_V 1.17 against Cloudy's 1.09, so MOCASSIN's H2 forms slightly too
deep - the direction too much dissociation would give.

**Falsifiable, and cheap.** Dump `Jdif` per frequency bin across 384-420 for a
handful of cells and see whether the diffuse excess is concentrated in the Lya
bin or spread across the band. If it is Lya, the fix is spectral - use the
Lyman-Werner sub-band for the molecular rates - and the angular model is a
second-order concern behind it. If it is spread, the angular model stands as
the next item and needs the path-history approach above, not twelve rays.

That measurement comes first. No field-splitting code written.

---

## D-345 - The diffuse FUV is scattered continuum, and the bracket on the angular model is wide (2026-09-25)

`runs/d345-fuvspec`: hiipdr, seed 1001, `pdrSplitField 1`, 22 iterations,
74.8553009%, 1 h 42 min. Every iteration matches `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001` to
nine digits, so the dump added here is physics-neutral.

### The prediction, and its refutation

The prediction - corrected once, before any result existed, after the user asked
whether this had been investigated before - was that the diffuse excess would
sit red of the Lyman-Werner window, carried by the optically thin diffuse lines
MOCASSIN transports (C III] 0.477, He II 0.556, C IV 0.588, C II 0.683 Ryd).
Signature: f_LW much smaller than f_band.

    shell  cells | f_band   f_LW   f_LW/f_band | Lya bin share of diffuse
        1     13 | 0.1713  0.1417     0.827    |  0.0176
        2     19 | 0.3279  0.2805     0.856    |  0.0170
        3     60 | 0.4775  0.4119     0.863    |  0.0157
        4    161 | 0.6305  0.5614     0.890    |  0.0142
        5    454 | 0.7611  0.6956     0.914    |  0.0123
        6   1212 | 0.8715  0.8094     0.929    |  0.0087
        7   3469 | 0.9456  0.8905     0.942    |  0.0047
        8   9816 | 0.9833  0.9596     0.976    |  0.0019

**Refuted.** `Jdif/Jste` is flat across the band - in the outermost shell it runs
0.99 at 0.454 Ryd to 0.93 at 0.999 Ryd, a mild blue-ward decline and nothing
more. The Lya bin carries 0.2-1.8% of the diffuse total, which is what D-291
predicted from the code (`ilow >= 2` excludes the Lyman series by construction)
and is now confirmed from MOCASSIN's own output rather than by inspection.

The diffuse FUV is **dust-scattered stellar continuum**. There is no spectral
inflation to fix. The band integral overstates the Lyman-Werner-relevant diffuse
content by 17% in the innermost shell - 13 cells, noisy - and by **2-9% through
the PDR proper**. Real, measured, and far too small to explain anything.

A useful cross-check falls out: `f_band` here, binned in log-radial shells,
runs 0.17 to 0.98, against D-344's 0.35 to 1.00 binned in A_V. Two different
binnings of two different runs agreeing in trend and magnitude.

### What is left, and why the bracket is alarming

The angular treatment. And both extremes are now measured on the same fixture at
the same seed, which is the first time this quantity has had any bracket at all:

    every ray gets the source-ward column   (today)   H/H2 crossing A_V 1.17
                                                      (Cloudy 1.09)
    every ray gets its own outward column   (D-342)   NO molecular zone

The truth lies in that interval, and the interval spans "a normal PDR" to "no
molecules". Since 75-100% of the PDR field is diffuse (D-344), the line
shielding of the scattered component is a **first-order control on molecular
content**, not a refinement.

The sign of the correction is not predictable from anything measured. A
scattered photon's path to a given cell is longer than the radial one, which
argues for more absorption, but part of it runs through gas that is less
molecular than the shielded interior, which argues for less. Both extremes are
wrong for the same reason - one uses only the inward leg, the other only the
outward leg - and neither bounds the answer tightly.

### Consequence for the production goal

D-331 and D-333 put molecular line observables - CO and H2 intensities - as the
thing this code is being taken to production for, with [C II] first because its
carrier is good to 1-3%. That ordering survives. What this measurement adds is
that **CO and H2 sit downstream of a quantity currently bracketed between
"normal" and "zero"**, and that was not visible before today.

[C II] is unaffected: C+ is the dominant carbon stage through the PDR, its
abundance was verified against 3D-PDR to 1-3% (D-333), and it does not depend on
line self-shielding the way H2 and CO do.

### The next step, stated but not started

H2 and CO line opacity accumulated along each packet's path during transport.
MOCASSIN is equipped for it - it already carries the packets and already
accumulates per-cell estimators - and a twelve-ray post-hoc geometry is not
(D-344). This is a design task in the transport, not a patch in the handoff.

Two cheaper things that would narrow the bracket first, either of which is worth
doing before the full implementation:

  - the check D-342 listed and did not do: compare `colRayAV` against the
    cell's own A_V, to confirm `computeRayColumns` has no scale error. If it
    does, one end of the bracket moves.
  - a single-scattering estimate: treat the diffuse field as scattered once, at
    a depth drawn from the local scattering rate, and use the column from the
    star to that point plus the column from there to the cell. That is a
    tractable approximation with the right limiting behaviour, and it would
    show whether the answer sits near the source-ward end or the outward end.
