## D-346 - H2 opacity exists, and D-100 already ruled out D-345's route (2026-09-25)

The user pointed out that H2 opacity has already been implemented. It has, and
the correction matters more than the fact.

### What is implemented, and where it sits

`yanH2xSec` (Yan, Sadeghpour & Dalgarno) at `ionization_mod.f90:385`, entering
the Monte Carlo opacity at :470 through `addOpacity`. It is the H2
**photoionization continuum**, and its own comment is explicit:

> Zero below the 15.4 eV threshold: H2 absorption in the 13.6-15.4 eV window is
> line opacity in the higher electronic bands, not a continuum, and Cloudy
> treats it that way too (D-139).

D-139 tried adding a continuum in 13.6-15.4 eV and reverted it, because Cloudy
puts zero there and nothing was leaking anyway.

The Lyman-Werner window is **0.821-0.999 Ryd = 11.2-13.6 eV**, entirely below
15.43 eV. So the implemented cross section returns exactly zero across the whole
band that dissociates H2. That is not an oversight - D-100 selected it for that
property:

> Its decisive property is *where it sits*: 15.43 eV is above the Lyman limit and
> far above the FUV band the PDR owns. **It cannot double-count against anything
> 3D-PDR is already doing** - and double-counting is the live hazard, not
> accuracy.

The hazard named there is D-050: handing the PDR an already-attenuated field
while its rate expressions re-apply `exp(-gamma*A_V)`.

### D-100 already answered what D-345 re-opened

Asked whether 3D-PDR's self-shielding function could serve as a MOCASSIN
opacity, D-100 said no, and gave three structural reasons:

1. **Column, not density.** The Monte Carlo accumulates `tau = sum kappa ds`
   cell by cell with no memory of what a packet already traversed. A shielding
   factor *is* that integral, already taken.
2. **Not an exponential**, so no `kappa` reproduces it. Defining
   `kappa_eff = -d ln f / dN` gives 3.22e-15 at N(H2) = 1e14 falling to
   6.90e-21 at 1e20 - a factor **4.7e5** - because absorption sits in ~30
   discrete bands whose cores black out early, after which the damping wings do
   the work. One opacity per frequency bin cannot represent a medium opaque at
   line centre and transparent between lines.
3. **No frequency resolution.** 17 bins across 912-1108 A, ~3564 km/s each,
   against a thermal H2 line width of ~0.9 km/s at 100 K.

### What that does to D-345's next step

D-345 said: "H2/CO line opacity accumulated along each packet's path during
transport." Read as *an opacity per frequency bin*, which is how it is written,
all three objections apply and it is refuted.

What survives - and what I should have written - is a different object: a
**per-packet accumulated-column estimator.** Each packet carries the H2 column
it has traversed, and contributes `weight x shield(N_traversed)` to a separate
dissociation-rate estimator. The band-integrated shielding function is applied
**per packet**, not to a mean column.

That answers each objection rather than evading it. It supplies exactly the
memory (1) identifies as missing. It never needs an exponential, because the
non-linear factor is evaluated once per packet at its own column (2). And it
needs no line resolution, because what is being weighted is the band-integrated
factor the chemistry already uses (3).

It is also honestly expensive: a new per-packet state variable carried through
`pathSegment`, and a new estimator array beside `Jste`/`Jdif`. A change to the
transport, not to the handoff.

D-345's *measurements* are untouched - the diffuse field is still scattered
continuum, still flat across the band, and the bracket on the angular treatment
is still "normal PDR" to "no molecules". Only the stated next step changes, and
the register entry that repeated it.

### Process

This is the third time this session that prior work has corrected a conclusion I
reached from the code in front of me: D-338/D-339 on what O-14 actually
contained, D-344/D-345 on Lyman alpha, and now D-100 on the H2 opacity route.
Each time the answer was already in the log, and each time the user found it
first. The log has 346 entries and searching it costs one grep. Searching before
proposing is the rule now, not the remedy after.

## D-347 - The angular model, specified (2026-09-25)

At the user's direction, and after they pointed out that my answers had become
circular. The specification below is theirs: one direct-to-source ray plus twelve
full-4pi HEALPix rays, through the ray tracer that already exists.

### The objection was never the rays - it was the column

`computeRayColumns` traces **cell -> outer boundary**. That column answers one
question: *how much is radiation arriving from outside attenuated on its way in?*

For 3D-PDR that is exactly the right question. Its FUV field is an external
boundary condition: `rad_surface(k)` is surface brightness in direction k,
streaming inward, and the ray column from the cell out to the surface is exactly
the attenuation it suffers. The tracer is correct for the geometry it was built
for.

Our geometry is the reverse. The star is **inside**, and the diffuse field is
produced by scattering **within** the cloud. So attaching a cell->boundary column
to 11 of 12 rays asserts illumination arriving from outside a nebula that has no
outside source. That is the entirety of D-342's result - H2 falling by a factor
500-1000 and the molecular zone vanishing - and it is why that experiment failed.
It is not an argument against 1 + 12 rays.

### The correct column is a two-leg path, and both legs already exist

A photon scattered at P and arriving at cell C has traversed

    N_eff  =  N(star -> P)  +  N(P -> C)

  - `N(star -> P)` is already stored **per cell** as `grid%pdrColH2`,
    `grid%pdrColC`, `grid%pdrColCO` (D-078). Inside the ray walk the step is
    always in a known cell `cP`, so this is a lookup, not a computation.
  - `N(P -> C)` is precisely what the loop already accumulates as `cH2`/`cC`/`cCO`.
  - the weight is the local scattering emissivity, and `scaOpac(cP)` is already
    read in that same loop, two lines below, to build `cAV`.

So per ray:

    sum_i  w_i * shield( pdrColH2(cP_i) + cH2_i )

evaluating the non-linear shielding factor **at each scattering site** rather
than once on a mean column. That is the property D-100 said a per-bin opacity
could not have, obtained without defining an opacity at all.

### The design

    ray 12    direct    weight 1 - f_dif    column: source-ward (today's)
    rays 0-11 diffuse   weight f_dif / 12   column: two-leg N_eff above

`f_dif` is not a free parameter. D-344 and D-345 measured it: 0.35 just inside
the front, rising monotonically to 1.00 at the far edge, and the diffuse light is
dust-scattered continuum, flat across the band, so a single band-integrated
weight is defensible.

Two properties to preserve, as in D-343: it must reduce to today's calculation as
`f_dif -> 0`, which it does because ray 12 *is* today's calculation; and the
weights must sum to the field the Monte Carlo actually measured, which requires
the direct ray's effective A_V to be inverted against `Jste - Jdif` rather than
against `Jste`.

### D-100's objections, checked one at a time

  1. *Function of the column, not the density; the MC has no memory.* Not hit:
     nothing here is a `kappa` multiplied by a path length. The column is
     constructed explicitly, per site, from two stored quantities.
  2. *Not an exponential.* Not hit: `shield()` is evaluated as itself, per site.
  3. *No frequency resolution.* Not hit: what is evaluated is the
     band-integrated factor the chemistry already uses.

### Withdrawn

D-346 concluded this needed "a new per-packet state variable carried through
`pathSegment`, and a new estimator array beside `Jste`/`Jdif` - a change to the
transport, not the handoff." **That is withdrawn.** It is a change inside
`computeRayColumns` plus the handoff in `pdrStep`, using arrays that already
exist. I reached the wrong conclusion by reasoning from `ionization_mod`, which I
had just been reading, instead of from what the ray tracer already held.

The per-packet estimator remains a valid and more general alternative - it would
handle multiple scatterings, which the two-leg form approximates as one - but it
is not the necessary route, and proposing it as such was over-engineering.

### Process

Three times this session a conclusion of mine was corrected by work already in
this log: D-338/D-339 on what O-14 contained, D-344/D-345 on Lyman alpha, and
D-346 on the opacity route. The user found each one. The common failure is not
forgetting - it is re-deriving from whichever file I had most recently opened
instead of from the design. Searching the log before proposing, and reading the
routine I intend to change before declaring what it cannot do.

### Status

Specified, not implemented. The test is already built: same fixture,
`randomSeed 1001`, exact comparison with no Monte Carlo noise, against both
measured extremes - source-ward-everything giving an H/H2 crossing at A_V 1.17,
and outward-everything giving no molecular zone at all.

## D-348 - The angular model, implemented; and D-342's collapse was mostly a rank-ownership defect (2026-09-25)

D-347 specified the angular model. This entry implements it, and records a
defect found while reading the code it replaces, which changes what D-342
measured.

### D-342's measurement ran on the wrong rank for 93% of the cells

`computeRayColumns` distributed its work by

    if (mod(cellP-(taskid+1), numtasks) /= 0) cycle        ! cellP = active index

while `iterateMC` distributes `pdrStep` by

    iCell = iCell+1                                        ! every (i,j,k), ACTIVE OR NOT
    if (mod(iCell-(taskid+1),numtasks)==0) call pdrStep(grid(iG),i,j,k)

and nothing reduced `colRayH2/C/CO/AV` between the two. Wherever inactive cells
exist, the two indices differ and a cell's columns were computed on one rank
and read on another, where the array still held the zeros it was allocated
with. hiipdr has `Rin` and a spherical `Rout` inside a cubic box, so 14587 of
29791 cells are inactive. Counted from `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001/output/grid0.out`:

    active cells                                      15204
    columns computed on the rank that read them        1011   (6.6%)
    read as zero on all twelve rays                   14193   (93.4%)

So in `runs/d341-percol` and `runs/d341-mirror`, 93% of the cells had **no
self-shielding at all** on any ray, and **optically thin line escape** on every
ray (`colRayAV = 0` gives `plen = 0` in the D-190 escape branch). D-342's
x(H2) x 0.002 and vanished molecular zone measured mostly that.

What this does and does not change:

  - **D-342's arithmetic stands.** Twelve `chi/12` rays each on its own
    cell->boundary column deliver the outward rays' share unshielded; that is
    a property of the formula, not of the run.
  - **D-342's measurement is withdrawn as a measurement of it.** The
    "outward-everything" extreme of D-345's bracket, and the second test
    target D-347 named, were never measured. The bracket's far end is unknown,
    not "no molecular zone".
  - **D-342's "the mirror fold is worth 0-1%" is withdrawn** for the same
    reason: 93% of the cells had zero columns with or without the fold.
    D-340's prediction stays untested.
  - D-342 listed "a scale error inside the tracer" as not excluded. It was not
    a scale error, but it was a tracer defect of exactly the kind that would
    look like the physics. The scale check itself is done below, on the new
    tracer.

The class is the D-341 class: nothing failed loudly. An array that is zero
where it should be a column is indistinguishable from a cell with nothing in
front of it.

### What was implemented

`computeRayColumns` and `nearestAxG` are removed, and with them the
`colRayH2/C/CO/AV` fields and the D-190 escape-probability branch that read
`colRayAV` when allocated (it was allocated only in the two D-341 runs, so every
other run has always taken the closed form that remains; no behaviour change).
In their place, in `pdr_mod.f90` under `RAYTHEIA`:

  - **`snapDiffuseSources`**, called at the top of `computeAVdust`, records per
    cell what the walk reads - shielding n(H2), n(C), n(CO) (zero outside the
    PDR zone, the D-088 rule), the FUV extinction `R_FUV*kappa_V` (D-109), and
    the FUV scattering emissivity `sum_nu kSca*J`. It is taken from the same
    abundances and zone flags the source-ward columns are integrated from, so
    the two legs agree. Reading the live `pdrAbun` instead would mix this
    coupling pass's values (cells this rank has solved) with the last pass's,
    and the answer would depend on the rank count and sweep order.
  - **`traceDiffuseSites`**, called per cell from `pdrStep` on the rank that
    consumes it - no ownership to get wrong, no per-(cell,ray) storage. Twelve
    HEALPix directions, the D-340 mirror fold, a bisection axis lookup. Every
    step is a scattering site with weight
    `w = S exp(-tau(C->P)) (1 - exp(-dtau))`, `S = emissivity/extinction` -
    the formal solution for isotropic scattering, from MOCASSIN's own grains
    and field - and two-leg columns `pdrColX(P) + N(P->C)`, the second leg
    excluding the target cell as the first does (D-088).
  - **`pdrStep`**: the chemistry now gets `12 + nSite` rays. Slots 0-11 are
    today's direct ray exactly (`chi0/12`, source-ward A_V and columns), kept
    as twelve twelfths so that with no diffuse field every rate sum is the old
    sum plus exact zeros. Each site is a ray of its own carrying
    `chi_dif * w_i / sum(w)`, `A_V = 0`, and its two-leg columns, so the vendored
    `H2SHIELD1`, `COSHIELD` and C I band are each evaluated per site on the
    site's own columns - never on a mean column (D-100). `chi_dif` is the MC's
    diffuse FUV in the cell, from `Jdif`.
  - **`Jdif` is live in every PDR run** (`lgJdifLive`, derived in `readInput`,
    not a keyword): mirrored in `photon_mod` and now also `fluorescence_mod`,
    reset, reduced and scaled in `iterateMC`. D-344 measured the mirroring
    physics-neutral by itself. Every physics read of `Jdif` elsewhere is
    behind `lgDebug`, checked site by site.
  - A cell with diffuse field but no scattering site on any direction (no
    dust) carries `chi_dif` on the source-ward column and is counted (`fb`).
    It has not occurred.
  - `[D348]` diagnostics per A_V bin, printed once per MC iteration after the
    last coupling pass.

The 1D flavour (`ONEDIMENSIONAL`) is unchanged: no diffuse rays, byte-for-byte
today's chemistry. All four flavours compile.

### One departure from D-347, deliberately

D-347 wrote `f_dif/12` per direction. That assumes the diffuse field isotropic,
which is the half of O-14's matched pair D-342 identified as the defect, and
the walk already computes each direction's formal-solution intensity. So the
MC sets the magnitude (`chi_dif`) and the walk distributes it over directions
and sites by weight. The smoke test measures the diffuse field as markedly
anisotropic - the brightest of the twelve directions carries **1.9-3.1x** the
mean - so the choice matters. The `R_difIso` column reports what the literal
`f_dif/12` split would give on the same sites, so the departure is measured,
not asserted; reverting it is one line.

(`chi_*` in Draine units; `dir_MC = chi_MC - chi_dif`; `dir_ext` is `chi0` on
MOCASSIN's own extinction over the source-ward A_V; `dir_3DPDR` is what the
direct ray hands H2, `chi0*SCATTER(A_V, 1000 A)`; `R_*` are H2
photodissociation rates per unit alpha from the vendored `H2PDRATE`: direct,
diffuse on the source-ward column, diffuse on the two-leg columns.) No
fallback cells, no unset first legs, clean exit, 20 min.

What it says:

  1. **The tracer's scale is right.** Walked from the cell to the star with
     the new stepping, N(H2) and A_V agree with `computeAVradial`'s
     independent star-to-cell trace to **0.2-2%** wherever the column spans
     more than a few cells (the shallow bins differ by step placement over a
     column of one or two cells). This is D-342's listed check, done.
  2. **The chemistry now sees the MC's field.** Direct prescription plus
     `chi_dif` against `chi_MC`, in the H2 band: **+0% / +6% / +8% / +4% /
     +2% / ~0 / ~0 / ~0** by bin. So the concern that 3D-PDR's `SCATTER`
     (which carries its own FRR80 slab scattering) double-counts scattered
     light is bounded at **8%**. Before this, the heating took `chi_MC` and
     the reaction rates a field ~100x smaller at depth: two realities of one
     field.
  3. **The effect is the magnitude, not the angle.** At fixed abundances the
     H2 rate rises **x3.4** (A_V 0.8-1.2), **x8.6** (1.2-1.6), **x19**
     (1.6-2.1), **x60** (2.1-2.6), **x170** (2.6-3.05). The two-leg columns
     take back only **5-32%** of the diffuse part against the source-ward
     column (`R_dif2leg/R_difSrc` 0.68-0.95). D-344's corollary - "the
     slab-equivalent treatment is a better approximation than it looks" -
     holds for the column. What was missing was the field.
  4. **The formal solution recovers 53-130% of the MC's diffuse field**
     (`chi_pred/chi_dif` 1.30 at the front falling to 0.53 at A_V ~2.8). Right
     order everywhere, so no scale error; but it falls short deep, and that is
     **not explained**. Candidates, none tested: gas FUV emission the walk
     does not model (H two-photon continuum from the H II region falls partly
     in 6-10.2 eV); the isotropic phase function against the grains' g = 0.35;
     twelve directions as quadrature for an intensity that peaks star-ward.
     It does not enter the physics - the MC sets the magnitude - only the
     relative weights.
  5. **`dir_MC` exceeds `dir_ext` increasingly with depth** (1.04 at the
     front, ~4 at A_V 2.8). There `dir_MC` is the difference of two estimators
     1% apart at 600k photons, so this is read again at full statistics before
     anything is concluded.

### The prediction, committed before `runs/d348-angular` finishes

In `tools/d348_angular.py`, against `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001` at the same seed:

  1. the H/H2 crossing moves **deeper** than A_V 1.168, into **1.8-2.6**;
  2. a molecular zone still exists (2 x(H2) > x(H) somewhere);
  3. x(H2) and x(CO) fall at every sampled PDR depth; the C+ = C crossing
     moves deeper;
  4. the ionization front moves < 2%, T_dust < 1%;
  5. the hydrogen budget holds to the baseline's 1.7e-4.

T_gas not predicted either way. Falsified by: the crossing moving shallower or
by less than 0.05; x(H2) rising at any sampled depth; no molecular zone; the
front or dust moving more than stated; the budget breaking.

### Found, not fixed

  - **The column rescale between chemistry passes compounds.** `abun0 = abun`
    is set once before `do it = 1, pdrChemIter`, and each pass ends
    `colH2 = colH2*abun(NH2)/abun0(NH2)` - so pass 3 runs on
    `col0*(a1/a0)*(a2/a0)`, not `col0*a2/a0`. Pre-existing, applies to the
    direct and diffuse rays alike, and left alone so this comparison measures
    one change. Its size is unmeasured.
  - The line-escape column along 3D rays (what D-190 meant `colRayAV` for) is
    a separate question from the FUV angular model and is not addressed.

### Not yet known

The full-statistics result; whether `chi_pred/chi_dif` falling to 0.53 is gas
emission, phase function or quadrature; whether `dir_MC/dir_ext` rising to ~4
is noise; the cost at full statistics (sites per cell 200-350, against 12 rays
before).

     prediction's arithmetic used iteration 4's rates, on columns from the
     closed-form seed; the converged run's upstream H2 columns shield more
     (the direct H2 rate at A_V 1.2-1.6 is 5.2e-5 at iteration 22 against
     4.4e-4 at iteration 4), so the crossing lands shallower.
  2. **Molecular zone survives: confirmed.** Deep x(H2) 0.476 against 0.488.
  3. **x(H2), x(CO) fall everywhere: confirmed. C+ = C deeper: refuted** - it
     moved 0.007 the other way. The prediction forgot D-162: MOCASSIN
     re-imposes its own ionization ratio on every linked element after every
     chemistry solve, so C+/C is MOCASSIN's, and MOCASSIN's transfer always
     carried the diffuse field. The chemistry's C I rate reaches C+/C only
     through the carbon it locks in molecules.
  4. **Front and dust: confirmed.** Front identical to four digits, T_dust
     within 0.15%.
  5. **Hydrogen budget: confirmed.** Max deviation 1.87e-4 against 1.72e-4.

T_gas: -6.6% at A_V 1.34, +8.0% at 2.24, within 1.5% elsewhere.

Against Cloudy (`runs/d277-cloudy`), model over Cloudy:

    A_V    H2 s1001  H2 d348    CO s1001  CO d348
    0.8     0.648     0.011       3.62     0.14
    1.0     0.432     0.086       0.60     0.05
    1.3     0.918     0.205       2.46     0.04
    1.7     1.009     0.606      13.8      0.23
    2.2     1.014     0.908     120        1.64
    2.8     1.017     0.989      63        4.17

H2 moves away from Cloudy (crossing 1.64 against 1.09) and the deep CO excess
of D-282 largely closes. **Neither is taken as the answer**, because D-349 finds
that this run overstates the Lyman-Werner drive at depth.

Converged `[D348]` table (iteration 22): the H2 rate at A_V 1.2-1.6 is
5.2e-5 direct and 3.9e-4 diffuse; the literal `f_dif/12` split would give
0.78-0.99 of the diffuse term; the anisotropy, site counts and scale checks are
as in the smoke test.

**The direct-beam excess is spectral hardening, not transport.**
`tools/d348_hardening.py` carries the direct spectrum `Jste - Jdif` of one
shell to every deeper shell bin by bin, each bin on its own extinction
(`tau_nu/tau_V` from `tauNu.out`, 2.75 to 31): the prediction matches the MC to
**0-12%** at every depth, where the single band-mean extinction falls short by up
to **8x**. The least opaque frequencies survive, so a band-mean exponent
over-attenuates a band integral. The MC's direct beam is right; the `dir_ext`
diagnostic is the crude one.

Figures: `runs/d348-angular/figs/` - `d348_*` against s1001
(`tools/d348_figs.py`), `cloudy_*` against Cloudy (`tools/d260_roellig.py`).

## D-349 - The spectral branch reopened: the chemistry is handed the wrong band (2026-09-25)

Found while D-348 ran, from files the runs already write
(`pdrFUVspec.out`, the D-345 shell spectra; `tauNu.out`). It corrects D-345's
conclusion, bounds D-348's result, and answers the user's question of why the
previous results reproduced Cloudy reasonably well.

### The Lyman-Werner window's share of the field collapses with depth

H2 and CO dissociation and C I ionization respond only to 11.2-13.6 eV. Every
`chi` handed to the chemistry is the 6-13.6 eV band integral, and the rate
coefficients assume it has the Draine field's shape. The Draine (1978) formula
puts **0.1516** of that band's energy in the window; integrated, it gives
8.938e-14 erg cm^-3 for the band, matching `uDraine = 8.94e-14`, so this is the
unit's own definition, not a new constant. The MC's share, per D-345 shell
(`runs/d345-fuvspec`, baseline physics, `Jdif` live):

    shell  A_V    share (Jste)  share (Jdif)  Draine/MC
      1    0.07      0.299         0.249         0.6
      3    0.28      0.242         0.210         0.7
      5    0.74      0.152         0.139         1.1
      6    1.13      0.094         0.087         1.7
      7    1.70      0.041         0.039         3.9
      8    2.50      0.008         0.008        20

Dust extinction rises toward 912 A, and C I photoionization opacity switches on
at 11.26 eV (`tauNu.out`: tau 12.8 -> 18.5 across 1100 A), so the window is
emptied first. So a band-integrated field **understates** the window-driven
rates by 20-40% near the front - a 40 kK star is bluer than Draine - and
**overstates** them 1.7x at A_V 1.1, 3.9x at 1.7 and 20x at 2.5. D-348's run reproduces
these shares to within 0.001.

**D-345 is corrected.** It closed the spectral branch on `f_LW/f_band` =
0.83-0.98, the diffuse *fraction* in the window against in the band. That
ratio cannot see this: direct and diffuse harden together, so their ratio holds
while the window's share of both falls nearly forty-fold. Its measurements stand; its
conclusion does not. The branch was right to be opened (D-344) and closed on the
wrong quantity. Not Lya - D-345 settled that - but hardening.

### Why the previous results reproduced Cloudy

The user asked. The window field MOCASSIN transports, in Draine-equivalent
units, against the H2 field the old prescription handed the chemistry
(`chi0 * SCATTER(A_V, 1000 A)`), per shell:

    shell  A_V   band / prescription   window / prescription
      1    0.07          1.3                   2.46
      3    0.28          1.6                   2.57
      5    0.74          2.6                   2.62
      6    1.13          4.5                   2.77
      7    1.70         10.4                   2.83
      8    2.50         38.6                   1.98

The band ratio grows thirty-fold with depth; **the window ratio is flat at
2.0-2.8.** So:

  1. The diffuse field the reaction rates never saw (D-053) is almost all
     6-11 eV light, which dissociates nothing the angular model is about.
  2. The old prescription's decline with depth happens to track MOCASSIN's
     window field. Read as a cancellation in this model - MOCASSIN retains more
     scattered light, and its window loses more to C I and the rising dust
     curve. An inference, not a general property.
  3. The constant factor is the star: the 40 kK blackbody's window share is
     0.299 against Draine's 0.152, x1.97, and the prescription treats `chi0`
     as Draine-shaped. **The baseline has run H2, CO and C I photorates about
     2x low from the first PDR cell.** Pre-existing, independent of D-348.
  4. Fronts move only logarithmically with the dissociating field in this
     regime (N(HI) ~ ln(1 + alpha G/2), Sternberg et al. 2014), so x2.5 is
     worth ~0.1-0.2 mag. An estimate from the formula, not a run.

Cloudy's large non-stellar field is mostly lines (D-291: 66%, Lya alone 46%),
all outside the window, and Cloudy integrates its rates over the spectrum, so
its H2 also sees roughly the attenuated continuum there. The 1.17 against 1.09
residual is then for the formation rate, the shielding functions and the like -
**not decomposed**, and Cloudy's own window field is **not measured**
(`runs/d290-cloudy-field` should allow it).

**Corrected in conversation, recorded here:** the baseline's shallow C+ = C
(2.24 against Cloudy's 2.95) is not a weak chemistry field - C+/C is
MOCASSIN's (D-162), as D-348 demonstrated by leaving it in place while the
chemistry's field rose 8x. The deep CO excess, which the chemistry owns, is
consistent with a weak window field; untested.

### What it means for D-348

D-348 hands the diffuse sites the band-integrated `chi_dif`, so its
window-driven rates rise x3-x170 where the window field supports x2.0-2.8. Its
crossing at 1.64 and its CO are therefore **overshoots**, and the D-348 index
row's "almost all from the diffuse magnitude the reaction rates never saw" is
true of the band and not of the window. The run stays useful as the attributable
band-integrated step.

### Proposed, not implemented (awaiting the user)

Give the window-driven reactions - H2, HD, CO photodissociation and C I
photoionization - the window's own field on every ray, in Draine-equivalent
units:

  - direct ray: scale by the source spectrum's window share over 0.1516
    (from `inSpectrumProbDen`, x1.97 here);
  - diffuse sites: scale by the cell's `Jdif` window share over 0.1516;
  - via a small hook in `calc_reac_rates.F90`: a per-ray factor read by the four
    shielded branches, defaulting to 1 so 3D-PDR's own drivers are untouched;
  - on the sites, drop the C I continuum term (`1.1e-17 N_C`) as the dust term
    already is - MOCASSIN transports C I continuum absorption (the 1100 A jump
    above) - keeping the H2-line term, which the MC does not carry.

Expected size, from the table: window-driven rates about x2.5 the baseline at
every depth - a modest move, not D-348's.

### Decided: hiipdr runs 11 iterations

At the user's direction. Both runs plateau by iteration 9: convergence flat at
~75% (s1001) and ~82% (d348), mean molecular fraction flat at 0.883-0.889 and
0.716-0.732 with no drift. Iterations 12-22 cost ~55 min a run. Exact seeded
comparisons need the same iteration count on both sides, so the first
11-iteration test needs an 11-iteration baseline beside it.

**Follow-up, 2026-09-26, the user:** the committed fixture
(`benchmarks/pdr/hiipdr/input/input.in`) stays at `maxIterateMC 22`; the 11 is
set in each run's own copied input. D-350's pair was the first run this way,
and its baseline matched s1001 for all 11 iterations.

### Not yet known

Cloudy's window field; the effect of the window fix itself; whether the
prescription's tracking of MOCASSIN's window field (point 2) holds in other
models; why the formal solution recovers only 52-130% of `chi_dif`.

## D-350 - The photorates on MOCASSIN's own field, after an audit against the project rules (2026-09-26)

### The audit

The user asked whether I had read the project rules in CLAUDE.md. Measured
against them, the D-348/D-349 work broke six.

  - **"All four must compile before any change is called done."** Commit
    `fe4816c` said all four flavours build, but the `R_difIso` diagnostic was
    added after the 1D, plain and warm-start builds and only the 3D flavour was
    rebuilt. Rebuilt from the committed code: all four compile. The claim was
    true and unverified.
  - **"Reverted work is tagged rather than deleted."** `computeRayColumns`, its
    D-340 mirror fold and the `colRay*` arrays were deleted with no tag. Now
    tagged `d348-raycolumns-removed` at `c7a7075`.
  - **The top rule - no prescribed value standing in for what the model
    knows.** D-348 kept the direct ray on 3D-PDR's diffuse-ISM prescription:
    the Savage & Mathis curve, FRR80 slab scattering (albedo 0.3, g 0.8),
    per-reaction gamma and an assumed Draine spectral shape - where MOCASSIN
    transports the direct field itself, per bin, on its own grains. D-349's flat
    x2.0-2.8 is that bug measured, and D-349's proposed fix patched the
    prescription with a x1.97 factor instead of replacing it. It also departed
    silently from D-347's "direct weight 1 - f_dif" - MOCASSIN's own direct
    fraction - where only the `f_dif/12` departure was flagged.
  - **No artificial gates.** `snapDiffuseSources` copied `computeAVradial`'s
    `pdrZone == 1` test. Its reason (D-088: seedPDR's x(H2) = 0.3 outside the
    zone) was removed by D-198 and D-208 - the chemistry runs in every cell,
    seeded from MOCASSIN with no molecules - so the test was stale in both
    places, and was propagated rather than questioned.
  - **One reality per quantity.** `difSrc` is a lagged second copy of n(H2),
    n(C), n(CO), and the 1D flavour still has two FUV fields (heating on the MC
    field, chemistry on the prescription). Not changed here.
  - **Artifacts.** The D-348 page compared against the baseline and Cloudy and
    left out the standalone 3D-PDR reference the practice includes as a sanity
    range.

**Decided, the user's direction:** fix the first two now; implement the top
rule and the gate removal next, in place of D-349's proposal; test at 11
iterations against an 11-iteration baseline.

### The design

Every photorate is driven by MOCASSIN's local field, split only so each part is
shielded by the column its photons crossed:

    direct   Jste - Jdif   ray 0          source-ward columns
    diffuse  Jdif          D-348's sites  two-leg columns

  - **A_V = 0 on every ray.** MOCASSIN's transfer has applied the dust;
    `exp(-gamma*A_V)` again would count it twice (D-343's argument, now for the
    direct part too).
  - **The window.** H2, HD and CO dissociation and C I ionization take each
    part's Lyman-Werner field: `radSurf` stays the 6-13.6 eV integral the other
    photoreactions use, and a new vendored hook, `ray_lw_factor` in
    `global_module` (D-195's pattern: not allocated means upstream behaviour),
    multiplies it in those four branches by the part's measured window share
    over the Draine field's. The Draine share is computed from the Draine (1978)
    formula on MOCASSIN's own FUV bins (`draineWindowShare`), the formula that
    also reproduces `uDraine`. Recorded in `UPSTREAM.md`.
  - **The C I continuum term goes** (`colC = 0`): MOCASSIN's opacity carries C I
    photoionization absorption (`tauNu.out`, tau 12.8 -> 18.5 across 1100 A).
    The chemistry keeps what the MC does not transport: H2 and CO line
    shielding and the H2-line term of the C I rate.
  - **The zone test is removed** from `computeAVradial` and
    `snapDiffuseSources`; every cell shields with what the chemistry holds.
    What that adds to the H2 columns is measured in the run (`[D350] zone test
    gone`), so the two changes can be told apart without a second run.
  - The 1D flavour is unchanged: no site walk, the prescription on twelve
    twelfths, the hook unallocated. Changing it is item 5 of the audit, not
    decided.

Cost stated plainly: the other ~48 photoreactions lose 3D-PDR's per-reaction
dust factors and take the band-integrated MC field - an approximation, but on
MOCASSIN's own data.

All four flavours compile.

### The test, and the prediction committed first

Two runs, seed 1001, 14 ranks each, 11 iterations: `runs/d350-window` (this
code) and `runs/d350-base11` (commit `c7a7075`, the physics of s1001, built in a
worktree). Run side by side, 28 ranks on the 14 physical cores; results depend
only on the seed and the rank count, so this costs time, not correctness.

In `tools/d350_window.py`:

  1. H/H2 crossing deeper than the baseline's, by much less than D-348's: into
     A_V **1.25-1.45**;
  2. x(H2) and x(CO) fall against the baseline at every sampled depth, and at
     A_V >= 1.3 by less than in D-348 (no bracket claimed nearer the front,
     where the window factor exceeds D-348's band-shaped one);
  3. C+ = C moves by less than 0.05;
  4. ionization front and T_dust each move by less than 1%;
  5. the hydrogen budget holds to better than 3e-4;
  6. non-zone cells supply more than 1% of the H2 column in fewer than 1% of
     PDR cells;
  7. in the first A_V bin the direct window field over the old prescription's
     H2 field is 1.9-2.6 - the star's window share over Draine's;
  8. the baseline reproduces s1001's first 11 iterations to nine digits.

T_gas and the minor species are not predicted.

### Result (added after the runs)

`runs/d350-window` and `runs/d350-base11`, 11 iterations each, seed 1001, run
side by side: 76.1% and 75.0% converged, 1 h 15 each. Clean exits; no fallback
cells, no unset first legs. `tools/d350_window.py`, against the prediction
committed before the runs:

    front                     base11    d350     (D-348, 22 it)
    ionization front [pc]     3.8616    3.8614      3.8416
    H/H2 crossing A_V          1.184     1.364       1.635
    C+ = C A_V                 2.289     2.290       2.276

    A_V    x(H2) new/base  (D-348/s1001)   x(CO) new/base  (D-348/s1001)
    0.82       0.164          0.026            0.195           0.025
    1.05       0.699          0.193            0.787           0.057
    1.35       0.596          0.258            0.244           0.019
    1.74       0.938          0.638            0.276           0.016
    2.24       0.999          0.906            0.890           0.015
    2.89       1.000          0.975            1.309           0.076

  1. **Crossing into 1.25-1.45: held** - 1.364.
  2. **Half held.** The bracket held: at A_V >= 1.3 H2 and CO fall less than in
     D-348, everywhere. "Fall at every depth" did not: deep H2 is unchanged and
     **CO rises 31% at A_V 2.9**, because there the window field falls below
     the old prescription (0.79x in the last bin) - MOCASSIN's window is
     emptied by C I continuum and dust absorption at 1000 A, which the
     prescription never had.
  3. **C+ = C: held** (+0.001).
  4. **Front and dust: held** (front 1.0000, T_dust within 0.16%).
  5. **Budget: held**, 2.7e-4 against the baseline's 1.6e-4 - larger, not
     investigated.
  6. **Zone removal: wrong as stated, negligible in effect.** 247 PDR cells
     (1.6%) take more than 1% of their H2 column from non-zone cells, 149
     more than 10%. Recounted offline from the output: the 150 above 10% all
     sit at the front, A_V 0.47-0.71, where the whole H2 column is ~1e12
     cm^-2; the largest non-zone contribution to any cell is 2.7e12, two
     decades below where H2 self-shielding begins. The fraction fired only
     where the column is itself negligible.
  7. **Plumbing: held** - 1.96 in the first bin.
  8. **Baseline = s1001: held** - 11 of 11 iterations identical to every
     printed digit. The seeded comparison at a shorter iteration count works.

T_gas: -5.3% at A_V 1.35, +2% deep. Against Cloudy the H2 crossing sits at 1.36
against 1.09 (the baseline's was 1.18); CO at A_V 0.8-1.7 moves from 0.3-13.7x
Cloudy to 0.3-3.8x, while the deep excess stays at 83-100x - D-348's apparent
closure of the deep CO gap was its overshoot. Against standalone 3D-PDR, as a
sanity range: H2 forms later than in the slab, as before.

### D-349's "flat 2.0-2.8" is corrected

The per-cell `[D350]` values, as ratios of sums over narrow A_V bins, give the
window field over the old prescription's H2 field as

    A_V     0-0.2  0.5-0.8  0.8-1.2  1.2-1.6  1.6-2.1  2.1-2.6  2.6-3.05
    ratio    2.5     3.1      3.6      4.1      4.6      3.7      0.8

D-349's table came from D-345's radial-shell means, and within a shell the
prescription falls about ten times faster than the MC's window field, so each
shell's mean is set by its shallow edge. So the old prescription understated the
window field 2.5-4.6x through the PDR and overstated it at the far edge. The
answer D-349 gave the user survives in substance - a factor of a few, not the
band's thirty-fold - but "the prescription tracks it flat" was the averaging.

### Status

Accepted. The photorates follow the top rule; the headline moved inside the
predicted range; the two failed predictions are understood. Open: the deep CO
excess against Cloudy (83-100x, untouched by the field); the larger hydrogen
budget deviation; the formal solution's 52-130%; items 3 and 5 of the audit
(`difSrc` as a lagged copy, the 1D flavour's two fields).

Figures: `runs/d350-window/figs/` - `d348_*` against the baseline,
`cloudy_*` against Cloudy, `roellig_*` against the 3D-PDR reference.

## D-351 - A full audit of the code, and what stands between it and science production (2026-09-26)

The user asked for a full audit of the code and an evaluation of the standing
issues that must be resolved before science production. D-333 (2026-09-23)
ranked the blockers three days and seventeen entries ago; this entry re-ranks
them against the code as it stands at `51289e5`. The criterion is D-333's: *does
it stop us publishing a number*. It also records the measurements taken to rank
the issues, three of which found something no earlier entry had.

### What was audited, and how

  - `source/pdr_mod.f90` read in full, every routine. `iteration_mod.f90`'s PDR
    sequence (setup, updateCell, the coupling passes, the reductions, the
    rescale, the output). The PDR-facing parts of `update_mod.f90`, namely
    coolant substitution, extra heating, the cosmic-ray block, the zone probes
    and `NePDR`. The vendored routines MOCASSIN actually calls: `calc_reac_rates`,
    `escape_probability`, `heatingfunctions`, `h2_form` and `odes_reduced.c`.
    `set_input_mod` for keywords and defaults, `grid_mod` for checkpointing,
    and the Makefile for flag reach.
  - Every live use of `pdrZone`, of each `pdr*` keyword, and of each
    environment variable, traced to what it changes.
  - The 3D flavour built from a clean `git archive` of HEAD in the scratchpad
    with `-Wall -Wuninitialized -Wmaybe-uninitialized`. It produced 117
    warnings. None are in `pdr_mod.f90` or the vendored units. All are in
    legacy MOCASSIN (`grid_mod`, `ph_mod`, `emission_mod`, `update_mod`), and
    nearly all are gfortran array-descriptor false positives. The scalar ones
    (`heatIonDif`, `enPacket%weight`, `normDust`, `nwavold`) sit on paths
    guarded by `lgDebug` or by the model type, and were not chased further.
    The code has not changed since D-350's four-flavour build, so the other
    three flavours were not rebuilt.
  - The run logs of `runs/d350-window`, `runs/d350-base11` and
    `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001`, and the four-seed ensemble
    `runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001-s1004`. No new runs.
  - Checked clean: no `RAYTHEIA`/`ONEDIMENSIONAL` guard outside `pdr_mod.f90`,
    so the D-341 flag-reach trap does not recur. The retired keywords sampled
    (`pdrAllCells`, `pdrIonFromMocassin`, `pdrCoolFeedback`,
    `pdrTeFromMocassin`, `pdrOwnIon`, `pdrAtomicH`, `pdrSyncAbun`) each print
    that they are retired. `pdrCoolTdep`, `pdrCoolTfac` and `pdrZoneLim`'s
    second value `pdrBlendLo` are read silently. An unrecognised keyword gets
    a warning and the run continues. Reactions 330/331 (He+/C+ + e- on grains, a fixed diffuse-ISM
    coefficient) are absent from the generated `odes_reduced.c`, so they are
    dead and no fixed grain rate reaches the ion balance. `pdrIonRate` (D-118)
    is computed and reduced but read only by the `[D183]` diagnostic, so the
    network's ionization channels are not double counted into ionBalance.

### Three measurements the ranking needed

**(1) The chemistry passes oscillate, on inputs that do not change.** Within an
MC iteration, updateCell runs once. The five coupling passes then re-solve the
chemistry with Te, ionDen, Ne, the field and the snapshot columns all frozen
(D-216; the `[D119]` residual reads exactly zero). Yet the mean f_mol after
each pass, from the `[D205]` lines, reads:

    run / last iteration        after pass 1   2        3        4
    d334-hiipdr/s1001            0.8879   0.8904   0.8870   0.8914
    d350-base11                  0.8834   0.8888   0.8840   0.8902
    d350-window                  0.8462   0.8546   0.8435   0.8596

It alternates with period 2, and in all three runs the swing *grows*
from pass to pass. The extra heating does the same: 2.009 / 1.956 / 2.031 /
1.923e-27 per H in `d350-window`, swings of 2.6, 3.8 and 5.3%. The published
state is whatever pass 5 lands on, and the phase varies between iterations: in
`d350-window` iteration 10 decays onto its low phase, iteration 11 grows onto
its high one.

One channel carries state from one pass to the next other than the CVODE
starting point: `pdrStep` rescales every shielding column by the target cell's
own abundance ratio, `colH2 = colH2*abun(NH2)/abun0(NH2)` (`pdr_mod.f90:3236`),
compounding over the `pdrChemIter = 3` inner passes. Since D-088 those columns
exclude the target cell, so the target cell's H2 has no business scaling them.
The rescale is a leftover from D-078's `NHcol*abun` form. It adds positive
self-shielding feedback: more local H2 lengthens the column in front, which
shields more and makes more H2. A loop gain near or past -1 would give exactly
this signature. **Hypothesis, not yet tested:** delete the rescale and the
alternation disappears. It is inert at an exact fixed point, since the ratio
tends to 1. What it corrupts is the approach to that fixed point, and on a
bistable front it may select the branch.

**(2) The hydrogen budget test cannot fail where it is printed, and D-350's
chemistry converges three times worse than its baseline.**
`rescaleIonToAvail` normalises MOCASSIN's H stages to the chemistry's `x(H) +
x(H+)` before `[D196]` prints the budget and before `writeGrid`. So `x(HI) +
2x(H2) + x(HII) = 1` holds in the log and in every output file by construction,
up to H held in other species. **D-350's prediction 5, "budget holds to 3e-4",
was a free pass**, the D-176..D-181 failure CLAUDE.md warns about. The
informative number is the `[D220]` "before" figure: the lag between
MOCASSIN's ion stages and the chemistry's newest molecules. Last three
iterations of each run:

    run            [D220] mean |budget-1|   cells >1% off   |dx(H0)|/x p90   f_mol moved >0.1
    s1001          0.0102 0.0088 0.0086      9.3-9.8%          0.100             2.47%
    d350-base11    0.0123 0.0076 0.0068      8.7-11.3%         0.094             1.69%
    d350-window    0.0156 0.0258 0.0201      28.3-30.2%        0.337             5.49%

D-350 reported 76.1% converged against the baseline's 75.0%, which reads as
unchanged. Measured on the molecular state itself, the D-350 handoff moves
three times as much per iteration. The convergence percentage did not show it.

**(3) Why: every photorate now reads the Monte Carlo's per-cell noise.** In the
four-seed ensemble (`runs/d334-hiipdr/s1001-s1004`, 22 iterations, 6e6
packets), the seed-to-seed scatter of each cell's `chiFUV` is:

    A_V bin     cells   chi_MC     per-cell sd/mean
    0.80-1.20     914   11.3       median 0.023   p90 0.039
    1.20-1.60    1565    3.15             0.041       0.070
    1.60-2.10    3180    0.91             0.074       0.132
    2.10-2.60    4812    0.27             0.138       0.242
    2.60-3.05    4131    0.096            0.223       0.379

Before D-350 the photorates ran on `chi0*exp(-gamma*A_V)` from a geometric
A_V, which is deterministic, so they carried no Monte Carlo noise at all. Since
D-350 they take this field, and 12,000 of the 15,204 cells sit where it
scatters 7-22%. Each MC iteration draws fresh packets and MOCASSIN does not
accumulate J across iterations, so every iteration's chemistry sees a new
draw. Deep x(H0) is set by the photodissociation rate, and a 15-22% field draw
against a 10% `convLimit` accounts for the p90 of 0.34. D-350's one-reality fix
is right. Its price is that the deep chemistry is now **noise-limited per
cell**. The bin means that the published profiles show average over thousands
of cells. The per-cell values that a 3D map would show do not average, and
through the non-linear photorates the noise can also bias bin means (Jensen:
`<1/chi> = (1+sigma^2)/<chi>`, +5% at 22%). *Estimate, not measured.*

### The ranking

**Tier 1 - defects in the current code that move numbers now**

  1. **The pass-to-pass oscillation** (measurement 1). Fix: delete the column
     rescale. Test: a seeded pair at 11 iterations, where the alternation should
     vanish. Do this before anything that reads per-cell chemistry.
  2. **Noise-limited chemistry** (measurement 3). The options are more
     packets (noise goes as N^-1/2, so 20x to reach 5% at A_V 2.8, which is not
     practical), accumulating the FUV estimator over the iterations once the
     field has settled (the standard MC remedy; noise then goes as
     (N_iter N_packets)^-1/2), or FUV variance reduction. This is a design
     decision, and it must be taken before any per-cell product is published.
  3. **Verification that cannot fail.** Report the pre-rescale `[D220]` budget
     as the conserved-sum test. Convergence should be judged on the molecular
     state (f_mol, x(H0) at depth) rather than on the cell percentage alone.
     `doc/pdr-status.md` section 2's "holds" row is corrected to say what it
     now measures.
  4. **Line escape in the 3D flavour is the slab closed form, with 4 of the 12
     rays never escaping** (`pdr_mod.f90:3588-3606`: `mu = 0` gives
     `colA = 1e30`, so beta_ray is about 1e-30). `escape_probability` divides
     by all 12 rays, so beta is at most 2/3 even for a thin line. In the
     two-level limit the cooling goes as `1/(1 + n/(beta n_crit))`. For [C II]
     (n_crit ~3e3 on H) the loss is about 2% at n_H = 1e2 (hiipdr), 11% at 1e3
     (pn150k), 28% at 1e4 and 33% at 1e5. *Estimate, not measured.* On top of
     that, the rays toward the star carry the cell's own populations over the
     whole column back to the star. That overstates tau for CO, whose
     abundance rises with depth. The cap was known at D-061/D-063 and D-190,
     but it is absent from the limitations register and was never measured on
     a 3D fixture. It blocks dense-PDR science and every line observable.

**Tier 2 - blocks the science the code is being taken to production for**

  5. **No PDR line observables, and the line output that does exist disagrees
     with the thermal balance.** In PDR cells, `lineFlux.out` reports [C II],
     [O I] and [C I] from MOCASSIN's electron-only excitation. The gas, however,
     is cooled by 3D-PDR's level populations with H, H2, He and H+ partners.
     That is two realities for one line. The per-transition emissivities
     (`escape_probability.F90`, `line(i,j)`) are computed and discarded, and
     `pdrCoolSp.out` holds each coolant's total, not each line (D-331, D-333
     item 5).
  6. **The 3D capability is unvalidated** (D-338). Every fixture is a uniform
     sphere. D-348's site walk carries real direction dependence even there
     (anisotropy 1.9-3.1), but no clump, shell asymmetry or gradient has been
     run. A structured fixture with an internal reference, smooth against
     clumped at equal mass, is still not built.
  7. **pn150k has no result on the current code.** Its last run is D-336's
     ensemble, before D-348 and D-350. `hiipdr Against Cloudy` (v12) and
     `150 kK PN Against Cloudy` (v11), both from 2026-09-24, and `hiipdr
     Against 3D-PDR` (2026-09-14) all show pre-D-348 physics.
  8. **The carbon transition** (L-3/O-01, and the deep CO excess). C+ = C sits
     at A_V 2.29 against Cloudy's 2.95. Against 3D-PDR, C+ collapses to 0.38 at
     A_V 2.33. Deep CO is 83-100x Cloudy's. **Hypothesis:** one cause. MOCASSIN
     owns C+/C (D-162), and a transition placed too shallow puts neutral carbon
     where the CO chemistry can use it. The test needs no run: compare
     MOCASSIN's per-cell C I photoionization and C II recombination rates
     against Cloudy's at matched A_V. One related gap: MOCASSIN's C I
     photoionization has no H2 line shielding, because the MC does not
     transport Lyman-Werner lines. The chemistry's `CIPDRATE` has it, but the
     chemistry's C+/C is overwritten. At A_V 3 this is a few tens of per cent
     *(estimate)*, and it has the opposite sign to L-3, so it does not explain
     it.

**Tier 3 - paths that are compiled and offered but not exercised**

  9. **Warm start** (L-14). Beyond the untested equivalence, `pdrLevPop`,
     `pdrCoolTab`, `pdrHeatXtra` and `pdrCoolSp` are not checkpointed.
     updateCell runs before pdrStep in each iteration, so the first resumed
     thermal balance runs without the PDR coolants or the PDR heating.
  10. `mocassinOutput` and `mocassinPlot` have never been run (L-20).
  11. **The plain flavour.** Its last Lexington comparison was D-270/D-279
      (2026-09-14/15). At least ten core-physics changes have landed since:
      g-averaging and path stretching (D-280), Case A recombination cooling
      (D-286), the WD01 yield (D-289), grain-charge units (D-290), line
      transport on by default (D-307), the Q-file path (D-313), sticking
      (D-326), and CHIANTI 10.1 data (D-330).
  12. **The 1D flavour**, which is what `make PDR=1` builds by default, still
      runs its chemistry on the prescription: two FUV fields (D-350 audit
      item 5).
  13. **Rank-local state.** `pdrCoolTab` and `pdrHeatXtra` are never reduced.
      They are correct only because updateCell and pdrStep happen to share the
      ownership formula `mod(iCell-(taskid+1),numtasks)`. That is D-348's
      defect class. It needs either a reduction or an assertion.

**Tier 4 - rule compliance (CLAUDE.md)**

  14. **Alternative-physics switches.** The keywords `pdrFUVmode`,
      `pdrDustModel`, `pdrOwnDust`, `pdrDustFeedback`, `pdrPEfromPDR`,
      `pdrUseNePDR`, `pdrCoolZoneGate` and `pdrFcritConv` all select
      alternative physics, as do the environment variables `MOCASSIN_LINES`,
      `_RECCOOL`, `_YIELD` and `_GRAINQ`. The environment variables are recorded
      in the log only, not in the input or any output file. Every default is
      the adopted physics, and every other branch is an untested path.
      `pdrZone` (x(H+) < `pdrZoneLim`) now reaches only diagnostics, three of
      those off-by-default switches, and the vestigial `pdrTgas`. **No gate
      remains on the default path.** That corrects the impression a grep gives,
      of zone tests still deciding ownership.
  15. **Constants still standing in for the model** on live paths:
      - `pdrMetal` multiplies H2 formation on top of MOCASSIN's measured grain
        area (`h2_form.F90:119`) and multiplies `AV_fac`
        (`pdr_mod.f90:2736`). It is harmless at 1 and double counts otherwise.
      - `escape_probability`'s dust background, `NGRAIN = 2e-12 n Z` with a
        fixed emissivity, although MOCASSIN has J_nu at the line.
      - `L_TURB = 5 pc` in turbulent heating.
      - `seedMolecules` applies SCATTER(A_V) to `chiFUV`, which is already
        attenuated. This affects the seed only.
      - The 1D flavour's `X_GRID` curve is taken from one calibration cell.
  16. **Vestigial code.**
      - pdrStep's thermal bracket is computed and then overwritten by Te.
      - `pdrTgas` is a lagged copy of Te, written to `pdrGrid.out` in the
        temperature slot.
      - The `[D119]` ionDen damping is zero by construction.
      - Stale comments: pdrStep's header still says "slab-equivalent,
        chi/12, A_V,eff". CLAUDE.md says "185 entries" and still calls
        `PDRGEOM=3D` "per-ray columns".
      - `doc/pdr-status.md` has a duplicated L-19 line and still gives L-22's
        "Next: set sticking", which D-326/D-328 did.
  17. **Diagnostics are about 155 `[D...]`-tagged prints** in the three core
      files, with per-cell probes in hot loops. A run log is 91,000 lines.

**Tier 5 - provenance and infrastructure**

  18. **Nothing off this machine.** `pdr-photoionization` is 102 commits
      ahead of `origin/main` and has no remote branch. Every tag and the whole
      DEVLOG since 2026-09-15 exist only locally.
  19. Fixtures carry an absolute `pdrDataDir` into this home directory, and
      D-330's `data/` against `~/.local/share` question (D-333 tier 5) is
      unresolved.
  20. **No fast regression test.** Every check is a 1.25 h run. There is no
      per-phase timing either, so the cost of the four chemistry passes that
      add nothing but item 1's oscillation is unknown.
  21. The memory model (~58^3 per rank, full grid replicated) caps 3D science
      resolution.

### What changed against D-333

D-333's Tier 1 item 1 (reproducibility) is closed (D-334..D-336). Its item 2
(two contradicting fixtures) is sharpened by D-338 into item 6 here. Its tier 3
(the photoelectric deficit on pn150k, L-19, L-9) stands, and is folded into the
register rather than repeated. Four items are new: 1, 2, 3 and the
line-output half of 5. Item 4 was known and unregistered.

### Corrections to D-350

Its prediction 5 could not fail (measurement 2). Its "76.1% against 75.0%
converged" hid a threefold rise in per-iteration movement of the molecular
state (measurements 2 and 3). The headline profile shifts are bin means over
thousands of cells, and they stand to within the Jensen bias noted above. The
per-cell state does not.

### What is not known

  - Whether the column rescale is the whole of the oscillation. It is the only
    channel found, and the test is the run in item 1.
  - How much of the deep MC noise the Jensen bias converts into bin-mean bias.
  - Whether L-3 and the deep CO excess share a cause (item 8's test).
  - The run-time split between transport, chemistry and thermal balance.

### Recommended order

Item 1 costs one line and one run pair, and it must precede item 2, since the
oscillation and the noise both feed the same convergence numbers. Item 3 is
reporting and costs nothing. Item 2 is a design decision for the user. Then
item 7 (pn150k and the three artifacts on the current code), then item 8's
no-run test, then items 4 and 5 together, since both need per-ray line
transfer. Item 18 needs the user's word before anything is pushed.

No code changed in this entry. `doc/pdr-status.md` gains L-25..L-29 and its
stale lines are corrected.

## D-352 - pdrZone removed, and every switch that selected physics at run time (2026-09-26)

The user, after D-351: the old `pdrZone` threshold (x(H+) < 0.3) and the input
keywords and environment variables that still select alternative physics are
major issues against the project's first rule. Investigate them and fix them.
Mid-investigation: *"perhaps it is a good idea to remove pdrZone completely."*
Done, together with everything the investigation found in the same class.

### What was found

**pdrZone** (D-007's latch, `x(H+) < pdrZoneLim = 0.3`, set in
`mocassinToPDR`, reduced by MPI, checkpointed) had 44 references in 7 files.
Traced one by one, none of them decided physics on the default path any more:

    lgChemOnly (pdrStep)          decided only whether pdrTgas was written
    T seed (mocassinToPDR)        seeded pdrTgas, which pdrStep overwrote with Te
    update_mod:642                inside if (.false.) since D-193
    pdrPEfromPDR / pdrUseNePDR    zone-gated, both default 0
    pdrCoolZoneGate               the zone gate on coolant substitution, default 0
    ~20 probe conditions          prints only, and D-350's zone-removal diagnostic
    d260_roellig.py (tool)        chose the neutral H/C/O source and set the A_V
                                  zero point of the 3D-PDR reference by it

So `pdrZone` was an ownership rule that had gone dormant: three
alternative-physics switches were one keyword away from reviving it, and the
analysis tools still took it as model data.

**pdrTgas/pdrTlow/pdrThigh** are the PDR's own temperature and bracket. pdrStep
still computed a one-pass bisection (`do itherm = 1, 1`) and overwrote it with
Te. The result was stored, reduced, checkpointed, and written twice per cell
to `pdrGrid.out` in the temperature slot: a second, lagged copy of Te. That
is one reality held twice.

**Input keywords.** Of the PDR keywords, these selected alternative physics or
stood in for a model quantity:

    pdrFUVmode       1 = heat the gas with 3D-PDR's prescription (default 0)
    pdrDustModel     0/1/2 = MOCASSIN / max(MOCASSIN, HTT91) / HTT91 T_dust (0)
    pdrOwnDust       0 = Savage & Mathis curve in SCATTER (default 1)
    pdrDustFeedback  1 = 3D-PDR's PE and gas-grain terms drive the GRAIN
                     balance (default 1 - see below)
    pdrPEfromPDR     1 = 3D-PDR's PAH PE heats the gas in the zone (0)
    pdrUseNePDR      1 = ionBalance uses the chemistry's Ne in the zone (0)
    pdrCoolZoneGate  1 = coolant substitution only in the zone (0)
    pdrFcritConv     1 = PDR heat/cool imbalance clears lgConverged (0)
    pdrZoneLimit     the threshold itself
    pdrMetallicity   multiplied H2 formation (h2_form.F90:119) ON TOP of
                     MOCASSIN's measured grain area, and AV_fac (pdrStep)
    pdrGrainRadius   3D-PDR's fixed 0.1 um grain for its gas-grain term

Eleven more were inert and settled earlier: pdrTseed, pdrThermIter,
pdrCoolTdep, pdrCoolTfac, pdrFcrit, pdrCoupleDamp (an identity since D-216),
pdrHealpix (pdrStep hardcodes level 0), pdrAVfac (always overwritten by the
measured value), pdrUVfac (read only under GRAINRECOMB, not built), and the
D-193/D-198/D-208 retirements already printing "retired". No production
fixture sets any of them. The core-MOCASSIN solver keywords this project
added (`teSolver`, `ionMatrix`, `teFloor`, `cvUseH2`, `iterDamp`,
`pathStretch`) choose numerics, not physics, and are left alone. `teFloor`
(10 K) is a clamp, but it holds no cell in `runs/d350-window`, where the
coldest is 10.9 K.

**Environment variables.** `MOCASSIN_LINES` (discard the thin diffuse lines),
`MOCASSIN_RECCOOL` (Case B recombination cooling), `MOCASSIN_YIELD` (Baldwin
yield) and `MOCASSIN_GRAINQ` (the 4 pi^2 grain-charge units). Each switched
physics with no trace in the input file, and only a log line said which mode a
run had used. `MOCASSIN_DUSTPROBE` only prints, and stays.

**The default that was itself wrong: `pdrDustFeedback = 1`.** In every dusty
cell of every PDR run, the grain energy balance (`getDustT`) replaced MOCASSIN's
per-grain photoelectric loss and gas-grain exchange (`photoelHeat_d`,
`gasDustColl_d`) with 3D-PDR's `heat(2)` and `heat(11)`, spread over the grains
by area. `heat(2)` is a PAH formula times metallicity, on a PAH population this
dust does not carry. `heat(11)` uses a fixed `NGRAIN = 2e-12 n Z` of 0.1 um
grains. Meanwhile the gas is heated by MOCASSIN's own `photoelHeat_g` (D-131
excludes `heat(2)` from the gas side). So **the energy leaving the grains as
photoelectrons is not the energy the gas receives**, which is one quantity
with two realities. Measured on `runs/d350-window`, per H:

    A_V bin     PE the grains lose   PE the gas gets   ratio
                (3D-PDR heat(2))     (MOCASSIN)
    0.00-0.20      5.86e-23             7.61e-23          0.77
    0.20-0.47      1.67e-23             1.65e-23          1.02
    0.47-0.80      1.02e-24             2.17e-25          4.7
    0.80-1.20      2.54e-25             3.97e-26          6.4
    1.20-1.60      1.38e-25             1.67e-26          8.3
    1.60-2.10      6.17e-26             3.70e-27         16.7
    2.10-2.60      2.09e-26             4.42e-28         47
    2.60-3.05      8.38e-27             5.51e-29        152

### What was done

Tag `d352-zone-and-switches` marks the last commit that carries all of it.
Building it reproduces any legacy mode.

**Stage 1 - physics-neutral on the default path.**
  - `pdrZone` is gone: the array, its allocation, MPI reduction and checkpoint
    field, the latch and the T seed in `mocassinToPDR`, `lgChemOnly`, and every
    probe condition. Probes that sampled "PDR-zone cells" now sample all gas
    cells (they keep their A_V conditions).
  - `pdrTgas/pdrTlow/pdrThigh`, the vestigial bracket in pdrStep, the
    redundant first `CALC_HEATING` (the one kept is evaluated at Te, as the
    old second one was), and iterateT's dead PDR short circuit are gone.
  - `NePDR` (read only under `pdrUseNePDR`), the D-119 pass-to-pass ionDen
    damping (`ionDenPrev`, an identity) and the `pdrFcritConv` probe
    (`cvPdrCleared`) are gone.
  - Every keyword above is retired through one handler
    (`set_input_mod: retiredKeyword`). The inert ones print why and run on.
    The eleven that selected physics or stood in for the model **stop the
    run**, because running on with the adopted physics would silently not do
    what the input asked.
  - The vendored metallicity is pinned at 1 and the grain radius at
    upstream's 0.1 um, with a comment on what each still reaches. AV_fac is
    reset per cell from the measured dust, as before; UV_fac is set from the
    measured R_FUV. The Savage & Mathis replacement is unconditional.
  - The four environment variables are gone with their legacy branches (Case
    B, the Baldwin yield and its Y0/Y1 constants, the 4 pi^2 units, the
    line-discard path). readInput stops if any is set.
  - `pdrGrid.out` is **v2**: a `# pdrGrid v2` header line, then chiFUV, AVeff,
    pdrCool, pdrHeat and pdrHeatPE per grid point, followed by the
    abundances. A reader built for the 45-token v1 layout fails on the header
    instead of silently misreading. resetGrid refuses v1 checkpoints.
    `tools/d260_roellig.py` reads both layouts (`read_pdrgrid`), and so does
    `d304_budget.py`. The tools now take neutral H, C and O from MOCASSIN in
    every cell. On `d350-window` the chemistry's values agree to a median
    of 1e-7, 1.2% in the worst cell, so the old zone switch of source
    changed nothing. They also derive their "zone" label (for `A_front` and
    cell selection) from MOCASSIN's x(H+) < 0.3, as an analysis convention.
    It differs from the stored flag in 1 cell of 15,204 and gives the same
    `A_front` (0.465900719).

All four flavours compile.

**Stage 2 - the grain energy balance on MOCASSIN's own terms.** getDustT's
D-093 branch is removed. PDR runs now take `gasDustColl_d - photoelHeat_d`
exactly as a plain run does, which are the per-grain counterparts of the gas
terms the thermal balance uses. `pdrHeatGG` is dropped, since nothing reads it
now. `pdrHeatPE` remains in `pdrGrid.out` as 3D-PDR's reference value only.
The cap `nDustCapped` goes with the branch. The gas-grain term MOCASSIN uses
still omits H2 (L-9); that is negligible at these densities and is not
changed here.

### Predictions, recorded before the runs

Stage 1, `runs/d352-s1` (seed 1001, 14 ranks, 11 iterations) against
`runs/d350-window` (the same physics, built before this change):

  1. `grid0-3.out`, `dustGrid.out`, `thermBudget.out`, `pdrCoolSp.out`,
     `pdrRad.out`, `pdrFUV.out`, `pdrFUVspec.out`, `tauNu.out`, `lineFlux.out`,
     `SED.out`, `temperature.out` and `ionratio.out` are **byte-identical**.
     `pdrGrid.out` is identical in every retained column.
  2. The run log differs only in the removed diagnostics and the relabelled
     census, and every `[D205]` per-pass line is identical.

Any difference is a defect in the removal, not physics.

Stage 2, `runs/d352-s2` against `runs/d352-s1`, same seed. Note that the pair
decorrelates from the first iteration at which T_dust differs (pdrStartIter =
4), because the dust emission changes which frequencies the re-emitted packets
draw. So beyond the dust temperature itself, this is a comparison at the
Monte Carlo noise floor, which since D-350 is several per cent per cell at
depth (D-351, L-26):

  3. T_dust rises, because grains stop losing an energy the gas never
     received. By less than 0.2% at A_V < 0.8, and by 0.1-1.5% at A_V > 1.6.
     *Estimate:* heat(2) is 1-6% of the absorbed FUV at depth, and T_dust
     goes as E^(1/6).
  4. The ionization front moves less than 0.1%, and the H/H2 crossing and
     C+ = C less than 0.03 in A_V.
  5. T_gas and the bin-mean x(H2) and x(CO) move within twice the per-bin
     scatter between the two runs' last iterations. No systematic shift is
     predicted: Cazaux & Tielens' formation efficiency is near unity and flat
     in T_dust well below 100 K, and gas-grain coupling is negligible here.

### Result (added after the runs)

Both runs ran side by side, 14 ranks each, and exited cleanly in 1 h 07.

**Stage 1** (`runs/d352-s1` against `runs/d350-window`). Convergence is
76.1181259% in both, to every digit. `tools/d352_identity.py`:

  1. **Held for every physics-state file.** These are byte-identical:
     `grid0-3.out`, every retained column of `pdrGrid.out` (chiFUV, AVeff,
     pdrCool, pdrHeat, pdrHeatPE and all 33 abundances), `pdrCoolSp.out`,
     `pdrFUV.out`, `pdrFUVspec.out`, `pdrRad.out`, `tauNu.out`, `lineFlux.out`,
     `SED.out`, `temperature.out`, `ionratio.out` and `photoSource.out`.
     Three files are not:
     - `summary.out` differs only in wall-clock timestamps. The prediction
       should not have listed it.
     - `dustGrid.out` differs in 1 of its 1.07 million temperatures:
       51.0816574 against 51.0816612, a relative change of 7e-8.
     - `thermBudget.out` differs in 1 value, the gas-dust cooling of one deep
       cell (A_V 2.96): 1.2e-6 relative.

     **Cause found, not assumed.** `pdrGrainRadM` used to be set as
     `dble(pdrGrainRad)`, and that variable is the single-precision 1.0e-5,
     which widens to 9.99999975e-6. Stage 1 pinned it to `1.0d-5`, which
     moves the vendored grain radius by 2.5e-8. Its only live consumer on
     the stage-1 path is 3D-PDR's gas-grain term heat(11). The D-093
     feedback fed that term into T_dust, and T_dust sets MOCASSIN's
     gas-dust term. So the two quantities that moved are exactly that
     chain, in its order. Stage 2 removes the chain, so stage 1 was not
     re-run.
  2. **Failed as stated, for a reason of my own making.** The census lines
     `[D196]`, `[D202]`, `[D205]`, `[D210]`, `[D213]`, `[D217]` and
     `[D218]` differ because stage 1 widened them from zone cells to all gas
     cells, which the prediction overlooked. The diagnostics that were not
     touched agree exactly: all 80 `[D350]` photorate-table lines and all
     `[D220]` lines are identical.

So stage 1 is physics-neutral.

**Stage 2** (`runs/d352-s2` against `runs/d352-s1`, same seed).
Convergence is 76.40% against 76.12%. `tools/d352_grainbal.py`, bin means
new/old:

    A_V bin    cells   T_dust    T_gas     x(H2)     x(CO)
    0.00-0.20    43   1.00219   0.99994   0.99661   0.99968
    0.20-0.47   109   1.01088   0.99994   0.97904   0.98865
    0.47-0.80   450   1.00487   1.00087   1.51982   1.18431
    0.80-1.20   914   1.01014   0.99935   0.97503   0.95870
    1.20-1.60  1565   1.02358   0.99815   0.99211   0.98842
    1.60-2.10  3180   1.03569   0.99963   0.99885   1.00519
    2.10-2.60  4812   1.02941   0.99989   0.99986   0.99936
    2.60-3.05  4131   1.02076   0.99932   0.99995   1.00079

  3. **Direction held; size failed, 2-3x the estimate.** At A_V < 0.8 T_dust
     rose 0.2-1.1%, against a predicted < 0.2%. Beyond A_V 1.6 it rose
     2.1-3.6%, against a predicted 0.1-1.5%. The seed scatter of a bin-mean
     T_dust is 0.01-0.05% (the `d334` four-seed ensemble), so these rises
     are 10-100 sigma. The estimate put heat(2) at 1-6% of the absorbed
     FUV, using a bulk cross section per H. Measured, the loss was ~10-20% of
     what the grains that set the mean absorb. One plausible reason: D-093
     spread the loss by geometric area, while small grains absorb less than
     their area at long wavelengths. Not decomposed further.
  4. **Held.** The ionization front moved from 3.8614 to 3.8615 pc, the H/H2
     crossing from 1.3641 to 1.3701, and C+ = C from 2.2896 to 2.2906.
  5. **Held.** T_gas moved within 0.2%. x(H2) and x(CO) moved within the
     seed scatter of the bin mean, which the ensemble puts at 23-30% at A_V
     0.47-1.2, where both are trace, and below 1% deeper. The +52% in x(H2)
     at 0.47-0.8 is 1.6 sd of a pair difference, and the ensemble predates
     D-350's noise, so it is a lower bound.

What it means: the PDR's grains were being cooled by an energy loss the gas
never received, and removing it raises their temperature 2-4% beyond A_V 1.
That is toward Cloudy. L-19's "9-13% cool" was measured on pn150k before this
change and should be re-measured. Figures in `runs/d352-s2/figs/` (`d348_*`,
new against stage 1, with the 3D-PDR reference).

### Also found and fixed on the way

  - **The chemical networks were never under version control.**
    `.gitignore`'s boilerplate `*.d` (compiler dependency files) matched
    `dataPDR/species_*.d` and `rates_*.d`, so a fresh clone could not run
    any PDR model. They are now tracked, through a `!dataPDR/*.d`
    exception. sha256 of the two in use: `species_reduced.d`
    `9c7ffbf0...62878c5`, `rates_reduced.d` `06c6c453...d01a4f` (full hashes
    in the commit). Whether they are byte-identical to upstream's
    `chemfiles/` was not checked, since there is no local upstream copy.
  - `tools/__pycache__/` was tracked despite being ignored; it is now
    untracked.
  - The man page's PDR section is rewritten. It documented `pdrDustModel`
    with default 1 (it was 0), `pdrFcrit` 0.10 (0.005) and `pdrZoneLimit`
    0.5 (0.3), and listed options that did nothing.
  - `tools/regress.sh` is now a seeded new-against-baseline regression with
    the retired variables removed from the environment. `doc/dust.md` is
    updated.

### Left open in this class (not changed)

  - **Clamps.**
    - The chemistry's rates are evaluated at Te clamped to [pdrTmin,
      pdrTmax], its heating at the unclamped Te; this touches 3 cells of
      pn150k and none of hiipdr.
    - `teFloor` holds T at 10 K or above; it binds nowhere in hiipdr today.
    - The chemistry's T_dust is floored at T_CMB, because MOCASSIN
      transports no CMB. Where the floor binds, MOCASSIN's own dust emission
      sees a colder grain.
  - **Vendored stand-ins on live paths.** `escape_probability`'s fixed
    NGRAIN dust background, and the turbulent heating length L_TURB = 5 pc.
    The 1D flavour still hands the chemistry the prescription (D-350 audit
    item 5).
  - **Diagnostic-only switches.** `MOCASSIN_DUSTPROBE` and `pdrSplitField`.
  - **Reference-only outputs.** `pdrHeat` and `pdrHeatPE` in `pdrGrid.out`
    are 3D-PDR's reference values; nothing uses them.
  - **pn150k** has not been run on the current code (D-351 item 7).

### Status

Accepted.

### pn150k on the current code

`runs/d353-pn150k`: clean exit, **90.13% converged at iteration 9** (against
`d334-pn150k/s1001`'s 90.52% at 10), 1 h 28 min. No cell missed ion or Te
balance in any iteration. The two runs track each other iteration for
iteration until the chemistry engages (0.161% and 0.161% at iteration 3, 0.820
and 0.828 at 4), then part. From `tools/d285_kpis.py` and `tools/d326_check.py`
against `runs/d302-cloudy-trim-rad/150k`:

    quantity                 old code (s1001)   now      Cloudy
    H+ front [pc]                 0.1280       0.1282    0.1279
    He2+ front [pc]               0.0844       0.0831    0.0880

    against 1.09). The cause is the same, D-348/D-350: in this run's last iteration
    MOCASSIN's Lyman-Werner window field is 4.9 / 6.1 / 6.4x the old
    prescription's H2 field in the A_V bins 0-0.2 / 0.2-0.47 / 0.47-0.8 (the
    direct beam alone 2.8 / 2.2 / 1.9x), against 2.5-4.6x on hiipdr. A
    150 kK star is harder still in the window than a 40 kK one. That one
    fixture now agrees and the other does not is itself the result: whatever
    separates MOCASSIN's H2 from Cloudy's on hiipdr is no longer the
    chemistry ignoring the field MOCASSIN transports.
  - **CO fell toward Cloudy.** n(CO) at A_V 0.30 / 0.50 / 0.65 went from

    Cloudy's 2.7e-6 / 4.2e-6 / 2.4e-6. The edge excess went from 60x to 2.6x.
    At A_V 0.30 it is now 0.15x, below Cloudy.
  - **T_gas fell 6% and 4% at A_V 0.28 and 0.37**, the depths the H2
    transition moved through (n(H2) at A_V 0.30: 374 to 107 cm^-3, Cloudy 110).
    It is unchanged within 1.2% elsewhere. The photoelectric heating moved
    by 2.2% at most, so the change is not in the heating's input; the
    mechanism is not decomposed. The ensemble bars at those depths are
    0.07-0.21%, so it is 30-60 of those sigma, and they are now a lower
    bound (L-26).
  - **T_dust rose 3-7% in the PDR, toward Cloudy: 0.935 / 0.930 / 0.921 /
    0.930 of it at A_V 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.50 / 0.65** (0.907 / 0.899 / 0.869 /
    0.872 on the old code). This is D-352's grain balance, and larger here
    than on hiipdr (2-4%).
  - **But T_dust fell 7-8% in the ionized gas, away from Cloudy**: 82.5 and
    57.3 K at A_V 0.05 and 0.10 (88.7 and 62.1 before), against Cloudy's 87.5
    and 70.8, so 0.943 and 0.809 of it (was 1.014 and 0.877). The grain
    balance is the only change here that acts on T_dust. It swapped two terms
    in every dusty cell: 3D-PDR's `heat(2)` (a PAH photoelectric loss) and
    `heat(11)` (gas-grain exchange for fixed 0.1 um grains, evaluated here at

    T ~ P^(1/5.5), a 7% fall means roughly a third less net heating. Which of
    the two swaps supplies that has **not been decomposed; open.** Only
    MOCASSIN's versions of the two terms describe this dust, so the new
    balance is the self-consistent one either way.

    0.62-0.71) stands as it did.
