## D-367 - The mirror-reflection fix on `dev` (2026-09-27)

The user: "this seems like an important bug to be fixed in the dev branch
also", then "I mean the dev branch in this repository. Do not touch any other
repository".

### Misstep first

I read "the dev branch" as the core fork's `dev` (`~/software/mocassin_HM_2026`,
pushed to GitHub), because it carries this branch's earlier fixes as its own
commits (901a7f8 is D-281's 411ff93) and is newer than this repository's `dev`.
I made a worktree there on a new branch `fix/mirror-scattering-direction`,
applied the fix uncommitted and built. On the user's correction all of it was
removed: worktree, branch, edit. The one `git stash`/`pop` made in that worktree
left the stash list empty. That repository is as it was: `dev` at fea0149, the
user's 31 uncommitted files, no new reflog entries. Recorded in the memory
notes: ports go to this repository's `dev`, and other repositories are not
touched.

### The port

Worktree of this repository's `dev` (a3f5ce5) at `~/software/mocassin_dev`.
`photon_mod.f90` there has CRLF endings (3260 of 3260 lines), and the four
reflection sites are the same as on this branch: two `symmetricXYZ` blocks in
the step loop, the four `planeIonization` walls, and the end-of-segment block.
Each gets `enPacket%direction = vHat`, with the explanation at the step-loop
reflection and no DEVLOG numbers (dev's comments carry none). Diff: 22 lines,
endings kept. Built without and with the fix by swapping the file (no stash).
All four targets build. Tracked binaries restored before the commit, as in
D-281. Committed as **da02212**, not pushed. Worktree removed.

### The check on dev

`dev` has no `randomSeed`, so a byte-identity test is impossible there.
`dust/1D/p0tau10` cannot see the defect: its grains are heated in the IR by a
2500 K star and scatter little, so both binaries give 0.1-0.3%.

The discriminating test is hiipdr run by dev as a dust+gas model: the same
input with the `pdr*` and `randomSeed` lines removed, `maxIterateMC 5 90.`, 3
ranks each (`runs/d366-dev-before`, `runs/d366-dev-after`). Both converged and
stopped at iteration 3. Median deviation of ln T_dust from its radial profile,
by radius quartile:

    quartile            1        2        3        4
    axis    before   +0.0122  +0.0265  +0.0313  +0.0276
            after    -0.0023  -0.0007  -0.0010  +0.0005
    planes  before   +0.0204  +0.0390  +0.0422  +0.0405
            after    +0.0002  -0.0021  -0.0023  +0.0001
    diag    before   -0.0258  -0.0268  -0.0230  -0.0191
            after    -0.0138  -0.0020  -0.0014  -0.0023

This is the PDR flavour's pattern (this branch, the same measure: +2.8/+3.5/
-2.0% before, <0.2% after). The innermost diagonal -1.4% has 103 cells and
shows in every fixed run on both branches. Hbeta 13.401 -> 13.425 E36 (+0.18%).

### Not done

  - Not pushed.
  - The slab (planeIonization) change is argued neutral (D-366) and was not run.

chi 0.3-1.2%, an upper bound.

### Lines (intrinsic / Hbeta)

    line          41^3 6e6   81^3 1e9   Cloudy    81^3/Cloudy  (41^3/Cloudy)
    [O I] 63      0.252      0.236      0.187     1.26         (1.35)
    [O I] 145     0.0211     0.0196     0.0145    1.35         (1.46)
    [O I] 6300    0.423      0.367      0.292     1.26         (1.45)
    [C II] 158    0.199      0.202      0.311     0.65         (0.64)
    [C I] 609     1.29e-4    1.32e-4    2.41e-4   0.55         (0.54)
    [C I] 370     1.81e-4    1.88e-4    4.26e-4   0.44         (0.43)
    C II] 2325    0.809      0.764      0.617     1.24         (1.31)
    Hbeta [E34]   2.624      2.590

**[O I] 63 is not a resolution artefact here.** Split by ionization class
(the chemistry's per-cell 63 um emissivity, `scratchpad/d365_oiwhere.py`), the
front cells (x(H+) 0.01-0.95) give 68% at 41^3 and 70% at 81^3, and their
absolute emission is **0.95x** for half the cell size - against 0.53x on
hiipdr. A 150 kK star's hard photons penetrate far past the 13.6 eV front, so
the partially ionized zone has a physical thickness the 0.015 pc grid already
resolves; hiipdr's 40 kK front does not have one. The 1.26x against Cloudy is
therefore a model difference to be explained, not a grid effect, and what
the version-15 pn150k page says ("the front is thinner still ... a finer grid is
the test") is wrong for this model.

### Profiles (tools/d285_kpis.py against runs/d356-cloudy-pn/150k)

H+ front 0.1282 -> 0.1279 pc (Cloudy 0.1279). H/H2 crossing A_V 0.402 ->
0.407 (Cloudy 0.368). PDR T_gas 25-44 -> 25-45 K (Cloudy 37-66); the selected
depths A_V 0.3-0.65 move by 1-6%. The PDR's radial means were converged at
41^3. The figures (`runs/d365-pn81/figs`) are those of D-363 with a smoother
front.

The ionized-gas lines moved more: He II 4686 0.301 -> 0.268 (-11%), [Ne II]
-15%, [S II] 6716/31 -11%, [O I] 6300 -13%, [O IV] 25.9 -6%, [N II] -4%. **The
He2+ front had not converged when the run stopped** (`scratchpad/
d365_fronts_pn.py` on the snapshots):

    it     5       6       7       8
    He2+   0.0683  0.0730  0.0769  0.0799 pc   (41^3 final 0.0833, Cloudy 0.0880)
    H+     0.1342  0.1309  0.1292  0.1283 pc

The H+ front has nearly settled; the He2+ front is still moving outward
0.003 pc per iteration. The 94% converged-cell criterion does not see it
(convLimit tests x(H0) only), so He II 4686's -11% is iteration count, not
resolution. This is L-40 again, now with a He front and a run that stopped
itself.

### Predictions

  - P5 ([O I] 63 1.35x -> 0.8-0.9x Cloudy): **fails** - 1.26x, for the reason
    above.

### Not known

  - Why pn150k's [O I] 63/145/6300 run 1.26-1.35x Cloudy's, now that the grid
    is excluded.
  - Where He2+ would settle, and whether He II 4686 then returns to 41^3's
    value.

### Status

Open (L-40).

## D-370 - Third audit against science production: Hbeta, line escape, the stopping rule (2026-09-27)

The user: "audit the code and decide on the next step considering science
production as the main objective". D-351 and D-360 ranked the blockers before;
D-360's decision ("one reality for every line MOCASSIN reports") was carried
out as D-361 (H I list), D-362/D-363 (PDR lines, one atom per ion), and its
third step, L-27, was not started - D-365..D-369 were the user's fine-grid
runs. This entry audits the code changed since D-360 and asks again what a
paper would quote from a run today, and whether it is right. Everything was
measured on files already on disk; no new runs.

### What was read

  - The D-361..D-366 diffs: `buildPdrAtomMap`, `setLineColliders`,
    `pdrNeutralRates`, the `equilibrium` changes in `emission_mod`, the
    `escape_beta` hook, the retired D-133 substitution, the D-365 packet count
    and the four D-366 reflection sites.
  - pdrStep's line-escape set-up and the vendored `escape_probability`.
  - The per-cell convergence test (`update_mod`) and the stopping logic
    (`iteration_mod`).
  - The H recombination-line path in `output_mod`, `emission_mod` and
    `mocassinPlot`, and `data/e1bx.dat`.
  - Every `(nCells, nbins)` allocation and its lifetime.
  - **Checked clean.**
    - D-363's neutral colliders cannot double count H2: every coolant file
      lists either total H2 or o/p-H2 for a transition, never both, so the
      thermal o/p split is applied once. The collider H0 is atomic H only
      (x(HI) excludes H2 since D-177). The rate interpolation holds at the
      table ends as `FIND_CCOEFF` does.
    - `pdrLineEm`/`pdrLineBeta` reach every rank: the temporaries are zeroed,
      only the owner fills a cell, and the sum is allreduced, so rank 0's
      `outputGas` and every rank's next thermal balance see every cell.

### Finding 1 (new): the reported Hbeta is 5% low, and every line ratio 5% high

`output_mod.f90` `RecLinesEmission` sets Hbeta = 2530/T^0.833 [1e-25 erg cm^3
s^-1] and takes every other H I line as a ratio to it from Storey & Hummer's
case B table, `data/e1bx.dat`, via `hlinex` (`HIRecLines = (fh/hb)*Hbeta`).
`hlinex(4,2)` is the table's own Hbeta, already computed on the line above and
used only as the ratio's denominator. Against it, at n_e = 100:

    T [K]            3000   5000   7500  10000  12500  15000  20000
    power / table   0.984  0.954  0.948  0.954  0.965  0.977  1.005

The commented-out fit beside it, 10^(-0.870 log T + 3.57), is 0.996-1.005 of
the table over 7.5-15 kK. That fit is the one the transport uses
(`emission_mod.f90` `RecLinesEmission`, with the fixed n_e = 100 ratio table
`r1b0100.dat`). So Hbeta has three realities: the table (H I line ratios), the
fit (the energy the MC carries in H I lines), and the power law (the Hbeta
that `lineFlux.out` reports and that divides every other line). `mocassinPlot`
carries a copy of the power law. It is upstream code, present since the
import (`38aca36`) and on `dev`, and it touches the plain flavour as much as
the PDR ones.

**Size, per run** (`tools/d370_hbeta.py`: the table at each cell's T and n_e,
weighted by n_e n_p dV, octant x8, symmetric-plane cells at half width, which
reproduces the sphere's volume to 0.07%):

    run            <T>_EM   factor   Hbeta reported -> table [E36]
    d366-hii        9005 K   1.0546    8.843 -> 9.325
    d363-hii        9009 K   1.0546    8.821 -> 9.303
    d363-pn        12357 K   1.0404    0.02624 -> 0.02730
    d365-pn81      12263 K   1.0411    0.02590 -> 0.02697

Every non-H I line ratio in those runs' `lineFlux.out` is high by the same
factor. H I ratios are not (both sides come from the table).

**What it does to the gap to Cloudy.** Integrating Cloudy's own zones with the
same table:

    hiipdr   EM MOCASSIN/Cloudy 0.989   <T>_EM 9005 K / 8628 K (1.044)
             Hbeta 9.325 (table) against 9.804 (Cloudy's zones, same table),
             0.951 - the hotter gas (emissivity ~0.96) and the EM (0.99)
    pn150k   EM 1.004   <T>_EM 12357 K / 12339 K (1.001)
             Hbeta 0.02730 against 0.02717, 1.005

Against Cloudy's printed Hbeta, hiipdr goes from 8.843/10.00 = -11.6% to
-6.7%. The D-365/L-40 reading of the gap as "not yet a converged number" was
incomplete: most of it is this formula and the rest the ionized gas's 4.4%
excess temperature. On pn150k the nebula's structure matches Cloudy's to 0.4%
in emission measure and 0.1% in temperature, and the formula was the only
Hbeta difference. (Cloudy's integrated zones fall 2% short of its own printed
Hbeta on hiipdr; the pn150k page's Cloudy Hbeta has been ambiguous since
D-303/D-359, which is why the like-for-like integral is used here.)

### Finding 2 (L-27, re-sized): the line-escape flaw is now in the cooling and the lines

Since D-363 MOCASSIN's own C I, C II and O I atoms take the chemistry's escape
probability per transition, so L-27 now sets both the thermal balance and the
reported fine-structure lines. pdrStep still hands `escape_probability` the
slab closed form: HEALPix nside 1 read as three rings about the radial
direction, the four `mu = 0` rays given `colA = 1e30`, so beta <= 2/3 for a
thin line, and the cell's own populations carried over the whole column to the
boundary. In the two-level limit the emission goes as beta/(x + beta), x =
n/n_crit, so taking beta from 2/3 to 1 raises [C II] 158 (n_crit ~3e3 on H)
by 2/12/38/50% at n_H 1e2/1e3/1e4/1e5 - the same numbers as L-27's "2/11/28/33%
lost". hiipdr (1e2) does not see it; pn150k (1e3) does; the PDRs of real
planetary nebulae (1e4-1e5) are dominated by it. It is the D-360 step still
open.

### Finding 3: the stopping rule does not test helium

The per-cell test (`update_mod`, D-155/D-179/D-229) passes a cell when x(H0),
x(H2) (PDR runs) and T_e have each changed by less than `convLimit` since the
iteration began. L-40 said "x(H0) only"; that is corrected. Helium is not
tested, so pn150k 81^3 stopped at 94% with its He2+ front still moving 0.003
pc per iteration and He II 4686 11% low (D-368). In a planetary nebula, He II
4686 is the stellar-temperature diagnostic.

### Finding 4: the memory model, measured

Three measured points - 31^3 hiipdr 1.05 GB/rank (PSS, D-243), 61^3 hiipdr
4.97 GB (cgroup peak / 7, D-365), 81^3 pn150k 10.3-11.5 GB (D-368) - fit

    per rank = 0.47 GB + 38 kB per ACTIVE cell     (nbins 600, dust+gas+PDR)

(15,204, 117,262 and 275,545 active cells; the fit through the first two
predicts 11.05 GB for the third). The documented 234 MB + 10.5 kB/cell was
per cell of a smaller configuration and understates these fixtures ~3.6x per
active cell. At 14 ranks and the ~31 GB budget that is ~46k active cells,
about 44^3 for an octant sphere - not 58^3. hiipdr 31^3 (15k) and pn150k 41^3
(35k) fit at 14 ranks, which is why nothing has hit it. Of the 38 kB, the nine
`(nCells, nbins)` real arrays (`opacity`, `absOpac`, `scaOpac`, `recPDF`,
`dustPDF`, `Jste`, `Jdif`, `escapedPackets`, `JPEots`) are 21.6 kB and at most
two transient reduction buffers another 4.8 kB. About 11 kB is not itemized
here. Five of the nine (opacity, abs/sca opacity, the two emission PDFs) are
read-only during transport; sharing them per node would give ~1.5x the cells
per rank.

### Smaller findings, recorded

  - `escape_probability` pumps the lines with a vendored diffuse-ISM grain
    emissivity (`NGRAIN = 2e-12 n_H`, rho 2, 0.01 x 1.3nu/3e11) - a constant
    standing in for the dust emission MOCASSIN transports (`Jdif` at the line
    frequency). It enters only the chemistry's own solve, i.e. CO's lines and
    cooling and the beta it hands on. MOCASSIN's atoms take beta but no
    background term at all; for [C I] 609 um the CMB occupation is ~2e-4, so
    that is negligible. To be taken with L-27, the same routine.
  - He II 4686 (10^(-0.997 log T + 5.16)) and Lya are single power-law fits as
    well. S&H's He II table is not on disk (`r2b0100.dat` holds ratios only),
    so neither is checked.
  - `pdrCoolTab` (CO's table) and `pdrHeatXtra` are still rank-local and
    right only because updateCell and pdrStep share the ownership formula
    (D-351 item 13).
  - The warm start is still unverified (L-14). It becomes the practical route
    once a production model needs more iterations than one sitting (L-40).
  - `pdr-photoionization` is 129 commits ahead of `origin/main` with no remote
    branch.

### The ranking, for science production

**A - wrong in what a paper quotes, now**
  1. Hbeta, and through it every line ratio (Finding 1, new L-41). Small.
  2. PDR line escape (Finding 2, L-27). Medium: the ray walk exists.
  3. The stopping rule without helium (Finding 3, L-40). Small.

**B - divergences to report, not blockers.**
  - hiipdr's ionized gas 4.4% hotter than Cloudy's (new; pn150k's matches to
    0.1%).
  - The H/H2 crossing; pn150k's colder PDR.
  - L-32, L-33, L-34.
  - L-37's resolution check, per model.

**C - maps.** L-26's per-cell noise. D-365/D-368 showed 21x the tracks buys
~5x; accumulating the estimator is the user's design decision.

**D - capacity.** Finding 4. Not the next step: pn150k's radial means were
already converged at 41^3 (D-368), and a PN model of the usual size fits.

**E - provenance.** Nothing is off this machine; pushing needs the user's
word.

### Decision

Next is to **finish D-360's A: one reality for every line MOCASSIN reports**,
in this order.

  1. **Hbeta from the table.** `output_mod` and `mocassinPlot` take Hbeta from
     `hlinex(4,2)` at the cell's T and n_e, the source the other H I lines
     already use. He II 4686 and Lya are checked against their sources in the
     same pass. The transport's copy in `emission_mod` (0.1-2% from the table
     at 5-15 kK) is brought onto the table as a separate seeded pair, because
     it changes the physics. Verification needs no new run: `mocassinOutput`
     on `runs/d366-hii`, `runs/d363-pn` and the four Lexington grids.
     - H I ratios must be unchanged.
     - Every other ratio must fall by that run's factor, and Hbeta rise by
       it.
     - Nothing else may move.
     The plain flavour is affected, so a port to this repository's `dev` is
     the user's call, as D-367 was.
  2. **L-27 along the real 3D rays.** Per-ray line columns along the twelve
     HEALPix directions the D-348 walk already takes, mirror reflection
     included, accumulating each traversed cell's level populations
     (`pdrLevPop` is on every rank). That is 3D-PDR's own tau along a ray.
     - Rays leave at the outer boundary.
     - The `mu = 0` rule and the slab closed form go.
     - The vendored grain emissivity is replaced by MOCASSIN's own field.
     Predictions go on record before the runs.
  3. **Helium in the per-cell test**, so the rebuild runs stop where their He
     lines have settled.

Then one seeded run of each fixture and both Cloudy pages rebuilt.

### What is not known

  - Why hiipdr's ionized gas is 4.4% hotter than Cloudy's when pn150k's
    matches to 0.1%.
  - Whether the He II 4686 and Lya fits are right.
  - Where ~11 kB per active cell of the memory goes.

### Status

Decided, awaiting the user's go-ahead. No model code changed; the tool
`tools/d370_hbeta.py` added.

## D-371 - Hbeta from Storey & Hummer's own table (2026-09-27)

The user: "start step 1 and apply Hbeta fix to dev then correct the memory
figure in CLAUDE.md". Step 1 of D-370's decision; closes L-41.

### What changed

`output_mod.f90` `RecLinesEmission`: Hbeta = `hlinex(4,2)` x 1e25 x n_e x
x(H+) x abundance, at the cell's T and n_e. That is the e1bx.dat value the
routine already computed as the denominator of every other H I line. The
power law 2530/T^0.833 stays as a comment, and the new value is computed only
where `hlinex` returned a finite, non-zero number (the existing guard).
`mocassinPlot.f90` carries the same change in its copy. The D-361 comment in
`hlinex` is corrected: below 300 K Hbeta is now the 300 K value too, not a
fit's.

### Verification (no new run)

The unfixed `mocassinOutput`, built in the PDR and plain flavours, run on
copies of six grids (`runs/d371-hbeta/<model>/base`), reproduced each run's
own `lineFlux.out`, and `lineFluxMol.out` where there is one, **byte for
byte**. The fixed build was then run on the same copies (`.../fix`):

    model       Hbeta [E36] base -> fix      F        (D-370 tool predicted)
    d366-hii    8.8427  -> 9.3004         1.0518        1.0546
    d363-pn     0.026241 -> 0.027263      1.0390        1.0404
    HII40       19.179  -> 20.211         1.0538
    HII20       4.6777  -> 4.9335         1.0547
    PN150       0.26953 -> 0.28108        1.0428
    PN75        0.055412 -> 0.058116      1.0488

The tool differs from the code by up to 0.3% because it interpolates the
table in its own way; `hlinex` uses 5-point Lagrange polynomials.

Every number in the files was compared row by row (`scratchpad/d371_cmp2.py`,
rows aligned on their integer keys):
  - Every changed He I, He II and heavy-ion value, and `lineFluxMol`'s
    L/Hbeta, is exactly 1/F of its old value, to 2e-6. Absolute luminosities
    do not change.
  - The [S II]/[O II] density and the [N II]/[O II]/[O III] temperature
    diagnostics are identical.
  - H I ratios move by -0.075% to +0.038%. Each H I line is now the table's
    own emissivity summed over cells. Before, it was the table's ratio times
    the power law, which weighted hot and cool cells slightly differently.
  - The one H I entry that falls by 1/F is the 30->8 slot, which holds Lya's
    fit (D-372).
  - Two lines of ~1e-33 and 1e-45 Hbeta fell below the print threshold.
  - No other output file changed.

### Against the references

**Lexington** (`scratchpad/lex371.py`, the codes' ranges from
`dev_bench/lex/lex.json`). Hbeta is now inside the codes' range on all four
models; before, three were below it:

    model   codes (median)       base     fix      fix/median
    HII40   2.02-2.10 (2.05)     1.918    2.021    0.986
    HII20   4.83-5.04 (4.89)     4.678    4.933    1.009
    PN150   2.47-2.86 (2.755)    2.695    2.811    1.020
    PN75    5.56-6.08 (5.74)     5.541    5.812    1.012

The line ratios, which all fall by 1/F, move both ways:
  - HII40: in range 14 -> 14; median |dex| 0.040 -> 0.032.
  - HII20: in range 8 -> 11; median |dex| 0.057 -> 0.034.
  - PN150: in range 24 -> 24; median |dex| 0.077 -> 0.091.
  - PN75: in range 15 -> 15; median |dex| 0.072 -> 0.085.
The PN lines were already low (D-362's unattributed 10-35% fall), and a
correct Hbeta moves them further down. That is D-362's open question, not
something this fix introduced.

**Cloudy.**
  - hiipdr: 9.300 against 10.00 (-7.0%). Like-for-like, with both codes'
    zones integrated with the same table, it is 0.95: emission measure
    0.989, ionized gas 4.4% hotter.
  - pn150k: 0.02726 against Cloudy's intrinsic 0.0278 (2.78e34 erg/s, from
    "print line flux earth" at 1 kpc). Like-for-like it is 1.003.
  - Cloudy's own saved per-zone Hbeta emissivity (`150k.emis`, fully ionized
    zones) over the S&H table is 1.001 at 11-15 kK, 1.014 at 15-20 kK and
    1.040 at 20-40 kK. That independently confirms the table as the right
    source.

### He II 4686 and Lya

**He II 4686** (`10^(-0.997 log T + 5.16)`). S&H's He II table is not on
disk, but He II is hydrogenic, so case B gives j(He II 4->3, T) = 8 j(H 4->3,
T/4) from the same e1bx.dat. The fit over that is 1.009/1.004/1.001/0.999/
1.008 at 5/7.5/10/12/14 kK, 1.022/1.030 at 17.5/20 kK and 1.054/1.074 at
25/30 kK. **The fit is right** to <=1% below 15 kK and <=3% below 20 kK.
Cloudy's He II 4686 emissivity (`150k.emis`, He++ zones) is 0.80/0.83/0.88
of case B at 12/14/17.5 kK. That is why the fit applied to Cloudy's zones
gives 4686/Hbeta 0.347 against Cloudy's printed 0.280. It is a divergence
to report; a departure from case B in He II's Lyman lines is the candidate,
not decomposed.

**Lya** (`10^(-0.897 log T + 5.05)`). The fit gives 2.9e-24 erg cm^3 s^-1
at 10^4 K, which is what alpha_B through 2p gives there. Its temperature
dependence has no source on disk to test against. Checking where it goes found
D-372.

### The transport's copy

`emission_mod`'s `RecLinesEmission` still uses S&H's fit
10^(-0.870 log T + 3.57), with ratios fixed at 10^4 K (`r1b0100.dat`).
EM-weighted it is 0.994 (hiipdr) and 0.997 (pn150k) of the table, and it
sets only the energy the Monte Carlo carries in non-Lya H I lines. No
reported number depends on it. Moving it onto the table changes the
physics, and `hlinex` lives in `output_mod`, which `emission_mod` cannot
use. It is left for its own seeded pair.

### Builds

`PDR=1 PDRGEOM=3D mocassin`, `PDR=1 mocassin`, `mocassin` and `PDR=1
mocassinWarm` all build. So do `mocassinOutput` and `mocassinPlot` in both
flavours.

### What it means for published numbers

Every Hbeta this project has published is 3.9-5.5% low, and every line in
Hbeta units high by the same factor. That covers both Cloudy pages (hiipdr
v17, 150 kK PN v15) and "Fine Grids Against Cloudy". They are corrected at
the rebuild after steps 2 and 3. Old runs need no rerun: `mocassinOutput`
regenerates `lineFlux.out` from the grids in seconds.

### Status

Done. L-41 closed. The `dev` port is D-373.

## D-372 - Lya is transported as an 8.15 um line (2026-09-27)

Found while checking Lya's fit for D-371.

### The defect

`emission_mod.f90` `RecLinesEmission` (line 566) adds Lya's emissivity to
`HIRecLines(15,8)`, and `output_mod` adds it to `HIRecLines(30,8)`. Upstream
used those slots only to carry Lya's energy into `totalLines` (the line/
continuum split of a diffuse emission) and the analytical sums. That was
harmless while every line packet was given nu = 0 and dropped.

D-292 gave each line in `linePDF` its own frequency, and D-307 made that
transport the default. The (15,8) slot is in the list (ilow = 8 >= 2), so
every packet drawn from it has been emitted at the 15->8 frequency, 1/64 -
1/225 = 0.01118 Ryd = 8.15 um, and traced from there. Lya is nearly all of
that slot. D-292's and D-296's comments that "linePDF starts at ilow = 2, so
the Lyman series and with it Lya is excluded" are wrong, because the slot
carries it.

### Measured, from `SED.out`

    run          spike bin   L [erg/s]    / Lya row   / emergent SED   / 1-1000 um
    d366-hii     8.33 um     1.705e38      0.78         5.6%             6.0%
    d363-pn      8.40 um     7.12e35       1.12         18.8%            27%

The neighbouring bins carry 1e-3 of that or less. pn150k's ratio above 1 is the
other lines sharing the bin plus Monte Carlo noise.

### What it touches

  - **The emergent SED.** It has a spurious line carrying 6-19% of the
    luminosity.
  - **The dust.** In a dusty nebula Lya is destroyed by grains near where it
    is made (D-293: within A_V 0.02 of the front on pn150k). Here that
    energy instead crosses the PDR at 8 um, where grains absorb weakly
    (silicate more than graphite).
  - **L-19.** 0.0112 Ryd lies inside the 0.01-0.44 Ryd band where MOCASSIN's
    field exceeds Cloudy's (1.16-1.36x bolometric, D-307). This is a
    candidate for part of L-19, not measured.
  - **Not touched:** the thermal balance (recombination cooling is computed
    on its own), the FUV photorates except through the dust, and every
    reported line except Lya itself.
  - **`lineFlux.out`** reports Lya in the H I 30->8 row, at 6.28 um and ~25
    Hbeta. It is undocumented in `man/mocassin.1`.
  - **`dev`** has the (15,8) slot but not D-292's transport, so there Lya is
    dropped as it always was, not misplaced.

### Options - the user's decision

  (a) **Absorb Lya by the local dust** where it is made. That is its physical
      fate in a dusty nebula and what D-293 measured. MOCASSIN already has
      resonance-line dust heating (`initResLinePackets`, Kwan & Krolik
      escape), but only behind `resLinesTransfer`, which is off by default
      (101). This keeps the energy in the model and puts it into the IR
      continuum. **Recommended.**
  (b) Emit it at 1216 A as an optically thin line. Wrong: D-293 sized that
      at 6x the stellar FUV in the front cells.
  (c) Drop it, as before D-292. That deletes 6-19% of the luminosity from
      the model.

Any of these also takes Lya out of the 30->8 row of `lineFlux.out` and gives
it a row of its own.

### Status

Open. Registered as L-42. No code changed.

## D-375 - Lya and the resonance-line treatment (2026-09-27)

The user, on D-372: "why not transfer Lya as the other resonance lines?"

### What MOCASSIN's resonance-line treatment is

It is behind `resLinesTransfer`: default 101, i.e. off, and set in no fixture
of this project except `benchmarks/test_Problem`. The code is upstream,
unchanged since the import except where D-233 and D-292 changed what it
calls. It covers the six lines in `data/resLines.dat`: H I Lya, C II 1335,
C IV 1549, N V 1240, Mg II 2800, Si IV 1397.

  - `setResLineEscapeProb` (`emission_mod`), per cell:
    - the line-centre optical depth from the cell to the grid edge, along
      125 directions, on MOCASSIN's own ion densities and T;
    - the escape fraction f_esc = 1/(1 + k_d 2 dx / (k_l P)), with k_d the
      cell's dust absorption at the line and k_l the line-centre opacity
      (Harrington, Cohen & Hess 1984, eqns A1, A5).
  - `resLineHeating` (`update_mod`, inside `getDustT`): the cell's grains
    absorb (1 - f_esc) of the line's local emissivity, shared by their
    cross sections (Harrington, Monk & Clegg 1988 sect. 3.2).
  - `initResLinePackets` / `energyPacketDriver`: that absorbed energy is
    launched from the cell as extra packets, one per stellar-packet energy.

So it is not a resonant-scattering transfer. It is local destruction by dust
with an escape probability, which is D-372's option (a). A real Lya
scattering Monte Carlo (tau_0 ~ 1e5-1e8, core-skipping) would be a project of
its own.

### What the other resonance lines do now

By default, they do what every line has done since D-307: they are drawn
from `linePDF` at full strength and traced as optically thin at their own
wavelength. Lya does the same at 8.15 um (D-372). So none of the six is
treated as a resonance line in any run of this project. In a dusty nebula the
thin treatment under-destroys C IV 1549 and the others as well, but only Lya
is also at the wrong wavelength.

### Why it cannot simply be switched on

  1. **Double counting.** With line transport on, the six lines are still in
     `linePDF` at full strength, Lya through the (15,8) slot. The absorbed
     fraction would go both into the grains and out as line packets.
  2. **The wrong re-emission.** The extra packets are launched as
     `"diffuse"`. Since D-233 that samples the gas's emission only: lines and
     recombination continuum, ionizing photons included. Upstream, the
     `"diffuse"` PDF still mixed in dust emission. Dust-absorbed line energy
     should leave as `"dustEmi"`.
  3. **A physics switch.** `resLinesTransfer` selects physics at run time,
     gated on the convergence percentage. D-352 removed every other such
     switch.

### Proposed

  - All six lines by this scheme, as the default.
  - The absorbed fraction (1 - f_esc) taken out of `linePDF` and re-emitted
    as dust emission.
  - The escaping fraction sent to the emergent spectrum. f_esc is escape
    from the nebula, so the escaping part should not be traced through the
    grid again.
  - Lya taken out of the (15,8) slot and given its own row in `lineFlux.out`.

Tested with a seeded pair on each fixture.

**Predictions, to be fixed before any run:**
  - the 8.3 um line disappears from `SED.out`;
  - the H II region's grains warm;
  - the far-IR continuum gains most of Lya's 5.6% (hiipdr) and 18.8%
    (pn150k) of the luminosity;
  - MOCASSIN's field at 0.01-0.44 Ryd in the PDR falls (L-19).

### Status

Proposed, awaiting the user. No code changed.

## D-376 - Resonance lines destroyed by the local dust, Lya in its own slot (2026-09-27)

The user, on D-375's proposal: "proceed".

### What changed

  - **Lya has its own slot.** `emission_mod`'s `RecLinesEmission` keeps Lya
    in `LyaEmis` instead of adding it to `HIRecLines(15,8)`. `setLineNuP`
    gives it the last slot of `linePDF`, at 1215.67 A (`lineTrLya`). It still
    enters `totalLines`, so the gas's line/continuum split is unchanged.
    `output_mod` does the same: Lya has a row of its own, "HI 1216 (Lya)",
    after He II 4686, and the H I 30->8 row is that line alone. `mocassinPlot`
    stops adding Lya to its 30->8 entry.
  - **The six resonance lines are found among the stored lines.** These are
    H I Lya, C II 1335, C IV 1549, N V 1240, Mg II 2800 and Si IV 1397.
    `setLineNuP` builds `lineTrRes(slot)` from `resLines.dat`'s levels.
    Each component's wavelength in MOCASSIN's own atomic data must be within
    2% of the file's, or the run stops. That guards against the level
    numbering having changed with the data files (CHIANTI, D-330). Every
    component was found on both fixtures.
  - **The escape probabilities are computed in every iteration of every
    dust+gas run.** `setResLineEscapeProb` is unchanged except that it zeroes
    before accumulating. It is called from `emissionDriver` for each cell,
    zeroed on every rank beforehand and allreduced afterwards.
  - **The draw.** In `newPhotonPacket`, a diffuse packet drawn on a
    resonance-line slot is destroyed by the dust with probability
    1 - f_esc(cell, line). It then leaves the cell as dust emission (a
    frequency from the cell's `dustPDF`). Otherwise it is traced at the
    line's own frequency, as every line is. `[D376]` reports per iteration
    how many were drawn and how many destroyed.
  - **The grains are heated by the destroyed fraction.** `getDustT`'s
    `resLineHeating` (Harrington, Monk & Clegg 1988) is always on for dust
    and gas. It was gated on `resLinesTransfer`.
  - **Removed:** `initResLinePackets`, `resLinePackets` and the extra-packet
    loop in `energyPacketDriver`, which launched the destroyed fraction as
    gas emission on top of full-strength lines, and `lgResLinesFirst`.
    `resLinesTransfer` is retired as a no-effect keyword (D-352's
    mechanism). The variable remains only for the grid checkpoint's format.
    The "dust temperatures may be underestimated" warning that every
    dust+gas run printed is gone with it.
  - **Checkpoint.** `writeGrid` writes `output/resLineEsc.out`.
    `mocassinOutput` and `mocassinWarm` call `initResLines` and
    `readResLineEsc`, so `lineFlux.out`'s "Resonance Lines Attenuated by dust
    absorption" table, now printed in every dust+gas run, regenerates from a
    grid.
  - **`man/mocassin.1`:** the keyword is documented as retired, with what
    replaced it. The entry's name `resLineTransfer` is corrected.

### A correction to D-375's proposal

D-375 said the escaping fraction should go straight to the emergent
spectrum, "f_esc is escape from the nebula". Reading the formula again, it
is not. The line-centre optical depth accumulates only where the ion exists,
and the dust term is the emitting cell's own k_d. So f_esc is escape from
resonant trapping, and once out of the ion's zone the photon meets only
dust. It is therefore traced, thin, at the line's frequency, and the PDR's
grains can still absorb it. For Lya it makes no difference, because f_esc is
~1e-5.

### The runs

  - hiipdr: `runs/d376-hii` (new binary) against `runs/d366-hii` (the
    committed physics). 31^3, seed 1001, 4 ranks, 11 iterations, 42:50.
  - pn150k: `runs/d376-pn-new` against `runs/d376-pn-base`. Both built from
    2bd8123 and this change, seed 1001, 5 ranks, exactly 9 iterations
    (`maxIterateMC 9 100.`).
  - Plain flavour: the four Lexington models at 2 ranks
    (`runs/d376-lex/*/{base,new}`), and PN150 and PN75 at seed 1002 for the
    scatter.

The three dust+gas runs ran concurrently. The predictions were written
before any of them (`scratchpad/d376_pred.md`). Tools:

## D-377 - Line escape along the real 3D rays (L-27; D-370 step 2) (2026-09-28)

The user: "proceed to step 2".

### What changed

  - **The rays.** `traceLineRays` (new, `pdr_mod`) walks the twelve HEALPix
    nside=1 directions from the cell. It uses the same fixed grid-frame set,
    the same stepping at the finest axis spacing, and the same mirror
    folding at the lower faces of a symmetricXYZ octant as D-348's
    `traceDiffuseSites`. Each ray becomes a run-length list of (cell, path
    length) to the upper faces. Inactive cells, beyond Rout or in an inner
    cavity, add nothing, and the ray runs on through them. The walk is done
    once per cell in pdrStep, before the coolant loop.
  - **The optical depth.** In the 3D flavour each ray's evaluation points are
    those cells. Each point carries that cell's level populations
    (`pdrLevPop`, last iteration's, on every rank) over its path. This cell's
    own points take its current iterate inside the level iteration.
    `escape_probability` already accepts several points per ray
    (`maxpoints`, `s_jjr`, `length`), so it sums tau per ray unchanged: this
    is 3D-PDR's tau along a ray.
  - **What goes.** The slab closed form is removed. It read HEALPix nside=1
    as three rings about the radial direction; it gave the four mu = 0 rays
    an infinite column, capping beta at 2/3 for a thin line; and it carried
    this cell's populations over the whole column, to the edge or to the
    star. Since D-363 that beta is what MOCASSIN's own C, C+ and O atoms
    cool the gas and report their lines with.
  - **The background.** `escape_bg` (new vendored hook, `modules.F90` and
    `escape_probability.F90`, recorded in `UPSTREAM.md`) replaces the
    vendored grain emissivity (`NGRAIN = 2e-12 n_H x metallicity` at the
    chemistry's T_dust, a diffuse-ISM constant) with MOCASSIN's own mean
    intensity in the bin the line falls in, J_nu = Jste/(4 pi dnu).
    - The CMB is still added analytically, since MOCASSIN does not transport
      it.
    - Each transition's bin is tabulated once (`buildTrBins`), by the rule
      MOCASSIN places its own line packets with.
    - The bin average includes the bin's share of the thin lines MOCASSIN
      transports there, a small pumping term at these wavelengths.
    - It applies in both PDR flavours. The 1D slab fixtures (L-11) have not
      been re-run.

### The runs

Pairs at the same seed, rank count and iteration count. The base is
a29d616 (D-376):
  - hiipdr `runs/d377-hii` against `runs/d376-hii`: 31^3, 4 ranks, 11
    iterations, 42:10 against 42:50.
  - pn150k `runs/d377-pn` against `runs/d376-pn-new`: 41^3, 5 ranks, 9
    iterations, 48:07 against 62:47. The base shared the machine with two
    other runs.

A 15^3 smoke pair (`runs/d377-smoke`, 6 iterations) came first. The
predictions (`scratchpad/d377_pred.md`) were written after it and before
these. Tools: `tools/d377_escape.py` (new: median beta per zone from
`pdrLineEm.out`), `tools/d285_kpis*.py`.

### Median escape probability

x(H+) > 0.5 ("ion.") and the PDR by A_V band; base -> new:

    hiipdr        ion.          A_V 0.5-1    1-1.5        1.5-2        2-2.5        2.5-3.5
    [C II] 158    0.659->0.498  0.139->0.159 0.110->0.178 0.109->0.239 0.396->0.439 0.435->0.621
    [O I] 63      0.666->0.338  0.114->0.106 0.093->0.114 0.095->0.135 0.128->0.184 0.228->0.326
    [C I] 609     1.000->0.592  0.666->0.229 0.664->0.209 0.635->0.187 0.107->0.154 0.158->0.223
    CO 1-0        0.667->0.974  0.667->0.933 ...                                    0.540->0.887
    [O I] 145     1.000->1.000  0.667->1.000 everywhere

    pn150k        ion.          A_V .15-.25  .25-.35      .35-.45      .45-.55      .55-.80
    [C II] 158    0.666->0.766  0.379->0.369 0.283->0.351 0.270->0.370 0.288->0.422 0.347->0.538
    [O I] 63      0.666->0.605  0.206->0.234 0.186->0.242 0.191->0.273 0.225->0.333 0.307->0.465
    [C I] 609     1.000->0.998  0.667->0.993 ... 0.657->0.989
    CO 1-0, 3-2, [O I] 145: 0.667 -> 1.000

  - **Thin lines lose the 2/3 cap everywhere.**
  - **Out of the PDR, escape rises.** The four rays that never escaped now
    leave through a finite chord.
  - **From the ionized gas it depends on the PDR the rays cross.** On
    hiipdr the thick shell (A_V 3) lowers it: [C II] 0.66 -> 0.50, [O I]
    0.67 -> 0.34, [C I] 1.0 -> 0.59. On pn150k's thin shell (A_V < 0.8),
    [C II] rises, 0.67 -> 0.77.
  - **[C I] depends on where the carbon is along the rays.** In hiipdr's
    shallow PDR it falls, 0.66 -> 0.21, because the rays now meet the deep
    neutral carbon that the cell's own tiny column never had. In pn150k,
    whose carbon is C+ throughout, it rises to 0.99.

### What moved

**hiipdr:**
  - Lines, as luminosities new/base:
    - [C II] 158 x0.907;
    - [O I] 63 x1.001, 145 x1.011;
    - [C I] 609 x1.038, 370 x0.922;
    - C II] 2325 x0.976;
    - [O I] 6300, [O III], [N II] and Hbeta within 0.1%;
    - CO 2-1/3-2/5-4/7-6 x0.985/0.928/0.820/0.712.
  - PDR T_gas 3-5% colder: 48.3 -> 46.8 K at A_V 1.0, 34.7 -> 33.5 at
    1.5, 12.5 -> 11.9 at 2.5, 10.9 -> 10.5 at 2.9.
  - H/H2 crossing 1.443 -> 1.446, C+ = C 2.274 -> 2.272; front and T_dust
    unchanged.

**pn150k:**
  - Lines, as luminosities new/base:
    - [C II] 158 x1.005;
    - [O I] 63 x1.007, 145 x1.007;
    - [C I] 609 x1.40, 370 x1.15;
    - C II] 2325 x0.995; the ionized-gas lines within 0.01%;
    - CO 2-1/3-2/5-4/7-6 x1.162/0.950/0.749/0.642.
  - PDR T_gas 4-6% colder: 48.4 -> 45.7 K at A_V 0.3, 31.3 -> 29.7 at
    0.5, 25.5 -> 24.5 at 0.65.
  - H/H2 crossing 0.399 -> 0.402; the H+ and He2+ fronts, Hbeta and T_dust
    unchanged.

**Why the PDRs cool although n_H is only 1e2-1e3.**
  - The atoms' escape probability in the PDR is 0.1-0.5, so x/beta =
    (n/n_crit)/beta is not small: 0.03/0.11 on hiipdr for [C II].
  - Raising beta raises the collisionally de-excited lines' emission per
    cell. The two-level form gives +11% for [C II] at 0.11 -> 0.18.
  - The heating does not change, so T falls until the cooling matches it
    again.
  - hiipdr's total [C II] still falls 9%. Its PDR part is pinned to the
    heating, and the loss is in the ionized gas and the front, where every
    ray now crosses the shell and beta fell to 0.50, well above n_crit(e).

**Against Cloudy**, in each code's Hbeta:
  - hiipdr [C II] 158 is 0.157 against 0.134 (1.29x -> 1.17x).
  - pn150k [C II] is 0.191 against 0.311 (0.61x, unchanged).
  - Both PDRs move further below Cloudy's T_gas: hiipdr 33.5 against 43.5
    at A_V 1.5; pn150k 45.7 against 68.6 at 0.3.
  - These are divergences to report. L-22's grain charging and L-19's FUV
    share remain the candidates.

**Round trip:** `mocassinOutput` on `runs/d377-pn` reproduces `lineFlux.out`
and `lineFluxMol.out` byte for byte.

### Predictions, scored

  - P1 holds: thin transitions 0.667 -> 1.000.
  - P2 holds for the PDR rise on both fixtures, except pn150k's shallowest
    band (-3%), and for hiipdr's ionized fall (0.50, inside 0.45-0.6). It
    fails for pn150k's ionized gas, which rose (thin shell).
  - P3 fails narrowly on hiipdr (-9.3% against -8..+2%) and holds on pn150k
    (+0.5%).
  - P4 holds.
  - P5 fails on pn150k ([C I] 609 +40% against -20..0%: its carbon is thin,
    not abundant along the rays) and holds on hiipdr (+3.8%).
  - P6 fails on hiipdr (-3..-5% against +-2%) and holds on pn150k (-4..-6%).
  - P7 holds for low-J CO and fails for J >= 6 on pn150k (-30..-36%).
  - P8 and P9 hold.

### Builds

`PDR=1 PDRGEOM=3D mocassin`, `PDR=1 mocassin`, `mocassin` and `PDR=1
mocassinWarm` all build. So do `mocassinOutput` in both flavours and
`mocassinPlot`. The rebuilt default binary is byte-identical to the one the
runs used.

### Not done, not known

  - The chemistry's first PDR iteration sees other cells' populations as
    zero, because none has been solved yet. That iteration's rays therefore
    under-count tau. The effect is gone by the next iteration, and it is not
    measured.
  - The rays are the twelve fixed-frame HEALPix directions, as the FUV sites
    are. How much a 48-ray set would move beta is not measured.
  - MOCASSIN's own atoms still take beta without a background term (D-363);
    the chemistry's solve has one.
  - Line widths are thermal plus pdrVturb at the target cell, with no
    velocity field (static escape).
  - Why the PDRs sit further below Cloudy's T_gas now.

### Status

Done. L-27 closed.

## D-379 - A correction factor for lines from front cells: evaluated, not adopted (2026-09-28)

The user asked: "would it be possible to obtain a correction factor for
lines from cells that straddle the ionization front like [O I]6300? Could we
estimate the thickness from the packet transfer and apply the fraction
correction accordingly? Do not write any code, just evaluate the
feasability". Nothing in the source changed. Two read-only measurement
scripts were written in the session scratchpad, `d379_where.py` (MOCASSIN
cells) and `d379_cloudy.py` (Cloudy zones).

### What the front cells carry now

Per-cell 6300 emissivity from `pdrLineEm.out` (16o.dat transition 4,
1D2 -> 3P2, column 59), times cell volume:

    run        cells x(H+) 0.01-0.95   share of 6300   T med    tau(912 A)/cell med
    d377-hii   67 (of 15204 active)    0.897           8502 K   594 (0.3-0.95), 1140 (0.01-0.3)
    d377-pn    392 (of 35384)          0.967           10940 K  67, 283

[O I] 6300 is 0.0667 Hbeta on hiipdr (Cloudy 0.0104, 6.4x) and 0.402 on
pn150k (Cloudy 0.292, 1.38x). hiipdr's fully ionized cells (x(H+) > 0.95)
give 0.0069 Hbeta, two thirds of Cloudy's total by themselves.

### How thick the emitting layer is (Cloudy, r^2-weighted)

hiipdr's Cloudy run saved no emissivities, so its layer is from the proxy
n_e x(O0) T^-1/2 exp(-22830/T). On pn150k the proxy's layer width matches
Cloudy's saved 6300 emissivity (`runs/d356-cloudy-pn/150k.emis`) to 2%
(4.36e16 against 4.27e16 cm).

                                      hiipdr (d356-cloudy-hii)   pn150k (d356-cloudy-pn)
    MOCASSIN cell                     2.00e18 cm, 2.0e20 cm^-2   4.68e16 cm, 4.7e19 cm^-2
    H+ 0.9 -> 0.1                     9.5e16 cm (0.031 pc)       4.3e16 cm
    H+ 0.99 -> 0.01                   5.1e17 cm                  1.8e17 cm
    6300, 10-90% of the emission      5.5e17 cm (0.18 pc)        4.3e16 cm (0.014 pc)
      as H column                     5.5e19 cm^-2               4.3e19 cm^-2
      layers per cell                 0.27                       0.91
      x(H+) at 10/50/90%              0.99 / 0.91 / 0.42         0.92 / 0.66 / 0.19
      T at 10/50/90%                  9840 / 9930 / 8700 K       11900 / 10900 / 9300 K

Three statements in the record do not survive this:
  - **L-37's "the front is ~0.01 pc".** The H+ transition is 0.031 pc and
    the 6300 layer 0.18 pc on hiipdr.
  - **D-080's 1/(n sigma) = 1.6e15 cm** is the threshold mean free path in
    neutral gas. The layer is ~340 times that, because it lies where x(H0)
    rises from ~0.01 to ~0.5 and is fed by the hardened spectrum. D-081's
    "N >= L_PDR/d_IF" was therefore ~340x too pessimistic for [O I] 6300,
    though its conclusion still stands for hiipdr (below).
  - **D-368's reading** that the hard 150 kK field makes a partially ionized
    zone the grid resolves while hiipdr's 40 kK front "does not have one".
    The H+ transition is indeed 4.5x thicker in column on pn150k (4.3e19
    against 9.5e18 cm^-2). The 6300 layer is not: 4.3e19 against 5.5e19. On
    hiipdr it sits on the ionized side (median x(H+) 0.91). What separates
    the fixtures is the column per cell, and it predicts both of D-365/D-368's
    resolution tests. At 61^3 hiipdr has 0.55 layers per cell, still
    unresolved, and the front-cell [O I] 63 fell 0.53x. At 81^3 pn150k has
    1.8 layers per cell and it fell 0.95x.

### Can the transfer give the thickness?

Not by itself. Inside a cell the opacity is uniform. Where packets are
absorbed within the cell is then exponential in that opacity, and carries
nothing the opacity does not. What the transfer does give is the spectrum.
`Jste` per bin, with the cell's opacity per bin, yields the spectrum
entering the cell under a plane-front assumption (J_in = J tau/(1 - e^-tau)),
or the upstream neighbour's spectrum can be taken instead.

From that spectrum the hydrogen profile through the cell is a cheap 1D
integration: one equation in the H0 column. Photon conservation fixes the
front's position. The homogeneous cell already balances recombinations
against the photons it absorbs, which in pure hydrogen in the thick limit
makes its x(H+) the square root of the ionized volume fraction.

[O I] 6300 also needs T and O0 through the layer. T comes from the thermal
balance with every coolant, so the thickness alone does not fix the
correction. Cloudy's layer is at ~9900 K against MOCASSIN's front cells'
8500 K, a factor 1.5 in exp(-22830/T) alone.

The orientation is not tallied either. MOCASSIN keeps scalar J, not the
flux vector, so the front's area inside a cell would have to come from the
neighbours' x(H+) gradient (as volume-of-fluid hydrodynamics reconstructs
an interface) or from a new flux tally.

### Why a factor on the reported line is not the fix

1. It breaks D-362/D-363: the reported lines are the ones the balance cools
   by. The front cells' T was set with the uncorrected [O I]. D-284 found O I
   cooling at the front was 1.4-1.8x Cloudy's total cooling there. A
   corrected line from a cell whose T it did not set is a second reality,
   and the cell's lines would no longer add up to its heating.
2. Every line of a front cell is off, not only 6300: [O I] 63/145, [C I], a
   third of hiipdr's [C II] 158 (D-365), [N I], [S II], and the ionized-side
   lines through T. Correcting one line is a line-specific gate, and
   selecting cells by x(H+) is a zone test.
3. A factor from the thickness alone leaves an order-unity term (T, n_e and
   O0 in the layer), and only a comparison with Cloudy could set it. That is
   tuning.

### What would be physics

A sub-cell front model, applied in every cell:
  - a 1D integration along the local flux from the entering spectrum;
  - MOCASSIN's own ionization and thermal balance per sub-zone;
  - emissivities and cooling taken as sub-zone integrals.

Optically thin cells collapse to one sub-zone, so there is no gate.

The compute cost is small: 67 cells on hiipdr and 392 on pn150k, times
~20-50 sub-zones, against a gas update of 15-35k cells.

The design cost is large:
  - sub-zone state in checkpoints and `mocassinOutput`;
  - ownership of the neutral sub-zones with the chemistry, which has one
    3D-PDR point per cell;
  - the dust temperature in a cell whose field varies by orders of
    magnitude;
  - where the diffuse field is emitted;
  - the convergence test.

It is the analytic 1D form of the nested sub-grids ruled out at D-081 (and
excluded by D-009).

Validation that does not use Cloudy:
  - resolution independence, hiipdr 31^3 (`runs/d377-hii`) against 61^3
    (`runs/d365-hii61`);
  - `benchmarks/pdr/ifront` (graded 1D, ~8 cells across the front, D-081)
    coarsened, against itself resolved.

Cloudy comes last.

Expected effect:
  - **hiipdr:** for the total to reach Cloudy's with the ionized cells' 0.0069
    unchanged, the front cells' 0.060 Hbeta would have to fall ~17x. The
    layer's volume fraction alone gives 3.7x; the rest would have to come
    from T and O0 in the layer. That cannot be predicted without the solve.
  - **pn150k:** little, since the layer is already ~1 cell. Its 1.38x stays
    a model difference (D-368).

### Resolving it on the grid instead

One cell per layer needs n_H dx <~ 5e19 cm^-2 (~35 cells per magnitude of
A_V at hiipdr's A_V/N_H):
  - **pn150k:** its 1.5e21 cm^-2 beyond the front needs ~34 cells and has 32.
  - **hiipdr:** its 4.8e21 cm^-2 (2.5 mag) needs ~88 and has 25, i.e.
    ~110^3 overall. That is 0.7M active cells, which fits only on one rank
    (D-374's 0.47 GB + 38 kB/cell).
  - Three cells per layer (~330^3) is out of reach.

### Cheap and legitimate now

A resolution diagnostic, not a correction. For each line, report the share
of its emission from cells whose H column exceeds the layer column the
cell's own spectrum implies (or, cruder, ~5e19 cm^-2 while thick at 912 A),
printed with the line table. It changes no physics. L-37 already requires a
resolution check before a front-sensitive line is published; this would
make it automatic.

### Not known

  - Whether the ~5e19 cm^-2 layer column is generic: two models, 40 and
    150 kK.
  - What the sub-cell model would give on hiipdr.
  - Whether HII20's [O I] 6300, 6.7x the Lexington median at D-270, is the
    same effect.

### Status

Open: evaluation delivered, nothing implemented. L-37's text is corrected in
`doc/pdr-status.md`.

## D-380 - The front fraction per frequency bin from the cell's n_e, T_e and field (2026-09-28)

The user, after D-379: "could we use the cell Ne, Te and the radiation field
that arrives there to estimate the fraction of the cell which is the front
in each frequency bin and coorect emited lines?" Evaluation only, as in
D-379. One more read-only scratchpad script, `d380_cond.py` (hiipdr,
`runs/d377-hii` against `runs/d356-cloudy-hii`).

### The per-bin fraction from the cell's own state

The fraction of the cell a bin reaches is ~min(1, 1/tau_nu), with tau_nu
the cell's own optical depth. At the Lyman edge the front cells have tau
594 (x(H+) 0.3-0.95) and 1140 (0.01-0.3). For a 40 kK blackbody, with H
only and sigma ~ nu^-3, the photon-weighted reach is:

    tau(912 A)   at 13.6 eV   at 25 eV   photon-weighted
    594          0.17%        1.0%       0.53%
    1140         0.09%        0.54%      0.28%

Cloudy's 6300 layer is 0.27 of a cell (D-379). He absorption above 24.6 eV
would shorten the reach further, and the hardening in the H II region would
lengthen it; neither changes the order of magnitude. With the x(H0) of the
ionized gas (~1e-3) instead of the cell's 0.5, the reach is the whole cell.

**So the fraction depends entirely on which x(H0) is assumed inside the
cell, and that is the unknown.** The layer is where x(H0) rises from ~0.01
to ~0.5, fed by photons already hardened. Its width is set by the profile
itself. The per-bin fractions have to be the outcome of one integration of
x(z) through the cell, with all bins attenuated together by the same x(z).
They cannot be separate estimates per bin. The integration is cheap: the
inputs are the arriving spectrum per bin, n_H, and alpha(T_e) at the
cell's T.

### The cell's n_e and T_e are not the layer's

The 6300-weighted conditions:

                        MOCASSIN front cells   Cloudy's 6300 layer
    x(H+)               0.497                  0.799
    n_e / n_H           0.501                  0.814
    O0 / O              0.532                  0.225
    T                   8328 K (6640-9320)     9496 K
    n_e (O0/O) q(T)     1.59e-4                1.08e-4

(q = T^-1/2 exp(-22830/T), per unit n_H^2 and O/H.) At the cell's
conditions the emissivity per volume is 1.47x the layer's. The factors
partly cancel for 6300: n_e is 0.62x the layer's and O0/O 2.4x. They do
not cancel for [O I] 63 (E/k 228 K, so no T factor, and O0 2.4x), nor for
the ionized-side lines. n_e is therefore an output of the profile, not an
input. T_e is the cell's balance, and would move once the cooling uses the
profile.

### What the idea becomes when it is allowed

Under D-379's conditions it is a sub-cell ionization model at one T per
cell:
  - the same sub-zone integrals for the lines and the cooling;
  - every line and coolant;
  - every cell, reducing to the homogeneous cell when thin;
  - the cell's x(H+), which the transfer and the chemistry read, equal to
    the profile mean.

The other elements need their profiles too. O0 follows H0 through charge
exchange (D-263, local), but the N, S and C stages need MOCASSIN's
`ionBalance` per sub-zone, with the attenuated field.

**Its limit is the neutral part of the cell.** In a cell with x(H+) ~0.5,
most of the volume is neutral. At one T, that gas radiates [O I] 63 and
[C II] 158 by H0 collisions at thousands of K, while its heating is
deposited in the warm part. That drags the cell's T down, and 6300 with it.
The real neutral gas is at PDR temperatures. How far the single-T model
errs is not known. A T per sub-zone removes the limit, but that is D-379's
full model, with its ownership question.

### A first stage that changes no physics

  - Save the per-bin field (`Jste`) and opacity of the cells that are thick
    at 912 A. This is a small output addition; the field is not in any
    output now, and `mocassinOutput` cannot regenerate it.
  - Integrate the H and O profile offline at the cell's T, and predict each
    front cell's 6300 and 63 um.
  - The test that does not use Cloudy: the prediction should make the 31^3
    and 61^3 hiipdr totals agree, where today they differ by 1.45x (6300)
    and 1.73x (63). Cloudy comes after.

That tells us whether the sub-cell physics is right before it touches the
thermal balance. It needs a re-run, or one resumed iteration, of each grid.

### Not known

  - What the single-T profile gives; whether its neutral-part error is
    small for 6300.
  - The arriving spectrum's hardness in MOCASSIN's front cells, since the
    field is not saved.

### Status

Open, awaiting the user's decision. Nothing implemented.

## D-381 - The sub-cell front profile, stage 1: [O I] 6300 made resolution-independent offline (2026-09-28)

The user, on D-380's proposed first stage: "lets give this a try". Stage 1
is a diagnostic: nothing below changes a run's physics.

### What was built

  - **`output/frontField.out`** (`writeGrid`, grid_mod.f90). Every gas run
    that carries a field writes it for every cell with x(H+) > 1e-4:
      - the Monte Carlo's `Jste` from the Lyman edge up;
      - the total opacity those packets were carried through (set before
        the transfer, untouched by the update);
      - its dust absorption part;
      - in the header, once, the H0, He0 and He+ cross sections, from the
        `xSecArray` slices `addOpacity` and `updateCell` use.
    Rank 0 writes it with the grid files, where `Jste` still holds this
    iteration's field. It is skipped where there is no field
    (`mocassinOutput`). Documented in `man/mocassin.1`.
  - **`tools/d381_subcell.py`**. Per cell:
      1. the entering field J_in = J tau/(1 - e^-tau) per bin, with tau
         the transport's opacity over the cell's chord along r;
      2. H and He integrated through the cell (midpoint steps of <= 0.05
         photon-weighted mean free paths or L/400), at the cell's own T;
      3. the recombination coefficients as the cell's own balance implies
         them (alpha = Gamma n_i / (n_i+1 n_e)). Where a helium stage is
         empty, MOCASSIN's radRecFit He/H ratio (data/radrec.dat, VF96) is
         applied to the cell's own H value, since the field's
         normalization cancels only within one unit system;
      4. O0/O+ locked to H0/H+ at the cell's ratio (charge exchange,
         D-263), and O++/O+ scaled with the rate above 35.1 eV;
      5. [O I] 6300 and 63 um at every depth from D-284's 5-level atom
         (16o.dat, Barklem's 1D/1S electron rates), applied only as the
         ratio C = profile mean / homogeneous cell, times the cell's own
         `pdrLineEm` emission.
  - All four flavours and `mocassinOutput` build. `make -j` fails on module
    order; the serial build is the one that works.

### Runs

hiipdr at three resolutions, the same binary, equal packets per cell, seed
1001, 11 iterations:

    run          grid  packets   ranks  time     converged
    d381-hii21   21^3  1.865e6   2      27:40    73.0%
    d381-hii31   31^3  6.0e6     4      49:40    = d377-hii
    d381-hii41   41^3  1.388e7   8      1:09:45  78.5%
    d381-pn41    41^3  6.0e6     5      41:15     = d377-pn

**P1 holds.** d381-hii31 is d377-hii byte for byte in every output file but
`summary.out`, which differs only in timestamps. d381-pn41 is d377-pn likewise.

### The test (P4): [O I] 6300, absolute

                           21^3       31^3       41^3      max/min
    uncorrected [erg/s]    8.83e35    6.20e35    5.13e35   1.72
    corrected   [erg/s]    0.971e35   1.143e35   1.086e35  1.18
    uncorrected / Hbeta    0.1028     0.0667     0.0583
    corrected / Hbeta      0.0113     0.0123     0.0124    (Cloudy 0.0104)
    Hbeta [E36]            8.584      9.296      8.799     (Cloudy 9.96)
    6300-weighted C, front cells   0.074  0.092  0.138

**P4 holds.** The corrected totals lie within 9% of their mean (-9.0%,
+7.2%, +1.8%), where the uncorrected ones fall 1.72x from 21^3 to 41^3. The
corrected values do not move monotonically: the front cells' part is
6.35/5.11/6.30e34, and the fully ionized cells' own 6300 is 3.36/6.32/4.57e34
as the layer's ionized side moves in and out of them. The remaining +-9% is
not separated from the Monte Carlo scatter, and a second seed would decide
it.

**P5 holds.** The corrected 6300 is 1.09-1.19x Cloudy's.

**P2 half holds.** The front cells' uncorrected 6300 is 1.54x from 21^3 to
31^3 (predicted 1.3-1.5) and 0.82x from 41^3 to 31^3 (0.70-0.85).

### [O I] 63 um: the single-T limit, as expected, but not for my reason

                           21^3       31^3       41^3      max/min
    uncorrected / Hbeta    0.0773     0.0517     0.0401    1.88
    corrected / Hbeta      0.0526     0.0368     0.0287    1.79   (Cloudy 0.00581)
    6300-weighted C63      0.645      0.657      0.661

**P6 half fails.**
  - **Holds:** the spread barely shrinks (1.88x -> 1.79x), and 63 um stays
    5-9x Cloudy.
  - **Fails:** C_63 is ~0.5 in the brightest cells, not >= 1, and the
    corrected total is 0.66x the uncorrected, i.e. closer. My reason was
    wrong. The homogeneous cell's 63 um is dominated by electrons exciting
    its half-neutral O; the profile separates O0 from the electrons, which
    halves it.
  - **What stays:** the neutral part of the cell, at the cell's warm T.
    Its 63 um scales with the cell's volume, hence the unchanged spread.
    Only a temperature per depth (stage 2) can remove that.

### Checks on the profile

  - **Photon conservation.** Absorbed by H + He + dust, plus transmitted,
    equals the entering photons to 1-1.7% (the integration error). The
    transmission is 1e-22..1e-15 in the front cells.
  - **H absorption, profile against the homogeneous cell: 0.79-0.93 in the
    brightest cells.** Two parts:
      - the saved ionization is one iteration further recombined than the
        opacity the packets saw. kappa_total(MC) / kappa_H(state) L is
        0.88-0.98, because the front is still moving inward at iteration
        11 (L-40);
      - the profile gives He a few % more of the photons, since its neutral
        side has He fully neutral.
  - **P3 holds where the 6300 is, fails as worded.** Among cells with
    tau(912) > 100:
      - **x(H+) > 0.3:** <x(z)>/x^2 is 0.88-1.00 (6300-weighted 0.87-0.96).
        These cells carry 64-80% of the 6300, and the photon-conservation
        reading (the cell's x(H+) = sqrt of the ionized fraction) holds.
      - **x(H+) 0.01-0.3:** 1.6-2.0.
      - **x(H+) <= 0.01:** 50-400x. The hard photons ionize the entrance
        of a cell that is otherwise neutral.
  - **Fully ionized cells:** the field varies across them. Above 54 eV the
    He+ zone is thick (tau ~30 per cell), so the rebuilt entering field
    restores hard photons the cell average hides, and in the innermost
    cells they open a small He++ zone at the entrance. C there is
    0.82-1.24; these cells carry 5-11% of the 6300. Bins with large tau
    amplify the Monte Carlo's noise by tau; that is where the method is
    weakest.

### pn150k (P7)

**pn150k: [O I] 6300 0.402 -> 0.293 Hbeta** (x0.729; Cloudy 0.292). [O I] 63
0.244 -> 0.225 (x0.92; Cloudy 0.187). 1926 cells in frontField.out. In the
brightest cells C6300 is 0.66-0.77. <x(z)> is 1.4x the cell's x^2, not ~1,
because a front the grid already holds at ~1 layer per cell is gradual, not
sharp. H absorbed, profile against the homogeneous cell: median 1.012
(1.002-1.033). pn150k's front is stationary, unlike hiipdr's, which
corroborates the L-40 reading of hiipdr's 0.79-0.93.

**P7 fails as worded:** -27%, not <= 20%. My bound came from D-368's -13%
for halving the cell, but if the error is proportional to the cell size,
halving it removes only half of it. D-368's step read that way (0.868 = (1 +
a/2)/(1 + a), so a = 0.360) implies the full correction is 1/(1 + a) = 0.735.
The profile gives 0.729. That run is on D-365's code, so the agreement is a
consistency check, not a measurement. The 0.3% agreement with Cloudy's value
is one seed on stage-1 approximations, with T not fed back; I do not read
more into it.

### An estimate independent of the profile: extrapolation in cell size

A straight line in cell size through hiipdr's three uncorrected rungs gives,
at zero cell size:
  - **6300:** 1.33e35 erg/s (0.95-1.91e35 from the three pairs), i.e. 0.0149
    Hbeta, against the profile's mean 1.07e35 (0.0120). The two agree within
    the extrapolation's own spread.
  - **63 um:** 0.59e35 (-0.3 to 1.16e35 from the pairs), i.e. 0.0066 Hbeta,
    against Cloudy's 0.0058. The profile-corrected 63 um is 0.039. So 63
    um's excess also looks entirely like resolution, carried by the front
    cells' warm neutral volume, which stage 1 leaves at the cell's T.
    Noisy: the pairs span zero.

The extrapolation holds only while the layer is under one cell (hiipdr: 0.27
to 0.55 layers per cell here).

### What this means

  - **For [O I] 6300**, the unresolved front is nearly the whole of the
    excess on both fixtures. A sub-cell profile at the cell's own T, built
    only from the transport's field and opacity and the cell's own balance,
    gives:
      - hiipdr: 1.1-1.2x Cloudy at every resolution tried, against 5.6-9.9x
        uncorrected;
      - pn150k: 1.00x, against 1.38x.
    Nothing was fitted, and the extrapolation in cell size agrees with it.
  - **This withdraws D-368's "pn150k's 1.26-1.38x is a model difference,
    not a grid effect"** for 6300. The front is ~1 layer per cell there,
    which is not resolved.
  - **For [O I] 63 um**, the correction is not enough. The neutral part of
    a front cell needs its own temperature, the PDR's. That is stage 2 and
    the ownership question of D-379.
  - **Stage 1 has not touched the thermal balance.** The cells' T is still
    set by the uncorrected cooling. Folding C into the cooling would move T
    and then C; that is the self-consistency step D-379 requires before any
    corrected line is reported.

### Not known

  - Whether the +-9% left between resolutions is scatter or bias.
  - The entering-field reconstruction assumes one face and a plane front
    normal to r. The diffuse field enters from every side, and how much
    that matters is not measured.
  - What folding the profile into the cooling would do to T and to C.

### Status

Open. Stage 1 done and passing its test for 6300. The next decisions are the
user's: stage 2 (a temperature per depth), and whether and how the profile
enters the run.

## D-382 - frontLines: the sub-cell front estimate as a post-processing option (2026-09-28)

The user: "Can we add this as an option afetr model convergence so the user
can set a keyword and line intensities will be calculated with a
correction? That way we could avoid touching main simulation code and just
use a postprocessing module?"

### The decision

Asked, because the answer touches D-362's rule (the reported lines are the
ones the thermal balance cooled the cells with):
  - **where:** a separate file, lineFluxFront.out, rather than overwriting
    rows of lineFlux.out. lineFlux.out stays the model's own lines.
  - **which lines:** [O I] 6300, 6363 and 5577 only, the lines stage 1 was
    tested for. [O I] 63/145 are left out, since stage 1 fails for them
    (D-381). Other lines only after their own resolution test.

The keyword changes no physics: the run, its convergence and every file it
wrote before are identical with or without it. That is why it is not the
kind of run-time switch CLAUDE.md rules out.

### What was built

  - **`source/frontLines_mod.f90`** (new). `writeFrontLines(grid, Hbeta)`
    is called at the end of `outputGas`, after lineFlux.out is closed and
    outside the slit pass. It therefore runs at the end of a run, in
    `mocassinWarm` and in `mocassinOutput`. It:
      - reads frontField.out and checks its bins against the model's;
      - integrates D-381's profile per cell (the same equations as
        `tools/d381_subcell.py`, with the quadratic for n_e solved without
        cancellation);
      - evaluates **MOCASSIN's own O I atom** (`equilibrium`) at every depth,
        with D-363's neutral colliders for the depth's H0, H+ and He0 and
        the cell's escape probabilities. So the corrected emission is the
        atom's own, not a ratio as in the Python tool.
    The O+ edge (for the O++ scaling) comes from `getOuterShell`/`elementP`,
    and the He fallback from `radrec.dat`, read in `radRecFit`'s order. It
    needs one grid, one ionizing source (the chord direction) and a 3D
    grid, and says so and skips otherwise.
  - **Keyword `frontLines`** (`set_input_mod`, `lgFrontLines` in
    common_mod). `writeGrid` now writes frontField.out only with it (D-381
    wrote it always). `mocassinOutput` makes lineFluxFront.out from a run
    that had the keyword.
  - **lineFluxFront.out.** A header saying it is an estimate beside the
    model, the count of cells integrated, the He fallback count, and the
    median photon-budget ratio over the tau(912) > 100 cells (the L-40
    flag). Then per line: the atom's wavelength, uncorrected and corrected
    /Hbeta and in E36 erg/s, their ratio, and the front cells' part.
  - `man/mocassin.1`: the keyword and both files. Makefile: the module
    between update_mod and output_mod.
  - All four flavours, and `mocassinOutput` plain and PDR 3D, build with no
    warnings from the new code.

### Validation

  - **lineFlux.out is not changed.** `mocassinOutput` with the keyword on
    copies of the four D-381 runs (`runs/d382-post-*`) leaves lineFlux.out,
    lineFluxMol.out, ionratio.out and temperature.out byte-identical to the
    runs'.
  - **The uncorrected column is lineFlux.out's.** [O I] 6300 on hiipdr 31^3
    is 6.73146322e-2 against lineFlux.out's 6.73146397e-2 (single
    precision), and 6363 and 5577 likewise.
  - **The corrected column matches the Python tool** within 1.4%, although
    here the atom is MOCASSIN's own at each depth:

                              21^3      31^3      41^3      pn150k 41^3
        uncorrected/Hbeta     0.1034    0.0673    0.0584    0.4072
        corrected/Hbeta       0.01123   0.01219   0.01219   0.2969
        Python (D-381)        0.0113    0.0123    0.0124    0.2928
        Cloudy                0.0104                        0.292
        photon budget, thick  0.982     0.987     0.985     1.012   (Python identical)

    The corrected absolute 6300 is 0.964/1.133/1.072e35 erg/s (max/min
    1.18), where the uncorrected falls from 8.87 to 5.14e35 (1.73).
    7 s per model.
  - **[O I] 5577** (1S, E/k 48,600 K), corrected/Hbeta 0.96/1.10/1.11e-4
    against 7.6/4.9/4.6e-4 uncorrected: the same behaviour, spread 1.16
    against 1.66. It was not tested separately, and its higher excitation
    makes the single T matter more. The file says it was tested for 6300
    only. 6363 shares 6300's upper level and has the same correction.
  - **Runs.** A 21^3 run with the keyword (`runs/d382-run21`, 10 ranks)
    took 6:39 per processor for 11 iterations. It wrote lineFluxFront.out
    itself: [O I] 6300 0.1033 -> 0.01126 Hbeta. The 2-rank d381-hii21 gave
    0.1034 -> 0.01123, another Monte Carlo realization. `mocassinOutput`
    with the keyword on its outputs reproduces lineFluxFront.out and
    lineFlux.out byte for byte. A 2-iteration run without it (`runs/d382-nokw`) wrote
    neither frontField.out nor lineFluxFront.out.

### What it does not do

  - The correction does not enter the cooling. The cells' T is the
    uncorrected balance's, so lineFluxFront.out and lineFlux.out do not
    share one energy budget. The file says so.
  - [O I] 63/145 and every other line are not corrected.
  - Single source, 3D, no planeIonization. Multiple sources or a diffuse
    source need a flux-direction tally.
  - The +-9% left between resolutions (D-381) remains, unseparated from
    the Monte Carlo scatter.

### Status

Done, at the user's request. The DEVLOG D-381 open items (stage 2, feeding
the profile into the run, a second seed) are unchanged.

## D-383 - Molecular line cubes from mocassinPlot; the H2 question (2026-09-28)

The user: "I think this is a good point to work on some outputs since we are
close to science production. I want a way to produce line emission maps for
the molecular lines of H2 and CO. Can we produe emissivity cubes for these as
done for atomic lines in mocassinPlot?"

### CO: done

The chemistry already stores every molecular coolant transition's net
escaping emissivity per cell (`pdrLineEm`, D-362, with D-377's escape
probabilities along the real 3D rays), and `resetGrid` restores it in every
driver. So CO needs no new physics.
  - **`mocassinPlot`:** `plot.in` takes `mol <coolant file> <upper>
    <lower>`, levels numbered as in lineFluxMol.out (`mol 12co.dat 2 1` is
    CO 1-0). The cell's value is `pdrLineEm` x dV, in the units of the
    atomic entries, which `plot.out` interleaves in `plot.in` order. A mol
    entry in a non-PDR build, or without `pdrLineEm.out`, stops with a
    message. The atomic entries were already on D-363's atom with the
    neutral colliders (`setLineColliders`).
  - **`tools/d383_maps.py`:** `grid4.out` + `plot.out` -> `lineMaps.fits`,
    with per line an emissivity cube j = L/(4 pi V) [erg/s/cm3/sr] and
    maps along x, y, z [erg/s/cm2/sr], plus the axes. A symmetricXYZ octant
    is unfolded, with the plane cells once at twice their octant width.
    `--png` gives quick-look images.
  - `mocassinPlot` builds plain, PDR=1 and PDR=1 PDRGEOM=3D. Documented in
    `man/mocassin.1`.

**Checks** on copies of the D-381 runs (`runs/d383-plot-pn41`,
`runs/d383-plot-hii31`), with plot.in listing CO 1-0, 2-1, 3-2, Hbeta and
[O I] 6300:
  - **Cube sums against the tables.** Each line's cube summed over the grid
    (x8 for the octant) against lineFluxMol.out (CO) and lineFlux.out
    (Hbeta, 6300): 0.999998-1.000011 on both models, the rounding of the
    printed values.
  - **The tool's own closure.** It checks each cube and each z-map against
    the grid's total: 1.000000 on every line. The widths it derives
    reproduce `getVolume`'s volumes (no warning).
  - **Peak surface brightness along z.** pn150k Hbeta 6.3e-3, [O I] 6300
    2.8e-3, CO 1-0 1.9e-11 erg/s/cm2/sr (~0.01 K km/s). hiipdr CO 1-0
    2.2e-10, limb-brightened in the PDR shell, faint inside the 3.8 pc H II
    region, with cell-scale Monte Carlo noise.
  - **The caveat, in the man page and the FITS header.** For optically
    thick CO the map is the sum of each cell's escaping emission, with no
    absorption along the line of sight beyond the cell and no velocity axis.
    Spectral cubes of thick lines need a line radiative transfer code on
    the model's populations and velocity field.

### H2: not modelled, so no map yet

No H2 line exists anywhere in the build. The chemistry's coolants are CO,
C+, C and O; dataPDR has no H2 file; 3D-PDR carries H2 as an abundance with
formation, destruction and a cooling function, but no level populations.
Cloudy's H2 data are on this machine (cloudy-c25.00/data/h2): X-state
energies and transition probabilities, collision rates with H (Wrathmall
2007, Lique 2015), o/p-H2 (Le Bourlot; Lee 2008 "ORNL"), He and H+, and the
B, C, B', D states for UV pumping. The options, put to the user:
  - **(a) Ground-state rovibrational levels, non-LTE, collisions and
    radiative decay only.** The pure rotational S(0)-S(7) lines (28-5.5 um)
    from warm gas. Moderate.
  - **(b) (a) plus UV fluorescence through the Lyman-Werner bands.** This is
    what makes the vibrational lines (1-0 S(1) 2.12 um) in a PDR. It needs
    the shielded FUV per line, since MOCASSIN's bins are coarse and 3D-PDR
    shields H2 with one factor. Large.
  - **Either way the same populations should cool the gas**, as D-363 did
    for C and O, or the lines and the thermal balance hold two H2s. And
    the E_u/k >= 510 K of every H2 line makes them hostage to the PDR gas
    temperature, which runs below Cloudy's on both fixtures (L-19,
    photoelectric heating).

### Status

CO done. H2 awaits the user's choice of scope and of how Cloudy's data are
used (read from the installation, or vendored with attribution).

## D-384 - No H2 line cooling in 3D-PDR (D-183 restated), and what it means for H2 maps (2026-09-28)

The user: "3d-PDR is not cooling using H2 lines?"

**No, and neither is anything else in this coupling.** Re-read in the
vendored source, unchanged since D-183 (2026-09-08):
  - **Cooling.** `coolingfunctions.F90` sums only the escape-probability
    line cooling of the files in `pdrCoolants` (here CO, C+, C, O), plus
    gas-grain.
  - **H2 as a collider.** It excites those four coolants (`H2_COL`,
    `PH2_COL`, `OH2_COL` in `FIND_CCOEFF`).
  - **H2 as heating**, three of `heatingfunctions.F90`'s terms, which the
    bridge passes to MOCASSIN as `pdrHeatXtra` (D-131): formation,
    photodissociation, and FUV pumping (2.2 eV x 9 x the dissociation rate,
    Hollenbach & McKee 1979).
  - **The radiative loss of pumped H2 enters only implicitly**, through the
    pumping heating's 1/(1 + n_cr/n).
MOCASSIN has no H2 term of its own. Cloudy runs a full H2 level model and
computes H2 heating and cooling from its populations.

**What it costs here: nothing measurable in pn150k.** The Cloudy reference
(`runs/d356-cloudy-pn`) ran with its full H2 model (`Database H2 limit
-10`):
  - **H2 lines, against Hbeta (log F -9.634):**
      - 0-0 S(0) 28.21 um, log F -13.406: 1.7e-4 Hbeta;
      - 1-0 S(1) 2.121 um, -13.732: 8.0e-5;
      - 2.953 um, -16.48: 7e-7.
    Beside them, [O I] 63 + [C II] 158 carry ~0.5 Hbeta.
  - **Heating:** H2 photodissociation reached at most 1.0% of the local
    heating, and grain photoelectric 96.9%.

As a coolant H2 is ~1e-3 of the fine-structure lines in this model. Its
lines start at E_u/k >= 510 K, against a PDR at 37-66 K (Cloudy) or 25-45 K
(MOCASSIN). The omission would matter in warmer or denser gas (dense PDRs
at hundreds of K, shocks). For hiipdr, whose Cloudy run did not have the H2
model on, it is not measured.

**What it means for H2 maps.** The upper level of 1-0 S(1) sits at 6,950 K,
and at 40-70 K essentially none of it is populated collisionally, so
Cloudy's 2.121 um must be UV-pumped. The pure rotational lines are fed by
that cascade too. So D-383's option (a), collisions and radiative decay
only, would predict next to nothing for the H2 lines of these models. The
H2 lines they do have come from fluorescence, option (b). **The
recommendation of D-383 is revised: if H2 maps are wanted for models like
these, only (b) delivers them.** Its populations would also give the H2
cooling and the pumping heating, replacing 3D-PDR's Hollenbach & McKee
factor, so that the lines and the balance hold one H2.

### Status

Answered; the H2 scope is still the user's decision.
