## D-401 - Audit of the chemistry coupling, and whether 3D-PDR's full network can be used (2026-10-10)

The user: "audit the code and the coupling to the chemical network and
evaluate if we could use the full network from 3Dpdr. We should stick to One
x(Cl+)." That takes D-400's first decision. Nothing in the repository's code
changed; the tools of this entry are in `tools/d401_netbox/`.

Read: `source/pdr_mod.f90` (the bridge), `update_mod.f90`'s `ionBalance`,
the vendored `read_species`, `read_rates`, `calc_reac_rates`,
`calculate_abundances.c`, the four `odes_*.c`, the four network files in
`dataPDR/`. Measured: the published pn150k model (`runs/h026-site-pn41` on
h2-model, 41^3, 18 iterations), Cloudy's (`runs/d396-cloudy-pn`), and a
one-cell box built in a scratch copy.

### How the network is coupled today

  - **Which network** is fixed at compile time (`-DREDUCED` and
    `odes_reduced.o` in the Makefile); `pdrNetwork` only validates. The
    species and reaction counts are read from the files and every array
    follows them (`pdrAbun`, the restart file, the per-species capture up to
    256), and a restart of another size is refused. **Nothing is sized by
    33.** The stop message advises `NETWORK=<name>`, a make variable that
    does not exist.
  - **Ownership** (D-193): `ionBalance` owns every ion stage, in every cell.
    The chemistry returns the molecular share of each element (`elemAvail`)
    and heating and cooling.
  - **What a cell's solve is handed**: the seed with no molecules (D-208);
    MOCASSIN's neutral-to-ionized ratio for each linked element, before the
    solve and again after it (D-153, D-162), the ion carrier standing for
    every ionized stage (D-266); MOCASSIN's electrons (D-212, D-231); and
    MOCASSIN's photoionization and recombination rates in the network's own
    first-order slots (D-358). `ionBalance` takes the network's cosmic-ray
    coefficients (D-280).
  - **What `ionBalance` is not handed**: any reaction in which a molecule
    makes or consumes the atom or the ion. `pdrIonRate` (the network's
    formation and loss of each linked species, D-118) is still filled at
    every solve and summed over the ranks, and since D-193 only a diagnostic
    reads it.
  - **The element list is written by hand in six places**: the ten
    `linkIon` calls and `pdrNlink`; `lnk358(5)`; the `select case` in
    `ionBalance`; `pdrPhotRate(.,6)` and `pdrAlphaRec(.,5)`; the three
    `setElemAvail` calls; the four `reportAbun` calls. **An element with no
    link is seeded zero** (`seedAbunFromMocassin`) and stays zero, and
    D-251's stop covers linked elements only.
  - Smaller things found: reactions 330 and 331 (He+ and C+ recombining on
    grains) are read and given a rate, and the generated right-hand side has
    no term for either, though the bridge's comment counts them as physics
    the network carries. `colS` is zero. The [D358] report covers H and O
    only.

### One x(X+) is not what the coupling delivers when a molecule consumes the ion

Already registered for H+ as L-34, and printed in every run log. The last
iteration's `[D358]` line, the solver's own X+/X against MOCASSIN's:

| | H: cells more than 2x apart | largest | O: cells more than 2x apart | largest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pn150k (h026-site-pn41, it. 18) | 44.8% | 0.69 dex | 78.5% | 6.37 dex |
| hiipdr (h026-site-hii31, it. 15) | 79.6% | 0.99 dex | 85.9% | 2.09 dex |

(Oxygen's largest values are the ionized zone, where one carrier stands for
every stage: L-32.) The re-imposition then keeps MOCASSIN's, so the stored
x(O+) and the one the molecules were solved with differ.

Chlorine is this case at full strength. MOCASSIN already solves it on pn150k
(Cl/H 3.16e-7), with photoionization, recombination and its own charge
exchange and no molecule:

| A_V | 2n(H2)/nH, ours | Cl+ of all chlorine, MOCASSIN now | Cloudy | box, full network | MOCASSIN over Cloudy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.22 | 2.8e-4 | 0.997 | 0.993 | 0.960 | 1.0 |
| 0.26 | 0.018 | 0.998 | 0.379 | 0.214 | 2.6 |
| 0.30 | 0.087 | 0.998 | 0.119 | 0.039 | 8.4 |
| 0.34 | 0.237 | 0.997 | 0.049 | 0.011 | 20 |
| 0.38 | 0.442 | 0.996 | 0.027 | 0.0044 | 36 |
| 0.46 | 0.744 | 0.991 | 0.012 | 0.0016 | 81 |
| 0.58 | 0.903 | 0.974 | 0.0051 | 0.0007 | 190 |
| 0.66 | 0.934 | 0.945 | 0.0032 | 0.0005 | 295 |

(MOCASSIN: median of the cells within 0.012 mag, `ions_by_av.py`. Cloudy:
`.ele_Cl`; 3-12% of its chlorine is in molecules from A_V 0.26 on. Box: see
below, H2* pumping off.) At A_V 0.30 Cl+ + H2 runs at 1e-9 x 43.5 = 4.4e-8
s^-1 per ion against 4e-12 for radiative recombination (UMIST's
coefficient, n_e 0.33): 1e4 times. So linking Cl and Cl+ into the present
scheme would give the solve one x(Cl+) and store another - MOCASSIN's, 2.6
to 295 times Cloudy's and 5 to 2,000 times the box's - which is what the
rule forbids. **One x(Cl+) needs L-34's decision first.**

What that decision looks like, from the code (a proposal, not designed):
D-193's own comment separates the two roles - `elemAvail` sets the sum of
the stages, rates set the ratios - and removed the injection because what
was injected was the species' whole right-hand side, ionization and
recombination included, on top of the sum. The matrix slots are still there
(`chemSrc`, `chemSnk`, zeroed). The molecular channels alone - reactions
where the atom or ion enters or leaves a molecule - would go into the stage
rows and set the ratio, with the sum still `elemAvail`. To be settled: which
reactions count (the network's charge exchange with H duplicates MOCASSIN's
`chex`), and which stage row the conservation row replaces. The test exists:
the `[D358]` line, for every linked element, should then read near zero.

### The full network, as vendored

`dataPDR/species_full.d`, `rates_full.d`, `source/pdr/odes_full.c`: 215
species, 2,926 reactions, 214 equations, sizes consistent. 13 elements: H,
He, C, N, O, F, Na, Mg, Si, P, S, Cl, Fe. The medium network (78) and
`mynetwork` (58) have no chlorine.

  - **It builds.** In a scratch copy: `-DREDUCED` to `-DFULL`,
    `odes_reduced.o` to `odes_full.o`, `tools/patch_odes_capture.py` on
    `odes_full.c` (214 capture points). No other edit; the readers, the rate
    routine and the bridge already branch on `FULL`.
  - **It is not the reduced network plus species.** Matching reactions by
    reactants and products, 9 of the reduced network's 332 have no
    counterpart in the full one: D-395's e- + H2+ -> e- + H + H+,
    H+ + H2 -> H2+ + H, C+ + OH -> CO + H+, He+ + CO -> O+ + C + He,
    CH3+ + e- -> C + H2 + H, CH + CH4, OH+ + photon, and the two grain
    recombinations. 148 of the other 323 have different coefficients (the
    full file is a later compilation, with DOIs: H + CH -> C + H2 is
    2.7e-11 (T/300)^0.38 in one and 1.31e-10 exp(-80/T) in the other).
    Moving to it changes the chemistry already compared with Cloudy.
  - **The slots D-358 needs**, by element:

    | | X + CRP | X + CRPHOT | own X + photon | X+ + e- -> X | X++ |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | H, He | yes | yes | none | yes | - |
    | C, N, O | yes | yes | C only | yes | yes |
    | Cl | yes (492) | yes (539) | yes (2618) | yes (2763) | - |
    | Na, Mg, Si, P, S, Fe | none | yes | yes | yes | Si, S, Fe |
    | F | none | none | none | none | - |

    Chlorine fits the mechanism as it stands, and that answers most of
    D-400's second decision: for a linked element the network's own
    photoionization is zeroed and MOCASSIN's rate takes the slot, from its
    own bins (five between 12.97 and 13.6 eV) and cross-section. What that
    rate lacks is H2's line absorption in the band, which the Monte Carlo
    field does not carry (D-346). F has no ionization slot, and D-358 stops
    the run for a linked neutral without one.
  - **Six doubly charged ions** (C, N, O, S, Si, Fe), formed by the X-ray
    reactions, which `calc_reac_rates` sets to zero (106 reactions), and for
    Si and Fe also by X+ + H+ -> X++ + H (endothermic by 30,000 K). Left
    unlinked, four stay empty and L-32 stays as it is; Si++ and Fe++ would
    fill in H II gas beside MOCASSIN's own. Linking them needs D-358's
    mechanism one stage up.
  - **Its own excited H2.** H2* is a species with 15 reactions:
    H2 + photon -> H2* through the same shielding function as dissociation,
    H2* + photon -> 2H unshielded, and H2* reacting with C+, O, OH. That is
    a two-level H2 beside the level model on h2-model: two realities.
  - **H-** (53 reactions): the gas-phase route to H2, whose absence D-358
    noted in H II gas (OH and H3+ below Cloudy's). Its photodetachment
    (threshold 0.75 eV) is
    1.43e-7 times the FUV field, a diffuse-ISM ratio of visible to FUV light
    that a 150 kK star does not have.
  - **159 photo-reactions** against 28. All but H2, CO and C I (and S I,
    on upstream's own function with a zero column) take alpha times the
    band-averaged field (D-350). N2 and CN, dissociated through lines below
    1000 A, get no shielding.
  - Eight PAH reactions (no PAH seed: inert, L-7), eleven anions.

### The box: the two networks at the run's own conditions

`boxTest.f90`: one cell, n_H 1000, at the median T, T_dust, chi, N(H2) of
pn150k's cells at eight depths, the seed MOCASSIN would hand over, and the
run's own grain formation coefficient and H2 dissociation rate (the
levels') imposed on both networks. Photo-rates are the network's alpha times
the cell's chi. Not the model: no feedback through the columns, CO
unshielded, MOCASSIN's ionization rates not inserted.

**Check**: the reduced box returns the run's 2n(H2)/nH to 2% at A_V 0.22
and 0.6% at the other seven.

| A_V | run | reduced | full as shipped | full, H2* pumping off | Cl photoionization x4 | x8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.26 | 0.0179 | 0.0180 | 0.0153 | 0.0175 | 0.0167 | 0.0163 |
| 0.30 | 0.0871 | 0.0871 | 0.0750 | 0.0841 | 0.0768 | 0.0702 |
| 0.34 | 0.237 | 0.237 | 0.210 | 0.229 | 0.208 | 0.185 |
| 0.38 | 0.442 | 0.442 | 0.404 | 0.428 | 0.394 | 0.353 |
| 0.46 | 0.744 | 0.744 | 0.708 | 0.724 | 0.683 | 0.632 |
| 0.58 | 0.903 | 0.904 | 0.876 | 0.881 | 0.853 | 0.816 |
| 0.66 | 0.934 | 0.934 | 0.909 | 0.911 | 0.890 | 0.863 |

| share of the H2 loss | 0.26 | 0.30 | 0.34 | 0.38 | 0.46 | 0.58 | 0.66 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| through H2*, as shipped | 0.126 | 0.115 | 0.104 | 0.093 | 0.070 | 0.038 | 0.022 |
| chlorine (Cl+ and HCl+), x1 | 0.033 | 0.038 | 0.042 | 0.048 | 0.067 | 0.085 | 0.079 |

| Cloudy's model (D-399) | 0.25-0.50 | | | | | | |

  - **As shipped the full network lowers H2 by 14% at A_V 0.30, and 11 of
    the 14 are its own H2***, dissociating pumped molecules the imposed rate
    already counts (0.3 of 2.8% at A_V 0.66).
  - **With H2* pumping off the full network lowers H2 by 2.5-3.5%** (A_V
    0.26-0.66), and chlorine carries 3-9% of the loss - not Cloudy's 25-50%.
    The x4 and x8 columns are a sensitivity, not a model. If photoionization
    is what makes Cloudy's Cl+, its Cl+ + H2 rate and its Cl0 give
    k n(H2) n(Cl+)/n(Cl0) = 1.6e-8 s^-1 at A_V 0.30 (n(H2) 110, Cl+ 0.119,
    Cl0 0.796), against UMIST's 9.5e-11 on our chi of 18: 1.7e-9. The ratio

    share is 21-44% at A_V 0.30-0.58 and its H2 10-22% lower.

    From `pdrFUVspec.out`, the share of FUV photons able to ionize Cl
    (12.97-13.6 eV) is 1.50 times the Draine field's in the shell holding

    2.2-2.5 times our chi in Habing units, the O-02 comparison (D-287,
    D-301) with its convention caveat; not rechecked here.

    unshielded) and x_e 7-13% higher: the other coefficients and the extra

**Cost**, one core, per solve:

| | reduced | full | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold (from the seed) | 2.0-3.9 ms | 57-161 ms | 25-48 |
| warm (from the answer) | 0.08-0.15 ms | 5.7-10.1 ms | 40-100 |

All solves returned status 0. If the box's times hold in every cell, one
iteration of pn150k (35,384 cells, 14 ranks, one solve per cell, D-354)
goes from 0.3-8 s to 19-300 s: 5-76 minutes on a run of 2 h 24 min with 15
chemistry iterations, the first of them cold. hiipdr: 2-26 minutes. Memory
(estimated, not measured): `pdrAbun` and its three reduction copies grow
from 1.1 to 6.9 kB per cell per rank, 38 to about 44 at the peak, which
lowers the 14-rank limit from about 46k to about 40k active cells; pn150k
41^3 still fits.

### Evaluation

**Can the full network be used: yes, and cost does not forbid it.** What
it needs before a result from it could be published:

  1. L-34's decision, for every element it adds, or each new ion a molecule
     consumes is stored twice.
  2. The link table built from the species file, not six hand lists: eight
     more elements (sixteen links, F without a slot).
  3. H2* out (the level model is the excited H2), D-395's reaction and
     H+ + H2 in. Both are edits to generated code with no generator in the
     tree.
  4. A window of MOCASSIN's field for what the band average gets wrong:
     Cl (D-400), H- photodetachment, N2 and CN.
  5. Every comparison with Cloudy rerun: 148 coefficients move at once.

**Recommended order** (mine; the user decides):

  1. L-34's decision, measured on the present network (the `[D358]` line
     for every linked element).
  2. The links from the species file.
  3. A generator of our own for the right-hand side, from the species and
     rate files, accepted when it reproduces `odes_reduced.c` and
     `odes_full.c` numerically. It removes the hand edits (D-395 was one)
     and makes item 3 above possible.
  4. Chlorine alone: the reduced network plus the five species and D-400's
     24 reactions (38 species), Cl's photoionization on MOCASSIN's own rate
     through D-358's slot. Measured on pn150k, hiipdr as the control.
  5. The full network as a seeded A/B against that.

The reason for 4 before 5 is the one D-394 to D-398 followed: chlorine,
eight elements and 148 coefficients in one step could not be told apart.

### Not yet known

  - MOCASSIN's own Cl photoionization rate against Cloudy's. D-358 would
    put MOCASSIN's into the solve, not UMIST's; the box could not.
  - Why Cloudy's implied rate is 7-10 times UMIST's on our field, and
    whether Cloudy has other sources of Cl+.
  - Whether restoring the molecular channels to `ionBalance` is stable in
    the iteration; D-185 to D-193 is the history.
  - The full network's cost in ionized cells and in the model's own
    sequence of solves (the box brackets it, cold and warm).
  - What the full network does to CO and the other molecules in the model;
    the box has no CO shielding.
  - The memory figures.

### Status

Audited; nothing changed. Decisions for the user: L-34's, and the order.

## D-402 - One x(X+): the same neutral/first-ion balance in both solvers (2026-10-10)

The user, reading D-401: "The same defect already exists for O+: in 78.5% of
pn150k's cells the solver's O+/O is more than 2x. So currently this is still
an issue? This seems like a major self consistency problem we should solve
before anything". Yes, current; and my 78.5% lumped two defects together.

### Measured first: the published runs' sampled cells

`pdrReacRates.out` (D-356) holds, one cell per 0.1 dex of A_V on rank 0, the
solver's own abundances beside the re-imposed ones and every reaction's
rate. Both published runs have it (`h026-site-pn41`, 15 cells;
`h026-site-hii31`, 13). Solver X+/X over MOCASSIN's ionized/neutral, range
over the cells of each zone:

| | pn150k ionized (A_V 0.01-0.13) | pn150k PDR (0.18-0.65) | hiipdr ionized (0.13-0.42) | hiipdr PDR (0.6-1.3) | hiipdr deep (1.8-2.7) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H | 1.01-1.08 | 1.06-2.0 | 1.00 | 1.07-1.14 | 2.5-3.3 |
| He | 0.008-0.97 | 0.36-0.71 | 1.00 | 0.48-0.54 | 0.30-0.36 |
| C | 5e-5-0.84 | 0.98-1.04 | 0.016-0.99 | 1.00-1.03 | 0.86-0.96 |
| O | 4e-6-0.91 | 0.04-2.7 | 0.037-0.93 | 1.4-1.8 | 0.01-0.05 |
| Mg | 3e-5-54 | 1.2-2.4 | 0.012-7.3 | 1.03-1.17 | 1.9-579 |

x_e, solver over MOCASSIN: 0.93 in pn150k's inner zone (He++ counted once),
0.96-0.98 in both PDRs, 0.89 deep in hiipdr. The solver's C+ fraction at
hiipdr's C+/C transition is 0.166 and 0.162 against MOCASSIN's 0.183 and
0.184.

Two defects:

  - **Ionized gas: one carrier for every stage (L-32).** Since D-266 the
    species C+ held C+ to C4+, so inside the solve all of it recombined and
    exchanged charge as C+. The trace neutrals the molecules form from were
    1-5 dex too high. (The atoms MOCASSIN stores were not affected: they
    are its own.)
  - **PDR: `ionBalance` lacked the network's channels (L-34).** By channel,
    from the same file (`tools/d402_ions/chanclass.py`): He+ is consumed by
    H (the network's charge transfer; Kingdon & Ferland's fit gives 1e-18
    at 50 K against the network's 3.5e-15) and by H2 and CO; O+ by H2 (up
    to 95% of its loss); H+ is made from H2 by cosmic rays and by He+ + H2
    (9-14%) and exchanges with O at the front (60-97% of both its formation
    and loss); Mg is ionized by H+ (98% at the front) and by C+, H3+ and the
    other ions (to 55%). MOCASSIN had none of these.

### The design

**Step 1 - each carrier is its own stage** (5681869).

  - X is MOCASSIN's stage 1 and X+ its stage 2, in the seed and in both
    impositions. Before the solve the element's atoms outside molecules,
    A - M, are shared among all of MOCASSIN's stages in its proportions and
    the network gets the first two shares; after it, the solver's X + X+ is
    split in MOCASSIN's stage 1 : stage 2.
  - `elemAvail` = 1 - M/A, with M counted from the species' own formulae
    (`speciesAtoms`, `pdrMolAtoms`). D-102 read it off the two carriers,
    which is why D-266 had to give the ion carrier every stage. One rule
    for every linked element, hydrogen and helium included, and on restart.
  - **Electrons.** The generated right-hand side builds x_e as the sum of
    the network's cations at every evaluation; the imposed entry is only
    written back at the end (the bridge's comment said the rates inside the
    solve used the imposed value: they did not). So the solve never had the
    electrons of He++, of any higher stage, or of the elements the network
    has no species for (S+, Si+, N+): 0.93 of MOCASSIN's in pn150k's inner
    zone, 0.96-0.98 in the PDRs. They are MOCASSIN's electrons less the
    linked first ions, added to that sum: `xe_extra` in the vendored
    `modules.F90`, one term in `odes_reduced.c` through
    `tools/patch_odes_xe.py` (zero by default, recorded in UPSTREAM.md).
  - `[D402]` replaces `[D358]`: all five elements, ionized cells apart,
    more than 10% and more than 2x from MOCASSIN's stage 2 / stage 1.

**Step 2 - every channel in both solvers, each computed once** (5609d63).
For a linked element's neutral/first-ion pair:

| channel | computed by | used by |
|---|---|---|
| photoionization, collisional ionization, recombination | `ionBalance` | both (D-358) |
| cosmic rays | the network's coefficients, in `ionBalance` | both (D-280) |
| charge transfer with H and H+ | the network's coefficients, in `ionBalance` (`pdrCtRates`) | both (new) |
| every other reaction of X or X+ | the solve | both (new) |

  - **Charge transfer with H** was the one channel both had with different
    numbers. The network's reactions are used in both, for the linked pairs
    only; unlinked elements keep `chex`. Kingdon & Ferland's He fit is
    outside its range below 6000 K, and MOCASSIN's reverse rate for O is the
    statistical 9/8 exp(-229/T) with no fine structure (11.1 at 100 K where
    the network's pair gives 7.0). At 1e4 K the network's O+ + H is 2.0e-9
    against 1.04e-9, and its pair's ratio is 1.27 against 1.15: the nebula's
    O0/O+ moves with it. Evaluated in `ionBalance` at its trial temperature,
    from the first iteration, as D-280 evaluates the cosmic rays.
  - **Hydrogen takes the other side** of the same reactions, with the
    call's own O, O+, Mg, He+ densities, so the O+ + H <-> O + H+ exchange
    closes inside `updateCell` and not across two Monte Carlo iterations.
  - **Everything else** is classified per reaction by its net effect on X
    and X+ at the solver's own state: X -> X+, X+ -> X (added to `ionUp`,
    `ionDn`), lost to anything else (the matrix diagonal), made from
    anything else (its right-hand side). `pdrIonRate`, six numbers per
    element per cell; it had held D-118's whole right-hand side, read by
    nothing since D-193. The sum of the stages is still `elemAvail`: the
    ratio is these terms' to set, the total is not, which is D-193's own
    distinction.
  - **The chain estimate** scales and trims the matrix and stands for the
    stages trimmed out of it (below 1e-8 of the largest), so the first
    ion's molecular sink is in its ratio; else O+ at 1e-9 of O would never
    feel O+ + H2.
  - **The check**: the gross sums of the classified channels against the
    right-hand side's own totals (D-113), loss and formation of X and X+,
    every solve. 4e-16 in every cell: nothing missing, nothing twice. Two
    reactions of the rate file (He+ and C+ recombining on a grain) are not
    in the generated right-hand side at all and are left out.

Four flavours rc 0 at each step on production, and with both on h2-model
(one conflict in `iteration_mod.f90`, both sides' allocations kept).

### "Should we consider just one solver for everything?" (the user, mid-run)

Recorded as considered and not taken now. `ionBalance` is re-solved at
every trial temperature of a cell's thermal iteration, and the heating
there follows x(H0); it is a linear solve of at most seven stages. The
chemistry is a stiff nonlinear network integrated in time to its steady
state (2-4 ms a solve from cold for 33 species, D-401). One solver would
sit inside the thermal loop and carry every stage MOCASSIN has, in code
that is generated with no generator in the tree. So the ion solver needs
the equation, not the answer, and this entry makes it the same equation in
both places; a single solver would reach the same state without the
one-iteration lag between them. If the lag costs convergence on the full
runs, or when the generator exists (D-401's step 3), it is the next step.

hiipdr 21^3, 2e6 packets, 7 iterations (four chemistry passes), production

**A bug of mine on the way**: the first build of step 2 combined only 20 of

### The first full run found a flaw in step 2 (`runs/d402-b-hii31`, h2-model)

hiipdr 31^3, 15 iterations, seeded, against `h026-site-hii31`. The two
solvers agreed as in the short test, and the cell update had stopped
converging - which the short tests' own summaries also showed and I had not
read:

| | baseline | 5609d63 |
|---|---|---|
| ion balance not reached, last iteration | 0% | 4% (from iteration 1: 8, 1, 2, 2, 3 ...) |
| Te balance not reached, last iteration | 0% | 10% |
| cells flagged and left out of the line output | 4 | 2,170 |
| Hbeta | 9.1657e36 | -0.745% |
| CO 1-0, 2-1, 3-2 | | x0.68, 0.67, 0.64 |

Flagged cells by A_V: 0.45-1.5, 620 (16-55% of the cells there); 2.7-3.0,
1,547. Two causes.

  - **Mine: hydrogen followed oxygen's last value.** 5609d63 put the
    metals' charge transfer into hydrogen's balance with the metals'
    densities of the previous pass of `updateCell`. In the atomic PDR the
    exchange O+ + H <-> O + H+ is 60-97% of both the formation and the loss
    of H+, so each species tracked the other's last value and the pair
    cycled with nothing to damp it; the failures began at iteration 1,
    before any chemistry. The exchange nearly cancels for hydrogen. **Fixed
    in 21ac639**: hydrogen has no explicit charge transfer in `ionBalance`;
    the solve hands it the NET of the two directions with the metals, as a
    source of H+ or a specific sink. The metals keep the network's
    coefficients with the call's own H and H+, one way, as `chex` was.
  - **Not mine: the outer shell reached `teFloor`.** See below.

### The outer shell reaches the 10 K floor

L-30 had `teFloor` as a clamp that did not bind ("the coldest hiipdr cell is
10.9 K"). It binds now: 1,546 cells at A_V 2.7-3.0 are flagged (798 at
10.000 K, the rest stopped between brackets just above it), the residual at
the floor is net cooling (H - C = -4e-29 against +7e-31), and `outputGas`
leaves flagged cells out of every line - which is where neutral carbon and
CO are.

The gas is colder because its heating fell: the chemistry's heating (all but
photoelectric) is 10% lower from r 16 pc out (8.1e-28 -> 7.3e-28), T 3-5%
lower (12.98 -> 12.50 K at 16 pc, 10.85 -> 10.36 at 18). **That heating had
been overstated by the inconsistency.** `chemical_heating` counts twelve
exothermic reactions, three of them He+ + H2 and He+ + CO, and evaluates
them on the abundances after the re-imposition. In the baseline's sampled
cells He+ was re-imposed at 1.9-3.3 times the value the network - which has
those reactions as He+'s sinks - held, and the chemical heating so computed
was 1.13-1.49 times what its own state gives (1.35 in the two deepest).

Whether the floor should stand is a separate decision and is not taken
here. `runs/d402-c-hii31-cmb` repeats the run with `teFloor 2.725` (the
keyword exists) to show where those cells settle and what the lines are
with every cell counted.

**The floor is the user's decision.** What the run shows: at 10 K it now
decides the temperature of a tenth of hiipdr's cells and, through the flag,
removes them from every line; at the CMB it decides nothing here (coldest
cell 9.47 K). L-30 recorded it as a clamp that did not bind. The chemistry's
grain temperature is already floored at T_CMB (L-30), the value 3D-PDR
carries.

### pn150k with the corrected step 2 (`runs/d402-c-pn41`, 21ac639)

41^3, 18 iterations, seeded, against `h026-site-pn41`. Run time 2:58:43
against 2:24:17 on 2026-10-05, not a same-night pair: the level model, which
this entry does not touch, took 6,598 s against 5,151 for the same 16 calls
(x1.28) and everything else x1.18, so no cost can be read from it.

**The cell update converges as the baseline's, iteration for iteration**: ion
balance not reached 0% at all 18; Te 0% except iterations 5 and 6 (72, 33% -
the baseline's own figures). No cell is flagged in either run (coldest 21.5 K
against 20.8). Largest change of the integrated quantities over the last
three iterations 1.44% (He2+) against 1.49%.

**The two solvers** (`[D402]`, iteration 18; totals reproduced to 6.7e-16):

| | baseline (`[D358]`) | ionized cells (415), >10% | other cells (34,969), >10% | >2x | largest (dex) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H | 44.8% more than 2x apart | 0 | 20.4% | 0.7% | 1.00 |
| He | - | 0 | 1.1% | 0 | 0.21 |
| C | - | 0 | 1.6% | 0 | 0.36 |
| O | 78.5% more than 2x apart | 0 | 34.3% | 0.6% | 1.67 |
| Mg | - | 0 | 0.8% | 0 | 0.29 |

The fractions are level from iteration 12 (H 20.2-20.7%, O 33.6-34.9%). In
the fifteen sampled cells (`ionsplit.py`) the ionized zone and the front
agree to 1% in all five elements (were 4e-6 to 54x); deep (A_V 0.46-0.65) H
is within 2-13%, O 10-16%, He, C and Mg within 3%. What is left sits at the
H/H2 transition, A_V 0.22-0.33, with both signs in neighbouring cells:
solver over MOCASSIN for H 1.46, 0.48, 0.13, oxygen following hydrogen
through the exchange (1.45, 0.48, 0.13). There hard photons make the ions,
He+ passes 30-43% of its ionizations on to hydrogen by charge transfer, and
that term - part of the net `ionBalance` is handed for hydrogen - arrives
one iteration late from a field few packets sample. **Lag times Monte Carlo
noise; supported in the sampled cells, not shown cell by cell:**

  - The estimator is spiky. The ionization rate the solve was given for H
    at iteration 18 is the cosmic rays' 1.975e-16 s^-1 to four digits in
    all five sampled cells past A_V 0.25 (no ionizing packet crossed them
    that iteration), and 4.5e-15 and 3.5e-14 in the two at A_V 0.23 and
    0.18.
  - A_V 0.226, a cell with photons this iteration: MOCASSIN's H+ balances
    recombination against that direct rate alone (ratio 1.00). The solver's
    has, besides, He+ + H -> He + H+ at 0.65 of the direct rate (2.6% of
    its gross H+ formation against the direct rate's 4.0%; the other 93% is
    the O exchange, which cancels). (1 + 0.65)/1.135, the second number the
    two electron densities' ratio, is 1.45; measured 1.457.
  - A_V 0.321, no photons this iteration: MOCASSIN's H+ needs 15 times the
    cosmic-ray rate, the solver's has only that. It is what a cell looks
    like one iteration after a hard photon: the solve, a steady state, has
    forgotten it; the handed source has not.
  - Deep (A_V 0.46-0.65), where the handed sources are steady (H2 + cosmic
    rays, He+ + H2; 42-51% of H+ formation), the two agree to 2-13%.

What the outputs cannot give is the same test in every cell: they hold one
iteration. 85.9% of the neutral cells pass the cell convergence test at
iteration 18 (report only). **The step this points to**: carry He+ + H ->
He + H+ for hydrogen in `ionBalance` itself, with the call's own He+, as the
metals' side already is - it runs one way, so it cannot cycle as the H-O
pair did - and leave only the O and Mg exchange as a net. Not done here.

**The solve's electrons.** In the baseline the solve ran with x_e 3-4.5%
under MOCASSIN's through the PDR (2.77-2.88e-4 against 2.87-2.97e-4) and 7%
under in the He2+ zone (1.09 against 1.17): the right-hand side summed its
own cations, and the network has none for S, Si, N or helium's second
electron. It is MOCASSIN's now, to 1% outside the transition cells above.

### pn150k's front moved because of one coefficient: He+ + H -> He + H+

**Refuted in part by D-403, 2026-10-11.** The shell table and its
prediction for He+ hold. The inference from them to Hbeta, the temperature
behind the front and the rotational lines does not: with the K&F fit back
above 6,000 K He+ returns and those three stay. They follow the transfer
below 6,000 K, where `ionBalance` had effectively none before this entry,
and hydrogen receiving the H+ of each transfer. And the paragraph on
oxygen's coefficients below is withdrawn: the network's are Stancil et al.
1999, within 4% of the fits Cloudy uses. See D-403.

A proxy for Hbeta (n_e n(H+) T^-0.9 summed over the cells) gives +0.25%, of
it +0.23 in the shells r 0.115-0.145 pc: the front. There He+ falls and H+
rises:

| r (pc) | T (K) | He+ new/baseline | predicted from the coefficient | H+ new/baseline | He's transfer / hydrogen's recombinations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.125-0.135 | 9,870 | 0.994 | 0.966 | 1.012 | 0.5% -> 1.1% |
| 0.135-0.145 | 8,160 | 0.875 | 0.833 | 1.064 | 5.5% -> 10.7% |
| 0.145-0.160 | 4,810 | 0.646 | 0.629 | 1.194 | 22% -> 35% |
| 0.160-0.180 | 520 | 0.680 | 0.737 | 1.127 | 0.8% -> 16% |
| 0.180-0.220 | 117 | 0.606 | 0.671 | 1.50 | 0.1% -> 29% |

`ionBalance` now has this reaction at the network's coefficient, where it
had Kingdon & Ferland's fit - evaluated below the 6,000 K its range starts
at:

| T (K) | K&F fit (cm^3 s^-1) | network | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 120 | 8.6e-18 | 4.1e-15 | 480 |
| 500 | 1.4e-16 | 5.3e-15 | 37 |
| 5,000 | 4.3e-15 | 1.34e-14 | 3.1 |
| 8,000 | 6.8e-15 | 1.69e-14 | 2.5 |
| 12,000 | 1.19e-14 | 2.07e-14 | 1.7 |

The prediction column is that swap and nothing else (recombination
4.27e-13 T4^-0.678 n_e). Each transfer is an H+. More neutral helium at the
front takes more of the hard photons (helium's photoionization heating +4.9%
at r 0.135-0.145) and passes fewer on: hydrogen's is 4-8% lower from r 0.145
to 0.20 and the gas colder (4,805 -> 4,642 K, 519 -> 485, 173 -> 167), which
is where the two lowest rotational H2 lines lose 2.4 and 4.0%.

Cloudy, as I read `atmdat_char_tran.cpp` (read only): the Kingdon & Ferland
expression at the gas temperature plus a quarter of it held at 6,000 K below
that - 8.5e-15 at 8,000 K, 1.4e-15 at 500 K. The network's is 2.0 and 3.7
times those. For oxygen the two sets agree to 7-18% below 1,000 K in the
forward direction (the reverse 1.4-1.6x, the fit with fine structure against
the statistical reverse), and the network's is 1.7-2.3 times K&F's at
8,000-17,000 K in both directions; neutral oxygen in the ionized zone is
x1.2-1.5 for it (1.8 -> 2.8 times Cloudy's at 0.03 pc). And MOCASSIN had no
H+ + Mg -> Mg+ + H at all, which is 78-98% of the solver's Mg+ formation in
ionized gas (Mg+ x1.03-1.17 at r 0.09-0.115).

**Step 2 made each of these reactions one number in both solvers. It did not
establish that the network's is the better number above a few thousand K,
where UMIST's power laws are being used in photoionized gas.** The
alternative with the same one-number property is D-358's direction:
MOCASSIN's coefficient handed to the network's reaction. Not decided here;
the measured size of the choice is Hbeta 0.26%, the He I lines 1%, the
transition zone 3-6% in T - and, found later the same day (next but one
section), the Mg I lines x0.020 and [O I] 6300 +4.6%.

  1. `[D402]`: ionized cells 0% - held. More than 2x apart under 2% - held

  3. Crossing within 0.005 mag of 0.393 - held (-0.0004). H2 lines within

## D-403 - Charge transfer with H by the gas at hand; helium's transfer in hydrogen's own balance; the floor at the CMB (2026-10-10)

The user, on D-402's three open items and my recommendation for each:
"Proceed with your recommendations". They were: (1) for charge transfer with
H, the fits made for ionized gas (Kingdon & Ferland) inside their stated
temperature ranges and the network's below, in both solvers; (2) the
temperature floor's default at the CMB instead of 10 K; (3) hydrogen's side
of He+ + H -> He + H+ carried in MOCASSIN's own balance.

### Measured before coding: the recommendation was wrong for oxygen

D-402 said that both solvers now ran on "UMIST's power laws ... in
photoionized gas" and I recommended Kingdon & Ferland's fits there. Before
changing three reactions I put every data set on this machine side by side
(the network's rate file, MOCASSIN's `chex` table, and Cloudy c25.00's
`atmdat_char_tran.cpp`, `ctrecombdata.dat`, `ctiondata.dat`, read only).

**Oxygen.** Cloudy does not use Kingdon & Ferland for O+ + H and H+ + O. It
uses its own fits to Tables 2-4 of Stancil et al. (1999, A&AS 140, 225), and
the network's two reactions are fits to the same work, valid 10-41,000 K:

| T (K) | O+ + H -> O + H+: Cloudy's Stancil fit | network / it | K&F / it | H+ + O -> O+ + H: Cloudy's | network / it | K&F statistical reverse / it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 3.82e-10 | 0.92 | 0.97 | 5.41e-12 | 0.98 | 0.62 |
| 300 | 5.66e-10 | 1.03 | 0.90 | 2.82e-10 | 1.22 | 0.75 |
| 1,000 | 8.51e-10 | 1.04 | 0.87 | 5.80e-10 | 1.33 | 0.91 |
| 5,000 | 1.56e-9 | 1.00 | 0.65 | 1.23e-9 | 1.09 | 0.70 |
| 10,000 | 2.05e-9 | 0.98 | 0.51 | 1.65e-9 | 0.97 | 0.55 |
| 17,000 | 2.54e-9 | 0.96 | 0.42 | 2.08e-9 | 0.98 | 0.45 |
| 25,000 | 2.97e-9 | 0.94 | 0.36 | 2.46e-9 | 0.99 | 0.38 |

So the network's oxygen coefficients are not a cold-gas fit run past its
range: they are the modern calculation over the whole range, within 4% of
what Cloudy uses at nebular temperatures, and it is Kingdon & Ferland's fit
(stated range 10-10,000 K, a constant 1.0e-9) that is half of it at 1e4 K.
**Oxygen stays on the network's coefficients.** D-402's +4.6% in [O I] 6300
on pn150k was the better data reaching MOCASSIN's balance, not an artefact;
that our [O I] 6300 is 1.5 times Cloudy's is something else. The statement
in D-402 and in L-48 that the oxygen rates were a wrong choice in hot gas is
withdrawn.

**Helium, He+ + H -> He + H+** (cm^3 s^-1):

| T (K) | K&F fit (6,000-1e5 K) | network (10-41,000 K) | Cloudy | network / K&F | network / Cloudy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | (6e-18) | 4.0e-15 | 1.3e-15 | | 3.1 |
| 1,000 | (5e-16) | 6.0e-15 | 1.8e-15 | | 3.4 |
| 5,000 | (4.3e-15) | 1.34e-14 | 5.6e-15 | | 2.4 |
| 6,000 | 5.1e-15 | 1.47e-14 | 6.4e-15 | 2.9 | 2.3 |
| 10,000 | 9.0e-15 | 1.89e-14 | 1.12e-14 | 2.1 | 1.7 |
| 17,000 | 2.26e-14 | 2.47e-14 | 2.82e-14 | 1.1 | 0.87 |
| 30,000 | 7.2e-14 | 3.3e-14 | 9.0e-14 | 0.46 | 0.37 |

Cloudy's is 1.25 times the K&F expression above 6,000 K and, below, a
quarter of its 6,000 K value plus the expression itself. The network's low
range is 3.1-3.4 times Cloudy's: it is the size of the factor of 4 by which
Stancil et al. (1998) corrected the radiative rate of Zygelman et al.
(1989), which Cloudy's source notes; whether UMIST's fit predates that
correction I cannot establish here. Inside the K&F range, K&F is 0.80 of
Cloudy's at every temperature and the network's 0.37-2.3.

**Magnesium, H+ + Mg -> Mg+ + H.** K&F's ionization fit (Cloudy's
`ctiondata.dat`: 9.76e-12 t4^3.14 (1 + 55.54 exp(-1.12 t4)), 5,000-30,000
K) gives 3.6e-11 at 5,000 K, 1.87e-10 at 1e4, 4.8e-10 at 17,000, 9.0e-10 at
30,000. The network has 1.1e-9 at every temperature (UMIST's accuracy class
C). MOCASSIN had no such reaction before D-402.

### The design

One routine, `pdrCtCoef(T, k)` in `common_mod`, returns the coefficient of
every row of the network's charge-transfer list at T. For a reaction with an
ionized-gas fit (`pdrCtKF`: helium's from MOCASSIN's own `chex`, with its
stated range; magnesium's added, with its range) the row that carries the
reaction gets the fit inside that range and the network's own value outside
it, below and above. Oxygen has no entry. `ionBalance` sums the rows by
element and direction (`pdrCtRates`, now a wrapper); `pdrStep` writes the
same rows into the solve's rate array before the solve, at the cell's own
temperature and not the clamped one the network's other rates use (L-30: 3
cells of pn150k). One number per reaction in both solvers, by construction.

**The data sets do not meet at the range edges**: the coefficient steps down
x2.9 as T rises through 6,000 K (He) and x30 through 5,000 K (Mg), and x1.2
at 30,000 K (Mg). That is what "each fit in its own range" costs with these
two sets; a temperature iteration that brackets across 6,000 K sees a
small step in He+/H+. Watched in the runs (Te balance not reached).

**Hydrogen's side of He+ + H.** D-402 handed hydrogen the NET of its charge
transfer with the linked elements, from the last solve. Helium's part of
that net runs one way and follows helium's photoionization, which on
pn150k's transition is a hard-photon estimator that is zero in most cells in
any one iteration (D-402: the solvers 1.45x apart in H+ where predicted
1.45). `ionBalance` now adds ctDn(He) n(He+) to hydrogen's ionization with
the call's own He+ (and ctUp(He) n(He) to its recombination, zero in this
network); for hydrogen the two helium rows are marked as MOCASSIN's own
channels, so they leave the handed net. The H-O and H-Mg exchange stays a
net: those run both ways and cycled when carried explicitly (D-402).

**The floor.** `teFloor`'s default is `real(TcmbK)`, with `TcmbK = 2.725d0`
a constant of `common_mod` from which `pdr_mod` now also makes the
chemistry's `Tcmb` (bitwise as before). The keyword still overrides. The
flag on a cell that ends on the floor is unchanged.

Commit 4cabcd8; merged into h2-model as 6778adb (one conflict in
`pdr_mod.f90` before the solve, both sides kept: the level model's H2 rate,
H-012, and the new rows). Four flavours rc 0 on both; `h2Test`, `h2Slab`
rc 0.

### What this run refutes in D-402: it was not "one coefficient"

D-402 traced pn150k's +0.26% in Hbeta, the 3-6% colder gas behind the front
and the -2.4, -4.0% in the two lowest rotational H2 lines to "one
coefficient", the network's He+ + H being 1.7-3.1 times Kingdon & Ferland's
at 5,000-12,000 K, and I predicted that with the K&F fit back in its range
Hbeta would return to 2.6780 and the lines recover in part. **It does not
happen.** Above 6,000 K He+ is back at its value from before D-402 (19.2
against 19.3 cm^-3 at 0.14 pc; the coefficient alone predicts x1.15 from
D-402, measured x1.13) and He I 5876 comes half way back. Hbeta stays
(-0.016% from D-402, +0.25% over the run before it); the gas behind the
front stays at D-402's temperature; 0-0 S(0) and S(1) stay at -3.9, -2.5%.

What those follow is the two other things D-402 did with the same reaction,
both kept here:

  - **the transfer below 6,000 K.** Before D-402 `ionBalance` evaluated
    Kingdon & Ferland's fit there, outside its range, where it is 3 to 480
    times smaller than the network's - effectively no transfer. Since D-402
    both solvers have the network's. He+ behind the front fell by a third
    (4.67 -> 3.02 at 0.15 pc, 1.83 -> 1.24 at 0.17) and is unchanged by
    D-403, as is the temperature there;
  - **hydrogen receiving the H+ of each transfer**, which its balance did
    not before D-402 (the transfer removed a He+ and made nothing): H+ at
    0.14 pc 76.6 -> 81.5 -> 80.4 with the transfer's size more than halved
    in between.

D-402's shell table was right about He+ and its "predicted from the
coefficient" column held; the inference from He+ to Hbeta, the temperature
and the lines was mine and was wrong. The open data question is therefore
not the coefficient above 6,000 K but the one below it, where the network's
is 2.4-3.4 times what Cloudy uses.

### The two solvers: a quarter of the level is gone, and the rest has other carriers

Hydrogen's side of He+ + H made current: cells more than 2x apart 0.7 ->
0.1% (H) and 0.6 -> 0.1% (O); more than 10% apart 20.4 -> 15.5% (H), 34.3
-> 28.8% (O), 1.6 -> 0.1% (C), 0.8 -> 0.0% (Mg), 1.1 -> 0.4% (He); level
from iteration 12 (H 15.5-16.4%, O 28.8-30.3%). In the sampled cell where
D-402 tested the explanation (A_V 0.23) the solver's H+/H over MOCASSIN's
was 1.46 and is 1.00.

The same sampled cells show what is left. A_V 0.26: 0.48 -> 0.87. A_V 0.32
(grid cell 1,6,20): 0.13 -> 0.14, with MOCASSIN's x(H+) 3.0e-4 at D-402,
2.8e-4 now and 3.6e-5 before D-402, the solver's 3.9e-5 in all three. In
that cell MOCASSIN's H+ needs 8.6 times everything the network forms there
(2.1e-15 against 2.45e-16 per H nucleus per s), in an iteration in which
the ionization rate `ionBalance` itself had for hydrogen is the cosmic
rays' alone (the solve's slot is 1.975e-16 to four digits). The excess can
only have come with terms handed from the previous iteration. Helium's
direct transfer is no longer one of them. Candidates in the network's own
budget of that cell: H + H2+ -> H2 + H+ (10% of its H+ formation in a quiet
iteration, 28% deeper; H2+ is made by the same hard photons through H2's
photoionization, D-358) and He+ + H2 -> He + H+ + H. That a cell with the
same seed shows it at the same iteration in two runs fits a photon event at
iteration 17 common to both.

## D-404 - A second solve of `ionBalance` after the chemistry: measured every iteration, kept at the last (2026-10-11)

The user, on the open item D-403 left (L-47: `ionBalance` trails the
chemistry by one iteration; the general cure "a second solve of `ionBalance`
after the chemistry with the fresh terms, or one solver"):

> can we try including a second solve of MOCASSIN's balance after the
> chemistry only at the last iteration to see if that is indeed effective?
> Maybe that is enough for consistency?

and, while the work was under way: "perhaps we should also re-evaluate the
effect of damping since we have made many changes to the code since it has
been implemented. Make a note of that so we can come back to it later."
(Logged as L-49 in `doc/pdr-status.md`, 3f90e71; this entry supplies its
first numbers.)

### The two questions, and why they need different measurements

1. **Is the delay what holds the two solvers apart?** D-403 left that as a
   hypothesis: supported on pn150k by a few sampled cells, unexplained on
   hiipdr, and one explicit term had removed only a quarter of it. The test
   has to remove the delay and change nothing else.
2. **Is a second solve at the last iteration enough to make the model that
   is written out consistent?** That is a statement about the written model,
   which is not the iteration's solve but a blend of it with the state
   before (the damping, D-174/D-200).

### Design

`updateCell(grid, i, j, k, ionPass)`: with `ionPass` true the temperature
is left alone and `ionBalance` is solved once at the temperature the cell
holds, exactly as `iterateT` calls it at a trial temperature (`calcAlpha`,
then the balance with its own n_e iteration), on whatever `pdrIonRate` and
`elemAvail` hold at that moment. It flags nothing; it reports whether the
cell had a field to solve with and whether the balance was reached.

`ionSecondSolve` (`iteration_mod`) runs that pass over the cells each rank
owns - the ownership `updateCell` and `pdrStep` already share - and
`pdrIonCompare` counts the result against the solver's own X+/X, which
`pdrStep` now stores per cell and element (`grid%pdrSolIon`). Three uses:

| pass | when | terms | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, control | after `updateCell`, before the chemistry | the ones the first solve had | put back |
| 2 | after the chemistry and `pdrToMocassin` | this iteration's | put back |
| 3, kept | once the run has decided to stop | the last iteration's | kept |

Passes 1 and 2 restore the stages, n_e, their reduction buffers and the
rates `ionBalance` stores for the chemistry, cell by cell, so the iteration
goes on from the first solve as before. That is what makes the test of
question 1 clean, and it is also what lets the full runs pair exactly with
D-403's: until the run stops, nothing differs.

**(Replaced after the full runs: pass 3 as described in this paragraph - a
third solve once the run has stopped - is the third version withdrawn, see
"A third version withdrawn" below. What is kept now is pass 2's own result.)**
Pass 3 cannot sit where pass 2 does, because the run decides to stop after
the damping. So it is made at the temperature the last iteration's solves
ran at (kept in `teSolved404` before the damping) and its stages are then
damped against the iteration's start exactly as the first solve's were (the
D-200 snapshot, handed on with `move_alloc` instead of freed). The written
model then differs from the one without the pass in the terms of that one
solve and in nothing else. The stage sums and the chemistry's atoms and
electrons follow as they follow the first solve (`rescaleIonToAvail`;
`pdrIonsToAbun`, the D-162/D-231 rule). **Not done by the pass:** the
temperature is not solved again on the new ions, and the chemistry is not
solved again on them.

### Two versions withdrawn before the full runs

**The kept solve at the model's damped temperature** (first version,
`runs/d404-test-a`). It took the model as it stood after the damping and
solved the balance at that temperature, leaving the result undamped. On the
short test the written model then stood further from the solver in oxygen
and magnesium than before (42.3 and 43.9% of cells more than 10% apart,
from 22.8 and 11.2), Hbeta moved by -0.52%, [O I] 6300 by +8.7% and [S II]
by +5%. None of that is the delay: the pass had changed three things at
once (the terms, the temperature of the solve, and whether the stages are
damped), and the last two dominate in a model that is still moving. With
the version above, the same test moves Hbeta by -0.010% and no line above
1e-3 Hbeta by 1%.

**Flagging a cell whose second solve does not reach the balance.** Three of
4,661 cells on the short test; flagged, they would have left the line sums.
The first solve had reached its balance in those cells, so they now stand
as they were and are counted (`balance not reached in`).

One slip of mine on the way, recorded because it is the second of its kind
(D-403's merge was the first): a build that failed went unnoticed inside a
command chain and a test was launched on the previous binary
(`runs/d404-test-c`, marked in its README; not a result). The binary's
return code and time stamp are now checked before a launch.

### Short test: hiipdr 21^3, 7 iterations, seeded as `runs/d403-test-a` (`runs/d404-test-e`)

**The path is the one D-403's test took.** Every per-iteration line that
depends on the model's state is identical to the printed digit: the 16
`[D402]` lines, 8 `[D354]`, 8 `[D362]`, the four per-iteration `[D220]` and
the 32 summary lines (converged cells, packets). Run time 3:51-4:05 over
the four builds of these passes against 3:52 without them: any cost is at
most 6% here, which is inside what this machine varies by; the full runs
measure it better.

**The control moves nothing.** A second solve on the first solve's terms
leaves every element's X+/X within 10% in every cell at every iteration
(largest move 0.01 dex) and n_e likewise. So whatever pass 2 moves is the
terms.

**The delay is the whole of it for H, He, C and Mg, and half of it for O.**
Cells outside the ionized zone (x(H+) < 0.5; 4,608-4,611 of them) whose
solver X+/X is more than 10% from MOCASSIN's, per cent, the first solve
(the `[D402]` line, reproduced exactly by pass 2's own "before" count) and
the second:

| iteration | H | He | C | O | Mg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4, first solve | 71.9 | 84.7 | 57.4 | 88.7 | 88.6 |
| 4, second | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 8.2 | 0.0 |
| 5, first | 83.4 | 60.2 | 15.4 | 30.0 | 32.4 |
| 5, second | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 11.9 | 0.0 |
| 6, first | 52.8 | 13.3 | 0.9 | 28.2 | 11.1 |
| 6, second | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 12.2 | 0.0 |
| 7, first | 30.5 | 12.4 | 0.4 | 22.8 | 11.2 |
| 7, second | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | 11.6 | 0.0 |

Magnesium's 6.8% more than 2x apart at iteration 7 goes to 0.0 as well; the
largest remaining difference is 0.01 dex in every element but oxygen (0.19).
In the ionized cells both solves agree with the solver to 0.01 dex, as
before. The second solve moved n_e by more than 10% in 0.8% of the cells,
and reached its balance in every one.

**Oxygen's other half is a source the trimmed stage does not carry.** The
probe (`[D404p]`, 12 cells per iteration on rank 0) found the same thing in
all 24 cells it printed: A_V 2.72-3.03, T 9.7-11.2 K, x(H2) 0.488, the
solver's O+/O at 1.72-2.02e-9 and MOCASSIN's at 1.558-1.559e-9 in the first
solve and the second alike - a constant, whatever is handed over. At 1.6e-9
of the neutral the first ion is below `ionTrim` (1e-8), the stage is left
out of the matrix and keeps its chain value, and the chain is a ratio of
rates: it carries the handed loss (O+ + H2, 8.3e-8 s^-1) in its denominator
but has no place for a source that does not come from O (channel 6, O+ made
from molecules, 1.3-3.9e-17 per O atom per second). In each of the 24 cells
(solver - MOCASSIN) x loss / source is 0.984-0.993: the difference is that
source, to 2%. It is not the delay and a second solve cannot remove it. At
2e-9 of the oxygen it reaches no line; it is a count that will not go to
zero until the chain value of a trimmed first ion carries its source. Not
changed here: it would alter the first solve and with it the pairing with
D-403's runs.

**The kept solve, and the written model.** On this test, which stops at
iteration 7 with the PDR still cooling:

| cells more than 10% apart, per cent | H | He | C | O | Mg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| solver vs the kept solve, before the damping | 6.8 | 0.1 | 0.1 | 12.4 | 0.1 |
| solver vs the written model, without the pass | 41.7 | 15.9 | 29.0 | 55.4 | 37.8 |
| solver vs the written model, with it | 31.0 | 7.0 | 29.0 | 50.6 | 33.8 |
| the written model's X+/X moved by the pass | 13.3 | 8.5 | 0.2 | 7.3 | 10.7 |

The kept solve stands where pass 2 does except in hydrogen (6.8 against
0.0): it is solved on the molecular content the model holds, which is
damped, with sources the chemistry computed on the undamped one, and where
H+ is made from H2 rather than from H the ratio follows the mismatch. The
written model is far from the solver with or without the pass, because here
the damping is most of the distance: the written temperature is more than
1% from the one the last solves ran at in 98.9% of these cells and more than
10% in 53.8%. That is a property of a 7-iteration test and says nothing yet
about a settled run; it is the number the full runs are for. Three second
solves did not reach the balance; none of the lines saw it (Hbeta -0.010%,
0 of 68 recombination and 0 of 69 collisionally excited lines above the
thresholds moved by 1%; CO 2-1, 3-2, 4-3 x1.0001; no flagged cell).

### A third version withdrawn: the kept solve as a third solve from the damped state

The two full runs show what was wrong with solving once more after the run
has stopped. It starts from the damped stages and runs on the damped
molecular content with sources the chemistry computed on the undamped one,
so it is not the solve pass 2 made: it leaves hydrogen more than 10% from
the solver in 3.4% (hiipdr) and 1.7% (pn150k) of the neutral cells where
pass 2 leaves none, and on pn150k it does not converge in 549 cells of the
layer that matters. The user asked for the second solve after the chemistry
at the last iteration to be kept; pass 2 at the last iteration is that
solve.

**Now** (aa7a3ea; merged into h2-model 997efdf): pass 2 sets its result
aside in each iteration - stages and n_e, in the cells where the solve was
made and reached its balance - and puts the model back as before. When the
run stops, `ionKeepSecond` puts that result in the first solve's place,
damped against the iteration's start exactly as the first was, and n_e as
it is. No third solve, no stored temperature. The cost is one more copy of
the stages on each rank: 0.3 kB per cell on pn150k (11 elements, 7 stages),
under 1% of the 38 kB a cell costs per rank (D-370).

Short test again (`runs/d404-test-f`, the inputs of the other short tests):
the per-iteration lines are those of D-403's test and the 12 control and 28
second-solve lines those of the earlier build; the second solve is kept in
all 4,661 cells. The written model stands more than 10% from the solver in
H 27.1, He 6.7, C 29.2, O 49.6, Mg 33.8% of the neutral cells (31.0, 7.0,
29.0, 50.6, 33.8 with the third solve; 41.7, 15.9, 29.0, 55.4, 37.8 with
none). Hbeta -0.015%; no line above the thresholds by 1%; no cell flagged.

**The hydrogen budget closes.** `[D220]` prints, before its rescale, how
far x(H0) + x(H+) + 2x(H2) is from 1 in the stages as they stand. With the
first solve (every iteration, every run since D-220): off by more than 1% in
26.4% of the short test's cells at its last iteration, mean 0.0134. With the
second solve in its place: 0 cells, mean 0.0000. That is not a coincidence
of this test. The first solve normalises the stages to the molecular
content of the iteration before (the hand-back it has at that point), so
its damped stages sum to 1 - 2x(H2) of the previous iteration and the
D-220 rescale has to move them. The second solve is normalised to this
iteration's own molecular content, and 0.75 of it plus 0.25 of the stages
the iteration started with sums to 1 minus twice the damped x(H2) exactly.
The stale normalisation is the same delay, seen in the conserved sum
instead of in a ratio.

### What this answers

**Is a second solve after the chemistry effective?** Yes, and it settles
what D-403 could only argue. With the delay removed and nothing else
changed, the two solvers' X+/X agree within 10% in every neutral cell for
H, He, C and Mg on both fixtures at every iteration, and for oxygen on
pn150k in all but 0.0%; the control shows a second solve on the old terms
changes nothing. So the 15-29% of neutral cells D-403 left more than 10%
apart were MOCASSIN's balance running one iteration behind the chemistry -
in the terms handed over and in the molecular content the stages are
normalised to - and, on hiipdr, a second and unrelated thing in oxygen
(L-50).

**Is keeping it at the last iteration enough?** For the model that is
written, it does what the delay's removal can do, and no more is to be had
from it:

  - the written ions carry the balance on the last iteration's own
    chemistry in every cell of pn150k and all but one of hiipdr, and their
    hydrogen budget closes without being enforced (L-29);
  - nothing observed moves by more than 1.0% ([C I] 370 um on hiipdr), so
    the delay was not biasing any line of either fixture by more than that
    at the last iteration;
  - what still separates the written ions from the solver's (hiipdr:
    H 28.7 -> 13.4, He 14.7 -> 8.5, C 32.0 -> 32.1, O 25.7 -> 18.7, Mg 25.1 -> 18.1 per cent of neutral cells; pn150k: H 17.6 -> 6.4, He 9.1 -> 9.1, C 14.2 -> 14.1, O 43.5 -> 18.6, Mg 0.8 -> 0.7) is the
    damping, by construction: the written stages are 0.75 of a solve that
    agrees with the solver and 0.25 of the stages the iteration started
    from. That is L-49, which the user has set aside to come back to.

What it leaves untouched is the path. Every iteration before the last
still hands the transfer, the thermal balance and the chemistry ions
solved one iteration behind, and still relies on the D-220 rescale to mend
the hydrogen budget. Whether that matters is not measured. The
per-iteration numbers suggest little: the second solve moves n_e by more
than 10% in at most 0.1% (pn150k) and 2.1% (hiipdr) of the neutral cells
in an iteration, and no ion of the ionized gas. But that is an inference
from this run's counts, not a run with the second solve kept throughout.

### Not yet known

  - What keeping the second solve at every iteration does to the model's
    path. The code for it is the kept step moved to where pass 2 already
    runs; the run pair is hiipdr and pn150k again.
  - What the thermal balance and the chemistry would give on the second
    solve's ions at the last iteration: neither is solved again. hiipdr's
    [C I] 370 um, -1.0% from the ions alone, is the only size at hand.
  - The damping (L-49): whether the cycle it was put in against still
    exists, and what the written model looks like without it.
  - Oxygen's first ion where it is trimmed out of the matrix (L-50): the
    fix is not made.
  - Why the first version's third solve did not settle in 549 cells, and
    why the control moves oxygen by 0.1-0.2 dex in a handful of cells on
    terms that have not changed. Neither was looked into; both concern
    `ionBalance`'s own iteration from a state that is not already its
    solution.
  - hiipdr's jump at iteration 7 (H 86%, He 85% of neutral cells apart
    after the first solve, against 22% and 7% the iteration before): it
    follows two iterations in which most cells' temperature balance was
    not reached, and is in D-403's run too.

## D-405 - The damping across iterations, re-evaluated (2026-10-13)

The user, 2026-10-11, during D-404: "perhaps we should also re-evaluate the
effect of damping since we have made many changes to the code since it has
been implemented. Make a note of that so we can come back to it later."
That note is L-49. Today, after D-404 closed: "lets work on the Damping
re-evaluation".

### What the damping is, as the code stands

`iterDamp` (default 0.25; `common_mod.f90`) is the share of the previous
iteration kept at the end of each Monte Carlo iteration
(`iteration_mod.f90`, after the reductions):

  - the temperature, in every gas run and from the first iteration (D-174,
    2026-09-07): `Te = 0.75 Te_solved + 0.25 Te_start`;
  - the chemistry's abundances `pdrAbun`, with `H2den` and `elemAvail`
    derived again from the blend, and the ion stages `ionDen`, from
    `pdrStartIter` on (D-200, D-201, 2026-09-09);
  - since D-404 the second solve kept at the stop, against the same
    iteration-start stages;
  - **not** the electron density, which is the last solve's.

It was put in against a limit cycle: D-173 counted 44-76% of the cells
crossing the 1,000 K branch boundary on every iteration, in both
directions at once. Since then `updateCell` runs once per iteration and
not inside a coupling loop (D-216), the chemistry is solved once (D-354),
the cooling lines escape by their own optical depth, the scattered field
has its sites, and both solvers carry one neutral/first-ion balance
(D-402, D-403). Nobody has checked the cycle against any of that.

What the damping costs is known from D-404: the model that is written is
a blend and not a solution. Its temperature is more than 1% from the one
its last solves ran at in 51.2% of hiipdr's neutral cells and 37.4% of
pn150k's, and with the one-iteration delay removed its ions are still
more than 10% from the chemistry's own in 13.4% (H) and 32.1% (C) of
hiipdr's neutral cells where the undamped solve is off in 0.0% and 1.5%.

### The test

Seeded pairs, one per fixture. The damped arms exist: `runs/d404b-hii31`
(15 iterations) and `runs/d404c-pn41` (18), the published runs, on the
h2-model branch (997efdf; the level model in the loop). The undamped arms
are the same binary (md5 3ba0c9dc...), input, seed and 14 ranks with one
line added to the input, `iterDamp 0.`: `runs/d405-hii31-d0` and
`runs/d405-pn41-d0`, chained by `runs/d405-chain.sh`, launched 13:36.
Fixed iteration counts, as for every seeded pair (the integrated test is
printed at each iteration and not acted on, `convTotals 1e-6`), so each
arm also shows at which iteration the 2% stop would have fallen.

With `iterDamp 0` nothing else changes path: the snapshots are not taken,
the three blends are skipped, the rescale of the stages to the available
hydrogen (D-220) runs as before, and the kept second solve goes into the
written model as it is (`ionKeepSecond`'s other branch). Read from the
code, not yet from a run.

No code is added for this first pair. The logs of the damped runs already
print, at every iteration, what a cycle would show in
(`tools/d405_damp/readdamp.py <run> [<run> ...]` tabulates them side by
side):

  - cells that started the iteration cold and ended it above 3,000 K
    (`[D217]`), and the cells above 3,000 K (`[D202]`);
  - the step of x(H0) and of the molecular fraction over the iteration
    (`[D196]`, `[D202]`), and the share of cells in which the chemistry's
    H2 and CO moved by more than 1% (`[D354]`);
  - the model-integrated test and the share of cells converged;
  - the two solvers' agreement after the first and the second solve
    (`[D402]`, `[D404]`) and the hydrogen budget before its rescale
    (`[D220]`).

Two things about reading them. The steps of `[D196]` and `[D202]` are
taken on the model as written, after the damping, so a damped run's are
0.75 of what its solves moved by, and the integrated test is flattered
the same way (D-191 said so of the cell count). And the two arms part at
the first iteration, since the temperature is damped from there: they are
two realisations of the Monte Carlo field, so a difference between them
is the damping plus that scatter.

### What the damped runs show before the pair is read

hiipdr with the damping has not been still since about its tenth
iteration, it has been stationary. From iteration 10 to 15: the median
step of x(H0) is 2.4% and the 90th percentile 30%, every iteration; the
chemistry's H2 moves by more than 1% in 32-34% of the cells and CO in
97-99%; the cells counted converged stay at 67-70% of the neutral ones;
the first solve leaves 28-29% of the neutral cells more than 10% from the
chemistry in hydrogen. Branch crossings are none or one cell per
iteration (pn150k: 4-25 of 35,384). The integrated test falls 16, 8.3,
4.1, 3.2, 2.3, 2.0%.

So there is no branch cycle with the damping on, and there is a floor of
motion. A floor can be the Monte Carlo field's noise, answered afresh
every iteration, or a cycle of small amplitude that the damping holds
down. The two predict different things without the damping. For noise
that is independent from one iteration to the next, a blend
`y = 0.75 x + 0.25 y_before` has 0.6 of the variance of `x` and its steps
have 0.9 of it, against 2 for the steps of `x` itself: the undamped steps
are sqrt(2/0.9) = 1.49 of the damped ones, and the undamped model carries
1/sqrt(0.6) = 1.29 of the damped one's scatter. A cycle held down by the
damping would give more than that.

### Predictions (written before any undamped result was read)

  1. The branch cycle of D-173 does not come back: cells going from cold
     to above 3,000 K stay below 10 per iteration on hiipdr and below 100
     on pn150k from the eighth iteration on. Held with some confidence;
     the mechanisms that fed it have been taken out one by one.
  2. The floor is noise: the plateau of the median step of x(H0) is
     1.3-1.7 of the damped arm's (1.49 if independent), not several
     times it.
  3. The integrated test falls faster at first without the damping
     (iterations 8-11 below the damped arm's) and ends on a higher floor:
     hiipdr at 2-3.5% at iteration 15, so the 2% stop is **not** reached
     by 15. Held weakly.
  4. The written model is its solution: the written ions are more than 10%
     from the chemistry's in at most 0.5% of the neutral cells for H, He,
     C and Mg (carbon from 32.1% on hiipdr, 14.1% on pn150k), with
     hiipdr's oxygen at 8-12% (L-50).
  5. The first solve's disagreement, which is the one-iteration delay,
     grows with the steps: hydrogen from 28% of hiipdr's neutral cells to
     35-45%.
  6. The lines: Hbeta within 0.3%; [C II] 158, [O I] 63 and [C I] 609 and
     370 um within 5%; the H2 lines within 3%; CO within 20%; the H/H2
     crossing within 0.01 mag in A_V.

If 1 and 2 hold, the damping is no longer what keeps the model from
cycling, and what it does is trade a quarter less scatter in the written
model for a written model that is not a solution. If either fails, where
it fails is the next measurement.

### hiipdr, the undamped arm (`runs/d405-hii31-d0`, 15 iterations, 39:47)

Against `runs/d404b-hii31` (40:02). Tools, all in `tools/d405_damp/`:
`readdamp.py` (the logs, per iteration), `cvdamp.py` (the integrated
quantities of `convergence.out`), `cmpdamp.py` (the two written models cell
by cell), `cmplines.py` (the lines), `emdamp.py` (what the last solve emits
against what the written model emits).

**1. No branch cycle.** Cells that start an iteration cold and end it above
3,000 K: none or one per iteration in either arm, from the fourth iteration
to the last. Cells above 3,000 K at the end: 183 damped, 182 undamped.
D-173's 44-76% is not there with the damping off.

**2. The floor is noise, of the size independent noise predicts.**

| iterations 10-15 | damped | undamped | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| step of x(H0), median | 2.35-2.51% | 3.28-3.44% | 1.39 |
| step of x(H0), 90th percentile | 29-30% | 41-42% | 1.39 |
| step of the molecular fraction, 90th percentile | 0.024-0.030 | 0.033-0.035 | 1.3 |
| chemistry's H2 moved by more than 1%, share of cells | 32.2-33.9% | 31.8-32.7% | |
| chemistry's CO moved by more than 1% | 97.0-98.8% | 97.2-97.6% | |

(The first three are steps of the written model; the last two set the
chemistry's new answer against the stored state, which the damping changes
by less: sqrt(2/1.6) = 1.12 in size, invisible in a share of cells.) The
prediction for independent noise was 1.49 and "not several times".

A second measure needs no second run. The fixture is an octant on a cubic
grid with equal axes, so the cells (i,j,k), (j,i,k), ... are one cell of
the model, and their spread inside a run is that run's own Monte Carlo
noise in the written model. `cmpdamp.py` takes the 2,784 sets of three or
six such cells (15,187 of the 15,204 active cells). Standard deviation of
ln q inside a set, median over the sets of a band of A_V, undamped over
damped:

| A_V | T | H2 | H | C | CO | OH | n_e |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.46-1.00 | 1.33 | 1.24 | (0.95) | 1.21 | 1.18 | 1.35 | 0.99 |
| 1.00-1.48 | 1.37 | 1.24 | 1.28 | 1.28 | 1.28 | 1.30 | 1.04 |
| 1.48-1.91 | 1.31 | 1.30 | 1.28 | 1.31 | 1.26 | 1.23 | 1.00 |
| 1.91-2.29 | 1.27 | 1.05 | 1.11 | 1.35 | 1.34 | 1.25 | 1.00 |
| 2.29-2.65 | 1.17 | 1.17 | 1.16 | (0.10) | 1.23 | 1.15 | 0.84 |
| 2.65-2.99 | 1.20 | 1.21 | 1.21 | 1.15 | 1.30 | 1.28 | 0.96 |

(Table regenerated 2026-10-13 16:55 from `cmpdamp.py` as committed; the
first version, from the script before it was made a function, differed by
0.01-0.02 in nine entries.)

The prediction for independent noise through the blend is 1.29. The
electron density is the control: it is the one quantity the damping never
touched, and its noise is the same in the two arms. (H in the first band
is 99.99% of the hydrogen and has nothing to scatter.) Two cautions. The
ray directions of the column integration are not symmetric under the
permutations, so part of a set's spread is the same in both arms and
pulls a ratio towards 1; and the two arms share a seed, so their noise
need not be independent of each other. Neither changes the reading.

The size of that noise is worth having on record, damped arm, standard
deviation of ln q among cells that are the same cell: T 0.5% at A_V
0.46-1.00, 3.7% at 1.48-1.91, 12% at 1.91-2.29 and 11% at 2.29-2.65;
x(H) 22% and x(C) 28% at 1.48-1.91; x(C) 97% and x(CO) 58% at
1.91-2.29, where carbon turns from C+ to C.

The one place the ratio is far from 1.29 is C (0.10) and C+ (0.15) at A_V
2.29-2.65, just behind that turn: the damped arm's spread of x(C+) inside
a set is 34%, the undamped arm's 5%. There the written carbon stages of
the damped arm are noisier than the solve, not quieter. Not looked into
further; L-49 had the mechanism (a quarter of the previous state is most
of the new one wherever a stage follows a rate that changes by a large
factor).

**What is not yet read from the logs.** The share of cells whose molecular
fraction moves by more than 0.5 in one iteration is 0.41-0.47% undamped
(60-70 cells, steady from the eighth iteration on) against 0.03-0.05%
damped. The two are not the same test, since a damped step is 0.75 of the
solve's and a solve alternating between 0.9 and 0.2 writes steps of 0.42.
Sixty cells are about a sixth of a one-cell shell at the H/H2 crossing.
Whether they are the same cells going back and forth (a cycle of period
two in the front cells, which a negative feedback through the one
iteration between the temperature solve and the chemistry could give) or
different cells each time (a front sharper than a cell, moved by the
field's noise) the logs cannot say. Cell histories can: MOCASSIN rewrites
`grid1.out` and `pdrGrid.out` at the end of every iteration, and
`tools/d405_damp/snap.py` copies T, n_e and ten abundances of every
active cell to `<run>/hist/itNN.npz` each time, reading only. It is
running on pn150k's undamped arm from its third iteration.

fifteenth.**

| 8 | 54.9% | 29.9% | 47.5% | 63.0% | 72.0% | 76.2% |
| 9 | 42.6% | 10.5% | 62.4% | 65.0% | 74.2% | 78.9% |

The 2% stop falls at the fifteenth iteration in both arms (the undamped
arm misses the fourteenth by 0.002 of a percentage point). What the test
is reading at the end is not the PDR: the largest change is in Ne+, O+
or N+, the ionized gas, whose emission measures are still falling in
both arms. `convergence.out`, the hydrogen emission measure, change per
iteration from the twelfth to the fifteenth: damped -0.55, -0.46, -0.32,
-0.24%; undamped -0.38, -0.33, -0.20, -0.14%. Successive steps are in
the ratio 0.72 without the damping and 0.76 with it (a relaxation of
ratio q becomes q + 0.25(1 - q) under the blend: 0.72 -> 0.79). The
damped arm ends where the undamped arm was at iteration 12.1, and the
undamped arm is ahead at every iteration and in every ion: at the last,
EM(H+) -0.62%, He+ -0.86%, N+ -1.06%, O+ -1.28%, Ne+ -1.09%, S2+
-1.35%, S+ +1.76%. The gap closes as both go on (H+: -2.46% at the
sixth iteration). Carried on as geometric series the two arms have
-0.77% and -0.36% still to go and end 0.2% apart - one limit, to the
accuracy of that. **By that extrapolation (it is not a measurement)
neither arm's hydrogen emission measure, and so its Hbeta, is within 0.3%
of its limit when the 2% test stops it, and the damped arm's is 0.8% from
it.**
Why the ionized gas of a model like this relaxes with a ratio of 0.7
per iteration is not known; it is not the damping.

In the neutral gas the undamped arm is on its floor by the seventh
iteration (step sizes, the chemistry's H2) and the damped arm by the
tenth. The count of converged neutral cells is lower without the damping
(65% against 69%) because the step it tests is not shrunk by a quarter.
Contents at the last iteration, undamped over damped: n(H0) -0.29%,
n(H2) +0.06%, T(H2) -0.13%.

**4. The damping is what derails the first PDR iterations on the h2-model
branch.** D-404 left open "hiipdr's jump at iteration 7", after two
iterations in which most cells did not reach their temperature balance.
Share of cells in which the balance is not reached, iterations 4, 5, 6,
7: damped 13, 89, 79, 0%; undamped 14, 0, 0, 0%. Neutral cells with
hydrogen's first solve more than 10% from the chemistry's at iteration
7: damped 86.2%, undamped 31.4%. The run that removes only the damping
removes both. What the budget lines show (`[D217]`, cells that stay
cold): the damped arm enters the first PDR iteration at a mean 554 K -
the memory of `TeStart` 8000 K, a quarter at a time - where the undamped
arm enters at 15 K; both solve to 15 K; the damped arm then writes 157 K
and enters the next iteration there, with the gas now molecular. The
level model (H-013) computes H2's heating at that temperature - line
cooling, since the gas is far warmer than the levels - and the term is
held fixed through the temperature search: -1.7e-24 erg/s per H at
iteration 5 and -1.8e-26 at 6, against +1.9e-27 and +1.8e-27 without
the damping. No temperature balances that, the search ends at 5.9 K and
9.4 K, and the blend walks down 157 -> 47 -> 19 K before the term comes
right. Production, which has no level model in its heating, does not
have these two iterations: `runs/d391-new-hii31` has the balance
unreached in 55, 54 and 43% of cells at iterations 2-4 and in none from
the fifth on. (That the term is the level model's is read from the
budget lines and the code, not from a run with the term taken out.)

other bands the medians of C are within 7%. A running arithmetic mean of

lies above its median, as the mean of a log-normal does. The published

     oxygen 9.9%).
  5. The delay grows with the steps, hydrogen to 35-45%: **wrong** (28.4

     H2 within 3%: met. CO within 20%: met for what it is worth (6-5
     -17 +- 10%). Crossing within 0.01 mag: met (0.0008).

### What the damping was hiding at the carbon turn (hiipdr)

Drawn for the page's figure (C+ and C against A_V, both arms, with the
spread of the cells of each bin), the undamped arm's carbon is not a
profile with scatter: it is two states. Cells of each 0.1 mag bin by
C+ / (C+ + C + CO), last iteration:

| A_V | cells | undamped: below 0.18 | 0.18-0.9 | above 0.9 | damped: below 0.18 | 0.18-0.9 | above 0.9 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.9-2.0 | 669 | 24 | 25 | 620 | 0 | 66 | 603 |
| 2.0-2.1 | 763 | 74 | 67 | 622 | 3 | 187 | 573 |
| 2.1-2.2 | 828 | 209 | 128 | 491 | 29 | 424 | 375 |
| 2.2-2.3 | 859 | 400 | 122 | 337 | 113 | 566 | 180 |
| 2.3-2.4 | 978 | 687 | 111 | 180 | 363 | 559 | 56 |
| 2.4-2.5 | 1,033 | 887 | 71 | 75 | 681 | 338 | 14 |
| 2.5-2.6 | 1,068 | 1,006 | 33 | 29 | 891 | 174 | 3 |

Without the damping 85-97% of the cells of every bin are in one of two
states: carbon ionized (above 0.9), or the deep state, in which C+ sits at
3.6e-5 per hydrogen (0.16 of the carbon) from A_V 2.3 to the edge, the same
in every cell. The two coexist over 0.7 mag, six or seven cells in depth.
With the damping a half to two thirds of the cells of the three middle
bins (51, 66 and 57% at A_V 2.1-2.4) are written between the two, at
values no solve gave. (Corrected 2026-10-13: "two thirds of the cells of
the middle bins" held for one bin of the three.) That is where the damped arm's
excess [C I] comes from (neutral carbon held at a blended temperature), why
the median of n(C) is 1.9 times higher there, and what the peak of the
spread among equivalent cells at A_V 2.2-2.3 is (x(C) by a factor e^1.3,
n_e by e^0.5, T by 20%).

**The reading, which the log already half holds.** A cell whose carbon is
ionized is a cell that a packet of the carbon-ionizing band (11.26-13.6 eV)
crossed in that iteration; a cell in the deep state is one that none
crossed, where cosmic rays alone keep the C+. One crossing is far more than
enough: a packet of 6e6 carries L/6e6, and its path through a 2e18 cm cell
gives a photoionization rate of order 1e-10 s^-1 per carbon atom, against
a recombination rate alpha n_e of 1e-12 to 5e-12 s^-1 (an estimate from the
fixture's numbers, not read from the code's rates). So the per-cell field
in that band is not noisy around its mean at this depth, it is on or off,
and the share of cells in the deep state is the share that drew no packet:
if crossings are Poisson, 47% at A_V 2.2-2.3 is a mean of 0.76 crossings
per cell and iteration, and 3.6, 9.7, 25, 47, 70, 86, 94% down the table
are means of 3.3, 2.3, 1.4, 0.76, 0.35, 0.15, 0.06. The model's "C+ = C"
is then where half the cells are missed, and not where the mean
photoionization balances recombination, which at one hundredth of a
crossing would still hold. D-237 and D-241 found the one-packet floor in
the deep field, D-261 put C+'s cliff down to it ("exactly zero C I-ionizing
flux below one packet per bin... not re-measured"), D-365 saw C+ = C go
from A_V 2.26 to 2.72 (Cloudy 2.95) at 21 times the tracks per cell with
the resolution changed as well, and L-26 lists the remedies. What this run
adds is the two states themselves, counted.

**What it means for the damping.** The damping averages the *answers* of
successive iterations. Where the answer is a strongly non-linear function
of a field that is on or off, the average of the answers is not the answer
to the average field: it keeps the bias (carbon neutral in every cell-
iteration that drew no packet) and writes states that are no solution. An
average of the *field* over iterations would be the estimator the physics
wants - J is linear in the packets, so its running mean is unbiased, and
the solve on it is a solve. That is L-26's first remedy; it is a design
decision and nothing of it is coded here.

excess of cells with a cycle's signature. (The ionized cells have R
1.3-1.7 and c -0.07 to -0.32: noise on a drift, the relaxation of point 4.
The electron density of the neutral gas has R 1.1-1.5: its noise is 0.4%,
and a slow change shows under it.)

The molecular fraction's large steps, iterations 11-18:

  - above 0.5: 2, 5, 4, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2 cells per iteration, 15 steps in 8
    cells at A_V 0.53-0.65. Seven of the eight cells have exactly two such
    steps, one down and one back (median 0.94 -> 0.35 -> 0.94): one

  - above 0.25: 7-13 per iteration, 77 steps in 49 cells; 21 cells with
