## D-412 - What H-034's line maps found in the production model (2026-10-15)

The user asked for emission-line maps of H2 and CO, to start scientific
tests (D-411). The tool and its checks are in DEVLOG-H2's H-034. The maps
come from h2-model runs, whose photoionization and chemistry are this
branch's. Two of the findings belong to the production model, so they are
recorded here.

### The test

In an octant on a cubic grid, these pairs of map columns cross cells at the
same set of radii:
  - columns (a,b) and (b,a);
  - column (n,0) and column (a,b), when a^2 + b^2 = n^2.

So a spherically symmetric model gives each pair equal intensity, exactly.
Cells can be compared the same way, by the sets of indices with one
i^2 + j^2 + k^2.

The H2 maps pass. They show no orientation: the light-weighted ratios of
swapped columns are 0.993-1.016 at 1x and 0.996-1.000 at 64x, in all three
projections, the z axis's included. The pairs' scatter falls as the
packets' noise: H2 1-0 S(1) +-11-13% at 1x, +-1.4-2.7% at 64x. Two things
do not fall.

### 1. hiipdr's ionization front, by orientation

  - **In the maps:** at p = 3.2 pc, H2 1-0 S(1)'s axis columns are
    0.886-0.898 of the off-axis ones at 64x, in all six axis directions
    (0.86-0.97 at 1x).
  - **In the cells:** the spread of ln x(H0) across inequivalent index sets
    at exactly one radius:

| run | 0.50-0.80 r_front | 0.80-0.95 | 0.95-1.10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| hiipdr 31^3, 1x | 0.062 | 0.292 | 0.186 |
| hiipdr 31^3, 64x | 0.061 | 0.291 | 0.189 |
| hiipdr 31^3, 48 directions | 0.062 | 0.291 | 0.185 |
| hiipdr 41^3 (h007-full-hii41) | 0.073 | 0.282 | 0.187 |
| pn150k 41^3, 1x / 4x | 0.005 / 0.004 | 0.011 / 0.011 | 0.016 / 0.015 |

  - **Per pair:** at 2.7-4.0 pc x(H0) differs by 0.45-1.33x and chiFUV by
    0.92-1.17x. The sign changes from one radius to the next: (2,2,3) is more
    neutral than (0,1,4), while (0,0,5) is more neutral than (0,3,4).
  - **Not the packets, the ray set or the planes.** Two interior sets differ
    as much as a plane set and an interior set do (chiFUV 1.11 at
    r^2 = 41). A first reading was that the symmetry-plane cells are more
    ionized at the same radius. It came from comparing their medians with the
    interior's interpolated profile, and that comparison moved from 0.82 to
    0.59 at 3.0-3.5 pc when only the profile's bin edges changed. It was
    withdrawn.
  - **The front is unresolved.** x(H0) goes from 0.05 to 0.8 within 0.64
    cells at 31^3 and within 0.67 cells at 41^3 (0.415 and 0.325 pc), so
    the front narrows with the cell. pn150k's front spans 1.54 cells.
  - **Reading, not tested:**
      - Cells whose centres sit at the same radius straddle an unresolved
        front differently by orientation. A cube spans +-0.5 cell in radius
        along an axis and +-0.87 along the body diagonal.
      - That would not shrink while the front stays narrower than a cell,
        which it does at both resolutions.
      - It does not account for pn150k's spread being 20x smaller, where a
        front 2.4x gentler per cell gives about 2.4x. So the reading is
        incomplete.
  - **What it costs:** pixels near the front in a map of a line made there,
    by ~10%, deterministically. The cells of the symmetry planes hold 35% of
    the volume inside hiipdr's front at 31^3 (7.3% of the sphere), and the
    axis columns are made of them. What it does to totals is not measured.
    The radial means average it.

### 2. hiipdr's outer CO, per cell

CO 1-0's per-cell emissivity about its radial profile (rms of ln):

| shell [pc] | 1x | 16x | 64x |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10-12 | 0.29 | 0.09 | 0.09 |
| 12-14 | 0.71 | 0.16 | 0.09 |
| 14-16 | 0.86 | 0.27 | 0.16 |
| 16-18 | 0.48 | 0.55 | 0.45 |
| 18-19.4 | 0.32 | 0.60 | 0.60 |

  - **Inside 16 pc it falls with the packets. Beyond 16 pc it does not.**
  - **Little of it repeats cell by cell.** The residuals correlate 0.18
    between 16x and 64x at 17-19.4 pc, against 0.52 at 10-14 pc.
  - **It is the abundance.** 92-106% of the variance is x(CO)'s. The escape
    probability carries 0.4-1% rms and the excitation 1-19%. The cell's T
    and chiFUV do not follow it (|r| <= 0.42 and <= 0.29).
  - **The outer carbon moves with the packets** (D-408): C+/C is 0.2 at
    16-18 pc at 1x and 4.0 at 64x.
  - **In the maps** it gives CO 1-0 +-17% per pixel pair at 64x. pn150k's CO
    is the packets' noise: +-15% at 1x, +-7-8% at 4x.
  - **CO is a trace at the grid's edge in both fixtures.** CO/(C+ + C + CO)
    is 4-9e-4 on hiipdr at 16-19.4 pc and 1-2e-5 on pn150k at
    0.50-0.62 pc. CO's emissivity peaks in the outermost shell, so a CO
    map's brightness and ring radius follow the boundary.

### Not yet known

  - What sets the front's direction spread, and why pn150k has 20x less.
    A test would be hiipdr at a resolution where the front spans several
    cells, which is past what 14 ranks can hold.
  - What sets the outer CO's per-cell scatter. Untested candidates: the
    outer chemistry's state at the iteration a run stops, and the deep field
    at the CO-forming wavelengths.

Status: Recorded. No code changed. The packet item in doc/pdr-status.md's
open list carries the CO point.

## D-413 - Five-column Q dust files and D-313's column test (2026-10-15)

Found while test-running the manual of DEVLOG-H2's H-035 (the user asked for
a manual to run a PDR + H2 model from the test_Problem benchmark). The run
stopped at start-up:

    At line 1342 of file source/ph_mod.f90 (unit = 20, file = '.../dustData/PAHneu_30.cat')
    Fortran runtime error: End of file

### Cause

D-313 added an optional sixth column to Q files, Im(m), so that a Q species
can have a photoelectric yield. Its test read six values list-directed, took
`ios == 0` as "six columns", and backspaced one record. A list-directed read
does not fail on a five-column record: it takes the sixth value from the next
one. Measured with a three-line file: `ios = 0`, values 1-6, and after one
backspace the file is at the second record.

So every five-column file was taken as six-column. The first record was
lost, and the reads ran off the end. PAHneu_30.cat has 36,030 five-column
records (30 radii x 1,201 wavelengths).

All four of Draine's Q files in dustData have five columns: PAHneu_30.cat,
Car_90.cat, Sil_21.cat and suvSil_81.cat. Only grph-avg.cat, written for
D-313 by tools/mkqfile.py with the sixth column, read right, and it is the
one the pn150k fixture uses. No PDR fixture uses a five-column Q file, which
is why this went unseen. A file could have been misread silently rather than
crash only if enough records followed its table; none here does.

### Fix

The first data record is read as text and its columns counted (blank, comma
or tab separated). `lgHaveK` is true at six or more. Each Q file now gets
one line in the log:

    ! makeDustXsec [D-413] dustData/grph-avg.cat:   35 radii x    900 wavelengths,  6 columns

### Verified

  - All four flavours compile.
  - **pn150k's fixture input** (3D PDR binary, 2 ranks): grph-avg.cat is
    read as 35 x 900 with 6 columns, and the run goes on.
  - **test_Problem's dust**: PAHneu_30.cat is read as 30 x 1,201 with 5
    columns. The run then stops with D-313's own refusal: a Q file with no
    Im(m) column cannot give a photoelectric yield. The message says to add
    the column (tools/mkqfile.py) or use `noPhotoelectric`.

### What follows

test_Problem, the standard MOCASSIN test, does not run as committed in any
build. Its dust includes PAHneu_30.cat and photoelectric heating is on by
default, so D-313's refusal now applies, where before it crashed. To run it,
remove the PAH species, give it a six-column file, or set
`noPhotoelectric`. The benchmark is not changed here. H-035's manual says
so and drops the PAHs for a PDR run.

Status: Done.

## D-414 - The mean dust temperature over the bins that hold grains (2026-10-16)

The user, on the open question of DEVLOG-H2 H-035: "H2 formation average
only over bins that actually contain grains."

### What was wrong

getDustT (update_mod.f90) builds two means:
  - Tdust(nS,0) = sum T(nS,a) grainWeight(a), over the bins within species
    nS's size range;
  - Tdust(0,0) = sum over species of Tdust(nS,0) grainAbun(nS).

grainWeight is normalised over the whole size grid. A species that covers
part of the grid therefore put the weight of every bin outside its range in
at T = 0. This is the trap benchmarks/pdr/README.md records (D-073, D-092).

H-035 measured it. test_Problem's silicates alone, 0.07-50 um on a
1e-4 - 5 um grid, came out at 2.0-8.0e-6 K in every cell. The bridge
passes Tdust(0,0) to H2 formation, so no cell formed H2 on grains, and the
shell stayed atomic: x(H2) <= 2e-7.

### The fix

  - **Each species' mean is renormalised over its own bins.** The factor is
    fIn, the share of the grid's weight in those bins.
  - **Tdust(0,0) weights each species by the grains it has:**
    grainAbun x fIn. The result is a number-weighted mean over the grains
    present. The weighting itself is unchanged.
  - **It is written as ratios to the grid's weight**, summed in the same
    loop order. A species that fills the grid gets fIn = x/x = 1 exactly,
    and the mixture's factor is exactly 1.

Every consumer reads the corrected mean:
  - the chemistry's dust temperature (pdr_mod, with its CMB floor);
  - the level model's H2 formation;
  - the H2 seeding;
  - the dust-only convergence test;
  - pdrRad.out's T_dust column.

The temperature per bin, which the dust emission uses, is not touched.

### Verified

  - **All four flavours compile.**
  - **Exact where nothing should change.** Variant c of H-035 (graphite,
    whose grid spans exactly its range) ran for 5 iterations at seed 1001
    on 14 ranks, with the binary before (4551160) and after. 21 of 22
    output files are byte-identical. summary.out differs only in its
    "finished at" times.
  - **Where it should change** (DEVLOG-H2 H-036): test_Problem's
    silicates alone now sit at 39.5-155 K and form H2 on grains in every
    cell, where none did. The original astrosilicate + PAH mixture runs at
    97-423 K. Its shell stays atomic (x(H2) <= 4e-7) because its grains
    carry 3.4e-23 cm^2 per H, a fiftieth of interstellar. That is the
    dust's limit, not the mean's.

### Not changed, for the record

H2 formation uses one T_dust for both of its channels, silicate and carbon.
In a mixture of two materials, a temperature per material, each a mean over
its own grains' area, would follow the physics more closely. Not done; the
user's decision was the occupied-bins mean. (Registered for future
development by the user on 2026-10-16: D-417.)

Status: Done.

## D-415 - Im(m) for a PAH Q file, from graphite as WD01 take it (2026-10-16)

The user: "How can we obtain the necessary constants for PAH? The code
should be able to run with the astrosilicate plus PAH mixture as in the
original test problem."

### What is needed, and why there are no PAH constants

D-313's photoelectric yield is WD01's. Its size effect y1 (WD01 eq. 13)
needs the photon attenuation length, l_a = lambda/(4 pi Im(m)) (eq. 14). A
Q file tabulates Qabs, Qsca and g with no optical constants, so D-313
refuses one without a sixth column, Im(m).

PAHs have no measured dielectric function. Li & Draine (2001) build PAH
cross sections from Drude profiles and a continuum, not from n and k. WD01
say so and use graphite (p. 8, read in the arXiv text, astro-ph/9907251v4):

    1/l_a = (4 pi / lambda) [ 2/3 Im(m_perp) + 1/3 Im(m_par) ]      (eq. 15)

They take it "from Draine & Lee (1984) and Laor & Draine (1993)", and: "Since
PAH dielectric functions are not available, we use graphite dielectric
functions for all carbonaceous grains."

### What was done

  - **tools/qfile_addk.py** appends Im(m) to a five-column Q file, from n,k
    files with weights.
      - It reads the header as MOCASSIN does.
      - It keeps every data record's five columns verbatim.
      - It adds a header comment saying where the sixth column came from.
      - It refuses a file whose records do not have exactly five columns.
  - **dustData/PAHneu_30.cat is rewritten in place** with
    dustData/grph2-dl.nk (E perpendicular to the c axis, 2/3) and
    grph1-dl.nk (parallel, 1/3).
      - These are the weights and the files of tools/mkqfile.py's
        grph-avg.cat. Which axis is which was checked from k itself:
        grph2-dl has n = 25.6, k = 10.0 at 100 um, the basal plane's
        metallic response; grph1-dl has k = 0.07 at 1 um.
      - The two n,k files share the PAH file's 1,201 wavelengths.
      - Checked: 36,030 records with five columns verbatim; Im(m) the same
        in all 30 radius blocks; within 3.5e-4 of grph-avg.cat's column at
        the wavelengths the two share.
      - Im(m) is 1.38 at 0.1 um, 0.82 at 0.2 um, 1.31 at 1 um and 7.6 at
        100 um.
  - **The PAH species is carbonaceous for the yield**, from its MsurfAtom of
    12.004: W = 4.4 eV, WD01 eq. 16. It is also carbonaceous for H2
    formation (its label contains "pah").

### What it rests on

The yield of a grain much smaller than l_a is insensitive to l_a's exact
value. For a = 5 A, l_e = 10 A and l_a ~ 100 A, y1 is about 10 and
y0 y1 >= 1, so WD01's min(y0 y1, 1) caps it. The graphite choice is WD01's
convention, which they state, not a fit.

The other Draine Q files in dustData (Car_90, Sil_21, suvSil_81) still have
five columns. The carbon one could take the same graphite column; the
silicates would need astrosilicate's. Not done.

Status: Done. The test of the original test_Problem mixture is in
DEVLOG-H2 H-036.

## D-416 - A long PREFIX truncates the atomic-data paths (2026-10-16)

Found while testing H-036's install into a scratch prefix of 116
characters. Every worker rank died at start-up with SIGSEGV; rank 0 went
on. Two runs of one minute separated the causes:
  - the previous binary at 7 ranks runs;
  - the new one crashes at 14 ranks as well.
Rebuilt with a 46-character prefix, the same code runs.

The cause is in makeElements (hydro_mod.f90). `filename` is
`character(len=128)` and is assigned trim(PREFIX)//'/share/mocassin/'//
dataFile(elem,ion). The assignment truncates, `inquire(..., exist=)` returns
false, and the ion's atomic data are skipped with no message. What the
workers then read uninitialised is not traced.

Every other path built from PREFIX goes straight into an `open`, or is held
in 200 or 300 characters (pdr_mod's dataDir, h2Dir).

Recorded, not changed. A 512-character `filename`, and a message when a
listed data file is missing, would fix it. Until then the manual says to
keep PREFIX under about 90 characters.

Status: Open.

## D-417 - A dust temperature per grain material for H2 formation, registered for future development (2026-10-16)

The user: "log the Dust temperature per material idea for future
implementation."

Registered, not started; no code changed. It was D-414's "not changed, for
the record" and the first open item of DEVLOG-H2 H-036.

### What the code does now

H2_FORMATION_RATE (source/pdr/h2_form.F90, -DH2FORM_CT02) sums two
channels:

    R = 1/2 v_th(T_gas) [ sigma_sil eps_sil(T_d) + sigma_gra eps_gra(T_d) ] S(T_gas, T_d)

  - sigma_sil and sigma_gra are this cell's grain area per H by material,
    measured by measureH2grainArea and classed by isCarbonGrain (D-195).
  - One temperature, T_d, enters both efficiencies and the sticking
    coefficient.

T_d is Tdust(0,0), getDustT's number-weighted mean over every species
(D-414). It reaches H2 formation at three places:
  - the chemistry: pdrStep, pdr_mod.f90:3323 (with the CMB floor), then
    CALCULATE_REACTION_RATES;
  - the H2 seeding: seedMolecules, pdr_mod.f90:2918;
  - on h2-model, the level model's formation (h2LevelModel's solveCell,
    pdr_mod.f90:5842-5851 there). It already evaluates the two surfaces
    apart, wSil and wGra, but both at the one T_d.

The gas-grain energy exchange is not among them: MOCASSIN's own term runs
per species and size (gasDustColl_d; L-9).

### Why it matters in a mixture

Number weighting hands the mean to the smallest grains. In test_Problem
(DEVLOG-H2 H-036):
  - The size grid runs from 1e-4 to 5 um, MRN-like (slope -3.54).
  - The silicates' bins (0.08-5 um) hold 6.9e-11 of the grid's weight. The
    PAHs' bins (1e-4 - 1.75e-3 um) hold all of it, to that precision.
  - With grainAbun 0.98 and 0.02, the silicates carry 6.8e-11 of
    Tdust(0,0)'s weight and the PAHs 0.02.
  - So Tdust(0,0) is the PAHs' temperature: 143.5 K, the median over the
    384 dense neutral cells. The same cells in the silicates-alone run sit
    at 57.7 K.

CT02's efficiencies, with 3D-PDR's surface energies and FLUX = 1e-10
monolayers per second:

| T_d [K] | 40 | 58 | 100 | 143.5 | 200 | 300 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| silicate | 0.368 | 0.198 | 0.100 | 0.074 | 0.061 | 0.051 |
| carbonaceous | 0.974 | 0.833 | 0.432 | 0.257 | 0.172 | 0.118 |

### What it would change, from the formula (not a run)

Taken in tp-orig's 384 dense neutral cells (n_H = 8e4, x(H) > 0.5 in both
runs), at each cell's own T_gas:
  - the silicate channel at the silicates-alone run's T_d of the same cell,
    its sticking coefficient included;
  - the PAH channel at Tdust(0,0), as now.

The result:
  - **R_form rises by a median factor of 1.68** (5-95%: 1.35-1.73).
  - **The silicate share of the formation rises from 35% to 60%.**
  - **x(H2) would rise from ~5e-8 to ~8e-8**, since nothing self-shields
    there and x(H2) follows R_form. The shell stays atomic: its limit is
    the grain area (H-036).

Two caveats:
  - tp-sil's T_d is itself a number-weighted mean, so its smallest
    silicates set it. An area-weighted mean would be colder, which gives a
    higher silicate efficiency.
  - The silicates' temperature is borrowed from another run, not computed
    in tp-orig. The two runs' fields are close (A_V 0.72 and 0.71 in these
    cells), not equal.

### Three designs

  - **(a) One temperature per material, number-weighted as now.** A
    single-material model gets today's T_d exactly.
  - **(b) One temperature per material, weighted by grain area**, the
    weight the formation rate itself carries.
  - **(c) The rate summed over the size bins**, each bin at its own
    temperature and with its own sticking coefficient. CT02's efficiency
    is not linear in T, so the rate at a mean T is not the mean of the
    rates. Within CT02 this is the exact form.

(b) and (c) also change single-material models, hiipdr's silicate and
pn150k's graphite among them, because their T_d is number-weighted today.
By how much is not known: the per-bin temperatures are not written out.

### Where it would go

  - **h2_form.F90:** take the per-channel temperatures through
    GLOBAL_MODULE, as D-195 hands over the areas (h2form_xsec_sil and
    h2form_xsec_gra). A negative value keeps the argument, so a dust-free
    model is unchanged. Design (c) needs the bins' areas and temperatures
    instead.
  - **pdr_mod.f90:** set them per cell where the areas are set, in pdrStep
    (3286) and seedMolecules (2906). They come from grid%Tdust(nS,ai,cell),
    with isCarbonGrain deciding the material and the CMB floor applied per
    channel.
  - **h2-model's level model:** wSil and wGra, each at its own temperature.
  - pdrRad.out and the dust-only convergence test can keep the overall
    mean.

### The test

  - **Exactness first.** With (a), a single-species model at a fixed seed
    must be byte-identical before and after, as for D-414. H-035's variant
    c is that model.
  - **Then tp-orig** (runs/h036b-tp-orig's input on h2-model), against this
    entry's estimate. In the dense neutral cells: R_form 1.35-1.73 times
    today's, the silicate share near 60%, and x(H2) still under 1e-6.

Status: Deferred.

## D-418 - Levels listed out of energy order broke the collision rates, and below 13.96 K made NaN (2026-10-17)

Found by the NGC 7009 K1a model (Konstantinou et al. 2026, in
~/Documentos/NGC7009_K1a, run with the h2-model install). Its second run,
the star seen through the nebula's internal shell, crashed with SIGSEGV
in iteration 10. In iteration 9, five ambient cells (n_H = 100) straight
behind the knot had absorbed no ionizing photons (photo heating 1.7e-43
per H), and their T_e, cooling and grain charge were NaN.

The user asked: "can we just set a floor for Te? Maybe cosmic background?"
Neither one is the fix. The measurements below show why.

### Reproducing it

The reproduction is runs/starve-test in the K1a folder: the knot's
abundances and dust, the PDR from iteration 2, n_H = 100 on an 11^3 grid,
and LStar 1e-9, so that every cell gets almost no radiation.
  - **a** (default teFloor = T_CMB) and **b** (teFloor 10.) both crash
    (rc=139) with identical counts: 318,500 "Singular matrix in
    GAUSS_JORDAN", 15,825 CVODE failures, 7 [D120] non-finite dust
    integrals, 633 NaN cells in grid1.out.
  - The first printed symptom, "getGrainRecombination: insane eta NaN",
    is not the first NaN. A copy built with -ffpe-trap=invalid stops first
    at two NaNs that are already caught:
    - forLines' ionDenUp = 0/0, which equilibrium tests for, so the ion's
      lines are set to 0;
    - setResLineEscapeProb's (1-exp(-2 tau))/(2 tau) at tau = 0, which
      fails the "> 0" test, so fEscape is set to 0.
    Past those, the trap lands in lured (the level-population LU) inside
    thermBalance.
  - Prints in the debug copy put the first non-finite quantity at
    **trial step 35 of iterateT, T_e = 12.19 K**: coolColl is NaN; coolFF,
    coolRec, gasDust and pdrCoolMol are finite. The NaN is in the
    forbidden lines of **Ni II alone**, and in its level matrix the
    diagonal of level 2 is -Infinity.

### The cause

niII.dat, from CHIANTI 10.1 (Bautista 2004), orders its levels by
configuration, not by energy:

    1  3d9 2D5/2          0.0 cm-1
    2  3d8(3F)4s 4F9/2 8393.9
    3  3d9 2D3/2       1506.9
    4  3d8(3F)4s 4F7/2 9330.0
    5  3d8(3F)4s 4F5/2 10115.7

equilibrium sets up qeff for every pair (i-1, j) with i-1 < j, giving
i-1 the Boltzmann factor exp((E(i-1)-E(j)) 1.4388/T) and g(i-1).
  - When E(i-1) > E(j), that exponent is positive: the "excitation" is
    really a de-excitation multiplied by exp(+dE/kT), and the "de-
    excitation" lacks its exp(-dE/kT).
  - Detailed balance is therefore reversed for the pair at EVERY
    temperature. For Ni II 2-3 (dE = 6887 cm-1 = 9909 K) the error is a
    factor 2.7 at 1e4 K.
  - Below 9909/709.78 = **13.96 K** the exponent overflows double
    precision, the diagonal x(2,2) = -Ne qeff(2,3) becomes -Infinity, and
    the unpivoted LU returns NaN.
  - From there NaN spreads: coolColl, the residual and the next trial T_e,
    so ionBalance and setGrainPotential run at T = NaN ("insane eta"); then
    the chemistry ("Singular matrix", CVODE failures) and the
    grid; finally indices computed from NaN give out-of-range writes. That
    last step is the likely cause of the SIGSEGV, and it also broke the
    "insane eta" warning cap in a debug build, whose 13 GB log made
    prterun grow to 52 GB and get killed by the kernel OOM killer
    (2026-10-17 17:59).

teFloor 10 cannot help, since the overflow starts at 13.96 K. A floor of
14 K or more would hide it, but only by holding gas that is physically
colder (about 4 K in this test once fixed) at the floor: an artificial
gate. Cosmic-ray ionization and heating are already in MOCASSIN's own
balance (D-193, D-280). They are what set those cells at about 4 K, and
they cannot hold them above 14 K.

### Every file

A script reads each data file as hydro_mod.f90 does
(tools/level_order.py, run on the installed data directory; it
parses the iRats = 0 files). 31 files have at least one
pair out of energy order. The temperatures below which exp(+dE/kT) would
overflow are:

| file | pair | dE [cm-1] | overflow below |
|---|---|---|---|
| niII.dat | 2 > 3 | 6887.0 | 13.96 K |
| alviii.dat | 13 > 14 | 4459.4 | 9.04 K |
| cavii.dat | 16 > 17 | 2464.2 | 5.00 K |
| feiii.dat | 12 > 13 | 1218.0 | 2.47 K |
| neiv.dat | 6 > 8 | 938.0 | 1.90 K |
| the other 26 | | < 270 | < 0.62 K |

Only niII.dat matters for neutral gas above the CMB floor. All 31 had
their rates reversed for those pairs at every T, mostly over gaps of a few
to a few hundred cm-1, where exp(dE/kT) is close to 1 in ionized gas.

The A values of the inverted pairs are all zero except one: O II
2D5/2-2D3/2 (levels 2 and 3, 19.8 cm-1 apart, A = 1.32e-7 s-1). The code
treats level 3 as the upper one, so this transition gets a negative Eji
and a negative emissivity of about 1e-7 s-1 x 20 cm-1 per ion. Negligible,
and **not changed**.

### The change

emission_mod.f90, equilibrium. The Boltzmann factor and the statistical
weight of the excitation now go with the lower-ENERGY level of each pair.
For an ordered pair (dE <= 0) the arithmetic is unchanged. Nothing else
in the solve changes.

The chemistry's neutral-collider rates (pdrNeutralRates, D-363) loop over
the chemistry atom's own levels, which are energy-ordered, and are left as
they are.

### Test

The starvation test, with the fix applied in a scratch copy of the same
source (plus prints that stop the run at the first NaN):
  - it runs all 4 iterations, rc=0;
  - 0 NaN in grid1.out and pdrGrid.out (was 633 and 1270);
  - 0 "Singular matrix" (was 318,500) and 0 CVODE failures (was 15,825):
    all of them were consequences of the NaN;
  - 647 active cells at 3.8-45 K (median 3.9 K), with a median thermal
    residual of 0.6%.

Four flavours compile (3D, 1D, no PDR, Warm).

### Not yet known

  - **Attribution in the K1a run.** Its five cells had no ionizing
    heating, so they would have cooled toward a few K, through 14 K. That
    is consistent with this cause but not shown. The rerun of the filtered
    model is the test: it must pass iteration 9 with no NaN. (Answered
    below.)
  - **The size of the at-every-T change.** It is not measured. The pairs
    involved are mostly fine structure or close levels, so the expected
    effect on lines and cooling in ionized gas is small. The bare-star K1a
    model is rerun with the same binary so that the two K1a models stay
    comparable.
  - **Left as they are**, recorded:
    - lured/reslv have no pivoting and no zero-pivot guard;
    - the integrated stop test skips NaN totals silently (the
      `>= cvTotSig*cHtot` comparison is false for NaN);
    - the two caught 0/0s above turn into fLineEm = 0 and fEscape = 0
      rather than into the limits (no ion: no lines; tau = 0: escape = 1);
    - once a cell is NaN, out-of-range writes follow.

Status: Accepted.

### After the change (2026-10-17, evening)

Both K1a models were rerun with the fixed binary (DEVLOG-H2 H-040), each
at 14 ranks, seed 1001 and 10^9 packets, with nothing else changed.

  - **Filtered star** (runs/k1a-ps-filt, from 20:30). It passed iteration
    9, where the pre-fix run had produced its NaN cells, and every later
    iteration, with:
    - 0 "insane eta", 0 non-finite dust integrals, 0 "Singular matrix"
      (the pre-fix run had 33,475 in iteration 9 alone) and 0 CVODE
      failures;
    - convergence at iteration 15 (1.09%), rc=0, 0 flagged cells, the
      hydrogen budget closed to 6.0e-9.
    At iteration 12 the five former NaN cells sat at 6,900-8,750 K,
    partly ionized, and one cell of the grid was at 7.0 K, below the old
    overflow limit. The run differs from the crashed one only by the fix,
    so the crash is attributed to it.
  - **Bare star** (runs/k1a-ps, from 21:52). It converged at iteration 14
    as before (1.94%; 1.96% before). Against the pre-fix run
    (runs/k1a-ps_preD418):
    - every line in lineFlux.out within 0.1% (median 0.04%);
    - Hbeta +0.015%, H2 1-0 S(1) +0.04%;
    - n_e[S II] 6,378 -> 6,397;
    - the face cell's T_e 8,431 -> 8,424 K.
    In this model's ionized and warm gas the reversed rates changed the
    lines by less than 0.1%.

What is still not measured: the change in models whose gas spends time
below ~100 K with Ni II, Fe III or Ca VII populated. None of the
benchmarks has been rerun.

## D-419 - Code changes are planned at extra-high effort and implemented by a code-executor subagent at high effort (2026-10-19)

The user asked: "Define a reusable 'code-executor' subagent for this
project. The 'code-executor' should Follow the provided plan exactly. It
should not redesign. It should flag anything that blocks the plan. Create a
rule in our CLAUDE.md file that all code changes should be planned with
extra effort and the 'code-executor' implements the plan with high effort."

### What was added

  - **`.claude/agents/code-executor.md`**, a project subagent. This is the
    first file under `.claude/` in git: `.git/info/exclude` ignores only
    `.claude/worktrees/`. Its frontmatter:
    - `effort: high`;
    - `model: inherit` (the session's model);
    - tools Read, Edit, Write and Bash, plus Monitor for waits on long runs.
      It cannot spawn agents, publish artifacts or schedule anything.
    The frontmatter keys are the ones Claude Code 2.1.303 parses for agent
    definitions (name, description, tools, model, effort, ...; effort takes
    low, medium, high, max or an integer).
  - **The agent's instructions:**
    - Before the first edit, it reads the checkout's CLAUDE.md, checks the
      starting commit and a clean tree, and checks every file, routine,
      variable and quoted line the plan names against the code.
    - It does the steps in order, as written. It adds no steps, refactors
      or fixes outside the plan. It does not choose between alternatives
      the plan leaves open.
    - The only adaptation it may make is mechanical, such as a line number
      that has moved, and it must report it. Anything that changes what is
      computed, read or written beyond the plan is a redesign, and it flags
      it. A compile error in its own new code is part of the step.
    - **It stops and reports on:**
      - a false premise;
      - an ambiguous step or an open choice;
      - a step that breaks the rule that outranks the others: a hardcoded
        stand-in, an artificial gate, a second array for one quantity, or
        a fitted coefficient;
      - a failed build in any flavour;
      - a verification that disagrees with the plan's prediction. It must
        not tune, rerun until it passes, or edit the test.
      - a step reserved for the user: push, another repository, Cloudy,
        deleting runs, rebase or forced git, `make install` without the
        user's go-ahead quoted in the plan;
      - a run larger than the memory model allows.
    - It carries the standing rules:
      - all four flavours with `make clean` between them, plus h2Test,
        h2Slab and the PREFIX on h2-model;
      - the rc and time stamp of each build;
      - `-np 14` under `systemd-run --user`;
      - condition-loop waits;
      - `date` before any time is written;
      - awk's locale;
      - no push and no `rm -rf`;
      - commits and DEVLOG entries only where the plan puts them.
    - Its report gives:
      - the status;
      - each step as done, adapted or not done;
      - the diff stat and the commits;
      - each build's rc;
      - each verification with its output quoted, against the prediction;
      - each blocker with its evidence and the options, without choosing
        one;
      - what it noticed and did not act on.
  - **CLAUDE.md, new section "Code changes are planned, then executed"**
    (after Build). It covers `source/`, `source/pdr/`, the Makefile and
    `tools/`:
    - The main session plans in plan mode at `xhigh`. It holds the
      discussion and the DEVLOG history, and the user's settings
      (`modelSettings`, `effortLevel: xhigh`) already run it at `xhigh`.
    - A plan names, for every step:
      - the file and the routine;
      - the change;
      - the verification, with the prediction on record before any run.
    - The plan makes every choice.
    - The executor is handed the plan file's path, the checkout and branch,
      and the attribution lines.
    - A blocker goes back to planning at `xhigh`. Neither the executor nor
      the main session patches around it, and the blocker and its
      resolution are logged.
    - The main session reviews the report and the diff, checks the runs
      when they finish, and writes and commits the DEVLOG entry.

### Choices made here, open to the user

  - **"Extra effort" is read as the `xhigh` level** (extra high). That is
    one step above the executor's `high` and the level the user's settings
    already give the main session.
  - **Planning stays in the main session**, not in a Plan subagent. A
    subagent starts without the discussion and would have to re-derive it.
  - **The scope is the code that is built or that computes results.**
    These are outside it:
    - DEVLOG and documentation text;
    - run directories and their inputs;
    - the scratchpad's artifact page builders.

### What is not yet known

The agent has not been used on a change yet. A session started before the
file existed may not list it until it is restarted. The rule reaches
`h2-model` when production is merged in (DEVLOG-H2 H-041). No code changed,
so the four flavours were not rebuilt.

## D-420 - H2 becomes a collider in the gas-grain exchange (2026-10-19)

The user: "H2 probably isn't a collider in gas-grain heat exchange. This
is the most important new change we need. MOCASSIN's gas-grain term
(update_mod.f90) sums only over atoms and ions, and since D-220 those
exclude hydrogen locked in molecules. Meanwhile 3D-PDR's own gas-grain term
is switched off because MOCASSIN is supposed to supply it (D-131). So in a
molecular core almost nothing couples the gas to the dust. It fits the
cold-gas anomaly: shielded cores at 3.8 K and 6.6 K with dust at 16 K or
more. It needs a test run before it counts as established. Audit the
changes already logged and check if this is mentioned already, make a plan
for this fix and execute it."

This is the first change made under D-419's rule. The plan was made at
xhigh in plan mode and approved by the user; the code-executor implements
it. The plan file is ~/.claude/plans/iridescent-stirring-pie.md.

### The audit: it was already logged

  - **D-305 (2026-09-22), item (d)** found it. `gasDustColl_g` loops over
    the ionisation stages of the elements, so H2, 94% of hiipdr's gas at
    A_V 0.65, is not a collision partner. MOCASSIN's term there was
    2.88e-30 erg/s/H against Cloudy's dust cooling of 1.96e-28, 68x
    smaller. Both were negligible at n_H = 1e3, "decisive at high density".
  - **L-9** in doc/pdr-status.md records it. D-352 kept the grain side on
    the same MOCASSIN term, so H2 is omitted on both sides.
  - **D-333**, tier 3, item 9: "dense knots are out of scope until it is
    fixed".
  - update_mod.f90 (getDustT) says "(gasDustColl still omits H2: L-9.)",
    and D-417 cites L-9.
  - The NGC 7009 K1a report (~/Documentos/NGC7009_K1a/report/code_issues.md,
    item 2) lists it as NEW. The defect is not new. Its symptom is the new
    part: the first dense, shielded cores this project has run.

### The symptom

Both K1a runs used the h2-model install (bb4f9aa; the run copies'
md5 8bbe67d7 is the installed binary's), at 14 ranks and seed 1001. Both
stopped at the 30-iteration cap without converging (n(CO) 11.4% and Ar+
4.1% over the window). Cells with T_e < T_d - 3 K and x(H2) > 0.4:

| run | cells | n_H | T_e min / median | T_d median |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| k1a-flow-q-dust10 | 49 | 3.5e4 | 3.84 / 4.61 K | 20.40 K |
| k1a-flow-q-core3.5e5 | 62 | 3.5e5 | 6.55 / 9.19 K | 21.15 K |

The coldest dust10 cell (5082) is at 3.84 K with dust at 23.07 K,
x(H2) = 0.500, x(He) = 0.110 and x(H) = 1.4e-5. Its budget per H:
  - heating: PDR 7.01e-28 (cosmic rays and chemistry), gas-grain
    7.78e-29;
  - cooling: PDR 7.45e-28, collisional 3.2e-29.

### What the term does now, and the change

setDustGasCollHeatCool sums, for each neutral or ion and each grain size,
n_X <v> pi a^2 S (2kT xi - eta(...+2kT_d)), with BFM's accommodation
S = 2mM/(m+M)^2 for neutrals. Since D-220 the stages of hydrogen sum to
elemAvail(H), the part not in molecules, so the hydrogen in H2 never
strikes a grain. 3D-PDR's heat(11) is excluded from pdrHeatXtra because
MOCASSIN supplies the term (D-131).

The change adds H2 as a neutral: Z = 0, so eta = xi = 1 and no ionization
energy. Its mass is 2 aWeight(1), its accommodation is BFM's at that mass,
as Cloudy takes it (GrainCollHeating, grains.cpp), and n(H2) is
grid%H2den, the chemistry's, the one setLineColliders uses (D-363). It
goes on both sides, gasDustColl_d and gasDustColl_g, under #ifdef PDR.
The 4 pi that ends the routine still applies to it here (D-421 changes
that separately).

Per collider and n_H, x S / sqrt(m) is 0.0583 for H2 against 0.0152 for
He at M = 20.077 (astroSilD2003). In the cold cells H2 therefore adds 3.83
times the atomic coupling, x4.83 in all.

### Prediction, on record before the run (2026-10-19 11:15)

The test is runs/d420-k1a-dust10 on h2-model: the k1a-flow-q-dust10 input
plus `convTotals 1.e-6` (30 iterations, as the baseline ran; the keyword
only decides the stop), 14 ranks, seed 1001. It differs from the
baseline only by this change. A hiipdr 31^3 run (H-031's paired input)
goes with it as the baseline for D-421.

  - **Health:** rc=0, a clean exit, 0 NaN, 0 "Singular matrix", 0 CVODE
    failures and 0 flagged cells (the baseline has 0 of each).
  - **Coupling** (the code's term over the physical BFM rate with H2):
    - cold cells: 0.0175 -> 0.080-0.090;
    - atomic cells: 0.0865, unchanged within 0.002.
  - **Cold core:**
    - median T_e 4.61 -> 5.0-5.6 K;
    - the coldest cell 3.84 -> 4.3-4.9 K;
    - T_d unchanged within 0.2 K, x(H2) unchanged.
    The core stays more than 10 K below the dust: H2 alone does not
    explain the anomaly. These come from the cell's own budget, with
    cooling taken as T^1.4-3 (an estimate, not a run).
  - **Ionized gas:**
    - median T_e within 0.999-1.001;
    - Hbeta and the forbidden lines within 0.5%.
  - **The H2 lines:** within 2%.

### Results (2026-10-19, 12:39-12:50)

**What the code-executor did** (Part 1 of the plan, a general-purpose agent
following .claude/agents/code-executor.md at high effort, because this
session predates the agent file):
  - Every premise checked before the first edit. The change is ce32641
    (update_mod.f90 only, +47 -1), as the plan wrote it; the diff was read.
  - It was merged into h2-model as 1b5df3e. `--no-edit` gives git's default
    message without the attribution lines, as fa876a9 had.
  - Builds, rc=0 in all, error count 0:
    - production: the four flavours, 11:17:58-11:18:59;
    - h2-model: the four, then h2Test and h2Slab, by 11:20:57.
    The mocassin md5 is ac08827f, version pdr-coupling-v1.1-252-g1b5df3e,
    not -dirty. Nothing installed or pushed, and the K1a folder untouched.
  - Runs: queue launched 11:21:08, done 12:39:18. Run times ("total run
    time per processor"): d420-k1a-dust10 00:37:55, d420-hii31 00:40:13.
  - Two mechanical adaptations, reported:
    - the liveness check needs `pgrep -x mocassin.d420`, because the binary
      is named so;
    - `python3 -I` cannot import numpy here, so compare.py ran with
      `-P -E`, which computes the same.

**Against the prediction**, d420-k1a-dust10 against k1a-flow-q-dust10:

| item | predicted | measured | |
|---|---|---|---|
| health | rc 0, clean, 0 NaN / Singular / CVODE / insane eta / flagged | all 0, 30 iterations each | met |
| coupling, cold cells, /(atoms+H2) | 0.0175 -> 0.080-0.090 | 0.0175 -> 0.0849 | met |
| coupling, cold cells, /atoms | x4.83 | 0.0850 -> 0.4103 (x4.83) | met |
| coupling, atomic cells | 0.0865 within 0.002 | 0.0859 -> 0.0860 | met |
| cold core median T_e | 4.61 -> 5.0-5.6 K | 4.92 K | **missed** |
| coldest cell (5082) | 3.84 -> 4.3-4.9 K | 4.15 K | **missed** |
| T_d median, x(H2) median | 20.40 K within 0.2 K; 0.500 | 20.40 K; 0.500 | met |
| gas still > 10 K below the dust | yes | 4.15 K against 23.16 K | met |
| ionized gas T_e ratio | 0.999-1.001 | 1.0000 (16-84%: 0.9991-1.0008) | met |
| gas-grain share of the ionized gas's cooling | 3.6e-3 | 3.59e-3 -> 3.59e-3 | met |
| Hbeta and the forbidden lines | within 0.5% | Hbeta 0.9999; extremes He II 4686 0.9991, [S II] 1.0012 | met |
| H2 1-0 S(1), 2-1 S(1), 0-0 S(2) | within 2% | 0.9991, 0.9972, 1.0057 | met |
| H2 0-0 S(1), S(0) | within 2% | 1.0577, 1.0590 | **missed** |

d420-hii31: clean on every count (15 iterations, 0 flagged), gas-grain share
of the ionized gas's cooling 6.28e-3. It is D-421's baseline.

**The executor stopped on the three misses** as verification disagreements,
as its definition requires, and did not rerun. Neither is a defect in the
planned code, and the plan is not revised.

**(a) The cold core warmed less than predicted because its cooling is
steeper than the T^1.4-3 the estimate took.** The coldest cell's budget
per H [erg/s]:

| | T_e | gas-grain heating | PDR heating | PDR cooling | collisional |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 3.840 K | 7.78e-29 | 7.005e-28 | 7.445e-28 | 3.17e-29 |
| d420 | 4.151 K | 3.825e-28 | 7.013e-28 | 1.027e-27 | 5.01e-29 |

  - The gas-grain heating rose x4.92 as designed: x4.83 in the coupling,
    times the slightly larger T_d - T_e.
  - The total heating rose x1.39, and the cooling rose with it (x1.39) for
    T_e x1.081. The cooling's slope there is therefore 4.1-4.4.
  - The PDR cooling is CO's (8.8e-28 at the table point, against C 1.5e-29
    and O -4.9e-29 net). The balance reads it from D-215's per-cell table at
    the cell's T, so 4.1 is the slope of the cooling function the code
    solves.
  - The same budget estimate with s = 4.1 gives 4.17 K for the coldest cell
    and 4.91 K for the median, against 4.15 and 4.92 measured. With s = 3,
    the top of the range assumed, it gives 4.30 and 5.04 K, the bottom of
    the ranges predicted. So the miss is the slope assumed, not the
    coupling.
  - Not established: why the CO cooling is that steep near 4 K. CO's J = 1
    and J = 2 levels lie at 5.5 K and 16.6 K, and any background the escape
    probability includes would also steepen it.

**(b) The 6% in H2 0-0 S(1) and S(0) comes from two warm transition cells
whose chemistry moved, not from the new term.**
  - Rebuilt from output/h2Pop.bin, the cell volumes and n(H2):
    new/base is 1.0575 and 1.0589, as lineFluxH2.out gives.
  - Cells at 100-200 K give +5.5 of S(1)'s +5.8 points. Two cells give
    6.3 points, and the rest net -0.5:
    - (50,2,3), A_V 5.8: T_e 120 -> 150 K, +4.2 points;
    - (47,2,4): T_e 155 -> 165 K, +2.1 points.
  - In both the gas is warmer than the dust, so the new term *cools*. It
    is 0.1-0.2% of their heating: (50,2,3)'s gas-grain cooling went
    4.2e-27 -> 1.6e-26 against heating near 1.3e-23.
  - What moved is the chemistry. In (50,2,3) the PDR heating went 9.37e-24
    -> 1.83e-23, x(H) 0.287 -> 0.182 and x(CO) 9.1e-5 -> 2.4e-4.
  - Both runs stopped at the 30-iteration cap unconverged (n(CO) 11.4% over
    the window). The likely reading is that any change sends the
    unconverged H/H2 transition cells along another trajectory. That is a
    hypothesis: no run that removes only the change has been read.
    Consequence: K1a's H2 rotational lines carry at least 6% of trajectory
    scatter at this iteration count, and the 2% predicted was tighter than
    the model can hold. The vibrational lines (within 0.3%) come from other
    cells.

**A limit of compare.py's "atomic cells" ratio.** In those cells the
rebuilt BFM rate is mostly electrons: 82% of it in K1a, 95% in hiipdr. The
rebuild leaves out the grain charge (xi, eta) and the ions. That is why
hiipdr's 32 atomic cells give 0.258 against K1a's 0.086: they are partly
ionized cells (median x_e 4.4e-2, T_e 3900 K), and cell by cell the ratio
runs from 4.8 at x_e 2e-3 to 0.17 at x_e 9e-2. So only the cold-cell ratio,
which is all neutral collisions with xi = eta = 1, is a clean measure of
the normalisation. There it is 0.085 in K1a and 0.0948 in hiipdr, against
1/(4 pi) = 0.080.

**What it means.**
  - H2 is now a collider, at exactly the designed strength: x4.83 in the

## D-421 - The gas-grain term was divided by 4 pi in both balances it enters (2026-10-19)

Found while planning D-420, reading the end of setDustGasCollHeatCool:

    ! factor of fourpi to make up for the lack of fourpi
    ! in the balance eqns for J
    gasDustColl_d(:,:)= gasDustColl_d(:,:)/fourpi
    gasDustColl_g= gasDustColl_g/fourpi

Each sum is the physical exchange rate, n <v> pi a^2 S times the energy per
collision: per grain [erg/s] for _d, per H nucleus for _g. The two
balances they enter are in different units, and neither is "physical over
4 pi":
  - **The gas balance** (coolInt in thermBalance) is physical per H.
    photoelHeat_g carries no factor, and the PDR cooling enters as
    pdrCool/Hden: D-135 removed a 4 pi there on the measurement that
    coolColl is a physical cooling rate.
  - **The grain balance** in getDustT is physical divided by pi.
    radField = Jste/pi, Jste being the angle-integrated flux (D-290), is
    set against an emission integral of 4 C_abs B (dust_mod.f90), and
    photoelHeat_d is divided by pi.

So the gas term is 4 pi (12.6x) too weak, and the grain term 4x.

**Measured on k1a-flow-q-dust10** (thermBudget.out's gas-dust column
against BFM's rate rebuilt from the cell's own grain area per H, x(H),
x(He), n_e, T_e and the mean T_d):
  - 58 atomic cells (x(H) > 0.9, T_e > 3 T_d): 0.0865 (16-84%:
    0.060-0.148);
  - 49 cold molecular cells: 0.085;
  - against 1/(4 pi) = 0.080.
The rebuild ignores ions and the grain charge's xi and eta, and uses the
mean T_d. That probably explains why 0.085 rather than 0.080.

The same reading explains D-305's 68x against Cloudy: H2 (about 4x) times
4 pi, with the rest within the two codes' different temperatures.

**The change.** _d is divided by pi and _g is left as computed. The D-126
probe in getDustT, which rebuilds the electron term for a comparison,
follows.

revised ones held, for the reason the revision gave: the cold gas's cooling
slope stays near 4.

    s = 3.47. That is inside the 2.5-4.1 the revision assumed.
  - **One error of reasoning in the revision.** It said "since the slope
    probably falls as the gas warms, the lower half of each range is the
    more likely". That runs the wrong way: a slope that falls moves the
    result up, not down. The lower half held in dust10 because the slope
    did not fall much (3.98).

**(b) The core's coldest cell: photoelectric heating switched on.** It
landed above the revised range (12.50 K against 9.5-11.3 K), and the slope
is not the reason:
  - Its photoelectric heating was exactly 0 in the base run. In d421 it is
    4.62e-27 per H, 60% of the heating.
  - Its gas-grain heating rose 5.36e-29 -> 2.08e-27, x38.8. The coupling
    (x4.83 for H2, x4 pi), T_d - T_e (11.10 -> 5.74 K) and the thermal
    speed together give about x43.

The cold cores are starved of FUV packets:

| | cold cells | PE = 0 in base | switched on in the new run | their T_e | PE's median share where PE > 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| core | 62 | 32 | 4 | 7.34 -> 12.45 K | 0.82 |
| dust10 | 48 | 30 | 3 | 4.29 -> 11.51 K | 0.91 |

  - Where the heating is non-zero it moves with the packets. In dust10's 18
    cold cells with it, the median T_e went 13.87 -> 12.40 K, against the
    coupling's push. Row 5093 went 16.60 -> 5.18 K as its photoelectric
    heating went 1.89e-25 -> 0.
  - So a cold-core T_e in these runs is the coupling's answer only where no
    FUV packet arrives; elsewhere it is the packet sample's. The medians
    above mix the two.

**(c) The H2 rotational lines: a held heating that nothing rebuilds.** It
is the same in all three pairs. The details are in DEVLOG-H2.md H-043,
because this was measured on h2-model only.
  - **dust10.** (51,1,1), row 6050, sits at A_V 7.3 with n_H 3.5e4 and
    x(H2) 0.497.
    - It went 76.9 -> 955 K and carries the 0-0 S(2) and S(1) changes.
    - The gas-grain term only cools it (2.2% of its heating).
    - What holds it at 955 K is the PDR heating held through the
      temperature search: pdrHeatXtra/Hden, 1.51e-22 per H (3.23e-24 in
      d420).
    - Rebuilt on the finished model, that term's parts are:

      | part | per H |
      |---|---|
      | cosmic rays, heat(8) | 3.7e-28 |
      | turbulence, heat(9) | 7.0e-29 |
      | chemistry, heat(10): the 13 tagged reactions, from pdrGrid's abundances and rates_reduced.d | 7.3e-27 |
      | the H2 level model's terms, which is its own line cooling at 955 K | -1.73e-22 |

    - The cell has no FUV pumping (1.6e-37 s^-1), and 3D-PDR's own
      photodissociation and pumping heating there are exactly 0.
    - With no pumping, the levels' direct steady-state solve can return to
      the gas at most what formation puts in, about 2e-25 per H.
    - So about 1.5e-22 per H of the heating that held the cell is not
      accounted for.
  - **core.** 0-0 S(1) x1.10 comes from three cells:
    - (39,3,3), 84 -> 132 K: +9.3 points;
    - (43,1,4), 58 -> 108 K: +2.8;
    - (46,3,4), 102 -> 88 K: -3.5.
    In each, the unaccounted part of the held heating moved with T_e. In
    (39,3,3) it went 7.4e-24 -> 2.8e-23 per H; in (43,1,4), -1.0e-24 ->
    +1.5e-23.
  - **hiipdr.** Cells at A_V 2.2-2.6 sit at about 11 K or at 35-50 K, and
    some swapped between d420 and d421 in both directions: (22,9,14) went
    37.5 -> 11.7 K and (19,9,15) 12.4 -> 49.7 K. In the hot state the held
    heating is 1.3-2.0e-26 per H against a rebuilt 7e-28, and in the cold
    state the two agree. The cold core's maximum, 13.16 -> 38.57 K, is one
    of these cells. The H2 lines did not move.
  - **It is older than D-420.** In molecular cells (x(H2) > 0.1), with held
    over rebuilt:

    | run | molecular cells | median held/rebuilt | cells over 3x | cells over 10x |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | k1a-flow-q-dust10 (bb4f9aa, before D-420) | 218 | 0.970 | 18 | 6 |
    | k1a-flow-q-core3.5e5 (bb4f9aa) | 271 | 0.985 | 22 | 8 |
    | d420-k1a-dust10 | 223 | 0.969 | 18 | 6 |
    | d421-k1a-dust10 | 218 | 0.970 | 23 | 11 |
    | d421-k1a-core | 268 | 0.995 | 23 | 7 |
    | d420-hii31 | 13549 | 1.000 | 95 | 44 |
    | d421-hii31 | 13547 | 1.000 | 119 | 56 |

    The cells over 3x are warm transition gas, with median T_e 25-57 K. In
    them the unaccounted part is 38-80% of all the heating. In cold cells
    the rebuild closes to 2%.
  - **The comparison spans two iterations (found after the first version of
    this entry was committed).**
    - thermBudget's column is written by the last temperature search. It
      runs before the last pdrStep: updateCell at iteration_mod.f90:1261,
      pdrStep at :1986. The D-404 ion-only pass after them returns before
      the thermal balance (update_mod.f90:337-344).
    - So the held value is from iteration 29's pdrStep. Everything rebuilt
      is iteration 30's: pdrGrid.out, h2Cells' 3D-PDR terms, and the levels
      on the finished model.
    - What (c) calls unaccounted is therefore, at least in part, the change
      in these cells' PDR heating between the last two iterations. It is
      not shown to be a missing term. A cell whose heating moves 10-1000x
      from one iteration to the next has T_e following the previous
      iteration's value.
    - The energy bound in (51,1,1) holds for iteration 30's field. Whether
      iteration 29's field pumped it is not known, and the cold cores are
      FUV-starved (b).
  - Ruled out by reading the code: damping (iterDamp is 0); pdrStep
    skipping a cell (no return); a local cosmic-ray rate (ZETALOCAL is the
    input's); the level model's per-rank results being summed twice
    (cleared each sweep); and an inconsistent level solve (h2CollHeat uses
    the solve's T, colliders and populations).
  - A one-iteration warm restart cannot trace it: pdrHeatXtra is not in
    the checkpoint (D-351), so the first resumed balance runs without it.
    The decisive measurement records heat(1:12) at each pdrStep for a few
    such cells. That is a code change, and it needs a plan and the user's
    word.

**(d) Not attributed:** Hbeta +2.0% in hiipdr, and [S II] -15% in K1a.

**What it means.**
  - The gas-grain term now has its physical strength in both balances. The
    cold-cell coupling is 1.08 (dust10), 1.13 (core) and 1.20 (hiipdr) of
    BFM's rate, rebuilt without grain charge.
  - The cold-gas anomaly is smaller but not closed. The dust10 cold core's
    median is 7.16 K against T_d 20.4 K, and its coldest cell 6.41 K
    against 22.96 K. The core's median is 13.26 K against 21.18 K. Where no
    FUV arrives, the CO cooling at s near 4 still holds the gas at 0.3-0.6
    of the dust's temperature. Whether that is right is for a comparison to
    say, and none has been made: Cloudy, or 3D-PDR with its own gas-grain
    term on.
  - Every dusty model moves:
    - the ionized gas is 2.3% (K1a) and 3.4% (hiipdr) cooler;
    - [O III] 5008 falls 4.6% (K1a) and 16% (hiipdr), and 4363 falls 9%
      and 30%;
    - every published number for a dusty model predates this;
    - pn150k and the other benchmarks are not rerun.
  - The H2 line misses are not the change. They come from cells whose held
    heating swings between iterations, as in (c), and the K1a baselines
    already had those.

**Not yet known.**
  - What the held heating in (c) was made of at the iteration that set it.
    Whether production has the same swings: production has heat(5..7) from
    3D-PDR rather than from the levels, and has not been checked.
  - Why Hbeta rose 2% in hiipdr, and why [S II] fell 15% in K1a.
  - How much of the cold-core T_e is FUV packet sampling. A run with more
    packets, or a seed pair, would say.
  - L-9 is closed in doc/pdr-status.md.

## D-423 - Pushing production to GitHub, and why the checkout keeps its name (2026-10-20)

The user (2026-10-20): "I want to push this repository to my github
repository mocassin-pdr. I tried to rename this local one earlier. Should I
do it?" Pushing has been off limits in this project by the user's standing
rule, so this entry records the state and the advice, not a push.

**The remote.** `origin` is already https://github.com/hektor-monteiro/
mocassin-pdr.git. GitHub's API (read 11:48): public, not a fork, default
branch main, last push 2026-09-15 11:51 UTC. The remote holds main at
0fc4536 (D-284) and the tag pdr-coupling-v1.0, nothing else
(`git ls-remote`).

**What a push would do.**
  - pdr-photoionization tracks origin/main (branch.*.merge refs/heads/main)
    and push.default is `upstream`, so a plain `git push` from this branch
    updates the remote's main. No branch has to be renamed for it.
  - origin/main is an ancestor of HEAD: a fast-forward of 269 commits, from
    D-284 to D-422, with no force.
  - 268 files change, 108 of them new (49 in tools/, 29 in data/, 8 in
    dataPDR/). The largest blob is 2.8 MB (dustData/PAHneu_30.cat), well
    under GitHub's limits. A scan of the added lines for tokens, keys and
    passwords found none.
  - Everything in it becomes public: DEVLOG.md mentions the NGC 7009 K1a
    model 32 times and gives one ~/Documentos path, and the commit messages
    carry Claude session links. That is the user's call; nothing in it is a
    credential.
  - No tag goes with a plain push. pdr-coupling-v1.1 (this branch's science
    tag) and the reverted-work tags are local only. Pushing the release tag
    on its own would be `git push origin pdr-coupling-v1.1`.
  - h2-model and the other local branches stay local unless pushed by name.
  - No credential helper is set, so the push over HTTPS asks for a GitHub
    token, which is easier in the user's own terminal.

**Why the checkout should keep its name.** The directory name plays no part
in a push. Renaming ~/software/mocassin_HM_2026_3DPDR would break three
things that hold its path:
  - the h2-model worktree: ~/software/mocassin_h2/.git points at
    .git/worktrees/mocassin_h2 under this path (`git worktree repair` would
    fix it);
  - Claude Code's memory for this project, which is keyed by the path;
  - the ten benchmarks/pdr fixtures, whose input.in sets pdrDataDir to this
    checkout's dataPDR by absolute path, as do DEVLOG.md (3) and
    .claude/agents/code-executor.md (1).
None of the h2 or K1a runs' inputs depend on it (they read the h2 prefix's
dataPDR).

**Advice given.** Push; keep the name. Optionally push pdr-coupling-v1.1.

**Release notes** (for the GitHub release's description; the same text is in
runs/_release_check_v1.2/release-notes.md):

```markdown
## MOCASSIN-PDR pdr-coupling-v1.2 (2026-10-21)

The production coupling of MOCASSIN and 3D-PDR at DEVLOG D-425. It has 126 commits since
`pdr-coupling-v1.1` (2026-09-28, D-388), 18 of them changing the source or data files. Science
results should cite this tag. Each item names its DEVLOG.md entry.

### Changes that move results

- **Gas–grain energy exchange (D-420, D-421).** H2 now collides with the grains. Before,
  only atoms, ions and electrons did, so in molecular gas almost nothing coupled the gas to
  the dust. The term also enters each energy balance in that balance's own units. The gas
  side had been 4π too weak and the grain side 4 times too weak. In dusty models the ionised
  gas is 2–3.5% cooler.
- **Ionisation balance (D-402, D-403, D-404):**
  - Each network ion is its own ionisation stage.
  - Both solvers carry every channel of the neutral/first-ion balance, each computed once.
  - Charge transfer with H uses fits made for the gas at hand (He, Mg).
  - The temperature floor defaults to the CMB.
  - `ionBalance` is solved a second time after the chemistry, and the final iteration keeps
    that solve.
- **Chemistry (D-395).** Electron-impact dissociation of H2+ (reaction 332) is added. It was
  the network's missing H2+ sink in ionised gas, whose H2+ had been about 90 times Cloudy's.
- **Shielding columns (D-397, D-398).** The columns are integrated over the exact path through
  each cell. Before, they were sampled once per cell width. Scattered light's first leg now
  runs to the scattering site.
- **Convergence and iteration (D-391, D-392, D-406):**
  - A run stops on a model-integrated test (`convTotals`, default 0.02). It checks the
    emission measures, the H0/H2/CO contents and the weighted temperatures over three
    iterations.
  - The cell percentage is reported, not tested.
  - Damping across iterations is off by default (`iterDamp 0`; 0.25 gives the old blend).
- **Warm start (D-393).** `mocassinWarm` continues the PDR state instead of reseeding it.
- **Dust (D-413, D-414, D-415):**
  - Five-column Q files had failed at start-up since D-313; they load again.
  - The mean dust temperature now averages only the size bins that hold grains.
  - `PAHneu_30.cat` carries Im(m), taken from graphite as in Weingartner & Draine (2001), so
    PAHs heat the gas.
- **Atomic data (D-418).** Levels listed out of energy order broke the collision rates, and
  below 13.96 K gave NaN and crashed cold models.

### Validation

`doc/pdr-status.md` gives what is validated and what is known to be wrong (as of D-410). Its
figures were measured before D-420/D-421. The reference models in `benchmarks/pdr/` have not
been rerun with this release's gas–grain term.

### Known issues

- A bare `make` builds only one object file, because of the Makefile's default goal. Build
  with `make PDR=1 PDRGEOM=3D all` (see README).
- The `benchmarks/pdr` fixtures set `pdrDataDir` to an absolute path on the author's machine.
  Change it, or delete the line, before running them.
- A `PREFIX` longer than about 90 characters silently loses atomic data and crashes (D-416).
- The 1D slab flavour builds, but its models are out of scope (D-338).
- Shielded gas carries FUV packet noise (D-408, D-421). The twelve ray directions put an
  orientation pattern of up to about 11% into x(H2) at A_V 0.5–1 (D-410).
- The man page does not yet document `convTotals`, `iterDamp` or the newer PDR output files.

### Building

The four flavours (`PDR=1 PDRGEOM=3D`, `PDR=1`, no PDR, `PDR=1 mocassinWarm`) build from a fresh
clone of this tag with gfortran/Open MPI and SUNDIALS 7.8.0. Run `make clean` between flavours.

The H2 level model is developed on the `h2-model` branch and is not part of this release.
```

**To publish (the user's step; nothing pushed here).** From this checkout:

was merged into production.

both at today's tips):
  - four files exist only on the branch: source/h2_mod.f90 (1,570 lines),
    h2Lines_mod.f90 (169), h2Test.f90 (190), h2Slab.f90 (188);
  - hooks on the branch: pdr_mod.f90 +944, iteration_mod.f90 +23,
    common_mod.f90 +20, grid_mod.f90 +10, output_mod.f90 +8, Makefile;
  - 3,139 lines in all; production's source/ has no lineFluxH2 writer.

**Production's H2 is 3D-PDR's** (source/pdr/, read today):
  - formation on grains, Cazaux & Tielens (-DH2FORM_CT02), at MOCASSIN's
    grains and dust temperature (D-414);
  - photodissociation H2PDRATE (shield.F90): K0 G0 times the Federman,
    Glassgold & Kwan (1979) self-shielding H2SHIELD1 times dust scattering
    SCATTER(A_V); the Lee et al. (1996) table H2SHIELD2 is commented out;
  - heating by formation, photodissociation and FUV pumping (Hollenbach &
    McKee's 1/(1 + n_cr/n), D-384);
  - H2 as a collider for the line level populations (D-363) and in the
    gas-grain exchange (D-420).
It has no H2 level populations, no H2 line cooling (D-384) and no H2 line
spectrum. README.md says so ("H2 physics on this branch is 3D-PDR's",
Branches and versions).

**Release notes** (for the GitHub release; the same text is in
runs/_release_v2/release-notes.md):

```markdown
## MOCASSIN-PDR pdr-coupling-v2.0 (2026-10-21)

The first release with a detailed H2 level model. It is `pdr-coupling-v1.2` plus the `h2-model` branch,
merged at DEVLOG D-429. It has 156 commits since v1.2, most of them the H2 model's development since
2026-09-28 (DEVLOG-H2 H-001 to H-045). Science results should cite this tag.

### New: the H2 level model

- **What it solves.** In the 3D build (`PDRGEOM=3D`), H2's 302 rovibrational levels of the ground state
  X are solved in every cell with gas, on MOCASSIN's Monte Carlo radiation field:
  - collisions with H, He, ortho- and para-H2 and H+;
  - ultraviolet pumping through the B, C+, C−, B′, D+ and D− states (1,592 levels, 32,453 lines to X),
    with the cascade back into X and the Solomon dissociation;
  - formation on grains into the levels, in Takahashi & Uehara's distribution;
  - self-shielding with Voigt profiles and line overlap, and photon trapping along the rays.
- **What it feeds back.** Every PDR iteration it sets the chemistry's H2 photodissociation rate and the
  H2 heating: formation, dissociation, and collisional exchange within X, which is also H2's line
  cooling. Results of every 3D PDR model therefore differ from v1.x.
- **Outputs.** `lineFluxH2.out` (the H2 line spectrum), `h2Cells.out` (per cell) and `h2Pop.bin` (the
  populations, which `mocassinWarm` resumes).
- **New files:**
  - executables `h2Test` and `h2Slab`;
  - data in `dataPDR/h2/`: Cloudy c25.00's H2 data, copied unmodified under its zlib licence;
  - documentation: `doc/manual-pdr-h2.md`, `doc/h2-radiation-molecules/main.pdf` and `DEVLOG-H2.md`.
- **Where it runs.** The 3D build only. It is skipped, and the log says so, for more than one grid or
  for `planeIonization`. No keyword turns it off.
- **Cost.** About half to two thirds of a 3D PDR run's time: 22 of hiipdr's 42 minutes, 98 of
  pn150k's 149.

### Validation

- **The H2 model's own checks** (DEVLOG-H2):
  - the X-level populations match Cloudy's large H2 model to 0–0.5% (15 one-zone models);
  - the pumping and Solomon rates match Cloudy's to 1.000 when given Cloudy's populations;
  - line overlap is within 0.2–1.6% of the exact integral;
  - hiipdr's H2 lines are packet-converged to +0.8% from 6×10⁶ to 3.84×10⁸ packets.
- **Against Cloudy's large H2 model:**
  - hiipdr ortho lines 0.82–0.84, para lines 1.13–1.19;
  - pn150k ortho lines 0.96–1.17, para lines 1.95–2.72. Most of the para excess is the line width: a
    line's natural width is its upper level's total decay rate, and Cloudy uses the line's own A.
- **The release check (D-429)**, with the production build of the merge:
  - **hiipdr 31³:** reproduces the H2 branch's tested run in every output file, apart from
    `summary.out`'s clock times.
  - **pn150k 41³** (seeded, 18 iterations, against its last H2-model run). This is the first
    measurement there of D-418, D-420 and D-421:
    - health clean, with 3 flagged cells;
    - ionised-gas median T_e ×0.996, with the gas–grain share of the cooling 1.2×10⁻³ → 1.5×10⁻²;
    - Hβ +0.5%; forbidden lines −0.8% to −2.7%; [O I], [N I] and [C I] −0.7% to −1.6%;
    - H2 lines within 0.25%;
    - the last integrated change was 1.55%, under the 2% default stop.
- **Not yet updated:** `doc/pdr-status.md` is as of D-410 and does not cover the H2 model, and the
  published comparison pages predate D-420/D-421.

### Known issues

- **Transition-zone H2.** Where the gas is partly ionised, H2 is 14–62 times Cloudy's in hiipdr and
  30–230 times in pn150k (H-021, H-023). Cloudy forms excited H2 there, which electrons destroy before it
  relaxes.
- **Molecular cells whose PDR heating swings.** In some molecular cells the PDR heating swings between
  iterations, so treat the H2 rotational lines they carry as unconverged (H-043).
- **The test problem's face-on maps** are 3–5.5% fainter on the y side, although the model is symmetric
  under x ↔ y. The cause is not known (H-037).
- **Carried from v1.2:**
  - a bare `make` builds only one object file, so build with `make PDR=1 PDRGEOM=3D all`;
  - the `benchmarks/pdr` inputs set an absolute `pdrDataDir`;
  - a `PREFIX` longer than about 90 characters loses atomic data (D-416);
  - the 1D models are out of scope (D-338);
  - FUV packet noise in shielded gas (D-408, D-421);
  - the twelve ray directions (D-410);
  - the man page does not document `convTotals`, `iterDamp` or the newer PDR outputs.

### Building

At the merge (D-429), all four flavours and `h2Test`/`h2Slab` built with gfortran/Open MPI and SUNDIALS
7.8.0:
- `make PDR=1 PDRGEOM=3D all` (with the H2 model);
- `make PDR=1 all`;
- `make all`;
- `make PDR=1 mocassinWarm`.

Run `make clean` between builds. H2 development continues on the `h2-model` branch.
```

## D-432 - A Read the Docs site for the project (2026-10-21)

The user (2026-10-21): "Now I want to start creating the documentation for
the project using readthedocs. ... I want the documentation to describe all
the details and assumptions of the code with direct references to code
blocks where it is implemented. I also want the documentation to have a
quickstart section ... show the current results of the benchmarks for gas,
dust and PDR models. We should adopt the hiipdr and 150kkpn models as the
pdr benchmarks, including the Cloudy comparisons. It should also have a
section with a tutorial on how to run a full dust+gas+PDR model based on
test_problem." The plan was held until the H2 model reached production
(D-429/D-430) and then made against v2.0. Documentation and its tooling,
not a change to what the code computes.

**What exists (surveyed 2026-10-21).** No docs tooling (no conf.py,
mkdocs.yml, .readthedocs.yaml or CI). Prose is in README.md, man/mocassin.1
(Ercolano 2015, missing 23 of the keywords readInput parses: convTotals,
teSolver, iterDamp, randomSeed, pathStretch, cvUseH2, ...), doc/dust.md,
doc/pdr-status.md, doc/manual-pdr-h2.md, the LaTeX report
doc/h2-radiation-molecules/ and source/pdr/UPSTREAM.md. The release runs
runs/_release_v2/rel-hii31 and rel-pn41 (binary built at c1ea374,
source-identical to 53c17eb, 14 ranks, randomSeed 1001, 6e6 packets) are
the only benchmark runs at v2.0; the Cloudy c25.00 references are
runs/d396-cloudy-{hii,pn}. Gas (Lexington x4), dust (1D x3, 2D x4) and
test_Problem have not been run at v2.0. No dust reference solution exists
in the tree. GitHub cannot display DEVLOG.md (2.4 MB), so the site cannot
link into it.

**Decided** (the user's answers, 2026-10-21):
  - Code references are resolved on the docs side: a Sphinx extension
    (docs/_ext/fortref) finds a routine by `file::host/routine`, optionally
    narrowed by a unique text match, and links to a source viewer on the
    site plus a GitHub permalink at the built commit. No markers are added
    to the Fortran. An unresolved or ambiguous reference fails the build.
  - Delivered in increments. The MVP: install and running; complete keyword,
    output and build references generated with build-time checks against
    readInput, the writers and the Makefile; the PDR coupling and H2 physics
    chapters, converted from the LaTeX report (which becomes their source;
    main.tex frozen, main.pdf kept as the v2.0 snapshot); limitations; the

## D-433 - Documentation site, increment 1 (2026-10-22)

D-432's first increment, built on branch `docs` (worktree
~/software/mocassin_docs, from 6d8007c; commits ad98936, e30428f, 3b9bb3c,
12a59d5, b077f54, 7645c8e). Documentation and its tooling only: nothing
under source/, the Makefile, tools/ or dataPDR/ changed. Not pushed and not
merged into production yet.

**What the site holds.** docs/ (Sphinx 8.2.3, myst-parser 4.0.1, furo;
.readthedocs.yaml, fail_on_warning):
  - overview, installation, running, citing, licence;
  - generated references, each with a build-time completeness check: input
    keywords (docs/reference/keywords.yaml against every `case` label of
    readInput: 91 active, 31 retired), output files (outputs.yaml against
    every `open(... 'output/...')`: 42), build flavours and flags (Makefile),
    changelog (DEVLOG release notes), code map (every compiled unit);
  - the H2 report (doc/h2-radiation-molecules, now frozen; main.pdf kept as
    the v2.0 snapshot) converted into docs/physics/pdr (14 pages), its 446
    line references turned into routine + text anchors and updated for
    D-414, D-418, D-420, D-421;
  - doc/pdr-status.md, doc/dust.md, doc/manual-pdr-h2.md and
    source/pdr/UPSTREAM.md included in place;
  - hiipdr and pn150k against Cloudy c25.00 from runs/_release_v2 (reduced by
    docs/bench/reduce.py to 0.5 MB of CSV/JSON with sha256 provenance; figures
    drawn at build time by docs/bench/plots.py).

**Checks.** `sphinx-build -W --keep-going` rc 0, 0 warnings (about 9 s
fresh); `python -m fortref check docs` 1172 references, 0 problems; pytest
113 passed. reduce.py reproduces the d405 hiipdr page numbers to the %.6g
rounding (worst 1.06e-6), gives identical CSVs for rel-hii31 and d421-hii31,
and finds the committed Cloudy inputs' physics commands identical to the
D-396 runs'.

**Referee reviews** (two agents: PDR/molecules, transfer/photoionisation;
every major finding checked against the code or DEVLOG before applying).
Corrected in the pages, among others: the 7.4% gas-grain share is the
ionised gas's (D-421), not H2's; hiipdr's deeper H/H2 crossing is +0.21 mag
from the damping width and -0.09 mag from the rest (H-026), not grain
formation first; pn150k's width test is H-026's stage B (para 0.70-0.93,
ortho 0.45-0.69 of Cloudy's), not H-008's stage A; hiipdr's last-window
change, 2.04% (Ne+), is above the default 2%; the ionised gas of both models
shows low-ionisation excesses (hiipdr x(O+) 1.4-1.6x, x(C+) 1.5-1.8x at
A_V 0.17-0.31; pn150k [O II] +13-18%, [N II] +10-23%, He II 4686 +24% with
a smaller, cooler He2+ zone - not explained), and MOCASSIN's A_V is 1-4.5%
below Cloudy's at fixed radius.

**Code behaviour found while documenting (not fixed; each needs its own
plan):**
  - `pdr` without its integer swallows the next input line, which is lost
    silently (list-directed read, set_input_mod.f90:642-643; agent's
    gfortran test).
  - `fillingFactor` < 1 zeroes whole cells at random from an unseeded
    generator called on every rank before the seeding (grid_mod.f90:1043-1048;
    photon_mod.f90 seeds later), so ranks may hold different grids and
    `randomSeed` does not make such runs reproducible.
  - Secondary ionisation by fast photoelectrons is absent: `secIonP` is set
    (hydro_mod.f90:345) and never used. A likely contributor to pn150k's low
    x(H+) and n_e behind the front (0.21-0.48 and 0.36-0.52 of Cloudy's),
    not measured.
  - `MdMg`, `MdMh` and `Ndust` exclusivity is checked only when all three are
    given (set_input_mod.f90:932); the per-cell MdMg/MdMh file is read as
    three integers and the ratio (grid_mod.f90:1105).
  - Keywords parsed with no effect: `H0Start`, `NeStart`, `pdrDiagAV`.
  - `lineFlux.ext` is never written (no program passes outputGas an
    extinction map).
  - SED.out's footer labels the total as erg/s x 1e36 while writing
    totalE*1e-36 of a value already in 1e36 erg/s (output_mod.f90:3457).
  - With multiChemistry + debug, ionDen.out is closed inside the loop and
    later writes go to fort.60 (output_mod.f90:1770); with sub-grids,
    qHeatPss.out's later writes go to fort.89 (iteration_mod.f90:425) and
    summary.out keeps only the last grid's first-iteration block.
  - h2Pop.bin is written with the outputs, not the grid files, so a warm
    start after a crash restarts the H2 populations.
  - `CC ?= gcc` has no effect (GNU make predefines CC=cc).
  - The v2.0 release notes (D-430) and README quote hiipdr H2 line ratios
    from H-019 (ortho 0.82-0.84, para 1.13-1.19); the release run gives
    ortho 0.71-0.80 and para 0.95-1.09 (pn150k: notes 0.96-1.17/1.95-2.72,
    run 0.89-1.16/1.65-2.69).
  - README's "standard test problem (Meudon standard HII region)" describes
    benchmarks/test_Problem wrongly (it is the dusty ring-and-slab model).

**Not yet done in increment 1:** pushing `docs` and creating the Read the
Docs project (the user's actions); merging `docs` into production after the
user has seen the site. Later increments as planned in D-432 (quickstart and
Lexington, the test_Problem tutorial, dust benchmarks, the original MOCASSIN
physics).

## D-434 - Licensing audit (2026-10-22)

The user (2026-10-22): "now do a full audit focusing on licensing. Check that
all the code is properly credited and flag any use that is inconsistent with
the original licences. We do not want to use anything irregular."

Three read-only audits (code provenance; bundled data; licence texts and
compatibility), each finding then checked by the main session against the
files. Upstreams compared: rwesson/mocassin @50c0706 and this fork's import
38aca36, 3D-PDR @fabcdc6, Cloudy c25.00 (~/software/cloudy-c25.00),
HEALPix pix_tools.F90, DUSTY's Lib_nk, the providers' terms pages. Not a
legal opinion. Nothing was changed.

**Compatibility.** MOCASSIN (GPL-2.0-or-later, stated only in mocassin.f90's
header; upstream has no LICENSE file), HEALPix (GPL-2.0-or-later), 3D-PDR
(GPL-3.0-or-later; its LICENSE is byte-identical to ours), Cloudy (zlib) and
SUNDIALS (BSD-3, linked) combine as GPL-3.0-or-later. LICENSE is the
unmodified GPL v3 text. No non-commercial or no-redistribution term was
found anywhere except Numerical Recipes.

**Licence conflicts (must be fixed).**
  1. Numerical Recipes, whose licence forbids redistributing source or
     executables that contain it, so it cannot be conveyed under the GPL:
     - source/pdr/spline.F90: "Copied from Numerical Recipes" (SPLINE,
       SPLINT, SPLIE2, SPLIN2, hunt), NR's comments kept word for word;
       compiled, used for H2 and CO shielding (shield.F90). Inherited from
       3D-PDR.
     - source/pdr/solvlevpop.F90: GAUSS_JORDAN is NR gaussj (header says so,
       NR's variables IPIV/INDXR/INDXC/PIVINV); compiled, every coolant
       level-population solve. GAUSS_JORDAN_writes: never called. Inherited.
     - source/interpolation_mod.f90 polint/spline/splint: NR-derived, compiled,
       never called (MOCASSIN upstream).
     - Written in this project with NR's heapsort structure: cvSortD
       (iteration_mod.f90, D-196), indexSort (h2_mod.f90), heapSortIdx
       (pdr_mod.f90).
     D-271's licence check missed these.
  2. data/badnell_dr.dat, badnell_rr.dat: N. R. Badnell's fits from Cloudy's
     copies, "(C)20230512 N. R. BADNELL" line stripped, no grant to
     redistribute; brought in by the D-330 sync and read by nothing in
     source/.

**Notice and attribution gaps (compatible licences, obligations unmet).**
  - Cloudy (zlib): yanH2xSec (ionization_mod.f90, "Ported from Cloudy c25's
    Yan_H2_CS"), h2ShieldFederman (h2_mod.f90; Cloudy's shieldFederman line for
    line, its literals 0.66666 and 0.78540) and h2FormDist (adapted from
    mole_h2_create.cpp) carry no zlib notice, and README, licence.md, h2_mod's
    header and dataPDR/h2/README.md say the H2 code is "not Cloudy's"; the 15
    Stout ports in data/ are marked but the notice is not reproduced.
  - HEALPix: source/pdr/healpix.F90 holds pix_tools.F90 routines with the
    copyright header removed (already upstream); credited nowhere.
  - DUSTY (BSD-3, (C)2016 Z. Ivezic): about 17 dustData/*.nk files from Lib_nk,
    no notice.
  - SUNDIALS (BSD-3): calculate_abundances.c's check_flag is the SUNDIALS
    example helper, no notice.
  - Modification notes missing: hydro_mod.f90, fluorescence_mod.f90,
    readdata_mod.f90 (R. Wesson's, no header), the Makefile, man/mocassin.1.
  - UPSTREAM.md: "GPL-3.0 (same as MOCASSIN)" (MOCASSIN is GPL-2.0-or-later),
    "six files" (eight), and the D-357 swap in dataPDR/species_reduced.d (H2+
    and CH5+ lines exchanged) is not declared.
  - Uncredited: SEREN (heapsort.F90, definitions.F90), Storey & Hummer 1995
    (hdatx/hlinex), EQUIB (probable, luSlv), Starburst99 spectra in
    examples/multistars.tar.gz, HeIrecLines.dat (fits to Porter et al. from
    PyNeb), dust optical-data sources (no dustData README; enstatite files carry
    crSil's Jaeger 1994 footer over 5,330 rows of other data).
  - Citations: 3D-PDR asks for its JOSS paper; RAYTHEIA (Zhu et al. 2026) is
    compiled into the 3D build and not cited; Cloudy's current release paper.
  - Docs: no copyright line (the live footer reads "(C) Copyright ."); make
    install does not install LICENSE.

**Unclear rights (decisions for the user).** dust_nk_Nwright.tar.gz and
dustData_POwen.tar.gz (private compilations "provided by Dr. Mike Barlow",
publication permission unrecorded, stored up to three times with editor
backups); dustData/H2Oice-15-200um-Curtisetal2005.txt (an OSA-copyright table
transcribed whole, unused); benchmarks/test_Problem/input/200000_7.00__He (a
stellar spectrum of unknown origin, unused); the unused UMIST full/medium
networks (UDfA states no licence); data.chianty-7/ and data.chianty-10/ (old
CHIANTI sets, unused, undocumented); accessories/compare_Mie_CDE.py's copy of
the circulating bhmie.py (no licence stated).

### Status
